Even though no concrete duties are listed and the activities shown are generic HR references, the managerial nature of the role makes action planning and implementation oversight materially relevant. Because the description still lacks explicit governance or planning responsibilities, the relevance is Medium rather than High.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the work description explicitly centers on collection operations and collection methods. The subprocess covers preparing collection strategy, instruments, methods, respondent interaction, and monitoring mechanisms. The position participates in 'the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' and 'provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding.' Those statements show direct operational involvement in collection design choices and ongoing refinement of collection approaches. The capability involved is operational expertise in collection methods, procedures, respondent/data-supplier interaction, and translating business needs into workable collection processes. Evidence also includes preparing 'procedures, operational specifications and training for the manual and automated collection' and meeting with specialists, clients and service providers to understand 'the conditions within which statistical operations will occur.' Future-state drivers indicate this work will change materially. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production point to chatbot-assisted interaction, automation, monitoring-heavy workflows, and reduced manual effort. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure indicate stronger use of online-first collection, APIs, digital tools, and mixed-source acquisition. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access is relevant because the role already works in collection operations and must apply awareness of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act 'with respect to the security and confidentiality of data'; future collection design will increasingly embed secure access, privacy and cyber controls. Workforce implications are also direct: the role already contributes to training materials and delivery, and the drivers emphasize tools and training, digital readiness, and a shift from traditional manual collection toward more automated and digitally enabled collection operations.

This subprocess is materially connected because the position works directly on coding and processing operations and on specifying how systems should support those activities. The subprocess covers design of coding, editing, validation, integration and estimation methods for the Process and Analyse phases. The work description states the incumbent participates in 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' evaluates 'methods, procedures and results of statistical collection, coding and processing operations,' develops 'system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers,' and develops 'test cases and data from functional specifications' to ensure applications meet requirements. That is direct evidence of involvement in the operational and methodological design of processing activities. The capability involved is knowledge of statistical processing methods, verification practices, systems analysis, data flows, and translating operational requirements into processing specifications. The description also cites 'knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications' and 'knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows.' Future-state drivers strongly intensify this connection. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will reshape coding, validation, editing and integration toward AI-enabled automated coding, automation, and more reusable processing routines. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will shift work toward orchestrated, modular processing steps and exception handling. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the importance of standardized metadata in processing rules. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push redesign toward lower-manual-effort processing. Workforce implications are significant because the role already bridges operations and systems, and future changes will require more skills in modern tools, workflow integration, and oversight of automated processing rather than only manual execution.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position helps define how collection, coding and processing activities fit together operationally and technically. The subprocess concerns end-to-end workflow design, reuse of systems and databases, and how staff interact with systems and who is responsible for what and when. The work description provides strong evidence: the incumbent 'develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems,' 'assesses and reviews system requirements,' prepares 'procedures, operational specifications and training,' and develops testing approaches to ensure applications meet requirements. The role also participates on operational teams and meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients and service providers to understand operational conditions and resolve differences affecting efficiency and output quality. That is direct workflow and production-system involvement, even if not at a senior architecture level. The capability involved is operational systems thinking: understanding data flows, system interactions, specifications, testing, and operational handoffs across collection and processing. Future-state drivers make this even more central. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development all point to more integrated, reusable, automated workflows with clearer handoffs and stronger monitoring. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward leaner, standardized workflows with fewer redundancies. Workforce implications are direct because the role already writes procedures and training and participates in teams improving methods; future work will increasingly involve adapting to pipeline supervision, exception handling, reusable enterprise workflows, and modern platforms.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because the position contributes requirements, testing logic, and operational specifications for processing applications and components, even if it is not described as the primary software builder. The subprocess covers reusing or building components needed for Process and Analyse. The work description states the incumbent 'develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers,' 'assesses and reviews system requirements,' and 'develops test cases and data from functional specifications and specifies testing approaches' to ensure applications meet requirements. This shows meaningful contribution to component development and reuse through business requirements, functional interpretation, and testing support. The capability involved is translating operational processing needs into component requirements and validating that built components support coding and processing operations. Future-state drivers increase the importance of reusable processing components, AI-enabled coding services, workflow tools, metadata services, and enterprise platforms. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development all suggest that processing components will become more standardized, reusable, and automation-heavy. Workforce implications include greater need for modern technical literacy, validation, and collaboration with technical teams. The role's existing evidence of working with analysts/programmers and specifying tests indicates it will be meaningfully affected by these changes.

This subprocess is relevant because the position helps operationalize workflows through specifications, procedures, testing approaches, and support to users of divisional systems and processes. The subprocess concerns configuring workflows, systems and transformations from collection through dissemination based on prior design. The work description does not say the incumbent is the primary workflow configurator, but it does show regular contribution: preparing and distributing 'procedures, operational specifications and training,' developing system requirements, specifying testing approaches, and responding to enquiries about 'the operation of divisional systems and processes.' The capability involved is configuring or supporting configured operational workflows by defining how they should work, documenting them, and validating them. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment indicate more standardized, automated, and monitored workflows with fewer manual checkpoints. That means a role currently focused on procedures, specifications, and testing will likely shift toward supporting automation-first workflow execution, exception handling, and clearer role-based handoffs. Evidence from the work description about manual and automated operations, system requirements, and testing supports this connection.

This subprocess is directly relevant because testing is explicitly part of the work description. The subprocess covers technical testing and sign-off of assembled services, routines and workflows, including checking files, metadata and interactions between services. The work description states the incumbent 'develops test cases and data from functional specifications and specifies testing approaches for own use and use by other program staff to ensure that computer applications meet requirements.' It also notes knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows, and responsibility for assessing system requirements for existing or new processing systems. This is direct evidence of capability in production-system testing. The capability involved is designing test cases, validating applications against requirements, and ensuring operational systems support collection, coding and processing correctly. Future-state drivers make this more important: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development all increase the complexity of integration, automation, interoperability, and secure testing. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access also matters because the role already works under confidentiality and security obligations, and future testing will increasingly include secure transmission, access controls, and protected environments. Workforce implications include stronger need for validation, governance, and skills to test automated and modular systems rather than only traditional applications.

This subprocess is relevant because the role contributes to documentation, user guidance, and training needed to put systems into production, though it is not described as owning deployment. The subprocess includes producing technical documentation and user manuals, training users, and ensuring systems work in production. The work description provides direct evidence: the incumbent 'writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports,' 'provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery,' and prepares procedures and operational specifications for manual and automated collection, coding and processing. The capability involved is operational readiness support: documenting processes, preparing users, and helping ensure systems can be used effectively in production. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production indicate that production finalization will require more training, clearer documentation, and stronger user readiness for automated, platform-based, and digitally modernized systems. The role is therefore meaningfully affected because its current responsibilities already include manuals, training packages, and operational guidance.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position supports operational readiness for collection through procedures, training, user advice, and participation in collection operations teams. The subprocess covers preparing people, processes and technology for collection, including training staff, configuring systems, preparing instruments, ensuring security, and setting up non-survey source receipt processes. The work description states the incumbent participates in 'implementation, conduct and maintenance' of collection operations, prepares and distributes 'procedures, operational specifications and training for the manual and automated collection,' provides assistance and advice on collection methods and practices, participates on data collection teams, and contributes to training materials and delivery. The capability involved is operational setup and readiness for collection activities, including staff preparation and procedural support. Future-state drivers strongly affect this work. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production point to mixed-source collection, online-first operations, APIs, and digital setup. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure point to more digital tools, automated channels, and infrastructure readiness. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access is especially relevant because the work description explicitly requires awareness of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act to ensure security and confidentiality compliance. Workforce implications are direct because the role already supports training and operational readiness, and future collection setup will require more digital skills, technical support, and adaptation to modernized collection environments.

This subprocess is one of the most directly connected to the work description. It covers implementing collection, respondent and supplier interaction, monitoring collection, making adjustments, and producing collection reports. The position explicitly 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'participates on data collection and operations teams,' contacts 'data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities,' and responds to enquiries about divisional systems and processes. It also analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports on how the survey was conducted and problems encountered. The capability involved is hands-on collection operations, respondent/supplier liaison, issue resolution, and operational monitoring. Future-state drivers indicate major change: AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase automated follow-up, monitoring, and digital respondent interaction; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will shift some work toward supplier-based receipt and mixed-source collection; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will intensify deadline-driven monitoring and intervention; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will strengthen secure live collection requirements. Workforce implications include reduced manual effort, more digital monitoring, and the need for adaptable staff who can operate in mixed-source and automated collection environments. The work description provides strong evidence that this role is already central to collection execution and will be heavily affected by these drivers.

This subprocess is relevant because the role works across collection, coding and processing and therefore participates in the handoff from collected data into processing environments, even if the description does not explicitly mention loading or archiving. The subprocess includes loading collected data and metadata, format conversion, metadata/paradata analysis, versioning and archiving. Evidence comes from the role's participation in 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' knowledge of computer processing and data flows, and knowledge of databases for regular production and ad hoc manipulations and retrievals. The capability involved is operational understanding of how collected data move into processing and how formats, systems and procedures must support that transition. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will make this handoff more automated, metadata-rich, and platform-based. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access is also relevant because the work description explicitly emphasizes confidentiality and compliance. The connection is medium rather than high because the description supports involvement in the collection-to-processing continuum, but does not explicitly assign ownership of loading, archiving, or pseudonymisation.

This subprocess is relevant because the role works in processing operations, understands data flows and databases, and analyses changes to data sources and outputs for their impact on program integrity and completeness. The subprocess covers combining data from multiple sources, harmonising values, linkage and prioritisation. The work description does not explicitly mention record linkage, but it does state the incumbent has 'knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows,' knowledge of databases for production and ad hoc retrievals, and 'analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results.' It also notes knowledge of data sources within and outside Statistics Canada. The capability involved is operational assessment of source changes, consistency, and downstream processing implications. Future-state drivers make this more important: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure all increase multi-source integration, harmonisation, and reusable integrated data environments. The role will likely be increasingly affected because source changes and integration complexity will alter the collection/coding/processing operations it supports. Relevance is medium because the description supports meaningful involvement and impact, but not explicit ownership of linkage or integration methodology.

This subprocess is directly relevant because coding is explicitly named throughout the work description. The subprocess covers classifying and coding input data using automated or manual routines. The position participates in 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' evaluates 'collection and coding methods, procedures and results,' provides advice on 'methods and practices of collection and coding,' and has knowledge of 'the underlying statistical and economic principles and concepts required for the collection, coding and processing of data.' The capability involved is operational coding expertise, method evaluation, and support to users on coding practices. Future-state drivers are especially strong here. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production explicitly point to AI-enabled automated coding, reduced manual effort, and integration of AI assistants into daily work. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment reinforces pressure to replace clerical coding with automation under reduced staffing. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will strengthen standard classifications and coding definitions. Workforce implications are substantial because the role's current coding responsibilities will likely shift toward supervising automated coding, handling exceptions, validating outputs, and supporting training and adoption of new tools. The work description provides direct evidence of both current coding responsibility and future susceptibility to automation-driven change.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role explicitly evaluates methods, procedures and results, verifies data reliability and consistency, analyses reported data and work results, and reports on problems encountered in survey implementation. The subprocess concerns identifying errors, discrepancies, duplicates, miscoding and other quality issues before correction. Evidence includes 'evaluates methods, procedures and results of statistical collection, coding and processing operations,' knowledge of 'methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications,' and 'analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports' presenting findings and recommending alternatives. The capability involved is operational quality review, validation, and issue identification across collection, coding and processing. Future-state drivers intensify this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment all point to more automated validation, anomaly detection, and exception-based review. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increases heterogeneity and validation complexity across sources. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the need to validate metadata as well as data. Workforce implications include a shift from broad manual checking toward oversight of automated validation outputs and targeted investigation of flagged cases. The role's current evidence aligns strongly with this subprocess.

This subprocess is relevant because the role works in coding and processing operations, evaluates procedures and results, and has knowledge of verification and consistency methods, although the description does not explicitly mention performing imputation. The subprocess covers correcting incorrect or missing data, applying rule-based methods, and producing metadata on changes. Evidence supporting relevance includes participation in coding and processing operations, evaluation of methods and results, and knowledge of methods used to verify data and ensure reliability and consistency. The capability involved is understanding and supporting data correction processes within operational processing environments. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment suggest more automated and model-assisted editing and imputation, reducing manual intervention and increasing the need for oversight and documentation. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is also relevant because edit/imputation metadata become more important. Relevance is medium because the role is clearly adjacent to and affected by edit/imputation processes, but the supplied work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for selecting or applying imputation methods.

This subprocess has plausible but limited relevance. The role works across collection, coding and processing, understands data flows and databases, and analyses outputs and source changes, which means it may be affected by derivation logic used in processing. However, the work description does not explicitly state responsibility for deriving variables or units. The capability connection is indirect: knowledge of computer processing, databases, and statistical concepts supports understanding of derived outputs, and the role analyses changes to data sources and outputs for impacts on integrity and completeness. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production suggest more reliance on derived variables from linked and administrative sources, which could affect operational processing roles like this one. Still, because no explicit derivation responsibility is stated, relevance remains low.

This subprocess is relevant because the role spans collection, coding and processing operations and has responsibilities tied to system requirements, data flows, databases, and reporting on operational results. The subprocess brings together processing outputs into datasets for analysis. Evidence includes participation in 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' knowledge of 'computer processing and data flows,' and knowledge of databases for regular production and ad hoc retrievals. The capability involved is operational preparation of processed data for downstream use, including understanding how outputs from multiple processing steps become usable datasets. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and AI and Automation in Statistical Production indicate more standardized, automated, metadata-rich finalization and handoff to analysis. The role is likely to be affected because its current work already sits in the operational chain that produces those files, though the description does not explicitly assign ownership of final file assembly.

This subprocess is relevant because the role prepares analytical and explanatory materials derived from operational results. The subprocess transforms processed data into outputs and prepares methodological notes and supporting materials. Evidence from the work description includes 'designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications,' writes 'management reports,' and analyses reported data and work results to present findings and recommend alternatives. The capability involved is preparing operationally informed draft outputs, explanatory material, and reporting products. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production suggest more automated output preparation, richer metadata, and greater need to explain AI-supported or mixed-source methods. Workforce implications include stronger need for analytical communication and use of modern tools. Relevance is medium because the role clearly contributes to draft outputs, though it is not framed as the primary analytical release authority.

This subprocess is relevant because the role analyses outputs, compares results, and reports on operational problems affecting output quality and consistency. The subprocess concerns validating outputs against expectations, metadata, quality indicators and auxiliary information. Evidence includes knowledge of data sources within and outside Statistics Canada 'to locate, analyze and compare statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability,' analysis of changes to data sources and outputs to determine impacts on integrity and completeness, and preparation of reports for managers or subject matter specialists on survey conduct and problems encountered. The capability involved is output-level consistency checking and operational interpretation of quality issues. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the need to validate outputs affected by source substitution, linkage, and automated methods. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability also matters because metadata completeness becomes part of validation. Relevance is medium because the role clearly contributes evidence and analysis used in output validation, though it is not explicitly described as the final statistical validator.

This subprocess is relevant because the role prepares explanatory text, communicates with users and stakeholders, and reports on findings from survey operations and outputs. The subprocess concerns understanding and explaining the meaning of outputs. Workforce implications include changing collection workload, reduced manual effort, and need for staff adaptation to digital and mixed-source environments. The work description directly supports this subprocess.

This subprocess is relevant because the position oversees collection, capture, coding and processing activities and advises on capture and processing of statistical data, which connects to the handoff from collection into processing. The capability involved is ensuring collected data and associated metadata/paradata are prepared for downstream processing. Evidence includes responsibility for 'collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data' and coordination of those activities across programs. The research section also notes investigation of gaps and inconsistencies in collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation, Administrative and Alternative Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Cyber Security will increase automation of loading, versioning, metadata handling, pseudonymisation and secure handoff into downstream pipelines. Because the work description supports oversight of these functions but does not explicitly describe loading, archiving or versioning tasks, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is one of the most directly connected to the role. The capability involved is combining, harmonising, prioritising and interpreting data from multiple sources to produce coherent statistical information. The work description repeatedly emphasizes this: the incumbent identifies appropriate data sources; recommends 'data integration from different sources'; reviews programs involving 'the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses)'; assesses methods used to 'integrate and interpret massive volumes of data'; and requires knowledge 'to integrate conceptually different data from other programs.' It also notes that source data collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts must be translated into common concepts. Future-state impacts are very strong. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production make integration, linkage and harmonisation central production capabilities. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will support scalable, reusable integration environments and automated flows. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will improve interoperability and reuse through standardized metadata. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase the importance of controlled linkage environments, de-identification and secure access. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will further push substitution of direct collection with integrated existing sources. The work description provides direct evidence of responsibility and expertise in this area, so relevance is high.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position directly coordinates and advises on coding activities and determines standards and techniques used in coding and processing. The capability involved is applying and governing coding approaches, classifications and related quality controls. Evidence includes 'coordinates and reviews collection, coding, processing and client-relation activities,' 'provides expert advisory and consultative services to users on the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data,' and knowledge of 'advanced statistical theories, methods ... used in the collection, capture, coding, processing and interpretation of statistical data.' The role also determines concepts, definitions, standards and techniques to be applied. Future-state impacts are significant. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production directly affect this subprocess through AI-enabled automated coding, reduced manual effort, and embedded workflow automation. Administrative and Alternative Data Expansion will increase recoding and harmonisation needs for non-standard source-system codes. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will strengthen use of common classifications and semantic consistency. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will intensify pressure to replace clerical coding with automated routines. Workforce implications include upskilling staff to supervise, validate and tune automated coding rather than perform routine manual coding. Because coding is explicitly named in the work description, relevance is high.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position analyzes data quality, investigates inconsistencies, determines reasons for variances, and reviews comparability and relevance of outputs. The capability involved is detecting errors, anomalies, inconsistencies and quality issues across collected and integrated data. Evidence includes that the incumbent 'analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.' The role also 'researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures used' and assesses techniques used to integrate and interpret large volumes of data. Future-state impacts are strong. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase validation complexity because of heterogeneous sources, linkage risks, source drift and automated methods. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase use of automated anomaly detection and exception-based review. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will embed validation checkpoints into automated flows. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata completeness and consistency part of validation. Workforce implications include a shift from broad manual checking to targeted review of flagged exceptions. The work description clearly supports this subprocess.

This subprocess is relevant because the position recommends imputation methods and oversees processing methods where correction of missing, inconsistent or unreliable data is part of production. The capability involved is selecting and governing editing and imputation approaches within statistical operations. Evidence includes that the incumbent 'recommends survey content and design, sample estimation and imputation methods' and provides expertise on coding and processing. The role also reviews methods used in processing and resolves analytical and operational problems. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push editing and imputation toward more automated, model-assisted and source-prioritized methods, especially where administrative data can replace missing survey values. Metadata-Driven Data Management will increase the importance of documenting edits and imputations. Because the work description shows methodological influence rather than explicit hands-on execution of edit/impute routines, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is relevant because the position works with concepts, definitions, integration of multiple sources, and production of statistical information where derived variables and harmonized constructs are needed. The capability involved is deriving analytical variables and units from existing data and integrated sources. Evidence includes responsibility for determining concepts, definitions, standards and techniques; integrating conceptually different data; identifying and measuring relationships among variables to produce statistical information; and recommending data integration from different sources. The work description also notes that source data collected for other purposes must be translated into common concepts, which often underpins derivation. Future-state impacts from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase reliance on derived variables and units from linked, administrative and geospatial sources, while Integrated Data Pipelines and Metadata-Driven Data Management will require explicit sequencing and documentation of derivations. Because derivation is implied through methodological and integration responsibilities rather than explicitly named as a core duty, relevance is medium.

This subprocess has plausible but limited relevance. The capability involved is weighting and calibration methodology for sample-based or hybrid estimation. The work description provides some evidence through 'recommends survey content and design, sample estimation and imputation methods, data integration from different sources, sample sizes and allocations,' which suggests methodological influence over estimation-related choices. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may increase the importance of weighting redesign for hybrid survey-administrative models and adaptive collection. However, the work description does not explicitly mention weighting, calibration, grossing-up, or benchmarking totals. Therefore the connection is limited and rated low.

This subprocess is relevant because the position leads operations to produce, evaluate, analyze and present statistics, and prepares analytical material for dissemination. The capability involved is transforming processed data into aggregate statistical information and related analytical outputs. Evidence includes 'plans and leads the development of statistical operations to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of statistics,' 'writes and presents analytical material,' and 'prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material to be published by Statistics Canada.' The role also determines standards and techniques used in reporting, analysis and presentation of findings. Future-state impacts from Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production include more granular, geospatial and model-based aggregates, while AI/automation and integrated pipelines will make aggregate generation more standardized and automated. Because the work description emphasizes production and analysis of statistics but does not explicitly describe aggregate calculation mechanics, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is relevant because the position oversees the end-to-end operational chain from collection through processing and analysis, and prepares outputs for publication. The capability involved is bringing together processed results into analysis-ready datasets and ensuring coherent handoff to analysis. Evidence includes coordination of collection, coding and processing activities; management of statistical program operations; and preparation of analytical material for publication. Future-state impacts from Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will make standardized, metadata-rich, analysis-ready file finalization more important and more automated. Because the work description supports oversight of the chain rather than explicit file-finalization tasks, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position directly analyzes, presents and publishes statistical findings and prepares analytical material for varied audiences. The capability involved is transforming processed statistics into draft outputs with explanatory and methodological content. Evidence includes that the incumbent 'plans and leads the development of statistical operations to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of statistics,' 'writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience,' and 'prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material to be published by Statistics Canada.' The role also explains findings and their practical application to policy makers and other users. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase automation of recurring output preparation while also increasing the need for methodological notes, metadata-rich packaging, and clearer explanation of AI-assisted, linked-data, geospatial and model-based outputs. Workforce implications include use of AI assistants in daily work and stronger need for analytical and communication skills. This subprocess is directly aligned with the work description.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position validates statistical findings against expectations, trends, comparability over time, and client needs, and defends the validity of methods and results. The capability involved is quality assurance of outputs using domain knowledge, auxiliary information and methodological understanding. Evidence includes that the incumbent 'analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance,' and writes/presents analytical material while defending 'the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.' The role also explains variances and recommends changes to other statistical programs. Future-state impacts from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the need to validate outputs affected by source substitution, linkage, advanced methods and methodological breaks. AI and Automation will require stronger scrutiny of automated outputs and associated metadata. Operational efficiency pressures will encourage more targeted, risk-based validation. Because output validation is already embedded in the role’s analytical and quality responsibilities, relevance is high.

This subprocess is highly relevant because interpreting and explaining outputs is a central feature of the position. The capability involved is substantive analysis, contextual interpretation, communication of meaning, and explanation of results to internal and external audiences. Evidence is extensive: the incumbent 'provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia,' 'explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information,' 'writes and presents analytical material,' and 'provides guidance on survey results, methods of socio-economic analysis and statistical techniques and systems.' Knowledge requirements include extensive knowledge of socio-economic issues to analyze outputs and assess impacts. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Workforce Skills Transition will increase the need to explain outputs produced from mixed-source, AI-assisted and model-based methods in clear, trustworthy terms. Capability themes such as public trust, transparency, analytical expertise and clear communication are especially relevant. This subprocess is central to the role.

This subprocess is relevant because the position is responsible for ensuring confidentiality and applying departmental policies and legal requirements related to data protection. The capability involved is protecting confidential information in outputs and operations in line with policy and legislation. Evidence includes knowledge of 'Statistics Canada policies, (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, and data quality),' and knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act 'to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.' The incumbent also provides input to management decisions on 'dissemination and confidentiality of information.' Future-state impacts from Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase disclosure risks for linked, administrative and geospatial outputs and require stronger controlled-access and privacy-preserving practices. Because the work description shows governance and policy responsibility rather than explicit application of suppression or perturbation techniques, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position prepares, edits, evaluates and approves analytical material for publication, explains findings, and supports dissemination decisions while ensuring quality and confidentiality. The capability involved is bringing outputs and supporting information to release readiness, including commentary, technical explanation, caveats and internal coordination. Evidence includes 'prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material to be published by Statistics Canada,' 'writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated,' and provides expert advice on findings and their interpretation. The role also contributes to decisions on dissemination and confidentiality and chairs/participates in meetings to build consensus. Future-state impacts from Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will intensify deadline-driven approval and release readiness; Metadata-Driven Data Management will increase the importance of complete metadata; Modern Statistical Methods and AI drivers will require stronger technical notes and caveats for advanced methods; Governance and Prioritization will sharpen approval accountability and trade-offs; and Workforce Skills Transition will increase demands on communication and disciplined decision-making. The work description strongly supports this subprocess.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position prepares and presents analytical material for dissemination, explains findings to varied audiences, and contributes to publication-quality products. The capability involved is assembling explanatory texts, analytical content, quality statements and publication-ready products. Evidence includes 'writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience,' 'prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material to be published by Statistics Canada,' and explains findings to policy makers, business, academia and the public. The role also defends results publicly when challenged, which indicates close involvement with dissemination products and standards. Future-state impacts from Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation, and Modern Statistical Methods will increase the need for metadata-rich, digital, reusable and possibly more automated dissemination products, with stronger explanatory content for mixed-source and AI-assisted outputs. Operational efficiency pressures will encourage templating and standardization. Because dissemination product creation is explicitly part of the role, relevance is high.

This subprocess is relevant because the position communicates released findings to external audiences, participates in dissemination-related decisions, and must defend and explain released results, though the work description does not explicitly assign release scheduling or embargo management. The capability involved is supporting release readiness, briefings, and communication around published outputs. Evidence includes writing and presenting analytical material for public and specialized audiences, explaining findings to policy makers and others, and defending the validity of results when challenged by media representatives. The role also provides input on dissemination policy and confidentiality. Future-state impacts from Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will make release timing and disciplined approvals more important; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will affect controlled release and researcher access; and Enterprise Digital Platforms will shape digital release channels. Because the work description supports communication and dissemination support more than formal release management, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is relevant because the position provides expert advisory and consultative services to users, explains findings and methods, and responds to challenges or misinterpretations from external audiences. The capability involved is supporting users in understanding outputs, methods and access-related issues. Evidence includes 'provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia,' 'explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation,' and provides guidance on survey results, methods and techniques. The role also chairs meetings and participates in groups to share knowledge. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation may introduce chatbot and knowledge-base support models; Metadata-Driven Data Management will change how users discover and interpret assets; Cyber Security and Secure Access will affect support for restricted access; and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase pressure for self-service and triaged support. Because the role clearly supports users but is not framed as a dedicated service desk or access-management function, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is relevant because the position reviews program outputs, quality, variances, client requirements and operational impacts, all of which generate evaluation evidence for continuous improvement. The capability involved is collecting and using quality indicators, operational observations, client feedback and staff/management insights to assess program performance. Evidence includes analyzing data quality and comparability, investigating client requirements, reviewing collection/coding/processing activities to determine changes in data needs and assess impacts on divisional programs, and participating in committees to share knowledge. The role also manages staff and projects, which positions it to gather operational feedback. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation, Integrated Data Pipelines, Enterprise Platforms and Modern Statistical Methods will increase availability of monitoring data, paradata, workflow metrics and adoption feedback. Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition will make workload, sustainability, training and readiness indicators more important. Because the work description implies rather than explicitly names formal evaluation-input gathering, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is relevant because the position evaluates program outputs, methods, quality, comparability and operational impacts, and recommends changes to improve programs. The capability involved is synthesizing evidence on performance and quality into judgments and recommendations for future iterations. Evidence includes that the incumbent 'analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs,' 'determines reasons for variances,' reviews relevance and comparability, researches gaps and inconsistencies in methods and procedures, investigates client requirements, and presents recommendations to senior management to improve and expand programs. This is evaluative work even if not labeled as a formal evaluation report. Future-state impacts from Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Governance and Prioritization, AI and Automation, and Workforce Skills Transition will make evaluation more dashboard-driven, more focused on efficiency, quality, workforce readiness and implementation success, and more central to continuation or redesign decisions. Because the role clearly performs evaluative analysis and recommendation-making, but not necessarily formal enterprise evaluation reporting as a primary duty, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is relevant because the position has decision-making authority, sets priorities and milestones, allocates resources, recommends program changes to senior management, and manages implementation through units and project teams. The capability involved is turning evaluation and operational findings into prioritized actions with accountable ownership and monitored follow-through. Evidence includes 'determines program priorities and milestones,' allocates human and financial resources, presents recommendations to senior management, manages units and project teams, plans and schedules work, resolves conflicting priorities, and approves training plans. These are core ingredients of action planning. Future-state impacts from Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition will make action plans more explicit, time-bound, resource-constrained and dependent on clear accountability, leadership capacity and realistic sequencing. Because the work description supports action planning and implementation authority but does not explicitly describe formal post-evaluation action-plan governance, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes identifying what statistics are needed in light of respondent feedback, environmental change, and operational constraints. The position directly identifies and reviews trends in 'response patterns and respondent behaviour' and assesses their impact on 'statistical programs and operations within the department,' which is evidence of contributing operational intelligence into need identification. The role also 'develops and implements long term strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes,' showing responsibility for translating operational signals into future collection needs. The Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment driver increases the importance of this contribution because fiscal pressure, workforce reduction, and prioritization of services mean respondent burden, response rates, and lower-cost collection approaches will increasingly shape which needs are feasible to pursue. Evidence includes the duties to 'identify and review trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques,' to assess impacts of poor response rates, and to assess 'changes in both technology and the subject area.'

This subprocess concerns setting output objectives within resource, quality, confidentiality and operational constraints. The position is relevant because it defines operational conditions that materially affect what outputs can realistically be delivered: it 'defines the objectives, content and approaches for data collection activities in the regional district office and the framework and conditions within which statistical programs will occur.' The role also prepares work plans and summaries that 'influence the nature, scope and cost of divisional statistical activities,' and monitors cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security. That means the incumbent contributes practical constraints and trade-offs on scope, timeliness and quality. Future-state drivers make this more important: Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline will require clearer accountability and transparent trade-offs, while Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will tighten decisions on scope and service levels under fewer staff and flatter structures. Evidence includes budget authority, evaluation of quality and completeness of data, and advice on questionnaire content, survey coverage, and operational procedures.

This subprocess assesses whether existing sources, technologies, legal conditions and access arrangements can meet requirements. The position is materially connected because it evaluates collection methods, technologies, hardware/software suitability, respondent availability, data quality, security and operational feasibility. The work description states the incumbent 'identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations,' 'evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software,' and 'select[s] and integrate[s] new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture, conversion and dissemination systems and processes.' The role also negotiates agreements with departments/agencies and outside organizations for acquisition and dissemination of data and services, and applies Statistics Act, confidentiality and security requirements. Future drivers intensify this connection: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment all push source assessment toward reusable, secure, lower-cost, metadata-rich and digitally integrated inputs. Evidence includes knowledge of confidentiality, security, respondent relations, internal client structures, and negotiation of agreements for data acquisition and dissemination.

This subprocess is relevant at a limited level because the position develops strategic and operational proposals that resemble inputs to business cases, though the work description does not explicitly assign formal business-case preparation or approval authority. The incumbent 'develops and implements long term strategies and business solutions,' prepares work plans and summaries with time frames and resources, estimates salary, equipment and travel costs, and advises on changes to questionnaire design, survey content, systems and hardware/software. These are core evidentiary elements that would support option appraisal, implementation planning and resource justification. Future drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity would increase pressure for disciplined, milestone-based, resource-aware proposals. Evidence includes planning and budgeting for district operations, identifying development and operational requirements, and coordinating concurrent projects involving multidisciplinary resources.

This subprocess is relevant because the position provides advice on questionnaire design, survey content and coverage, which directly affects what variables are collected and how they are defined operationally. The work description explicitly states the incumbent 'develops proposals and provides advice regarding changes and improvements on questionnaire design; enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage,' and requires 'knowledge of questionnaire development to provide advice to subject matter experts.' While the role is not described as the primary designer of variables, it regularly contributes operational expertise on respondent understanding, response behaviour and collection feasibility that shapes variable design. Future drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase pressure to harmonize variables across sources, support derived variables, and document metadata more rigorously. Evidence includes determining changes in client statistical needs and providing advice regarding questionnaire design, concepts, respondent reaction and understanding.

This is one of the most directly implicated subprocesses. The position manages and shapes collection strategy, instruments, respondent relations, field operations and operational procedures for a '7-day collection operation.' The incumbent 'manages the work of the district office and the organization, planning, scheduling and control of statistical data collection activities,' develops collection applications, alternate work methods and models, advises on questionnaire design and survey coverage, improves respondent relations and transmission processes, and provides expert advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures. This is direct responsibility for collection design capability and operationalization. Future-state drivers have strong cumulative effects: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture and Reusable Components, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all point to more digital, online-first, automated, secure, reusable and lower-touch collection models. The role is already expected to assess technology change, integrate new hardware/software, manage respondent behaviour issues, and lead a large interviewer workforce, so these drivers will materially reshape how the work is done. Evidence includes management of SSO interviewers and senior interviewers, development of alternate work methods and models, advice on questionnaire design, and negotiation with subject matter and systems specialists on conditions for statistical programs.

This subprocess has plausible but limited relevance. The work description does not assign direct responsibility for sampling methodology or frame design. However, the role contributes operational intelligence on respondent availability, response patterns, non-response and survey operations that can inform frame and sample decisions. Evidence includes assessing 'availability of respondents,' analyzing variances in response rates, and reviewing comparability and relevance of data over time. Future drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may increase the importance of operational feedback from regional collection managers into more targeted or adaptive sample designs, but the work description does not show direct design ownership.

This subprocess is relevant because the position evaluates and proposes modifications to statistical systems and processes, including data quality control, data capture, conversion, dissemination systems, and alternative approaches. The incumbent 'monitors and evaluates the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of regional data collection systems and processes and determines the need for development, modification and adaptation,' and 'reviews and interprets the methods, concepts, techniques and practices applied in the operation of existing systems and processes; proposes modifications and enhancements or develops alternative approaches.' The role also identifies trends in data processing concepts and selects/integrates hardware and software for mass statistical data capture and conversion. Future drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative and Alternative Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Modern Statistical Methods, Modular Architecture, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition will increasingly automate coding, validation, integration and workflow control, meaning this operational-methods advisory role will be more affected. Evidence includes quality control responsibilities, evaluation of completeness of data, and identification of gaps and inconsistencies in collection methods and procedures.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position oversees end-to-end operational workflows, systems interaction, responsibilities and process improvement across regional collection operations. The work description shows direct responsibility for planning, scheduling and controlling collection activities; establishing frameworks for ongoing operation of statistical systems and processes; developing guidelines, instructions and procedures for use and evaluation of systems; safeguarding systems, equipment, databases and files; and coordinating concurrent projects involving multidisciplinary resources. This aligns closely with designing and refining production systems and workflows, especially from collection through transmission and operational handoffs. Future drivers have strong cumulative impact: AI and Automation, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Governance and Prioritization, Modular Architecture, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition all point to more standardized, automated, monitored, secure and reusable workflows with clearer handoffs and fewer manual interventions. The role's management of staff interaction with systems and assignment of responsibilities makes it especially sensitive to these changes. Evidence includes establishing organizational structures, assigning responsibilities, monitoring progress, developing alternate work methods and models, and establishing specifications and procedures for maintenance and safeguarding of systems and databases.

This subprocess is relevant because the position contributes to changes in questionnaires, collection applications and operational tools, though the work description does not indicate direct technical build responsibility. The incumbent 'develops and implements collection applications,' provides advice on questionnaire design and survey content, and assesses new hardware and software for data collection activities. The role also develops guidelines and procedures for use and evaluation of systems and processes. Future drivers such as AI and Automation, Administrative and Alternative Data Expansion, Enterprise Platforms, Metadata-Driven Management, Modern Statistical Methods and Modular Architecture will shift collection instruments toward digital, reusable, metadata-connected and more automated forms, increasing the operational impact on this role. Evidence includes advice on questionnaire design, implementation of new hardware/software, and development of collection applications and alternate work methods.

This subprocess is relevant because the position establishes and adapts operational procedures, alternate work methods, models and frameworks for ongoing statistical operations. The incumbent develops and distributes guidelines, instructions and procedures, plans and coordinates concurrent projects, and determines the need for modification and adaptation of systems and processes. That is consistent with configuring and tailoring workflows for operational use, even if not described in technical system-configuration language. Future drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation, Enterprise Platforms, Agility and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition will increase the need for standardized, automated, milestone-driven and exception-based workflow configuration. Evidence includes planning, scheduling and control of collection activities, development of alternate work methods and models, and advice on modifications to operational procedures.

This subprocess is relevant because the position trains and prepares the workforce, establishes procedures, and ensures operational readiness of systems and processes in live regional operations. The incumbent manages recruitment, development, retention and training plans for a professional data collection workforce; develops guidelines, instructions and procedures; and establishes specifications for maintenance and safeguarding of systems, equipment, databases and files. These are core production-readiness responsibilities. Future drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation, Modular Architecture and Operational Efficiency will increase the importance of training, documentation, role clarity and controlled deployment into production-ready environments. Evidence includes approving training plans, providing guidance and direction on career development, and establishing procedures used by staff in planning and performing their work.

This subprocess is directly implicated because the position ensures people, processes and technology are ready for live collection. The work description shows responsibility for managing the district office and 7-day collection operation, recruiting and developing the collection workforce, approving training plans, planning and budgeting district operations, establishing procedures, and safeguarding systems and data. The role also resolves respondent complaints and non-response issues and negotiates with internal and external partners for services and equipment. These are core collection setup responsibilities. Future drivers strongly affect this work: AI and Automation, Administrative and Alternative Data Expansion, Agility and Timelines, Cyber Security and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms, Integrated Pipelines, Modern Statistical Methods, Modular Architecture, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition all increase the need for digital readiness, secure setup, staff training, scalable infrastructure, and mixed-source collection preparation. Evidence includes management of recruitment and training, planning and budgeting for district operations, establishing procedures, and ensuring adherence to confidentiality and security policies.

This is the core operational subprocess for the position. The incumbent directly manages live collection operations, including planning, scheduling and control of statistical data collection activities, management of interviewers and senior interviewers, respondent relations, complaint resolution, monitoring of cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security, and adjustment of operations based on response patterns and respondent behaviour. The role also develops strategies to improve respondent relations and collection/transmission processes and evaluates impacts of poor response rates on departmental programs. Future drivers will materially transform this work: AI and Automation will introduce more automated monitoring and respondent support; Administrative and Alternative Data Expansion and online-first approaches will shift work toward mixed-source and digital operations; Agility and Execution Discipline will intensify deadline management; Cyber Security and Enterprise Platforms will increase secure digital operating requirements; Operational Efficiency will reduce tolerance for labour-intensive approaches; and Workforce Skills Transition will change supervisory and staff capability needs. Evidence is extensive throughout the work description, especially the first five key activities and the leadership, communication, contextual knowledge and research sections.

This subprocess is relevant because the position oversees collection systems, transmission processes, data security and quality, and determines modifications needed in regional data collection systems and processes. While the work description does not explicitly mention loading collected data into downstream environments, it does include improving 'data collection and transmission processes,' safeguarding databases and files, and evaluating quality and completeness of data. These responsibilities connect to the handoff from collection into processing. Future drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Cyber Security, Enterprise Platforms, Administrative and Alternative Data Expansion and Operational Efficiency will make automated loading, metadata handling, secure archiving and digital versioning more central. Evidence includes monitoring security of regional data collection systems, establishing safeguarding procedures for databases and files, and improving transmission processes.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance. The work description does not assign direct responsibility for record linkage or multi-source integration. However, the role does negotiate agreements for acquisition and dissemination of data, establish frameworks for collection, exchange and dissemination of information, and understand interrelationships among broad subject matter areas and statistical programs. These activities can support upstream conditions for integration. Future drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Platforms and Modern Statistical Methods may increase the degree to which regional collection operations are affected by integrated-source production, but the current description does not show direct integration execution responsibility.

This subprocess is only indirectly relevant. The work description does not mention coding operations directly. However, the incumbent evaluates data processing concepts, methods and processes, selects and integrates technology for mass statistical data capture and conversion, and monitors quality and completeness of data. Those responsibilities mean the role may be affected by changes in coding automation and classification workflows, especially as collection and processing become more integrated. Future drivers such as AI-enabled automated coding, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition may alter the systems and staff interactions overseen by the position, but no direct coding responsibility is stated.
