The work description already shows the role operating at the point where survey design, supplier negotiation, and resource constraints meet. Going forward, collection design will shift toward online-first, adaptive, mixed-source, API-based, and more automated models, with stronger security and platform requirements and reduced tolerance for labour-intensive approaches. This Assistant Director is highly implicated because the role already approves and negotiates the core collection choices that these drivers will transform.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it covers defining populations, frames, and sampling methodology. The work description explicitly states that the incumbent approves 'sample estimation and imputation methods' and 'sample sizes and allocations to maximize efficiency within resource constraints.' That is direct evidence of responsibility for sample design decisions at a senior level. The capability involved is methodological oversight of sampling strategy, representativeness, and efficiency. The role also directs unique surveys and resolves complex methodology issues, which supports involvement in frame and sample design where needed. Future-state impacts come from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production. As administrative registers, linked files, and geospatial inputs increasingly support frame construction and more targeted or hybrid designs, this role's sampling decisions will likely shift from traditional survey-only approaches toward source-based and adaptive designs. The work description's explicit reference to sample sizes, allocations, and estimation methods makes this a high-relevance subprocess.

This subprocess is one of the most directly connected. It covers design of coding, editing, imputation, integration, validation, estimation, and disclosure-control methods. The work description explicitly states that the incumbent approves 'sample estimation and imputation methods' and 'data integration from different sources,' directs 'the development of new methods and techniques for unique studies,' assesses implications of new approaches, develops solutions to complex methodology issues, and provides expert advice on 'advanced analytical methods and techniques and the relevancy of their use.' The role also directs review of overall quality and completeness of results. The capability involved is senior methodological design and stewardship across processing and analysis. Future-state impacts are very strong because AI and Automation, Administrative/Alternative/Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security/Privacy, Enterprise Platforms, Integrated Data Pipelines, Metadata-Driven Management, Modern Statistical Methods, Modular Architecture, Operational Efficiency, and Workforce Skills Transition all converge on this subprocess. The work description already shows responsibility for imputation, integration, advanced methods, and quality review. Going forward, these responsibilities will be reshaped by AI-enabled coding, automated validation and imputation, integrated pipelines, reusable components, stronger metadata dependence, and the need to maintain quality and transparency with fewer staff. This is clearly a high-relevance subprocess.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns end-to-end workflow design, reuse of systems, role allocation, and how staff interact with systems. The work description does not explicitly describe technical workflow architecture, but it does show that the incumbent directs a subdivision involved in end-to-end statistical program operations, including analysis, dissemination, and survey management, and determines strategic directions, parameters, priorities, and broad objectives for significant surveys. The role also manages human and financial resources, coordinates through subordinates, and chairs meetings to build consensus across teams. These are indicators of operational workflow and role-design responsibility at a managerial level. The capability involved is operational leadership over how work is organized across the production chain. Future-state impacts are meaningful because this subprocess is heavily affected by enterprise platforms, integrated pipelines, governance, agility, modular architecture, operational efficiency, and workforce transition. The work description's evidence is stronger on operational leadership than on explicit system design, so medium relevance is appropriate: the role is materially affected by workflow redesign and likely influences it through management and governance, even if not acting as the primary technical architect.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns readiness of people, processes, technology, training, supplier arrangements, and confidentiality procedures before collection begins. The work description shows that the incumbent directs high-profile surveys and projects, allocates human resources, directs recruitment for permanent and project staff, approves training and development plans, negotiates contracts and services, and mediates with data suppliers and stakeholders. These are clear readiness and setup responsibilities at a managerial level, even if the role is not described as performing operational setup directly. The capability involved is ensuring organizational readiness, staffing, supplier coordination, and operational support for collection. Future-state impacts are meaningful because collection setup will increasingly require digital readiness, secure access, online-first tools, mixed-source acquisition, and workforce reskilling. The work description's evidence on recruitment, training, contracts, and supplier coordination supports medium relevance: the role contributes materially to collection readiness through leadership and resource management.

This subprocess is implicated because it covers live collection operations, respondent and supplier interactions, monitoring, and adjustments during collection. The work description shows that the incumbent directs a subdivision involved in statistical program operations and high-profile surveys, mediates with data suppliers and stakeholders, negotiates resources and timeframes for projects requiring supplier participation, and maintains relations with the user community and suppliers. This indicates managerial oversight of collection execution, especially where supplier cooperation and operational issues are involved. The capability involved is executive oversight of collection operations and stakeholder management rather than front-line collection execution. Future-state impacts are meaningful because collection execution is shifting toward digital, online-first, adaptive, and supplier-based models with stronger monitoring and tighter deadlines. The role's evidence is indirect but material, so medium relevance is appropriate.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it concerns combining data from multiple sources, harmonising values, linkage, prioritisation, and creation of consolidated datasets. The work description explicitly states that the incumbent approves 'data integration from different sources' and directs the development of methods and solutions to complex methodology issues. It also notes expert advice on advanced analytical methods and the practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. The capability involved is senior methodological and program authority over multi-source integration and harmonisation. Future-state impacts are especially strong because Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security/Privacy, Enterprise Platforms, Integrated Data Pipelines, Metadata-Driven Management, Modern Statistical Methods, Operational Efficiency, and Workforce Skills Transition all make integration more central. The work description already places this role directly in source integration decisions; future drivers will expand the complexity of linked, administrative, alternative, and geospatial integration while increasing privacy, metadata, and platform demands. This is clearly high relevance.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns coding and classification of input data, increasingly through automated methods. The work description does not explicitly assign direct responsibility for coding operations, but it does show that the incumbent provides expert advice on advanced analytical methods and techniques, directs development of new methods and techniques, and approves survey content and design. The role also has deep knowledge of statistics and subject-matter concepts needed to improve concepts and analyze data. The capability involved is methodological oversight of classification approaches rather than direct operational coding. Future-state impacts are meaningful because AI-enabled automated coding, administrative and alternative data harmonisation, metadata standardization, operational efficiency, and workforce skills transition will change coding from clerical work toward automated, governed, and reusable services. Because the work description supports oversight of methods but not explicit coding responsibility, medium relevance is appropriate.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it concerns identifying errors, discrepancies, outliers, duplicates, and quality issues before and after integration. The work description explicitly states that the incumbent 'directs the review and assessment of the overall quality and completeness of statistical program results' and 'provides expert analysis and interpretation of program results.' It also notes responsibility for developing solutions to complex methodology issues and assessing implications of new approaches. The capability involved is senior quality assurance, methodological review, and validation judgement. Future-state impacts are strong because heterogeneous sources, linkage, automation, metadata-driven processing, and reduced staffing all increase the importance of scalable, automated, and exception-based validation. The work description's direct reference to reviewing overall quality and completeness makes this subprocess clearly high relevance.

This subprocess is directly connected because it covers correcting, replacing, or imputing data and documenting those changes. The work description explicitly states that the incumbent approves 'imputation methods' and directs development of new methods and techniques for unique studies. That is direct evidence of responsibility for the methodological side of editing and imputation. The capability involved is senior methodological approval and stewardship over correction and imputation strategies. Future-state impacts are substantial because AI, automation, administrative-source substitution, integrated pipelines, metadata requirements, operational efficiency, and workforce transition will push editing and imputation toward more automated, model-assisted, and source-prioritized approaches. Since the work description explicitly names imputation methods among the incumbent's approvals, this subprocess is high relevance.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns deriving variables and units needed for outputs. The work description does not explicitly mention derivation routines, but it does show responsibility for 'data integration from different sources,' advanced analytical methods, improving or developing new concepts, and implementing programs to produce statistics across a wide range of issues. Those responsibilities imply oversight of derived constructs and analytical transformations needed to produce outputs. The capability involved is conceptual and methodological leadership over how data are transformed into usable statistical measures. Future-state impacts are meaningful because linked and administrative data expansion, modern methods, metadata-driven management, and efficiency pressures increase reliance on derived variables rather than directly collected ones. Because the evidence is more conceptual than operational, medium relevance is appropriate.

This subprocess is implicated because it concerns weighting records to represent target populations and adjust for nonresponse or calibration. The work description explicitly states that the incumbent approves 'sample estimation' methods and sample sizes and allocations. While weighting is not named directly, it is closely tied to estimation methodology in survey programs. The capability involved is senior methodological oversight of representativeness and estimation quality. Future-state impacts arise from hybrid survey-administrative models, adaptive collection, online-first response patterns, and modern weighting approaches. Because the work description supports estimation oversight but does not explicitly mention weighting, medium relevance is the most evidence-based classification.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it transforms processed data into outputs and accompanying methodological notes. The work description directly states that the incumbent provides expert analysis and interpretation of program results, develops overall conclusions and recommendations, reviews and approves analytical material and research papers for publication, writes analytical papers and articles, and presents analytical material to media representatives. The role also directs work in analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination. The capability involved is senior analytical production and preparation of publishable outputs and explanatory materials. Future-state impacts are meaningful because AI assistants, automation, metadata-rich outputs, mixed-source methods, and timelier production will change how draft outputs and methodological explanations are prepared. The work description provides strong direct evidence, so relevance is high.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it concerns validating outputs against expectations, prior cycles, metadata, quality indicators, and domain intelligence. The work description shows that the incumbent 'directs the review and assessment of the overall quality and completeness of statistical program results,' provides expert interpretation of results, analyzes impacts on policy and regulatory issues, and advises senior officials on the implications of study results. The role also requires deep contextual knowledge of socio-economic and political issues and current trends, which is exactly the kind of domain intelligence used in output validation. The capability involved is senior substantive and methodological validation of whether outputs make sense and are fit for use. Future-state impacts are strong because linked and alternative data, advanced methods, automation, and timelier outputs increase the need for stronger validation against benchmarks and expectations. This role is highly implicated because it already performs the expert review and judgement central to this subprocess.

This subprocess is one of the clearest matches. The work description repeatedly emphasizes interpretation and explanation: the incumbent provides expert recommendations on 'the socio-economic implications of surveys and studies and the effect of their results on policies, programs and regulations,' explains results and statistical methods to governments, international organizations, media and the public, writes analytical papers and articles on interpretation and application, and analyzes the impact of study results on major program, policy and regulatory issues. The capability involved is authoritative interpretation of statistical outputs and communication of their meaning to senior decision-makers and external audiences. Future-state impacts are meaningful because outputs will increasingly reflect mixed-source data, advanced methods, and AI-assisted production, requiring clearer explanation of methodological change and comparability. The work description provides direct and extensive evidence, making this a high-relevance subprocess.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns ensuring outputs do not breach confidentiality rules. The work description explicitly states that knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act is required to ensure confidentiality and that the organization 'does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.' It also notes the need to explain legislative requirements to departments, agencies, industry, the public, and media. The capability involved is governance and oversight of confidentiality obligations in release and dissemination. The work description does not describe direct technical application of suppression or perturbation methods, so the relevance is not high. However, future-state impacts from linked data, geospatial outputs, secure access, and enterprise platforms will increase disclosure complexity and make this role's confidentiality oversight more important. Medium relevance is therefore justified.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it concerns ensuring outputs are fit for purpose, collating commentary and technical notes, conducting internal discussions, and approving content for release. The work description shows that the incumbent reviews and approves analytical material and research papers for publication, writes analytical papers and articles, presents analytical material to media, deals with sensitive and political issues that could embarrass the department, and chairs meetings to develop consensus or share knowledge. The role also directs review of quality and completeness of results and provides authoritative advice on interpretation and implications. The capability involved is senior approval, quality assurance, and release-readiness judgement for statistical content. Future-state impacts are strong because agility, governance, metadata requirements, privacy constraints, modern methods, and reduced staffing will intensify the need for disciplined sign-off, caveats, technical notes, and efficient approval workflows. The work description strongly supports high relevance.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it concerns assembling publications, press releases, websites, tables, maps, and explanatory texts. The work description states that the incumbent directs work in 'marketing and dissemination,' writes and reviews papers, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published, presents analytical material to media representatives, and mediates with stakeholders 'to market statistical products and services.' The capability involved is senior oversight and production of dissemination-ready analytical and communication products. Future-state impacts are meaningful because dissemination products will become more digital, metadata-rich, standardized, and potentially AI-assisted, while still requiring strong quality statements, accessibility, and confidentiality safeguards. The evidence in the work description is direct and substantial, so relevance is high.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns timing of release, briefings, embargoes, subscriber provision, and controlled access to confidential data. The work description shows that the incumbent explains results and methods to governments, international organizations, media and the public; presents analytical material to media representatives; and deals with sensitive and political issues that could embarrass the department. It also emphasizes confidentiality obligations under the Statistics Act and Privacy Act. These are strong indicators of involvement in release-related communications and risk management, though not explicit evidence of managing embargoes or release logistics. The capability involved is senior release-facing communication and judgement on sensitive outputs. Future-state impacts from agility, cyber/privacy/secure access, enterprise platforms, and metadata-linked release processes will likely increase the importance of disciplined release management and controlled access. Medium relevance is appropriate because the role is clearly involved in release-facing activities, but the work description does not show direct ownership of release operations.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns responding to user queries, supporting access requests, and maintaining knowledge resources. The work description shows extensive external-facing advisory and explanatory responsibilities: the incumbent provides expert recommendations and advice to senior officials, policy makers, business, social agencies and academics; explains results and methods to governments, international organizations, media and the public; mediates with stakeholders to maintain good relations and cooperation with the user community and data suppliers; and promotes understanding of programs and products. The capability involved is high-level user support, stakeholder engagement, and interpretation support rather than transactional help-desk service. Future-state impacts include AI-enabled support tools, more questions about mixed-source methods and access conditions, and pressure to triage support efficiently under staffing constraints. Because the role clearly supports users and stakeholders but not necessarily through routine service channels, medium relevance is justified.

This subprocess is relevant because it gathers feedback, quality indicators, system metrics, and staff suggestions for evaluation. The work description shows that the incumbent monitors socio-economic trends, user needs, program results, and relevant concepts and practices related to the use and application of program results. The role also maintains relations with users and suppliers and chairs meetings to share knowledge and develop consensus. These activities generate and gather evaluation inputs, even if the role is not described as operating a formal evaluation system. The capability involved is strategic learning from users, stakeholders, results, and operational experience. Future-state impacts are meaningful because modernization will generate richer metrics, paradata, and workforce feedback, and this role's strategic oversight will likely rely more on such evidence. Medium relevance is appropriate.

This subprocess is implicated because it analyzes evaluation inputs, compares performance to expectations, and recommends changes. The work description shows that the incumbent directs review and assessment of overall quality and completeness of results, develops recommendations for senior management on objectives, content, and approaches of survey programs, reviews strategic directions, and analyzes impacts of study results on policy and regulatory issues. These are evaluative and recommendation-oriented responsibilities. The capability involved is senior assessment of program performance, quality, and strategic direction. Future-state impacts are meaningful because evaluation will increasingly focus on modernization outcomes, efficiency, timeliness, workforce readiness, and governance. The work description supports medium relevance because the role clearly evaluates and recommends, though it is not explicitly framed as producing formal evaluation reports or dashboards.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns bringing together decision-making authority to agree actions based on evaluation findings. The work description shows that the incumbent reviews strategic directions, recommends innovative solutions, develops recommendations for senior management, determines broad objectives and content of projects, develops long-term plans and objectives, allocates resources, and negotiates funding and contracts. These are clear action-planning and implementation-governance responsibilities. The capability involved is executive decision-making, prioritization, and translating findings into funded, resourced actions. Future-state impacts are meaningful because governance, prioritization, agility, operational efficiency, and workforce transition will require more explicit ownership, clearer trade-offs, and tighter sequencing of improvement actions. The work description supports medium relevance because the role clearly has decision-making power and planning authority, even though formal evaluation-action-plan language is not used.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description includes assessing data sources, methods, and legal/policy conditions to determine whether data are suitable for statistical use. The position 'reviews and verifies data sources and methods of data compilation,' has 'knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability,' and applies knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act in 'the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data.' Those duties align with checking source suitability, restrictions on use, and feasibility of using existing sources. Future-state drivers make this more important: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production expand the range of candidate sources beyond traditional surveys; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access increases scrutiny of privacy, confidentiality, authorizations and secure access; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability make platform fit, metadata quality, and discoverability more central to source assessment. The work description also states the employee 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services,' which shows the role is materially affected by these source-assessment drivers even if not solely responsible for enterprise source strategy.

This subprocess is implicated because the position contributes to how statistical outputs are prepared, explained, and made usable. Evidence includes assisting 'in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes,' preparing 'special data releases,' assessing 'the timeliness, completeness, accuracy and validity of data compiled for publication,' and writing technical concepts in common terminology as well as 'program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports.' These duties connect to designing outputs, supporting dissemination products, and ensuring outputs are understandable and publication-ready. Future drivers will change this work through stronger metadata-rich output requirements, digital-first dissemination, and privacy/security-by-design. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the need for standardized, searchable, metadata-linked outputs; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access affects what can be released and at what granularity; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development push toward reusable, platform-based dissemination patterns; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity increases the need for clear communication and accessible digital outputs. The role is not described as owning dissemination architecture, so relevance is medium rather than high.

The work description shows direct involvement in concepts, definitions, questionnaires, and methods, which are core to variable design. Evidence includes 'develops and outlines new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques and approaches to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions,' 'reviews and designs questionnaires for the collection of data,' and 'develops or modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches to improve existing surveys or to meet specific needs.' The role also requires 'knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey' and socio-economic concepts to assess validity. These are material links to defining what is collected and how concepts are operationalized. Future drivers will reshape this work by requiring variables to be harmonized across administrative, alternative, linked and geospatial sources, with richer metadata and more derived-variable logic. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production all increase the importance of standardized metadata, harmonized concepts, and variables designed for linkage and reuse. The position appears to contribute under guidance and through methodological improvement rather than lead enterprise variable standards, so medium relevance is appropriate.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the work description explicitly includes responsibilities tied to collection design, questionnaire design, and improvement of collection methods. Evidence includes: 'reviews and designs questionnaires for the collection of data'; 'develops and implements procedures for the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data'; 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection... methods and procedures'; and 'assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' The role also evaluates 'problems in the collection... of statistical information' and proposes solutions or recommendations. These are direct collection-design and collection-method responsibilities. Future-state drivers will materially change this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will shift collection from traditional survey-only approaches toward online-first, adaptive, mixed-source, and more automated acquisition models. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase the need to design secure collection channels and confidentiality protections. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will push collection design toward reusable digital instruments, APIs, platform-based tools, and tighter integration with downstream workflows. Workforce implications are also relevant: the role will need stronger digital, methodological, and tool-based capability as collection becomes less manual and more technology-enabled.

This is one of the most directly connected subprocesses. The work description repeatedly refers to designing and improving processing, editing, compilation, and analytical methods. Evidence includes: 'develops and implements procedures for the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data'; 'implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to collect, process, edit, compile and present statistical data'; 'develops or modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches'; 'evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information'; and 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' The role also participates in analysis of statistical program data and identifies trends and developments. This is a direct fit with designing coding, editing, validation, integration, estimation, and analysis approaches. Future drivers strongly intensify this connection. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase use of AI-enabled coding, automation, advanced methods, and streamlined processing. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will require more multi-source integration and source-specific validation logic. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will shift work toward modular, orchestrated, repeatable processing steps. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata operational in processing design. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase pressure to replace manual effort with automated, sustainable methods. Workforce implications include a shift toward oversight of automated methods, exception handling, and stronger skills in modern tools and methods.

The position is materially connected to this subprocess because it helps improve end-to-end methods and systems used across collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation. Evidence includes 'implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications,' 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services,' and 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' The role also writes manuals, training packages, and monitoring procedures, which supports operational workflow clarity. This aligns with workflow and production-system design, though the description does not show full ownership of enterprise workflow architecture. Future drivers make the role more affected by this subprocess: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development all push toward integrated, reusable, automated workflows with clearer handoffs and stronger monitoring. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity also matter because the role will need to operate within more standardized workflows, clearer accountabilities, and changing staff-system interactions.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because the position implements and modifies processing systems and analytical procedures, which is closely related to building or reusing processing components. Evidence includes 'implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to collect, process, edit, compile and present statistical data' and 'develops and implements procedures for the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data.' The role also writes manuals and monitoring procedures for use in development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs, indicating involvement in operationalizing components. Future drivers will increase the importance of reusable, modular, automated processing components. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will expand AI-enabled coding, validation, and analytical services; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will push toward shared enterprise components and open, reusable tooling; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will require components that fit automated end-to-end flows. The work description supports meaningful contribution, but not primary software-build ownership, so medium relevance is appropriate.

The role is connected to workflow configuration because it modifies systems and procedures across the production chain and contributes to monitoring and operational documentation. Evidence includes implementing 'enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications,' developing procedures across 'collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation,' and writing 'monitoring procedures' and manuals for implementation and assessment of statistical programs. These duties support configuring and adapting workflows, even if the role is not described as a workflow-platform specialist. Future drivers will increase the impact on this work: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will require more explicit workflow configuration, automated handoffs, and exception handling; AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will embed more automation and platform-based orchestration; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward standardized, lower-touch workflows; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require staff to work with new digital workflow tools. The role is therefore meaningfully affected by this subprocess.

This subprocess is relevant because the position designs questionnaires, develops collection procedures, writes training packages and manuals, and participates in improving survey methods and activities. Evidence includes 'reviews and designs questionnaires for the collection of data,' 'develops and implements procedures for the collection... of data,' and writes 'training packages' and 'monitoring procedures' for use in development and implementation of statistical programs. These duties support collection readiness, staff guidance, and operational setup. Future drivers will increase the role's exposure to digital collection setup, online-first tools, secure access, and mixed-source operations. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase setup needs for online response, adaptive collection, and source acquisition; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will make secure apps, credentials, and digital infrastructure more central; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase training and readiness demands. The role contributes to setup through methods, procedures, and documentation rather than direct operational deployment ownership, so medium relevance fits.

The work description is relevant to this subprocess because the position analyzes collection issues and provides feedback to improve live collection methods and procedures. Evidence includes 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection... methods and procedures,' evaluates 'problems in the collection... of statistical information,' and develops recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities. While the role is not described as directly conducting field operations, it is materially connected to collection execution through analytical support, troubleshooting, and method improvement. Future drivers will change how this work interacts with collection operations: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will shift collection toward digital, adaptive, online-first, and mixed-source execution; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will increase pressure for active monitoring and timely intervention; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will affect operational collection controls. The role will likely spend more effort interpreting collection performance and recommending adjustments in more automated environments.

This subprocess is materially connected because the position analyzes data from multiple sources, verifies data sources and compilation methods, and ensures consistency and reliability across outputs. Evidence includes 'reviews and verifies data sources and methods of data compilation,' 'knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability,' and 'assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.' These duties align with harmonisation, source comparison, and integration-related quality assessment. Future drivers make this more important: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production make multi-source integration, linkage, and harmonisation central; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access increases the importance of controlled linkage and de-identification; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability support scalable integrated environments; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration embeds integration into repeatable workflows. The role appears to contribute analytically and methodologically rather than own enterprise integration services, so medium relevance is appropriate.

This subprocess has a plausible but limited connection. The work description does not explicitly assign coding duties, but it does include modifying statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches, and working with questionnaires, processing, and editing. Those responsibilities can affect classification and coding frameworks indirectly. Evidence includes 'develops and outlines new statistical methods, concepts and procedures,' 'develops or modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches,' and 'knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data.' Future drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment may affect the role through increased automated coding and harmonisation of non-standard source data, but the supplied work description does not show direct responsibility for coding operations. Therefore relevance is low.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the work description directly includes assessing data validity, accuracy, completeness, consistency, and methodological impacts. Evidence includes: 'assesses the timeliness, completeness, accuracy and validity of data compiled for publication'; 'assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored'; 'knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data'; and 'locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability.' The role also evaluates problems in processing and editing and proposes solutions. These are core validation responsibilities. Future drivers will materially reshape this work. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase heterogeneity, linkage risks, and source drift, requiring stronger cross-source validation. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase automated anomaly detection and exception-based review. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata completeness part of validation. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will embed validation into scalable, automated workflows. Workforce implications include a shift from broad manual checking toward targeted review of flagged issues using modern tools.

This subprocess is relevant because the position works directly on editing-related methods and procedures, even though imputation is not explicitly named. Evidence includes developing and implementing procedures for 'processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data,' evaluating problems in 'processing, editing... statistical information,' and analyzing current methods and procedures to propose changes or alternatives. This indicates meaningful involvement in the methodological and operational basis for editing. Future drivers will affect this work through more automated, model-assisted, and source-prioritized correction methods. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward automated editing and reduced manual intervention. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase use of administrative values and source hierarchy in correction logic. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the importance of documenting edits and transformations. Because the work description does not explicitly mention performing imputations, medium relevance is more defensible than high.

This subprocess is implicated because the role develops statistical methods, concepts, and definitions and analyzes data to identify trends and produce analytical outputs, which often depends on deriving variables and analytical constructs. Evidence includes 'develops and outlines new statistical methods, concepts and procedures,' 'develops or modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches,' and knowledge of 'statistical estimation and economic modeling.' The role also participates in subject matter studies and reviews and prepares analytical material for publication. Future drivers will increase the importance of derivation as more outputs rely on linked, administrative, alternative, and geospatial data rather than directly collected responses. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase derived variables and units from linked records and model-based methods; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will require ordered, automated derivation chains; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will require clearer derivation lineage. The work description supports methodological contribution, though not explicit ownership of derivation pipelines, so medium relevance is appropriate.

There is a plausible but limited connection to weighting. The work description includes knowledge of 'statistical estimation' and survey methods, and participation in improving survey methods and activities, which could be affected by weighting changes. However, there is no explicit responsibility for creating weights, calibration, or non-response adjustment. Future drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may affect the role indirectly through redesigned surveys and hybrid estimation approaches, but the supplied evidence does not support a stronger classification. Therefore relevance is low.

This subprocess is relevant because the position analyzes statistical program data, identifies trends and developments, prepares analytical material for publication, and prepares special data releases. Those duties depend on producing and interpreting aggregate statistical outputs. Evidence includes 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data,' 'identifies statistical trends and developments,' and 'prepares special data releases.' The role also compares related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability. Future drivers will affect this work through more automated aggregate production, more granular geospatial and model-based outputs, and faster production cycles. Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may expand small-area and geospatial aggregates; AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will automate recurring aggregate generation; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will encourage standardized aggregate routines. The role is more focused on analysis and interpretation of aggregates than on the technical aggregation engine itself, so medium relevance is appropriate.

This subprocess is relevant because the position works across processing, editing, compilation, and presentation, and verifies data sources and compilation methods to ensure outputs are ready for analysis and publication. Evidence includes 'reviews and verifies data sources and methods of data compilation,' 'develops and implements procedures for the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data,' and assesses the validity of data compiled for publication. These duties connect to assembling coherent, analysis-ready datasets and ensuring their quality. Future drivers will increase the importance of standardized, metadata-rich, pipeline-based finalization. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will automate handoffs to analysis; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will change where final datasets are stored and accessed; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will require richer metadata packaging; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will increase pressure for timely preliminary and final files. The role contributes materially through methods and quality assurance rather than owning file-finalization infrastructure, so medium relevance fits.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the work description directly states that the position 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.' It also includes 'prepares special data releases,' identifies trends and developments, and writes detailed subject matter and technical concepts in common terminology. These are direct draft-output preparation responsibilities. Future drivers will materially affect this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production may accelerate drafting and standard output preparation but increase the need for transparency and methodological explanation. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will change the content of outputs and require clearer explanation of mixed-source, linked, geospatial, and model-based results. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the need to package outputs with richer metadata and methodological notes. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward templated, lower-touch production of recurring outputs. The role is clearly central to this subprocess.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position validates statistical outputs against quality expectations, source consistency, and subject-matter understanding. Evidence includes assessing 'timeliness, completeness, accuracy and validity of data compiled for publication,' identifying 'statistical trends and developments,' comparing related statistical output 'to ensure consistency and reliability,' and using knowledge of current and emerging economic and social issues 'to identify and assess trends and issues represented by statistical data series.' The role also participates in subject matter studies and reviews to support project teams or senior officers. These are core output-validation activities involving domain intelligence and comparison against expectations. Future drivers intensify this work: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will create more methodological breaks, linkage effects, and mixed-source comparability issues; AI and Automation in Statistical Production will require stronger scrutiny of automated outputs; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata and quality indicators more central; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward more targeted, risk-based validation. This is a strong direct fit.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role is fundamentally analytical and explanatory. Evidence includes participating 'in the analysis of statistical program data,' identifying 'statistical trends and developments,' preparing analytical material for publication, writing and presenting 'detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology,' and providing data and assistance to users within and outside Statistics Canada. The role also requires knowledge of economic and social issues to identify and assess trends represented by statistical series. These are direct interpretation and explanation responsibilities. Future drivers will materially change this work by increasing the need to explain outputs produced from linked, administrative, alternative, geospatial, and AI-assisted methods. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will require clearer explanation of automated and advanced methods; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will require interpretation of mixed-source outputs and comparability changes; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need for analytical expertise, communication, and confidence with new tools. This subprocess is central to the position.

This subprocess is relevant because the position contributes to publication-ready outputs, special releases, explanatory material, and communication of technical concepts. Evidence includes assisting in preparation of analytical material 'for internal use and publication purposes,' preparing 'special data releases,' assessing validity of data compiled for publication, and writing manuals, reports, and technical explanations in common terminology. These duties support final consistency checks, supporting information, and release readiness, though the description does not show formal approval authority. Future drivers will increase the need for caveats, technical notes, metadata, and disciplined release preparation. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will require more explicit explanation of methods and uncertainty; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata a core part of release readiness; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline and Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline will tighten approval and readiness expectations. The role contributes materially but is not clearly the final approver, so medium relevance is appropriate.

This subprocess is relevant because the position helps prepare publication materials and special releases and communicates technical content for users. Evidence includes assisting in preparation of analytical material 'for internal use and publication purposes,' preparing 'special data releases,' writing and presenting technical concepts in common terminology, and providing data and assistance to users within and outside Statistics Canada. These duties align with preparing explanatory texts, tables, quality statements, and publication-ready content. Future drivers will affect this work through more digital, metadata-rich, reusable, and possibly AI-assisted dissemination products. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the need for metadata-rich products; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will push toward reusable digital product assembly; AI and Automation in Statistical Production may support drafting and assembly; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need for digital communication and accessible product preparation. The role contributes to product content more than dissemination platform operations, so medium relevance fits.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description explicitly states that the position 'provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.' It also includes writing explanatory material in common terminology and participating in subject matter studies and reviews that support others. These are direct user-support and user-explanation functions. Future drivers will change this work by increasing user questions about methods, source changes, and digital products, while also introducing more self-service and AI-enabled support tools. AI and Automation in Statistical Production may introduce AI assistants, chatbots, and knowledge-base support; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will change how users find and access information; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the need to explain mixed-source outputs and methodological changes; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward more scalable, lower-touch support models. Because user support is explicit in the work description, this subprocess is materially connected.

This subprocess is relevant because the position explicitly identifies, assesses and compares data sources for statistical use. The work description states that the incumbent 'specifies sources of data to be used in the preparation of subject-matter statistics and forecasts, verifies the consistency and comparability of the various sets of data obtained and modifies the data to permit comparison,' and also has 'knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada related to the area of expertise in order to identify potential sources of information.' That is a direct match to checking whether available sources can meet requirements and under what conditions they are suitable. The capability involved is source assessment, comparability analysis, legal/policy awareness, and judging fitness of data for statistical production. The position fulfills this need by researching and compiling data from diverse sources, assessing constraints arising from concepts, definitions and collection conditions, and identifying data conflicts. Future-state drivers materially increase the importance and complexity of this work. Administrative, alternative and linked data expansion will shift source strategy beyond traditional survey inputs, so this role's existing responsibility for identifying sources and verifying comparability will increasingly involve administrative data, linked data and potentially geospatial or other non-traditional sources. Metadata-driven data management and discoverability will make source discovery more systematic, but will also raise expectations that staff can assess metadata quality and interoperability. Cyber security, privacy and secure access are also relevant because the work description explicitly requires awareness of the Statistics Act, Privacy Act, security and confidentiality obligations 'with respect to the security and confidentiality of data,' which aligns with future source suitability assessments that must account for privacy, secure access and legal constraints. Enterprise digital platforms and cloud infrastructure will further affect how source feasibility is judged, especially where systems, databases and secure environments are involved. Evidence includes: 'specifies sources of data,' 'verifies the consistency and comparability,' 'modifies the data to permit comparison,' 'identify potential sources of information,' and awareness of legal and confidentiality requirements.

This subprocess is implicated because the position works with subject-matter concepts, definitions and classifications that underpin variable design, even if it is not framed as full end-to-end questionnaire-variable design ownership. The work description states that the incumbent 'develops new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques and approaches to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions' and has 'knowledge of current or emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and resolve subject-matter concept and definition requirements.' The capability involved is defining and refining subject-matter concepts, ensuring comparability, and adapting data to new definitions or presentation formats. The position fulfills this need by modifying concepts and procedures, adapting data to new definitions, and resolving concept and definition issues in support of statistical programs. Future-state drivers suggest that variable design will increasingly be shaped by administrative, alternative and linked data, metadata standardization, and modern statistical methods. As variables are more often sourced, harmonized or derived rather than directly collected, this role's expertise in subject-matter definitions and comparability will become more important. Metadata-driven data management increases the need for standardized variable definitions and richer documentation. Evidence includes: 'changes in subject-matter content and definitions,' 'identify and resolve subject-matter concept and definition requirements,' and 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats.'

This subprocess is relevant because the position contributes feedback and recommendations on collection methods and procedures, even though it is not described as the primary designer of collection instruments. The work description states that the incumbent 'assists in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' It also notes knowledge of 'the concepts, methods and techniques used in the collection... of statistical data' and the ability to identify and evaluate problems in collection and provide solutions or recommendations. The capability involved is analytical review of collection effectiveness, translating subject-matter requirements into operational improvements, and advising on survey methods. The position fulfills this need by reviewing collection results, identifying problems, and recommending procedural modifications. Future-state drivers indicate that collection design will change substantially through online-first strategy, adaptive collection design, administrative and alternative data use, APIs, automation and digital platforms. That means a role already tasked with suggesting improvements to collection methods will increasingly need to assess digital collection models, mixed-source acquisition and more automated collection workflows. Workforce implications around tools, training and evolving collection roles are relevant because this position writes training packages and manuals and liaises with specialists and users to translate requirements into specifications. Evidence includes: 'suggests possible feedback on collection... methods and procedures,' 'development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities,' and 'identifies and evaluates problems in the collection... of statistical information.'

This is one of the most directly connected subprocesses. The work description repeatedly describes responsibilities that align with designing methods for processing, editing, compilation, validation and analysis. The incumbent 'develops new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques and approaches,' 'determines the need for and implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to collect, capture, process, edit, compile and present statistical data,' and 'identifies and evaluates problems in the collection, capture, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information.' The capability involved is methodological design, processing-rule improvement, system specification, analytical problem-solving, and integration of subject-matter requirements into processing environments. The position fulfills this need by reviewing current methods and procedures, examining revised processing specifications, determining effects on integration and coordination of capture and processing functions, and advising on subject-matter development. Future-state drivers strongly amplify this work. AI and automation in statistical production, integrated data pipelines and process orchestration, metadata-driven data management, modular reusable components, and modern statistical methods all point toward more automated, standardized, metadata-aware and enterprise-integrated processing designs. The work description already shows system analysis and design knowledge, generalized survey software knowledge, database maintenance, and use of statistical packages, which positions the role to be materially affected by transition to automated coding, integrated pipelines, reusable validation and processing modules, and modern platforms. Workforce implications are also relevant: staff will need stronger skills in AI, digital tools and exception-based oversight rather than only manual processing. Evidence includes: 'develops new statistical methods,' 'implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems,' 'reviews current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures,' and 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications.'

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position directly engages with systems, applications, workflow coordination and the interaction between subject-matter requirements and production processes. The work description states that the incumbent 'determines the need for and implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications,' 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' and 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' The capability involved is workflow and systems thinking across collection, processing and presentation; clarifying operational handoffs; and aligning subject-matter needs with system design. The position fulfills this need by coordinating work groups, writing manuals and monitoring procedures, and assessing how revised specifications affect integration with other systems. Future-state drivers make this even more material. Enterprise digital platforms and cloud infrastructure, integrated data pipelines and process orchestration, modular architecture and reusable components, governance and prioritization, and operational efficiency all point to redesigned end-to-end workflows with fewer manual handoffs, more reuse, stronger controls and clearer responsibilities. The work description already includes evidence of role clarity, coordination, system design knowledge and operational integration, so the position is likely to be significantly affected as workflows become more automated and enterprise-standardized. Workforce implications such as shift from manual execution to supervision, need for orchestration skills, and cross-functional coordination are especially relevant. Evidence includes: 'specifications for system development,' 'implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications,' 'integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems,' and 'writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures.'

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because the position helps specify, modify and maintain processing systems and analytical components, though the work description does not make it solely a software build role. The incumbent 'determines the need for and implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications,' has 'knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to design, develop, test, maintain and implement processing systems,' and uses programming languages and statistical packages 'to retrieve and manipulate data.' The capability involved is translating methodological and subject-matter needs into reusable or modified processing components and maintaining those components in production contexts. The position fulfills this need by implementing system enhancements, designing testing specifications, maintaining databases and using software tools to manipulate data. Future-state drivers such as AI and automation, enterprise platforms, integrated pipelines, modular architecture and reusable components will shift this work toward more standardized enterprise services, reusable modules and open or modern toolsets. Workforce implications include upskilling in modern tools and reduced reliance on bespoke manual approaches. Evidence includes: 'design, develop, test, maintain and implement processing systems,' 'implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications,' and 'knowledge of high level programming languages... or statistical packages.'

This subprocess is implicated because the position works with operational specifications, monitoring procedures, system interactions and coordination of activities, all of which support workflow configuration even if the role is not described as a dedicated workflow administrator. The work description notes that the incumbent coordinates work groups, monitors progress, writes monitoring procedures, and examines revised processing specifications for their effect on integration and coordination with other systems. The capability involved is operationalizing designed processes, clarifying handoffs, and ensuring configured systems and procedures support production objectives. The position fulfills this need by translating subject-matter requirements into system specifications, preparing manuals and procedures, and assessing operational impacts of revised specifications. Future-state drivers around integrated data pipelines, process orchestration, AI and automation, enterprise platforms and operational efficiency will make workflow configuration more standardized, automated and monitored. This role is likely to be affected because its current responsibilities already sit at the boundary between subject-matter analysis and operational system implementation. Evidence includes: 'monitoring procedures,' 'develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' and 'determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions.'

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance because the position contributes to training materials, procedural documentation and advice related to collection operations, though it is not described as directly setting up collection infrastructure. The work description states that the incumbent writes 'training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs' and provides feedback on collection methods and procedures. The capability involved is supporting operational readiness through documentation, guidance and analytical feedback. Future-state drivers such as digital collection, online-first strategy, AI-enabled tools and workforce skills transition may increase the importance of such support materials and procedural guidance. Evidence includes the preparation of training packages and monitoring procedures and the role in recommending improvements to collection methods.

This subprocess is only indirectly relevant. The position does not directly run collection, but it reviews collection results and identifies problems in collection operations. The work description states that the incumbent 'reviews statistical survey and production results' and 'identifies and evaluates problems in the collection... of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management.' The capability involved is analytical oversight of collection outcomes rather than direct operational execution. Future-state drivers such as adaptive collection, online-first operations and automated monitoring may increase the analytical importance of reviewing collection performance and recommending adjustments, but the role remains secondary to the subprocess. Evidence includes review of survey results and evaluation of collection problems.

This subprocess is strongly implicated because the position works with multiple data sources, verifies comparability, modifies data to permit comparison, and examines integration effects across systems. The work description states that the incumbent 'specifies sources of data,' 'verifies the consistency and comparability of the various sets of data obtained and modifies the data to permit comparison,' 'researches and compiles data from diverse sources,' and 'examines... revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' The capability involved is multi-source integration, harmonisation, comparability assessment, and resolving conceptual and technical conflicts across datasets. The position fulfills this need directly through source comparison, adaptation of data to new definitions, and assessment of impacts of different concepts and collection conditions. Future-state drivers make this even more central: administrative, alternative and linked data expansion, metadata-driven management, enterprise platforms, integrated pipelines, cyber/privacy controls and modern statistical methods all increase the scale and complexity of integration work. Workforce implications include stronger need for skills in linkage, harmonisation, metadata use and exception-based oversight. Evidence includes: 'diverse sources,' 'consistency and comparability,' 'modifies the data to permit comparison,' and 'integration and co-ordination... with other divisional systems.'

This subprocess has plausible but limited relevance. The work description does not explicitly assign coding responsibilities, but it does include knowledge of processing, editing, compilation and statistical packages, and the role develops methods and procedures that could affect coding approaches. The capability connection is therefore indirect: methodological and system changes may influence classification and coding routines. Future-state drivers such as AI-enabled automated coding and automation may affect the role through broader processing modernization, but the supplied work description does not provide direct evidence of coding work. Evidence is limited to general responsibilities for processing-system enhancements and knowledge of statistical methods and software.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position explicitly reviews results, assesses impacts of concepts and conditions on results, and identifies technical and subject-matter problems in collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation. The work description states that the incumbent 'reviews statistical survey and production results,' 'identifies and evaluates problems in the collection, capture, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information,' and 'assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.' The capability involved is analytical validation, quality review, discrepancy detection, and interpretation of how methodological or source conditions affect data quality. The position fulfills this need directly through review of results, trend identification, and assessment of constraints on outputs. Future-state drivers such as AI and automation, administrative and linked data expansion, metadata-driven management, integrated pipelines, modular validation components and operational efficiency will increase reliance on automated checks, exception handling and metadata-aware validation. The role's analytical expertise and subject-matter knowledge make it materially connected to this evolving validation environment. Evidence includes: 'reviews statistical survey and production results,' 'identifies and evaluates problems,' and 'assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results.'

This subprocess is relevant because the position works on processing, editing and methodological improvement, although the work description does not explicitly state that the incumbent performs imputation. The incumbent identifies and evaluates problems in 'processing, editing, compilation and presentation,' reviews methods and procedures, and develops new statistical methods and procedures. The capability involved is improving correction-related methods and understanding how data issues should be addressed within processing. The position fulfills this need by proposing changes to methods and procedures and resolving conceptual and technical problems affecting data quality. Future-state drivers such as automation, AI-assisted editing and imputation, administrative-source replacement and metadata-rich process documentation will likely change this work from manual or ad hoc correction support toward more rule-based and model-assisted approaches. Evidence includes: 'processing, editing,' 'develops new statistical methods, concepts and procedures,' and 'reviews current... editing... methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes.'

This subprocess is relevant because the position adapts data to new definitions and presentation formats, develops methods and concepts, and applies econometric and modelling knowledge in special studies. The capability involved is deriving analytically useful variables or comparable measures from existing data and definitions, even if the work description does not explicitly use the term 'derive variables.' The position fulfills this need by modifying data to permit comparison, adapting data to new definitions, and using statistical and econometric techniques in subject-matter studies. Future-state drivers such as administrative and linked data expansion, modern statistical methods, metadata-driven derivation logic and integrated pipelines will increase the importance of deriving variables from existing and linked sources rather than collecting them directly. Evidence includes: 'modifies the data to permit comparison,' 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats,' and knowledge of econometrics, modelling and statistical techniques.

This subprocess is relevant because the position participates in analysis of statistical program data, produces charts and tables, and prepares analytical material for publication. The capability involved is transforming processed data into aggregated analytical outputs and reviewing resulting trends and developments. The position fulfills this need by 'research[ing] and compil[ing] data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output' and by participating in analysis for internal and publication purposes.
