Future-state drivers such as modern statistical methods, geospatial outputs, timelier production and automated pipelines may change how aggregates are produced and delivered, but the role's connection remains through analytical use and preparation of aggregate outputs rather than specialized weighting methodology. Evidence includes: 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data,' 'preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes,' and 'produce statistical charts, tables and other output.'

This subprocess is relevant because the position brings together data from multiple sources, adapts them for comparison and presentation, and supports the transition from processing to analysis and publication. The capability involved is assembling analysis-ready datasets and outputs with sufficient consistency, comparability and documentation for downstream use. The position fulfills this need by compiling data from diverse sources, adapting data to new definitions or formats, and examining how processing specifications affect integration with other systems. Future-state drivers such as integrated pipelines, metadata-driven packaging, enterprise platforms and timelier production will make finalization more standardized and automated, affecting how this role prepares and hands off data for analysis and publication. Evidence includes: 'researches and compiles data from diverse sources,' 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats,' and participation in preparing analytical material for publication.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position explicitly participates in analysis and preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication, and produces charts, tables and other outputs. The work description states that the incumbent 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes' and 'researches and compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output.' The capability involved is transforming processed data into draft analytical products, explanatory material and publication-ready content. The position fulfills this need directly through analysis, output preparation and support to subject-matter studies. Future-state drivers such as AI assistants, metadata-rich outputs, integrated pipelines, modern methods and more granular or geospatial products will change how draft outputs are prepared, with more automation but also greater need for methodological explanation and transparency. Workforce implications include stronger use of digital and analytical tools and more emphasis on explaining outputs produced through modernized methods. Evidence includes: 'preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes' and 'produce statistical charts, tables and other output.'

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position identifies trends and developments, reviews survey and production results, and assesses impacts and constraints on results. The capability involved is validating whether outputs make sense in light of subject-matter expectations, source conditions and methodological context. The position fulfills this need by reviewing results, identifying trends, assessing implications for methods and procedures, and supporting subject-matter studies and reviews. Future-state drivers such as administrative and linked data expansion, AI-enabled production, metadata-rich quality indicators and modern methods increase the need for stronger output validation against prior cycles, auxiliary sources and domain intelligence. The role's subject-matter expertise and analytical responsibilities make it materially connected to this subprocess. Evidence includes: 'identifies statistical trends and developments and reviews statistical survey and production results,' 'assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results,' and 'assists in subject matter studies and reviews.'

This subprocess is directly connected to the role's analytical and advisory functions. The work description states that the incumbent participates in analysis, identifies trends and developments, provides data, assistance and advice to users within and outside Statistics Canada, and writes and presents detailed subject-matter and technical concepts in common terminology. The capability involved is interpreting statistical results, explaining their meaning, and communicating them clearly to internal and external users. The position fulfills this need by analyzing data, identifying trends, advising users on concepts and results, and translating technical concepts into common terminology. Future-state drivers such as AI-assisted analysis, mixed-source outputs, advanced methods and workforce skills transition will increase the need for clear explanation of methodological changes, source integration and modern analytical approaches. Communication, analytical expertise and transparency are especially relevant. Evidence includes: 'identifies statistical trends and developments,' 'provides data, assistance and advice to users,' and 'writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts... to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.'

This subprocess is relevant because the position contributes analytical material for publication, provides advice to users, and writes manuals, reports and explanatory material. The capability involved is helping ensure outputs and supporting information are fit for use, understandable and aligned with subject-matter and technical requirements. The position fulfills this need by preparing analytical material for publication, writing management reports and manuals, and communicating concepts and results to users and colleagues. Future-state drivers such as metadata-driven release readiness, AI-related caveats, governance and decision discipline, and modern methods will increase the amount and importance of supporting notes, quality explanations and internal review material. Evidence includes: 'preparation of analytical material for... publication purposes,' 'writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports,' and 'provides advice to data users and clients.'

This subprocess is relevant because the position helps produce analytical material and statistical charts, tables and outputs for publication, and communicates with users and clients. The capability involved is assembling substantive content for dissemination products and ensuring explanatory material accompanies outputs. The position fulfills this need by preparing analytical material for publication, producing charts and tables, and writing explanatory and technical materials. Future-state drivers such as metadata-rich dissemination, digital products, automation, standardization and accessibility will affect how these products are assembled and documented. Evidence includes: 'preparation of analytical material for... publication purposes,' 'produce statistical charts, tables and other output,' and 'writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts.'

This subprocess is directly relevant because the work description explicitly states that the incumbent 'provides data, assistance and advice to users within and outside Statistics Canada' and 'provides advice to data users and clients on matters relating to subject-matter concepts used in the development and operation of a statistical database and to the data processing environment in general.' The capability involved is responding to user needs, explaining data and methods, and supporting clients and internal users. The position fulfills this need directly through advisory services, liaison with users and clients, and preparation of manuals and training materials. Future-state drivers indicate that user support will increasingly involve AI chatbots, self-service platforms, metadata-rich repositories, secure access processes and more questions about modernized methods, linked data and digital products. This role is materially affected because its current responsibilities already center on user-facing explanation and support. Workforce implications include stronger need for communication skills, methodological understanding and efficient support practices under staffing pressure. Evidence includes: 'provides data, assistance and advice to users,' 'provides advice to data users and clients,' and liaison with specialists and users.

This subprocess is relevant because the position reviews results, writes monitoring procedures and management reports, and supports studies and reviews that can feed evaluation. The capability involved is generating and documenting evidence on program performance, methodological issues and operational impacts. The position fulfills this need by reviewing survey and production results, identifying problems, writing monitoring procedures, and assisting in subject-matter studies and reviews. Future-state drivers such as AI-enabled monitoring, integrated pipelines, metadata-rich process indicators, operational efficiency and workforce transition will increase the amount of process metadata, quality indicators and staff feedback available for evaluation. The role's current production of monitoring procedures and analytical reviews makes it a meaningful contributor. Evidence includes: 'reviews statistical survey and production results,' 'writes... monitoring procedures and management reports,' and 'assists in subject matter studies and reviews.'

This subprocess is relevant because the position assists in subject-matter studies and reviews, analyzes results, identifies trends and developments, and recommends improvements to methods and activities. The capability involved is synthesizing evidence about performance and quality into findings and recommendations. The position fulfills this need by reviewing methods and procedures for relevancy, proposing changes or alternative systems, assessing impacts on results, and supporting project teams or senior officers through studies and reviews. Future-state drivers such as operational efficiency, governance, AI and automation, modern methods and workforce transition will make evaluation more continuous, dashboard-driven and focused on quality, timeliness, efficiency and sustainability. This role is likely to contribute substantively to such evaluations through its analytical and methodological review functions. Evidence includes: 'reviews current... methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems,' 'identifies and assesses trends and developments,' and 'assists in subject matter studies and reviews.'

This subprocess concerns identifying what statistics are needed in response to user requests, environmental change, periodic review, or respondent feedback. The position is relevant because it "participates in the analysis of socio-economic trends and developments to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs," undertakes subject-matter studies/reviews, and provides advice to users. Those duties directly support identifying emerging statistical needs and assessing whether new needs should be pursued. The capability involved is subject-matter analysis, environmental scanning, and translating user or policy developments into potential program needs. Future-state drivers make this work more selective: under Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, need identification will be more constrained by prioritization, fewer staff, and the search for efficient alternatives using AI, automation, machine learning, and new tools and methods. Evidence includes the duties to assess feasibility and impact of new or modified programs, identify changes and developments in the subject area, and interpret program and user needs for statistical information.

This subprocess establishes the statistical outputs required to meet confirmed user needs, including quality, scope, timeliness and resource considerations. The position is materially connected because it "undertakes the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes," assesses user needs, and translates them into concrete products: it "interprets program and user needs for statistical information, assesses the suitability of existing data products and services and translates them into a concrete, timely and affordable product." That is direct evidence of contributing to output objectives. The capability involved is balancing subject-matter requirements, quality, affordability, and operational feasibility. Future changes will come from Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment: output objectives will be narrowed to highest-value outcomes, with more explicit trade-offs among scope, timeliness, granularity and quality under scarce resources and reduced staffing. Evidence also includes discussing content requirements with managers and clients, writing management reports, and recommending alternative statistical methods and approaches.

This subprocess assesses whether existing data sources can meet requirements and under what legal, technical, quality and access conditions. It is highly relevant because the work description explicitly states that the position "reviews data collection and information systems to determine the usefulness of the existing data sources, to propose changes to the system and to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs." It also requires knowledge of collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods; system analysis and design; databases; and legislative requirements under the Statistics Act and Privacy Act. The capability involved is evaluating source usefulness, feasibility, quality, legal constraints, and operational implications. The role fulfills this need by analyzing current methods, identifying data conflicts and gaps, and recommending changes to systems and sources. Future-state drivers intensify this work substantially. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will shift source strategy toward administrative data, alternative data, SDLE-enabled linkage, gridded data, and online-first approaches. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure increase the importance of assessing cloud feasibility, enterprise platforms, metadata, workflow integration, and data extraction from unstructured sources. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access is especially relevant because the work description explicitly emphasizes confidentiality, security, manipulation, storage and retrieval of data under the Statistics and Privacy Acts. Governance and prioritization drivers will also force more explicit trade-offs in source selection. Evidence includes reviewing existing data sources, assessing feasibility and impact of new programs, knowledge of databases and generalized survey software, and legal/privacy responsibilities.

This subprocess documents options, costs, benefits, risks, resources and recommendations for new or modified statistical processes. The position is relevant because it assesses the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs, develops recommendations for improvements, leads special studies, develops operational plans and project priorities, and plans and budgets for special projects. While the work description does not explicitly say the incumbent writes formal business cases, it clearly supports the analytical and planning inputs that business cases require. The capability involved is option analysis, feasibility assessment, cost-awareness, project planning, and recommendation development. Future-state drivers increase the importance of disciplined approval packages: Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will require clearer trade-offs, milestones, accountability and go/no-go logic; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will foreground savings and affordability; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require explicit consideration of training, staffing and sequencing. Evidence includes assessing feasibility and impact of new or modified programs, developing operational plans and project priorities, planning and budgeting special projects, and writing management reports and manuals.

This subprocess designs statistical outputs, products and dissemination approaches. The position is connected because it prepares analytical material for publication, suggests improvements to presentation methods and procedures, writes detailed subject-matter and technical concepts in common terminology, and writes program information manuals and reports. The capability involved is shaping how outputs are presented, explained and made usable to internal and external users. The role fulfills this need by analyzing outputs, advising on presentation methods, and communicating concepts clearly to managers, clients and users. Future-state drivers imply more standardized, metadata-rich and digitally delivered outputs. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the need for outputs to be structured and documented for reuse and searchability; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and AI and Automation in Statistical Production will push toward platform-based, reusable dissemination patterns; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will strengthen confidentiality-by-design considerations. Evidence includes assisting in preparation of analytical material for publication, suggesting feedback on compilation and presentation methods, and writing explanatory materials.

This subprocess defines collected and derived variables, units and classifications. The position is materially connected because it "modifies existing techniques and approaches... and develops subject-matter concepts and definitions," and has knowledge of concepts, methods and techniques used in collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data to resolve concept and definition issues. The capability involved is subject-matter conceptualization, definition of variables and classifications, and ensuring concepts align with analytical and operational needs. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase pressure to harmonize variables across linked and administrative sources, document metadata more rigorously, and support derived and model-based variables. Evidence includes developing subject-matter concepts and definitions, resolving concept and definition issues, and reviewing new subject-matter methods, concepts and definitions.

This subprocess designs collection strategies, instruments and methods. The position is relevant because it suggests feedback on collection methods and procedures following data analysis, develops recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities, identifies and evaluates problems in collection, and has working knowledge of survey design and sampling theory. The capability involved is using analytical evidence and subject-matter expertise to improve collection design and respondent-facing methods. The role fulfills this need by reviewing collection methods for relevance and recommending modifications or replacements. Future-state drivers indicate meaningful change: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will shift collection toward online-first, adaptive, administrative and alternative-source models; AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will embed digital tools, APIs and automated workflows; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push lower-touch collection. Evidence includes explicit references to collection processing, survey methods, survey design knowledge, and analysis of collection methods and procedures.

This subprocess defines populations, frames and sampling methodology. The position is materially connected because the work description requires "a thorough knowledge of ... sampling theory" and working knowledge of survey design, and includes analyzing geographic, demographic, social, economic and labour market characteristics and preparing profiles and forecasts. While the role is not described as directly selecting samples, it contributes subject-matter and methodological expertise relevant to frame and sample design. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increasingly tie frame design to administrative registers, linked data and geospatial inputs, making subject-matter analysis and sampling expertise more important in redesign. Evidence includes knowledge of sampling theory and survey design, and analytical work on population characteristics.

This subprocess designs coding, editing, imputation, integration, validation, estimation and disclosure-related methods. It is highly relevant because the position explicitly analyzes and evaluates problems in "collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information," suggests feedback on collection processing and editing methods, reviews current processing and editing procedures to determine whether modification or replacement is needed, and has knowledge of system analysis and design, generalized survey software, databases, statistical packages, and econometric methods. The capability involved is methodological design for processing and analysis, including choosing and improving analytical and operational methods. The role fulfills this need by reviewing methods, identifying technical and conceptual problems, and recommending alternative statistical methods and approaches. Future-state drivers strongly affect this work: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture and Reusable Components, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition all point toward more automated, metadata-driven, reusable, integrated and model-assisted processing. The work description's emphasis on changing methods, systems and approaches, plus knowledge of programming languages and statistical packages, indicates the role will be materially reshaped by these drivers. Evidence includes repeated references to processing, editing, compilation, system design, testing, databases, and statistical packages.

This subprocess designs end-to-end workflows, systems, databases and staff interactions across production. The position is relevant because it reviews collection and information systems, proposes changes to systems, has knowledge of system analysis and design and computer processing, and discusses requirements with operations managers, systems specialists and service providers to translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development. The capability involved is linking subject-matter requirements to operational systems and workflows. The role fulfills this need by liaising across functions, suggesting procedural modifications, and helping define specifications and project plans. Future-state drivers such as Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Governance and Prioritization, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition will increase standardization, reuse, automation, clearer handoffs and changed staff-system interactions. Evidence includes translating requirements into specifications for system development, knowledge of system analysis and design, and discussing operational frameworks with managers and specialists.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess concerns building or reusing processing and analysis components. The position is only plausibly connected because it has knowledge of generalized survey software, databases, programming languages and statistical packages, and helps design specifications for testing data and maintaining databases. However, the work description does not explicitly assign software build responsibility. The relevance is therefore limited to contributing analytical specifications and methodological requirements rather than directly building components. Future-state drivers around AI, reusable components, enterprise platforms and workforce upskilling may increase indirect impact on the role as more analytical staff contribute to reusable methods and component requirements. Evidence includes knowledge of system analysis and design, testing specifications, database maintenance and use of programming/statistical packages.

This subprocess tests assembled services and workflows. The position has limited but plausible involvement because it includes knowledge to "design specifications for the testing of data" and to manage design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems. This suggests contribution to testing criteria and suitability assessment, though not primary responsibility for system testing. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation, Enterprise Platforms, Integrated Pipelines and Modular Architecture may increase the need for analytical staff to validate whether systems and methods are fit for use. Evidence is limited to testing specifications and system design knowledge, so relevance remains low.

This subprocess prepares people, processes and technology for collection. The position is only indirectly connected through its role in writing training packages, monitoring procedures and manuals for operational staff and management, and through recommending improvements to survey methods and activities. The capability involved is supporting operational readiness through documentation and subject-matter guidance rather than directly setting up collection. Future-state drivers around digital collection, online-first operations, training needs and workforce transition may increase indirect effects on the role because more documentation, guidance and methodological support will be needed. Evidence includes writing training packages and monitoring procedures and discussing requirements with operations managers.

This subprocess executes collection operations. The position is not a collection operations role, but it is plausibly connected because it analyzes collection methods and procedures after the fact, provides subject-matter advice, and may encounter respondent or client resistance and criticism. The role is more affected by collection outcomes than directly responsible for running collection. Future-state drivers such as adaptive collection, online-first strategy and automated monitoring may change the kinds of collection feedback and analytical review the position performs. Evidence includes suggesting feedback on collection processing and analyzing collection methods, but no direct responsibility for live collection execution.

This subprocess combines data from multiple sources, harmonises values and supports linkage and prioritisation. The position is materially connected because it reviews usefulness of existing data sources, identifies data conflicts, analyzes and synthesizes multiple types of characteristics, and assesses suitability of existing data products and services. It also has knowledge of databases, data retrieval and manipulation, and collection/processing concepts. The capability involved is analytical integration of information from multiple sources and resolving conceptual conflicts. Future-state drivers make this more important: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security, Enterprise Platforms, Integrated Data Pipelines, Metadata-Driven Management and Modern Statistical Methods all increase the centrality of multi-source integration, linkage, harmonisation and secure handling. Evidence includes identifying and evaluating data conflicts, reviewing existing data sources, maintaining and developing databases, and retrieving/manipulating data with statistical packages.

This subprocess classifies and codes input data. The position has limited relevance because it works with processing, editing and compilation methods and uses statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data, but the work description does not explicitly assign coding responsibilities. The role may be affected by future AI-enabled automated coding and harmonisation of administrative or alternative-source classifications, especially when analyzing data quality and recommending processing improvements. Evidence is indirect: knowledge of processing and editing methods, statistical packages, and resolving technical problems.

This subprocess identifies errors, discrepancies, outliers, duplicates and other quality issues before correction. It is highly relevant because the position explicitly "identifies and evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information," analyzes current methods and procedures for relevancy, reviews survey results to interpret concepts and methods, and compares old and new versions of data. The capability involved is analytical quality review, validation of data and methods, and diagnosing conceptual and technical issues. The role fulfills this need by reviewing data and methods, resolving subject-matter and technical problems, and recommending solutions to management. Future-state drivers strongly affect this work: AI and Automation, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Pipelines, Metadata-Driven Management, Modern Statistical Methods, Modular Architecture and Operational Efficiency all increase automated validation, exception handling, metadata checks and multi-source quality assessment. Evidence includes identifying problems in processing and editing, reviewing results of projects and surveys, and occasional sensory observation when comparing old and new versions of data.

This subprocess corrects or replaces incorrect, missing or unreliable data and records metadata on those changes. The position is materially connected because it analyzes and evaluates problems in editing and processing, suggests feedback on editing methods and procedures, and reviews current editing methods to determine whether they should be modified or replaced. The capability involved is methodological oversight of editing approaches and recommending improved correction strategies. The work description does not explicitly say the incumbent performs imputation directly, so relevance is medium rather than high. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Pipelines, Metadata-Driven Management, Modern Statistical Methods and Operational Efficiency will push editing and imputation toward more automated, source-prioritized and metadata-documented methods. Evidence includes explicit references to editing methods and procedures and identifying problems in editing.

This subprocess derives variables and units not directly collected. The position is relevant because it develops subject-matter concepts and definitions, modifies techniques and approaches, analyzes and synthesizes characteristics to prepare profiles and forecasts, and reviews methods, concepts and definitions. The capability involved is deriving analytical constructs from existing data and applying econometric and statistical methods to produce needed measures. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase reliance on derived variables from linked, administrative and geospatial sources, while Metadata-Driven Management and Integrated Pipelines will require clearer derivation logic and sequencing. Evidence includes preparing profiles and forecasts, developing concepts and definitions, and using econometric methods and statistical packages.

This subprocess creates weights for records according to methodology. The position has plausible but limited involvement because it requires knowledge of sampling theory and survey design, which underpin weighting, but the work description does not explicitly mention weighting responsibilities. Future-state changes in hybrid survey-administrative designs and adaptive collection may affect the methodological context in which the role works, but evidence for direct weighting work is limited. Evidence consists mainly of knowledge of sampling theory and survey design.

This subprocess creates aggregate data and totals from microdata. The position is materially connected because it undertakes analysis of statistical program data, prepares analytical material for publication, analyzes and synthesizes geographic, demographic, social, economic and labour market characteristics, and reviews survey results to provide interpretation and analysis. The capability involved is transforming detailed data into analytical summaries, profiles, forecasts and interpretable outputs. Future-state drivers such as Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may expand granular, geospatial and model-based aggregates, while automation and integrated pipelines may standardize routine aggregate production. Evidence includes analysis of statistical program data, preparation of analytical material, and preparation of profiles and forecasts.

This subprocess assembles final datasets for analysis. The position is only indirectly connected through its work with databases, data retrieval/manipulation, and review of processing methods and outputs. The work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for final dataset assembly. Future-state integrated pipelines and metadata-driven production may affect the role through more standardized handoffs and analysis-ready files, but direct evidence is limited.

This subprocess transforms processed data into draft statistical outputs and methodological notes. It is highly relevant because the position "undertakes the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes," writes detailed subject-matter and technical concepts in common terminology, and reviews survey results to provide interpretation and analysis on concepts, methods and techniques used. The capability involved is converting analytical results into usable outputs with explanatory context. The role fulfills this need directly through publication-oriented analytical preparation and explanatory writing. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation, Metadata-Driven Management, Modern Statistical Methods and Operational Efficiency will increase automation of routine output preparation but also increase the need for methodological explanation, transparency and metadata-rich packaging. Evidence includes preparation of analytical material for publication and writing explanatory manuals and reports.

This subprocess validates outputs against expectations, prior cycles, metadata, quality indicators and domain intelligence. It is highly relevant because the position reviews project and survey results to provide interpretation and analysis, analyzes socio-economic trends and developments, identifies changes and developments in the subject area, and assesses suitability of products and services. The capability involved is applying subject-matter expertise and analytical judgment to determine whether outputs make sense and meet expectations. The role fulfills this need by comparing results to domain knowledge, identifying conflicts and gaps, and advising on concepts, methods and results. Future-state drivers such as Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods, AI and Automation, Metadata-Driven Management and Operational Efficiency will make output validation more complex because of methodological breaks, mixed-source outputs and automated production. Evidence includes analysis of trends and developments, review of survey results, and advice on methods, techniques and results.

This subprocess interprets outputs and explains their meaning using analytical tools and domain knowledge. It is one of the most directly connected subprocesses. The work description states that the position undertakes analysis of statistical program data, prepares analytical material for publication, analyzes socio-economic trends and developments, analyzes and synthesizes characteristics and prepares profiles and forecasts, reviews survey results to provide interpretation and analysis, and provides subject matter advice to users within and outside Statistics Canada. The capability involved is substantive interpretation, econometric and socio-economic analysis, and communication of meaning to users and management. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Workforce Skills Transition will change both the analytical basis of outputs and the tools used to interpret them, increasing the need to explain mixed-source, model-based and AI-influenced results clearly and credibly. Evidence includes multiple explicit references to analysis, interpretation, forecasts, advice to users, and writing/presenting technical concepts in common terminology.

This subprocess ensures outputs do not breach confidentiality rules. The position is materially connected because the work description explicitly emphasizes knowledge of the Statistics Act, Privacy Act and related policies, and states that security and confidentiality of information are particularly important to ensure that neither the incumbent nor subordinates release identifying information without prior consent. The capability involved is understanding confidentiality obligations and applying them when handling, storing, retrieving and communicating data. While the role is not described as a specialist disclosure-control function, it is clearly responsible for respecting and explaining confidentiality requirements in analytical and advisory work. Future-state drivers such as Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Administrative/Linked Data Expansion will increase disclosure complexity, especially with linked and geospatial data and broader digital access. Evidence includes explicit confidentiality and privacy responsibilities and advice to users on manipulation, storage and retrieval of data.

This subprocess ensures outputs and supporting information are fit for purpose and ready for release, including commentary, technical notes, uncertainty information, internal briefings and approval support. It is highly relevant because the position prepares analytical material for publication, writes management reports, manuals, training packages and monitoring procedures, writes and presents detailed subject-matter and technical concepts in common terminology, and provides advice to managers, clients and users. The capability involved is final analytical packaging, explanatory documentation, and supporting internal and external understanding of outputs. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Metadata-Driven Management, Modern Statistical Methods, AI and Automation, Governance and Workforce Skills Transition will increase pressure for timely finalization, clearer caveats, stronger metadata, and more explicit explanation of modern methods and trade-offs. Evidence includes publication-oriented analytical preparation, explanatory writing, and communication with managers and clients.

This subprocess assembles dissemination products such as publications, tables, maps and explanatory texts. The position is materially connected because it assists in preparing analytical material for publication, writes explanatory and technical material, and suggests improvements to presentation methods and procedures. The capability involved is producing the analytical and explanatory content that feeds dissemination products. The role is not a dissemination production specialist, but it contributes directly to product content and quality. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Management, Enterprise Platforms, AI and Automation, Modern Statistical Methods and Operational Efficiency will push toward more standardized, metadata-rich, digital and reusable products, affecting how this analytical content is prepared. Evidence includes preparation of analytical material for publication and writing manuals, reports and explanatory concepts.

This subprocess records and responds to user queries and service requests. The position is materially connected because it "provides assistance and subject matter advice to data users within and outside STC," provides information and advice to managers, data users and clients, liaises with users and client departments, and encounters resistance or criticism from external clients, media and the public. The capability involved is user-facing subject-matter support, explanation of concepts and methods, and responding to information needs. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation, Enterprise Digital Platforms, Metadata-Driven Discoverability and Operational Efficiency will likely shift some support toward self-service, FAQs, chatbots and knowledge bases, while increasing the complexity of questions about methods, data sources and confidentiality. Evidence includes explicit user support and advisory duties and liaison with client departments.

This subprocess gathers feedback, process metadata, system metrics and staff suggestions for evaluation. The position is relevant because it suggests feedback on collection processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods following data analysis; writes monitoring procedures and management reports; undertakes studies/reviews in support of project teams or senior officers; and reviews project and survey results. The capability involved is generating evidence on what worked, what did not, and where improvements are needed. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation, Enterprise Platforms, Integrated Pipelines, Modern Statistical Methods and Workforce Skills Transition will increase the amount of process metadata, monitoring information and staff feedback available and needed for evaluation. Evidence includes explicit feedback on methods and procedures, writing monitoring procedures, and reviewing results of projects and surveys.

This subprocess analyzes evaluation inputs and synthesizes findings into reports or dashboards with recommendations. The position is materially connected because it conducts studies and analytical projects to improve existing surveys and data, reviews results of projects and surveys, analyzes current methods and procedures to determine need for modification or replacement, and develops recommendations for improvements. The capability involved is evaluative analysis of program performance, methods and outputs. Future-state drivers such as Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Agility and Execution Discipline, AI and Automation, Modern Statistical Methods and Workforce Skills Transition will make evaluation more continuous, dashboard-driven and focused on quality, timeliness, efficiency, workforce readiness and sustainability. Evidence includes conducting analytical projects to improve surveys and data, reviewing methods for relevancy, and developing recommendations.

This subprocess agrees an action plan based on evaluation findings. The position has limited but plausible involvement because it develops recommendations for improvements, develops operational plans and project priorities, leads project teams, and plans special projects. However, the work description does not explicitly assign formal decision-making authority for enterprise action plans. The capability involved is contributing recommendations and planning inputs rather than final governance decisions. Future-state drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility and Workforce Skills Transition may increase the importance of disciplined follow-through on recommendations, but direct evidence remains limited. Evidence includes developing recommendations, operational plans and project priorities, and leading project teams involved in special studies.

This subprocess is relevant because the position directly investigates and identifies statistical information needs. The work description states that the Research Analyst "investigates client requirements for statistical information," determines data sources, and develops or modifies methods to meet specific needs. It also notes knowledge of client departments' policies and programs "to determine their information requirements and identify analysis opportunities," and knowledge of data users and suppliers to understand their needs for statistical data or studies. These are core need-identification responsibilities. The capability involved is substantive analytical scoping of user demand and translating it into feasible statistical work. Future-state change is driven by Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment: stronger prioritization under fiscal constraint, fewer staff, and pressure to find efficiencies will make this need-identification work more selective and triaged. Because the role already investigates requirements and defines approaches, it will likely face sharper decisions about which needs can be pursued and whether AI, automation, machine learning, or new tools and methods offer lower-cost ways to meet them.

This subprocess is implicated because the position helps define what outputs should be produced and at what level of scope, quality, and feasibility. Evidence includes: the analyst "defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources" and writes analytical material for publication and dissemination to audiences ranging from the general public to academics. The role also develops proposals and recommendations to improve surveys or initiate new projects, which connects directly to setting output objectives. The capability involved is balancing user needs, methodological quality, confidentiality, and available resources in deciding what outputs will be delivered. Future changes are shaped by Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. Those drivers will force clearer trade-offs among scope, timeliness, granularity, and quality, with scarcer resources focused on highest-value outcomes. Since this role already sets project priorities and prepares dissemination-ready analytical outputs, it will be increasingly affected by explicit accountability, transparent trade-offs, and tighter resource constraints when defining deliverables.

This is one of the most directly connected subprocesses. The work description repeatedly emphasizes assessing and integrating data from multiple sources: the analyst "determines data sources," selects methods to integrate and interpret "mass volumes of data," and works with data from "financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses" collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts. The role also researches gaps and inconsistencies in collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods; reviews conceptual compatibility with other statistical programs; and proposes new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions. The capability involved is judging whether existing sources are suitable, comparable, legally usable, and conceptually harmonizable for statistical purposes. This aligns strongly with the subprocess description. Future-state impacts are substantial and cumulative. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase reliance on administrative data, alternative data, SDLE-enabled linkage, gridded data, and online-first approaches. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase scrutiny of confidentiality, privacy, authorizations, and secure access conditions. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will make platform fit, centralized repositories, and secure ingestion more important. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata quality and interoperability more central to source assessment. Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will expand use of linked, unstructured, and integrated sources. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will intensify pressure to replace labour-intensive collection with reusable sources. The work description's explicit focus on integrating conceptually different data sources, assessing quality and comparability over time, and recommending source changes is direct evidence of material relevance.

This subprocess is relevant because the position develops proposals, recommendations, work plans, priorities, budgets, and resource estimates for analytical projects and survey/program improvements, even though the description does not explicitly say the incumbent prepares formal business cases for approval bodies. Evidence includes: "defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources," "develops guidelines, proposals and recommendations for divisional management to improve existing surveys or to initiate new surveys / projects," and plans and budgets for ongoing and special projects, including salaries, professional fees, implementation costs, contracts, and procurement. The capability involved is articulating options, costs, resources, timelines, and operational implications for management decisions. Future-state drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make these proposal and planning activities more formalized, comparative, and constrained. The role will likely need to frame recommendations more explicitly around trade-offs, affordability, implementation readiness, workforce capacity, and modernization options, even if final business-case approval is outside the position.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position directly produces and shapes analytical outputs for dissemination. The work description states the analyst "writes/edits analytical material for publication purposes," writes and presents analytical material to audiences from the general public to specialized users, and requires knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices to establish divisional policies for tables, charts, explanatory notes, and dissemination. The capability involved is designing analytical products so they are interpretable, methodologically explained, and suitable for dissemination under departmental standards. Future-state impacts come from Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity. Outputs will increasingly need richer metadata, discoverability, secure access controls for sensitive products, reusable digital dissemination patterns, and accessible design. The role's existing responsibility to explain complex data clearly, tailor outputs to different audiences, and maintain the department's reputation for high-quality data makes it materially connected to evolving output and dissemination design.

This subprocess is relevant because the position recommends modifications to study content, concepts, methods, and definitions, and integrates data collected under different definitions into common conceptual frameworks. Evidence includes determining data requirements, recommending modifications to the content and coverage of studies, procedures, concepts, methods and definitions, and integrating data from varied sources using different definitions or concepts. The capability involved is conceptual and methodological design of what variables mean, how they align across sources, and how derived concepts support analysis. The work description does not explicitly assign questionnaire-variable design responsibility, so relevance is medium rather than high. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase pressure to harmonize variables across administrative, linked, geospatial, and alternative sources and to document them with richer metadata. Because this role already translates diverse source concepts into common frameworks, it will be meaningfully affected by more metadata-driven and linkage-oriented variable design.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance. The work description does not state that the Research Analyst designs collection instruments or field operations. However, the role does recommend improvements to surveys and statistical programs, works with data suppliers and users, discusses data reporting agreements, and understands respondent relations, confidentiality, and data quality policies. Those responsibilities create some connection to collection design choices, especially where analytical requirements drive changes to content, coverage, or source arrangements. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may indirectly affect the role as collection shifts toward online-first, administrative, alternative, and linked-source acquisition. Still, because the supplied description centers on research, modeling, analysis, and program improvement rather than direct collection design, relevance remains low.

There is limited evidence for direct frame or sample design responsibility. The role has advanced statistical knowledge and recommends changes to studies and surveys, and it works with multiple data sources and quality/comparability issues. That suggests some analytical interaction with population coverage and source suitability. However, the work description does not explicitly mention defining target populations, sampling frames, or sampling methodologies. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may indirectly affect the role where register-based or linked-source designs alter the analytical basis of outputs the analyst interprets and improves. Because no explicit sampling responsibility is stated, relevance is low.

This subprocess is central to the position. The work description states the analyst develops and conducts research and modeling studies; selects and evaluates analytical techniques and quantitative methods; reviews and modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones; integrates and interprets massive volumes of data; identifies and measures complex relationships among variables; and interprets data quality, comparability, and relevance. It also researches gaps and inconsistencies in collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and conceptualizes enhancements or modifications to methods and operational procedures. The capability involved is methodological design for coding, validation, integration, estimation, and analysis. Future-state impacts are strong and cumulative: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all point toward more automated, metadata-driven, reusable, integrated, and advanced analytical methods. The role's explicit responsibility for selecting, evaluating, modifying, and developing analytical methods makes this subprocess highly relevant now and in the future.

This subprocess is relevant because the position leads project teams, manages units involved in statistical activities, plans and schedules work, resolves conflicting priorities, negotiates with system specialists and other service providers, and represents the division on development projects, task forces, and committees. While the description does not say the analyst designs enterprise workflows or systems architecture directly, it does show responsibility for coordinating multidisciplinary work and shaping how analytical projects operate. The capability involved is organizing end-to-end analytical work, clarifying responsibilities, and aligning methods, resources, and supporting services. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increasingly affect how analytical work is embedded in standardized, automated, cross-functional workflows. Because the role leads teams and negotiates with system specialists but is not explicitly a workflow architect, relevance is medium.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is materially connected because the role develops and modifies analytical methods and works with system specialists and contractors to deliver projects, but the description does not explicitly assign software/component build responsibility. Evidence includes selecting and evaluating analytical techniques, reviewing and modifying methods and approaches, developing new ones to meet specific needs, negotiating resources and timeframes with system specialists, and leading multidisciplinary project teams. The capability involved is specifying and shaping analytical components that others may implement, and ensuring methods are operationalized. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the importance of reusable analytical services, AI-enabled coding and validation components, and platform-based methods. The role is therefore regularly connected to this subprocess, though not clearly the primary builder.

There is some indirect relevance because the position leads projects, plans and schedules work, negotiates with system specialists, and manages priorities and resources. Those responsibilities can influence how analytical workflows are configured operationally. However, the work description does not explicitly mention configuring systems, transformations, or workflow tools. Future-state drivers around orchestration, automation, and enterprise workflows may affect the role's operating context, especially as analytical work becomes embedded in standardized pipelines. Still, based on supplied evidence, involvement appears limited and indirect.

The role has limited connection to collection setup through advising data suppliers and users, discussing data reporting agreements, and knowledge of respondent relations, confidentiality, and data quality policies. It may influence readiness where analytical requirements affect source arrangements or survey improvements. However, the description does not assign responsibility for training collection staff, configuring collection systems, or operational collection readiness. Future-state shifts toward digital, administrative, and online-first collection may affect the role indirectly through greater interaction with suppliers and source arrangements, but direct relevance remains low.

The work description does not indicate that the Research Analyst runs collection operations. There is some indirect relevance because the role provides advice to data suppliers and users, discusses data reporting agreements, and recommends changes to statistical programs based on analytical findings. Those activities may influence collection practices or supplier interactions. Future-state changes toward administrative and alternative data, online-first collection, and adaptive operations may increase the analytical implications of collection choices for this role, but the supplied evidence does not support direct operational responsibility. Relevance is therefore low.

This is one of the strongest matches. The work description repeatedly emphasizes integrating data from multiple sources and translating them into common concepts. Evidence includes selecting and evaluating methods "to integrate and interpret mass volumes of data," integrating data from financial statements, tax files, administrative sources, surveys and censuses, and making efforts to translate different definitions or concepts into common concepts. It also states there is a requirement to integrate data from diverse sources and concepts into a common conceptual framework and identify complex relationships among variables. The capability involved is multi-source integration, harmonisation, prioritisation, and interpretation. Future-state impacts are substantial from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. These drivers will expand linked, administrative, alternative, geospatial, and metadata-rich integration while increasing privacy, secure-access, and platform requirements. The role already performs the core integration work this subprocess describes.

The work description does not explicitly mention coding text responses or applying statistical classifications as a primary duty. There is some plausible connection because the role integrates data from varied sources using different concepts and classification systems, and requires knowledge of Statistics Canada classification systems. That suggests some involvement in harmonising coded data or interpreting classifications. Future-state drivers such as AI-enabled automated coding and metadata standardization may affect the role indirectly as coding becomes more automated and integrated into analytical workflows. However, without explicit coding responsibility in the supplied description, relevance is low.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role explicitly assesses data quality, comparability, relevance, and inconsistencies. Evidence includes researching gaps and inconsistencies in collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods; interpreting the relative quality of data produced; determining reasons for variances; assessing comparability over time and relevancy in light of changing requirements and socio-economic conditions; and integrating diverse data into common frameworks while identifying subtle relationships. The capability involved is analytical validation of inputs and outputs, including quality assessment across multiple sources. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase automation, heterogeneity, and metadata dependence in validation. Because the role already performs substantive quality interpretation and inconsistency analysis, this subprocess is materially connected.

This subprocess is relevant because the role develops and evaluates analytical methods for handling data quality issues and integrating inconsistent sources, though the description does not explicitly say the incumbent performs editing or imputation operations. Evidence includes modifying methods and approaches, developing new ones to meet specific needs, researching inconsistencies, and selecting techniques to integrate and interpret data from diverse sources with differing concepts. The capability involved is methodological judgment about correcting, reconciling, or replacing problematic data values within broader analytical processes. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will push editing and imputation toward more automated, model-assisted, source-prioritized methods. The role is meaningfully connected through method design and quality improvement, but direct operational editing is not explicit.

This subprocess is relevant because the role conducts modeling studies, integrates diverse data into common conceptual frameworks, identifies complex relationships among variables, and develops new analytical methods to meet specific needs. Those activities often require deriving variables conceptually or analytically, even though the description does not explicitly use the term 'derive new variables and units.' The capability involved is transforming existing data into analytically useful constructs through modeling, integration, and conceptual harmonisation. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase reliance on derived variables from linked, administrative, geospatial, and model-based sources. Because the role already performs advanced modeling and conceptual transformation work, relevance is medium.

The work description shows advanced statistical expertise and method selection responsibilities, so there is some plausible connection to weighting methodologies in analytical studies. However, the supplied information does not explicitly mention weighting, calibration, nonresponse adjustment, or grossing-up. Future modernization of hybrid survey-administrative methods may affect the analytical context in which the role works, but direct responsibility is not evidenced. Relevance is therefore low.

This subprocess is relevant because the role produces estimates, interprets trends and variances, writes analytical papers on survey and project findings, and prepares statistical tables, charts, and explanatory notes for dissemination. The capability involved is transforming processed data into interpretable statistical information, including estimates and aggregate analytical outputs. While the description does not explicitly say the analyst calculates aggregates as a distinct processing step, it clearly involves using and explaining aggregate statistical results. Future-state drivers such as Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will increase automation, timeliness, and granularity of aggregate production, including geospatial and small-area outputs. Because the role uses and communicates aggregate outputs extensively, relevance is medium.

There is limited evidence that the Research Analyst finalizes production data files as a formal processing handoff. The role does work with integrated data, quality assessment, and analytical outputs, so it may depend on or influence readiness of analysis datasets. Future-state drivers around integrated pipelines, metadata-rich assets, and timelier production may affect the role's interaction with finalized datasets. However, the supplied description does not assign responsibility for assembling or packaging final micro- or macro-data files. Relevance is low.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position prepares analytical outputs for publication and dissemination. Evidence includes: "develops and conducts research and modeling studies and writes/edits analytical material for publication purposes," writes analytical papers and articles on interpretation of surveys and project findings, and writes and presents analytical material to audiences ranging from the general public to academics. The role also explains complex data, methods, variances, and trends, and prepares tables, charts, and explanatory notes. The capability involved is transforming analytical results into draft statistical outputs with methodological explanation. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will change how draft outputs are produced, with more automation, richer metadata, more explanation of AI or linked-data methods, and stronger emphasis on timeliness and reusable output packaging. This aligns closely with the role's current responsibilities.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role interprets data quality, reasons for variances, comparability over time, and relevance in changing socio-economic conditions, and writes analytical material explaining results and methods. It also researches inconsistencies and assesses compatibility with other statistical programs. The capability involved is validating whether outputs make sense against expectations, prior knowledge, and methodological understanding. Evidence includes interpreting relative quality of data produced, determining reasons for variances, explaining trends, and assessing impact on the area of specialization. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make output validation more complex because of linked sources, methodological breaks, automated pipelines, and tighter timelines. The role's domain expertise and analytical judgment make this subprocess materially connected.

This subprocess is one of the clearest matches. The work description centers on interpreting and explaining statistical outputs: the analyst writes and presents analytical material, explains complex data and reasons for variances and trends, provides expertise and interpretation to decision-makers across governments, business, social agencies and academia, and writes analytical papers on survey findings and methodology. The role also requires knowledge of emerging socio-economic issues to analyze and interpret data and assess impacts in the area of specialization. The capability involved is substantive interpretation, contextual explanation, and communication of statistical meaning. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need to explain outputs produced from mixed-source, model-based, and AI-assisted methods while maintaining transparency and trust. The evidence in the work description is direct and extensive.

The role has some connection through required knowledge of confidentiality, security, the Statistics Act, the Privacy Act, and the need to ensure no identifying information is released without consent. It also prepares material for dissemination and explains legislative and policy requirements to others. However, the description does not explicitly assign responsibility for applying suppression, perturbation, or formal disclosure control methods. Future-state drivers around privacy, secure access, linked data, and geospatial outputs may increase the importance of confidentiality awareness in the role's work, but direct operational disclosure control is not evidenced. Relevance is low.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role prepares publication-ready analytical material, explanatory notes, tables, charts, and articles, and communicates results to varied audiences while protecting the department's reputation for high-quality data. Evidence includes writing/editing analytical material for publication, presenting analytical material to general and specialized audiences, explaining methods and variances, and knowledge of publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices to establish divisional policies for dissemination products. The capability involved is ensuring outputs are fit for release, properly explained, and aligned with quality, policy, and audience needs. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase demands for caveats, technical notes, metadata completeness, disciplined approvals, and timely release preparation. The role's current publication and explanation responsibilities make this subprocess materially connected.

The role is connected indirectly because it prepares dissemination-ready analytical material and requires knowledge of dissemination policies and practices, but the description does not state responsibility for loading data and metadata into dissemination systems or managing output databases. Future-state metadata-driven and platform-based dissemination may affect how the analyst's outputs are packaged and linked to metadata, yet direct system-update responsibility is not evidenced. Relevance is low.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position produces core dissemination content. Evidence includes writing/editing analytical material for publication, preparing statistical tables, charts, and explanatory notes for dissemination, presenting analytical material to different audiences, and explaining results and methods to maintain the department's reputation. The capability involved is assembling explanatory texts, analytical narratives, and supporting statistical products that meet publication standards and user needs. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will push dissemination toward more digital, metadata-rich, reusable, and partially automated products. The role's existing dissemination responsibilities make this a strong match.

This subprocess is relevant because the role presents and explains released results to the public, specialized users, media, and decision-makers, and must respond when media representatives challenge or misinterpret results. It also provides expertise to governments, business, social agencies, and academics, and participates in meetings and committees to share knowledge and build consensus. The capability involved is supporting release communications, briefings, and interpretation around published outputs, even if the description does not explicitly assign embargo or release scheduling authority. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will make release timing, controlled access, and coordinated communications more disciplined and platform-enabled. Because the role is clearly involved in post-release explanation and stakeholder communication, but not explicitly in release operations management, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role directly provides advice, expertise, interpretation, and consultative services to data suppliers and users. Evidence includes: "provides advice and consultative services to data suppliers and users," provides expertise and interpretation to decision-makers at all levels of government, business, social agencies and academics, adapts complex information into understandable formats, discusses data reporting agreements, and responds when media challenge or misinterpret results. The capability involved is answering user questions, supporting interpretation and access to statistical information, and maintaining relationships with users and suppliers.
