Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the need to harmonize variables across linked and non-survey sources, document derivations more rigorously, and support reuse through standardized metadata. The work description does not show primary questionnaire-variable design responsibility, so relevance is medium rather than high.

This is a major subprocess for the role. The work description shows direct responsibility for designing processing methods, specifications, testing approaches and analytical procedures. Evidence includes: 'Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications,' 'Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs,' 'develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs,' and 'Research and analysis are required to evaluate the effectiveness of processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications, to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria.' The capability involved is designing coding, validation, integration, estimation and processing methodologies and the associated system logic. The role fulfills this need by reviewing processing parameters, classification and coding systems, integrating multiple data sources, and evaluating technical and conceptual problems in manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data. Future-state drivers will strongly reshape this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development all point toward more automated, reusable, metadata-driven and orchestrated processing methods. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase the need to embed secure handling and disclosure-aware controls into processing design. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require more advanced technical skills and stronger oversight of methodological change. This is one of the clearest high-relevance matches.

This subprocess is directly implicated because the role leads development and implementation of statistical processing systems and coordinates staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving data. Evidence includes: 'Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data,' 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems,' and 'Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs.' The capability involved is designing end-to-end production workflows, system interactions, responsibilities, and reusable production arrangements. The role fulfills this need by planning and coordinating project teams, defining objectives and priorities, developing system guidelines, and ensuring compatibility and continuity across programs. Future-state drivers will have cumulative effects here: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all point to more standardized, automated, monitored, reusable and cross-functional workflows with clearer handoffs and fewer manual steps. The work description’s explicit leadership over new or modified processing systems makes this a high-relevance subprocess.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is highly relevant because the role develops specifications, evaluates processing systems, and leads implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems. Evidence includes: 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems,' 'develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs,' and 'Research and analysis are required to evaluate the effectiveness of processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications.' The capability involved is building or reusing processing components such as transformation routines, data compilation programs, workflow tools and related analytical services. The role fulfills this need by translating methodological and operational requirements into system specifications and by overseeing implementation and testing. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push this work toward reusable enterprise components, automated coding and validation services, open and modern tooling, and lower-touch production. The work description strongly supports direct involvement in this subprocess.

This subprocess is relevant because the role not only designs but also implements and operationalizes processing systems and procedures. Evidence includes leadership in 'development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems,' coordination of staff manipulating, storing and retrieving data, and review/approval of detailed processing parameters. The capability involved is configuring workflows, systems and transformations so designed processes operate in practice. The role is relevant because it approves parameters, resolves inconsistencies, and coordinates operational work units. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase the importance of standardized workflow configuration, automated handoffs, secure controls and exception-based operations. The work description does not explicitly mention workflow management systems or direct configuration tooling, so relevance is medium rather than high.

This subprocess is directly relevant. The work description explicitly states that the incumbent develops guidelines for 'design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications,' interprets results of tests and feasibility studies, and 'design[s] and create[s] test procedures and acceptance criteria to ensure that processing systems yield the desired outputs.' The capability involved is technical and operational testing of assembled systems, routines and workflows, including acceptance criteria and suitability for production use. The role fulfills this need by evaluating effectiveness of processing systems, reviewing revised systems for compatibility, and approving detailed processing parameters. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will make testing more complex and more central, with stronger needs for integration testing, secure transmission checks, metadata validation, reusable component assurance and monitoring of automated workflows. This is a strong direct match.

This subprocess is relevant because the role leads implementation of new or modified processing systems and manages staff, training plans and operational readiness. Evidence includes: 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems,' and under leadership, 'develops training plans' and coordinates human resources to meet project objectives. The capability involved is moving systems into production, preparing users, and ensuring operational readiness. The role fulfills this need through implementation leadership, staff coordination, and training-related responsibilities. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and AI and Automation in Statistical Production will increase the importance of user guidance, training, controlled deployment and readiness under tighter timelines and more modern platforms. The work description does not explicitly mention production cutover or user manuals, so relevance is medium.

This subprocess has a plausible but limited connection because the role works with loading, converting, storing and retrieving statistical data from multiple sources after receipt, including administrative and survey inputs. Evidence includes coordination of staff involved in 'manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data' and work on integrating data from 'financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses.' The capability involved is preparing collected data for downstream processing, including format compatibility and continuity. The role is relevant mainly where collection finalization overlaps with post-receipt loading and preparation of incoming files. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion may increase overlap because more external digital sources will require standardized loading, metadata handling and automated handoff. However, the work description does not explicitly assign collection-finalization responsibility, so relevance remains low.

This is one of the strongest subprocess matches. The work description repeatedly emphasizes integration of multiple data sources and ensuring conceptual compatibility. Evidence includes: 'Some studies may involve ... the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses),' 'must be translated into common concepts,' 'integrate conceptually different data from other programs,' and 'recommend changes to other statistical programs.' The capability involved is combining, harmonizing, prioritizing and reconciling data from multiple internal and external sources into coherent statistical outputs. The role fulfills this need directly through database development, source assessment, compatibility review, and specification of data compilation programs. Future-state drivers will intensify this work substantially. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production make integration of administrative, alternative, linked and geospatial data central to production. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase the importance of controlled linkage and de-identification. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will push integration toward scalable, metadata-rich, reusable enterprise pipelines. The evidence is explicit and direct.

This subprocess is relevant because the role reviews and approves classification and coding systems and develops new ones where needed. Evidence includes: 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats or develops new ones to meet specific needs.' The capability involved is applying and governing statistical classifications and coding structures so data can be processed consistently. The role fulfills this need through approval authority over coding systems and through integration work that requires harmonization across sources with different concepts and definitions. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will likely shift this work toward more automated coding, stronger metadata standardization, and reduced clerical effort. The work description does not show routine hands-on coding operations, so relevance is medium rather than high.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role explicitly assesses inconsistencies, technical and conceptual problems, test results and data quality issues. Evidence includes: 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies,' 'assesses technical and conceptual problems and inconsistencies in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data,' and 'Interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations and feasibility studies.' The capability involved is identifying errors, anomalies, incompatibilities and quality issues before or after integration and determining how they should be handled. The role fulfills this need by reviewing systems and data outputs, interpreting preliminary results, and ensuring continuity and compatibility of data. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase automation, exception-based review, multi-source validation complexity and reliance on metadata and quality indicators. The work description’s strong emphasis on data quality, confidentiality and compatibility reinforces the relevance.

This subprocess is relevant because the role devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies and recommends modifications to ensure continuity and compatibility of data. Evidence includes 'devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies' and work involving translation of conceptually different data into common concepts. The capability involved is determining how problematic or inconsistent data should be corrected or replaced so outputs remain coherent and usable. The role fulfills this need at a methodological and supervisory level rather than as a clerical editor, by setting rules and approving approaches for handling inconsistencies in integrated datasets. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will likely move this work toward more automated, source-aware and model-assisted correction methods with stronger metadata and governance requirements. Because the work description does not explicitly mention imputation, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is relevant because the role develops integrated databases and translates data collected for other purposes into common concepts, which often implies deriving comparable variables from heterogeneous inputs. Evidence includes the need to 'translate into common concepts,' integrate conceptually different data from other programs, and develop databases for time-series information and special studies. The capability involved is deriving analytically useful variables and harmonized units from existing source data rather than collecting them directly. The role fulfills this need through conceptual integration, interpretation of preliminary results, and development of data retrieval packages used for integrated statistical information. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will increase reliance on derived variables from linked and administrative sources and require clearer lineage and sequencing. The work description supports this indirectly rather than explicitly, so relevance is medium.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance because the role develops databases for time-series information, interprets preliminary results, and prepares statistical tables and charts for dissemination. These activities imply some involvement with aggregated outputs. The capability involved is producing or working with summarized statistical information for dissemination and analysis. The role is relevant insofar as integrated statistical information and time-series databases depend on aggregate production and interpretation. Future-state drivers such as Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production and automation may change how aggregates are produced and how granular or geospatial outputs are generated, but the work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for aggregate calculation itself. Therefore relevance is low.

This subprocess is relevant because the role brings together results of processing into databases and retrieval packages used for integrated statistical information. Evidence includes: 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information,' 'Interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations and feasibility studies to produce data bases and data retrieval packages used for the production of integrated statistical information,' and coordination of staff manipulating, storing and retrieving data. The capability involved is assembling and preparing coherent datasets and retrieval structures for downstream analysis and dissemination. The role fulfills this need by overseeing data compilation programs, compatibility checks and database development. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase standardization, metadata linkage, automated handoffs and reusable enterprise data assets. The role appears more focused on the substantive and system side of finalization than on purely clerical packaging, so relevance is medium.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the role prepares and explains statistical outputs for users and clients. Evidence includes knowledge of preparing 'statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination,' providing expert advice on 'statistical program results, methods, concepts and techniques,' and writing and presenting subject matter concepts and technical definitions to explain results of studies. The capability involved is transforming processed data into usable outputs with accompanying methodological and explanatory material. The role fulfills this need by interpreting preliminary results, adapting complex information into understandable formats, and supporting dissemination to internal and external users. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase automation of recurring output preparation while also increasing the need for methodological explanation, metadata-rich packaging and transparency about AI- or model-assisted methods. This is a strong direct match.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role interprets preliminary results, explains variances, assesses inconsistencies, and ensures compatibility and quality of outputs. Evidence includes 'interprets preliminary results, reviews and modifies approaches and techniques as necessary,' 'to explain variances,' and 'to resolve differences that can affect ... the quality of outputs.' The capability involved is validating whether outputs are credible, coherent, and fit for use in light of domain knowledge, prior expectations and methodological context. The role fulfills this need by reviewing results, integrating conceptually different data, and providing expert advice to governments, businesses, academics and agencies. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make output validation more complex because outputs will increasingly reflect linked, administrative, geospatial and automated methods. The work description’s emphasis on data quality, interpretation and explanation makes this a high-relevance subprocess.

This subprocess is central to the role. The work description explicitly states that the incumbent 'interprets preliminary results,' 'analyze[s], review[s] and present[s] survey findings,' and 'Provides expert advice and guidance ... on statistical program results, methods, concepts and techniques applied and on trends and developments in economic, sociological or related data programs.' It also notes that this often requires adapting complex information into understandable formats for decision makers. The capability involved is substantive interpretation, explanation of meaning, communication of trends and variances, and contextualization of outputs for users. The role fulfills this need directly through advisory, analytical and communication responsibilities. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need to explain outputs produced from mixed-source, linked and AI-assisted methods, and to communicate methodological changes clearly to maintain trust. This is one of the clearest high-relevance matches.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description places strong emphasis on confidentiality, privacy, security and legal compliance in handling and releasing data. Evidence includes knowledge of 'Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality),' and explicit reference to the Statistics Act and Privacy Act to ensure that neither the incumbent nor subordinates 'release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.' The capability involved is ensuring outputs and stored data comply with confidentiality rules and legal restrictions before dissemination or reuse. The role fulfills this need through policy knowledge, application of confidentiality requirements, and oversight of dissemination practices. Future-state drivers such as Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase disclosure risks, especially for linked and geospatial data and controlled-access outputs, making confidentiality controls more central. The work description does not explicitly mention suppression or perturbation methods, so relevance is medium rather than high.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the role prepares dissemination materials, explanatory notes and technical content, and provides expert interpretation and briefings to users. Evidence includes knowledge of preparing 'statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination,' writing and presenting technical definitions and study results, and providing expert advice to governments, business, agencies and academics. The capability involved is ensuring outputs are fit for release, accompanied by appropriate commentary, caveats, technical notes and supporting information. The role fulfills this need by interpreting results, resolving differences affecting output quality, and communicating methods and findings in understandable terms. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline will increase the need for disciplined release readiness, stronger metadata packaging, clearer caveats for modern methods, and explicit approval trade-offs under constrained resources. The role’s dissemination and advisory responsibilities make this a high-relevance subprocess.

This subprocess is relevant because the role develops and maintains databases used for time-series information and special studies and coordinates staff involved in storing and retrieving statistical data. Evidence includes 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information' and 'Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data.' The capability involved is preparing dissemination-ready data environments and ensuring outputs and metadata are stored and retrievable for release and user access. The role fulfills this need through database development, data retrieval package creation, and oversight of storage and retrieval operations. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase the importance of standardized loading, metadata linkage, secure repositories and automated updates to dissemination systems. The work description does not explicitly mention final dissemination-system loading, so relevance is medium.

This subprocess is directly connected to the role’s title and duties. Evidence includes the position title 'Production and Dissemination Specialist,' knowledge of dissemination policies and practices for preparing 'statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc.,' and communication duties involving writing and presenting technical definitions, explaining study results, and adapting complex information for varied audiences. The capability involved is assembling dissemination products that meet publication standards and user needs. The role fulfills this need by preparing explanatory content, supporting tables and charts, and advising on dissemination practices across divisions and clients. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push this work toward more digital, reusable, metadata-rich and standardized products, while still requiring strong quality statements and explanatory material. This is a strong high-relevance match.

This subprocess is relevant because the role supports dissemination to users and clients and provides expert advice externally, although the work description does not explicitly assign release scheduling or embargo management. Evidence includes providing consultative services to users within and outside Statistics Canada, advising governments and other organizations on program results, and knowledge of dissemination policies and practices. The capability involved is supporting release readiness, user-facing communication and controlled access considerations around dissemination. The role fulfills this need by preparing and explaining outputs and by representing subject matter divisions on projects and committees. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will make release timing, secure access and controlled dissemination more structured and technology-dependent. Because explicit release authority is not stated, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is strongly relevant because the role explicitly provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users and responds to complex information needs from internal and external clients. Evidence includes: 'Provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC,' 'Provides expert advice and guidance to all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics,' and adapting complex information into understandable formats for decision making. The capability involved is responding to user queries, explaining outputs and methods, and supporting access to statistical information. The role fulfills this need directly through advisory, communication and client-facing responsibilities. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will change how support is delivered: more self-service, AI-assisted responses, searchable knowledge resources, and stronger controls for restricted-access requests. The work description provides direct evidence of sustained user-support responsibilities, making this high relevance.

This subprocess is relevant because the role evaluates technological developments, interprets test results and feasibility studies, and prepares reports recommending approaches and guidelines. Evidence includes 'Evaluates the impact of technological developments on respondent operation and production procedures and prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines' and 'Interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations and feasibility studies.' The capability involved is gathering and using evidence on system performance, quality, feasibility and operational impacts to inform improvement. The role fulfills this need by producing evaluative evidence from tests, investigations and operational reviews. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the volume and importance of process metrics, monitoring outputs, staff feedback and efficiency indicators. The role is not framed as a formal evaluator of the whole process, so relevance is medium.

This subprocess is relevant because the role analyzes test and feasibility results, evaluates processing systems and technological developments, and recommends modifications and improvements. Evidence includes 'Research and analysis are required to evaluate the effectiveness of processing systems,' 'Evaluates the impact of technological developments on respondent operation and production procedures and prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines,' and 'recommends modifications and improvements to existing procedures.' The capability involved is synthesizing evidence into judgments about performance, quality, efficiency and future changes. The role fulfills this need by conducting analytical reviews of systems and procedures and by recommending changes based on findings. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make evaluation more dashboard-driven, more focused on efficiency and sustainability, and more attentive to workforce readiness and modernization outcomes. The role contributes materially to evaluation even if it is not the sole owner of enterprise evaluation reports.

This subprocess is relevant because the role not only evaluates and recommends changes but also leads project teams, defines priorities, prepares work plans, and manages implementation of new or modified systems. Evidence includes 'Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources,' 'recommends modifications and improvements to existing procedures,' and 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' The capability involved is turning evaluation findings into prioritized actions, assigning resources, and monitoring implementation. The role fulfills this need by planning projects, setting milestones, negotiating resources and leading implementation work. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make action planning more disciplined, time-bound, resource-constrained and dependent on clear accountability and training support. The work description supports a meaningful but not enterprise-governance-level role in agreeing and executing action plans, so relevance is medium.

This subprocess is relevant because the position helps identify emerging statistical and operational needs for divisional programs. The work description states that the incumbent 'plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs,' 'investigates client requirements for statistical information,' and has 'extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues... to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data.' That is direct evidence of identifying what statistics and services are needed and how needs are changing. The capability involved is strategic program scanning and need identification across users, policy environments and program operations. Future-state drivers make this more consequential: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will force sharper triage of which needs can be pursued, with explicit prioritization under reduced staffing and pressure to find efficiencies through AI, automation, machine learning and new tools and methods. Because the role prepares options and recommendations on new or modified programs and researches trends in mass data processing, it is materially affected by those future need-selection pressures.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position sets and governs program results, quality expectations and resource-constrained delivery choices. Evidence includes 'prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs,' 'reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results,' and 'determines the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied in the development and operation of statistical programs regarding the acquisition, production and dissemination of data.' The capability involved is defining output scope, quality, timeliness and feasibility within legal and resource constraints. The Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline driver is directly relevant because the role already makes recommendations, sets policies and manages trade-offs; future-state accountability, prioritization, cross-field decision-making and transparent trade-offs will intensify how output objectives are narrowed to highest-value outcomes. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment further affects this work because fewer resources and flatter structures will force tighter decisions on scope, service levels and acceptable quality-service trade-offs. The work description's repeated emphasis on proposals, resource implications, quality certification and management of budgets is strong evidence.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position assesses source suitability, integration feasibility, legal constraints and technology implications for statistical programs. Evidence includes reviewing 'the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs,' integrating data from 'financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses,' assessing 'the availability and reliability of new data sources,' investigating 'client requirements for statistical information,' and determining 'the capacity and ability of existing or modified systems to meet these requirements.' The role also requires knowledge of the Statistics Act, Privacy Act, confidentiality, security, and related legislation, which aligns with assessing restrictions on use and legal frameworks. The capability involved is evaluating whether existing and emerging sources can support program needs and how they can be operationalized securely and lawfully. Future-state drivers strongly amplify this work: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increases the importance of assessing administrative and linked sources; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access makes privacy, secure access, authorizations and cyber risk central suitability criteria; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure adds platform, repository and secure-ingestion feasibility; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the importance of metadata quality and interoperability; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production expands assessment to linked, unstructured and geospatial sources; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment pushes lower-cost source substitution. The work description directly supports all of these through source assessment, integration, security and technology review responsibilities.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position prepares proposals, options, recommendations, cost assessments and resource plans for new or modified statistical programs and systems. Evidence includes 'prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs,' 'defines, coordinates and evaluates the cost of statistical system development work,' 'plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes,' and manages budgets, contracts and staffing. The capability involved is translating program needs and design choices into implementable, costed, governable proposals. Future-state drivers materially reshape this work. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline raises the threshold for approval and requires clearer accountability and explicit trade-offs. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline means proposals must be more milestone-based, implementation-ready and tied to fixed timelines. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment makes savings, automation, reuse and affordability central approval criteria. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development mean business cases must increasingly justify alignment to enterprise platforms, reusable components, secure environments and long-term supportability. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is also relevant because the role manages staff, training plans and contractors, so future business cases will need to account for reskilling, leadership capacity and workforce adjustment pressures. The work description provides direct evidence of proposal development, costing, budgeting, contracting and implementation planning.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position is explicitly responsible for production and dissemination and for designing the systems and processes that support outputs. Evidence includes the title 'Head, Production and Dissemination,' responsibility to 'determine the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied in the development and operation of statistical programs regarding the acquisition, production and dissemination of data,' and to 'write and present subject matter and technical concepts... to explain and clarify developmental projects and operational systems and processes or program results.' The role also provides expert advice on program results and their interpretation. The capability involved is designing dissemination-ready outputs, associated systems, procedures and quality framing. Future-state drivers materially affect this work: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access strengthens secure-by-design dissemination and confidential output access; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure pushes platform-based, digital-first dissemination; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the need for metadata-rich, searchable outputs; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment pushes standardization and lower-cost digital products; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity affects how outputs are designed for accessibility, usability and staff operability. The work description's direct focus on dissemination systems and program results makes this a strong match.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position designs and governs statistical systems, methods and processes used in production. Evidence includes 'plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes,' 'develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes,' 'determines the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied,' and requires 'advanced knowledge of systems analysis and design.' The research and analysis section also shows assessment of new statistical methods, techniques, hardware and software, and analysis of data quality and comparability. The capability involved is specifying processing, integration, validation and analytical approaches for statistical production. Future-state drivers strongly affect this work: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modular Architecture and Operational Efficiency all point toward more automated, reusable, metadata-driven and integrated processing designs. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access is also relevant because the role establishes security and confidentiality procedures and must ensure protected handling of data and systems. The work description directly evidences methodological, systems and quality design responsibilities.

This is one of the most directly relevant subprocesses. The position leads the design, development and operation of statistical production and dissemination systems and manages units and project teams involved in systems design. Evidence includes 'plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes,' 'manages a unit and project teams involved in systems design,' 'develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes,' and 'advanced knowledge of systems analysis and design... to establish and manage mass statistical data collection, production and dissemination environments.' The capability involved is end-to-end workflow and production architecture design, including staff roles, systems, databases, controls and reuse. Future-state drivers cumulatively make this central: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all directly reshape how production workflows are designed, standardized, secured, monitored and staffed. The work description's emphasis on systems design leadership, policy setting, resource management and technology trend analysis is direct evidence.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because the position manages development work for statistical systems and processes and defines specifications for internal service areas, outside agencies and contractors. Evidence includes 'defines processing and production specifications and guidelines for the contracting of development work,' 'plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes,' and 'negotiates cost reductions and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services.' The capability involved is overseeing the build or reuse of processing-related components through design specifications, contracting and project management rather than hands-on coding. Future-state drivers such as Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modular Architecture and Operational Efficiency will increase reuse expectations, enterprise component adoption and automation. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity also matters because the role manages staffing and training plans for teams operating in these environments. Relevance is medium because the work description clearly governs and manages component development, but does not state direct technical build activity by the incumbent.

This subprocess is relevant because the position leads dissemination systems and processes and manages development work affecting dissemination products and services. Evidence includes the position title, responsibility for 'statistical production and dissemination systems,' and authority to define specifications and contract development work for production and dissemination applications. The capability involved is directing and governing the build or reuse of dissemination-enabling components, including systems and services used to deliver outputs. Future-state drivers such as Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Modular Architecture will increasingly push reusable, secure, metadata-rich dissemination components. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will also favour standardized components over bespoke builds. Relevance is medium because the role clearly manages and specifies dissemination system development, but the description does not explicitly say the incumbent personally builds components.

This subprocess is relevant because the position oversees implementation and operation of statistical systems and processes and manages project teams in systems design. Evidence includes 'plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes' and 'manages a unit and leads project teams for special projects.' The capability involved is ensuring designed workflows are operationalized through coordinated systems, priorities, staffing and contracted work. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance and Operational Efficiency will make workflow configuration more standardized, automated and tightly governed. The role's responsibility for resolving conflicting priorities, determining objectives and priorities, and managing implementation supports relevance, though the description does not explicitly mention hands-on workflow configuration, so medium is appropriate.

This subprocess is relevant because the position is accountable for quality and completeness of program results and for evaluating systems and processes. Evidence includes 'reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results,' 'develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes,' and assesses new hardware, software, methods and their impacts. The capability involved is assuring that assembled systems and routines are fit for operational use and produce acceptable results. Future-state drivers such as Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modular Architecture increase the importance of integration testing, secure transmission checks, validation of reused components and end-to-end coherence. Relevance is medium because the role clearly governs evaluation and quality certification, but the description does not explicitly assign direct system test execution.

This subprocess is relevant because the position manages implementation, staff, budgets, training plans and operational readiness for statistical systems and processes. Evidence includes planning and controlling implementation and operation of systems, managing human resources, approving training plans, and establishing policies and procedures for security, confidentiality and system protection. The capability involved is moving designed and built systems into sustainable operation with appropriate procedures, staffing and controls. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modular Architecture will increase the importance of documentation, training, secure deployment and production supportability. Relevance is medium because the role clearly manages readiness and operations, though the description does not explicitly mention final production cutover activities.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance because the role establishes and manages mass statistical data collection environments and determines methods for acquisition of data, but the description is not collection-operations focused. Evidence includes determining practices for 'acquisition, production and dissemination of data' and advanced knowledge to establish and manage 'mass statistical data collection, production and dissemination environments.' The capability involved is higher-level oversight of collection-related systems and readiness rather than direct setup of collection staff, devices or respondent materials. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Workforce Skills Transition may affect the role indirectly through system readiness, secure intake and training implications. Relevance remains low because direct collection setup responsibilities are not explicitly described.

This subprocess is only weakly connected. The role influences acquisition methods and mass data environments, but the work description does not assign direct responsibility for live collection operations, respondent follow-up or supplier management during collection. Evidence is limited to determining methods for 'acquisition' of data and managing mass data collection environments. The capability involved is strategic and systems-level oversight rather than operational collection execution. Future-state drivers such as online-first collection, administrative data acquisition and automation may indirectly affect the role through program redesign and system implications, but the supplied work description does not support stronger relevance.

This subprocess has limited relevance because the role oversees systems and processes that span acquisition through dissemination, but there is no explicit responsibility for loading collected data, archiving instruments or pseudonymisation at collection close. Evidence is indirect: the incumbent determines methods and practices for acquisition, production and dissemination and manages statistical systems. Future-state drivers around automated ingestion, metadata handling, secure loading and integrated pipelines may affect the role through system design and governance, but the work description does not explicitly place the incumbent in collection finalization operations.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the work description explicitly emphasizes integrating data from multiple sources and translating them into common concepts. Evidence includes 'integrate conceptually different data from other programs,' use of 'financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses,' and the need to translate source data 'into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the result on other statistical programs.' The capability involved is multi-source integration, harmonisation, conceptual alignment and stewardship across programs. Future-state drivers strongly intensify this work: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion makes integration central; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access raises controlled linkage and de-identification requirements; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure enables larger-scale integration; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration embeds integration in automated flows; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability strengthens interoperability; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production makes integrated reusable datasets core to production. The work description provides direct evidence of integration responsibilities and cross-program impacts.

This subprocess has plausible but limited relevance. The role determines methods and practices for statistical programs and has broad systems and methodological authority, but the description does not explicitly mention coding operations or classification assignment. There is contextual knowledge of classification systems and mass data processing methods, which suggests awareness of coding frameworks. Future-state drivers such as AI-enabled automated coding, metadata standardization and operational efficiency may affect the role indirectly through policy, technology recommendations and system design decisions. However, because no direct coding responsibility is stated, relevance is low.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position is directly accountable for assessing data quality, comparability, variances and completeness of results. Evidence includes 'reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results,' 'analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance,' and researches gaps and inconsistencies in production and dissemination methods. The capability involved is validation of inputs and outputs, quality assurance, discrepancy investigation and stewardship of statistical integrity. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Modern Statistical Methods and Operational Efficiency all increase the need for scalable, automated and metadata-aware validation with stronger exception handling. The work description's repeated emphasis on quality analysis and certification is direct evidence.

This subprocess has limited relevance. The role oversees methods, systems and quality, so it may influence editing and imputation approaches through methodological and systems decisions, but the work description does not explicitly mention editing, imputation or correction of records. Future-state drivers around automation, advanced methods and source substitution may affect the role indirectly through design and governance of processing methods. Because the supplied evidence does not identify direct responsibility for edit-and-impute operations, relevance is low.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description shows responsibility for integrating different sources, translating concepts and adapting conceptual frameworks, all of which support derivation of variables and analytical constructs. Evidence includes translating source data 'into common concepts,' integrating conceptually different data from other programs, and reviewing conceptual frameworks for development, modification and adaptation. The capability involved is conceptual and methodological transformation of source data into usable statistical constructs. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Integrated Data Pipelines increase reliance on derived variables from linked and administrative sources and require clearer lineage and sequencing. Relevance is medium because the role clearly influences derivation logic at a program-method level, though direct derivation execution is not explicitly stated.

This subprocess has only limited relevance. The role has broad methodological oversight and assesses statistical methods, but the work description does not explicitly mention weighting, calibration or non-response adjustment. Future-state modernization of survey methods and hybrid data models may affect the role indirectly through program redesign and methodological recommendations. However, without explicit evidence of weighting responsibilities, relevance remains low.

This subprocess is relevant because the position is responsible for certifying program results, explaining findings, and ensuring high-quality outputs used in policy and decision making. Evidence includes reviewing and certifying overall quality and completeness of results, explaining statistical program findings and their practical application, and defending the validity of statistical methods and approaches used. The capability involved is stewardship of aggregate outputs and their quality, interpretation and readiness for use. Future-state drivers such as Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will increasingly automate and diversify aggregate production, including more granular and geospatial outputs. Relevance is medium because the role is clearly accountable for aggregate results and their interpretation, though not explicitly for performing aggregation calculations.

This subprocess is relevant because the position oversees end-to-end statistical systems and certifies the quality and completeness of program results that depend on coherent final datasets. Evidence includes planning and controlling operation of systems and processes, evaluating systems and processes, and reviewing overall quality and completeness of results. The capability involved is governance of the final processing handoff into analysis-ready outputs. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Agility and Modern Statistical Methods will make standardized, metadata-rich, timely final datasets more central. Relevance is medium because the role governs and assures these outputs, though the description does not explicitly mention file assembly.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position is directly responsible for production and dissemination and for communicating program findings and technical concepts. Evidence includes providing expert advisory services on program results, explaining and elaborating on statistical findings and their interpretation, and writing and presenting technical concepts and program results in common terminology. The capability involved is transforming processed statistical results into usable outputs with supporting explanation. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, and Modern Statistical Methods will increase the need for methodological notes, metadata-rich packaging and explanation of AI-assisted or mixed-source outputs. The work description strongly supports direct involvement in preparing and framing outputs for users.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position explicitly validates and certifies outputs and analyzes their quality, comparability and relevance. Evidence includes 'reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results,' analyzes 'relative quality,' determines reasons for variances, reviews comparability over time and relevance in light of trends and changing requirements, and defends the validity of methods when findings are challenged. The capability involved is domain-informed output validation against expectations, prior results and methodological standards. Future-state drivers such as Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Operational Efficiency all increase the need for stronger benchmark comparison, metadata review, quality indicators and risk-based validation. The work description provides direct evidence of this responsibility.

This subprocess is highly relevant because interpreting and explaining outputs is a core stated responsibility. Evidence includes providing expert advisory and consultative services to governments, business, social agencies and academia; explaining findings and their practical application and interpretation; writing and presenting technical concepts in common terminology; and defending the validity of statistical methods and approaches when findings are challenged or misinterpreted. The capability involved is substantive interpretation, communication and contextual explanation of statistical outputs. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need to explain outputs produced from mixed-source, automated and model-based methods while maintaining public trust and clear communication. This is one of the clearest matches in the work description.

This subprocess is relevant because the position establishes policies and procedures for security and confidentiality and has explicit knowledge requirements related to the Statistics Act, Privacy Act and confidentiality of data. Evidence includes 'establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data and the maintenance and protection of computer systems, equipment, databases and files' and contextual knowledge of confidentiality, security and legislative requirements to ensure no identifying information is released improperly. The capability involved is governance of confidentiality protection and secure handling of outputs and data assets. Future-state drivers such as Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Administrative and Linked Data Expansion increase disclosure risk and make secure access, privacy controls and output checking more important. Relevance is medium because the role clearly governs confidentiality and security, though the description does not explicitly mention applying statistical disclosure control techniques.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position certifies results, prepares and communicates supporting interpretation, and participates in expert and governance discussions around outputs. Evidence includes reviewing and certifying quality and completeness of results, writing and presenting technical concepts and program results, defending methods and findings, and chairing or participating in meetings to develop understanding and consensus. The capability involved is ensuring outputs are fit for use, properly caveated and supported by interpretation and technical explanation before release. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Modern Statistical Methods will increase pressure for disciplined sign-off, stronger metadata and caveats, and clearer explanation of modern methods. The work description strongly supports this role in final output readiness.

This subprocess is relevant because the position manages dissemination systems and the operation of statistical systems and processes that support outputs. Evidence includes responsibility for 'statistical production and dissemination systems,' planning and controlling operation of systems and processes, and establishing security and confidentiality procedures for databases and files. The capability involved is ensuring dissemination-supporting systems are operational, controlled and aligned with output requirements. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase the importance of standardized loading, metadata linkage and secure output-system updates. Relevance is medium because the role governs these systems, though direct loading activity is not explicitly stated.

This subprocess is highly relevant because dissemination is central to the position. Evidence includes the title 'Head, Production and Dissemination,' responsibility for methods and practices related to dissemination of data, expert advisory services on program results, and communication responsibilities to explain findings and maintain the department's reputation for high-quality data. The capability involved is assembling and assuring dissemination products and their explanatory content. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will push more digital, reusable, metadata-rich and standardized dissemination products with stronger explanatory and quality statements. The work description directly supports strong relevance.

This subprocess is relevant because the position is accountable for dissemination results, external communication and maintaining trust in released outputs. Evidence includes explaining findings to external users, defending validity of results when challenged, and participating in interdepartmental meetings and groups to build understanding and consensus. The capability involved is supporting release readiness, external briefings and controlled communication of official outputs. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Metadata-Driven Data Management will affect release timing, secure access, embargo-like controls and release governance. Relevance is medium because the role clearly supports and influences release, though explicit release scheduling or embargo management is not stated.

This subprocess is relevant because the position provides expert advisory and consultative services to a wide range of users inside and outside Statistics Canada and explains findings and methods to support their use. Evidence includes 'provides expert advisory and consultative services to users within and outside Statistics Canada,' and to policy makers, business, social agencies and academia; explains findings, practical application and interpretation; and participates in meetings to share knowledge and build understanding. The capability involved is responding to user needs, clarifying outputs and supporting informed use of statistical products. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment suggest more self-service, chatbot-enabled and metadata-supported user support, while mixed-source outputs will generate more methodological questions. Relevance is medium because user support is clearly part of the role, though not framed as a formal service desk or access-request function.

This subprocess is relevant because the position researches trends, analyzes quality and variances, investigates gaps and inconsistencies, and uses client requirements and program evidence to inform change. Evidence includes researching trends and developments in data processing, analyzing relative quality and comparability, researching gaps and inconsistencies in methods and procedures, and investigating client requirements. The capability involved is gathering and interpreting evidence about program performance, quality and changing needs. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the volume and importance of process metrics, staff feedback, quality indicators and operational evidence. Relevance is medium because the role clearly gathers and uses evaluative evidence, though the description does not explicitly mention formal evaluation reporting inputs.

This subprocess is relevant because the position evaluates systems, methods, technologies, costs, quality and program impacts, and recommends changes to management. Evidence includes evaluating cost of system development work, assessing new methods and technologies and their short- and long-term impacts and benefits, analyzing quality and comparability, and recommending changes to management and other statistical programs. The capability involved is synthesizing evidence into judgments about program effectiveness, quality and future change. Future-state drivers such as Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Governance and Workforce Skills Transition will make evaluation more dashboard-driven and more focused on efficiency, modernization outcomes, workforce readiness and sustainability. Relevance is medium because evaluation is clearly embedded in the role, though not described as a formal end-of-cycle evaluation function.

This subprocess is relevant because the position has decision-making authority, prepares recommendations, manages resources and teams, and recommends changes based on analysis and evaluation. Evidence includes preparing proposals with options and recommendations, determining objectives and priorities, managing budgets and staff, recommending changes to management and other programs, and participating in or leading task forces and committees. The capability involved is turning evaluation and strategic analysis into prioritized actions with accountable implementation. Future-state drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make action planning more explicit, resource-constrained, milestone-based and leadership-dependent. Relevance is medium because the role clearly has the authority and responsibility to shape action plans, though the description does not explicitly use that term.

Positions.Branch/Division: Strategic Analysis, Publication, and Training (SAPT) Division

implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it concerns the design of statistical methodology, validation, coding, integration and analysis approaches, and the position provides training and subject-matter support on exactly those kinds of business practices and methodologies. The capability involved is methodological understanding, interpretation of business and survey practices, and the ability to explain and troubleshoot how methods are applied in practice. The work description states that the incumbent provides 'technical subject matter expertise and coaching support to course participants,' applies judgment on 'the interpretation of various methodologies applied in “live” case scenarios,' and conducts 'research and analysis of changes to Survey, Subject Matter and Statistical learning programs-related business practices.' That means the role does not design production methods directly, but it regularly supports staff capability to understand and apply them. Future-state drivers make this more important: Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all increase the complexity of processing and analysis methods and the need for staff training, technical support, and upskilling. The work description explicitly aligns with those workforce implications through ongoing coaching, adapting training to different knowledge levels, updating materials to reflect current practices, and working with subject-matter resources 'in the design of new products to reflect changes to business practices.'

This subprocess is materially connected because it includes how staff interact with systems and workflows and who is responsible for what and when, and this position is focused on translating Statistics Canada business practices into training, coaching, and learning tools that support those operational roles. The capability involved is workforce enablement for production workflows: clarifying responsibilities, supporting adoption of current practices, and maintaining training products that reflect operational changes. Evidence in the work description includes ensuring that 'training text, handouts, simulation exercises and testing tools reflect current business policies and practices,' monitoring deficiencies, and in complex situations working with subject matter resources in the 'design of new products to reflect changes to business practices.' The role also requires knowledge of 'TDL’s mandate, strategic objectives, business plans, organization, and accountability framework' to transpose technical knowledge into adult learning methodologies. Future drivers strongly affect this work even if the role is not itself designing enterprise workflows: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all change staff-system interaction, role clarity, exception handling, and training needs. The cumulative effect is that training content, simulations, and coaching will need to evolve toward more automated, platform-based, and standardized workflows, with stronger emphasis on role clarity, digital readiness, and support for staff transition.

This is one of the most directly implicated subprocesses because it explicitly includes producing documentation, user manuals, and training users on how to operate the process, which closely matches the core duties in the work description. The capability involved is operational training, documentation maintenance, coaching, and readiness support for users of statistical business processes. The work description provides strong evidence: the incumbent mentors and coaches course participants in day-to-day classroom and group training activities; develops, adapts and drafts training materials and tools; ensures training texts, handouts, simulation exercises and testing tools reflect current business policies and practices; identifies performance gaps; and develops and recommends coaching and training plans. The role also studies changes to business practices continually to provide 'up-to-date and accurate information to staff.' Future-state drivers intensify this connection. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is especially relevant because training is explicitly part of this subprocess and the role directly delivers that function. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production all imply more documentation, user guidance, and training as systems become more automated, digital, and methodologically complex. The workforce implications in the GSBPM records—upskilling, supporting employees through transitions, providing tools and training, and helping staff operate modernized environments—map directly to this position's responsibilities.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes training activities and readiness preparation for collection-related processes, and the position supports staff capability in survey, subject matter, and statistical learning programs. The capability involved is preparing staff to operate according to current business practices and methodologies, including troubleshooting and adapting learning to participant needs. The work description shows direct relevance through 'technical subject matter expertise and coaching support to course participants,' knowledge of 'Survey development,' knowledge of training delivery methods to determine training needs, and research on changes to survey-related business practices. Although the role does not run collection operations, it supports the human readiness component that this subprocess depends on. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will change collection setup through online-first, digital tools, APIs, mixed-source operations, and new staff skill requirements. That means this role's training materials, simulations, and coaching will likely need to cover more digital collection practices, source-management concepts, and updated confidentiality or operational procedures as business practices evolve.
