This subprocess has a plausible but limited connection because the role supports learning on survey, subject matter, and statistical business practices, and data integration is one of the increasingly important practices staff may need to understand. The capability involved is not direct integration work, but training and methodological interpretation that helps course participants understand evolving production practices. Evidence is indirect but present: the incumbent provides subject matter expertise on 'Business and Economic development, Survey development,' researches changes to business practices, and offers guidance on atypical methodological issues arising in live case scenarios. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity suggest that integration-heavy production will require more staff learning and adaptation. However, the work description does not state that the position performs or manages integration itself, so relevance remains low.

This subprocess is relevant only to a limited extent. The role does not classify or code data directly, but it does provide methodological coaching and training support that could include explaining current coding-related business practices where they are part of survey or statistical learning programs. The capability involved is instructional support for methodological application and troubleshooting. Evidence from the work description includes providing guidance on methodologies in live case scenarios, researching atypical issues, and ensuring training tools reflect current business policies and practices. Future drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity indicate that coding work will become more automated and staff will need new skills and explanations. That means the role may be affected through updated training content and coaching needs, but there is no direct responsibility for coding operations in the supplied work description.

This subprocess is materially connected because the role supports staff understanding of methodologies, compliance, troubleshooting, and quality assurance concepts that are central to review and validation. The capability involved is teaching and coaching staff to recognize problems, apply methodologies correctly, and respond to issues encountered in practice. The work description explicitly states that judgment is required 'to track and evaluate problems encountered, to ensure compliance to methodologies and to recommend solutions to resolve these issues,' and that the incumbent conducts 'monitoring and quality assurance exercises to ensure compliance.' It also notes analytical and problem-solving knowledge used 'to research, analyze and resolve interpretation problems.' Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the complexity of validation environments and shift staff work toward exception handling and quality oversight. This position is relevant because it helps build that capability through coaching, adapted learning sessions, and updated training materials.

This subprocess has limited relevance because the role sits in the Strategic Analysis, Publication, and Training Division and includes writing, reporting, and methodological explanation, but the work description does not say the incumbent prepares statistical outputs for release. The capability involved is communication and preparation of explanatory materials rather than direct output production. Evidence includes writing skills to 'develop, adapt and draft training materials and tools' and 'prepare reports and correspondence,' plus participation in case studies and responses to methodological questions. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity may increase the need for clearer explanatory materials and methodological notes in training contexts. Still, because the work description focuses on training rather than statistical output preparation, relevance is low.

This subprocess is relevant because a central part of the role is explaining methodologies, business practices, and case scenarios to course participants, which is closely aligned with the interpretive and explanatory capability needed when staff must understand statistical results and how they were produced. The capability involved is analytical interpretation, communication, and contextual explanation. The work description states that the incumbent provides subject matter expertise on the 'interpretation and application of these business practices,' mentors and coaches participants throughout the course, adapts communication style to different knowledge levels, and responds to questions on methodologies. It also requires knowledge of Statistics Canada's mandate and business practices so training programs accurately reflect them. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make outputs harder to interpret because of mixed sources, advanced methods, and AI-assisted processes. This role is therefore meaningfully affected as training and coaching will need to help staff explain and understand increasingly complex outputs and methods.

This subprocess is materially connected because the role provides ongoing coaching, responds to participant concerns and information requests, and adapts support to different knowledge levels, which is functionally similar to structured user support in a learning and internal service context. The capability involved is responsive support, communication, knowledge transfer, and issue resolution. Evidence from the work description includes mentoring and coaching participants in day-to-day activities, responding to questions on methodologies, writing responses to concerns and information requests from course participants, and identifying and analyzing coaching and training needs. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity suggest support models will become more digital, self-serve, and knowledge-base oriented, while staff still need expert escalation support for complex issues. This position is relevant because it already performs a human support and coaching function that will likely evolve as tools, methods, and service expectations change.

This subprocess is relevant because the role monitors participant performance, identifies deficiencies, tracks problems encountered, and contributes evidence that could inform evaluation of training effectiveness and business-practice adoption. The capability involved is gathering operational feedback, identifying gaps, and documenting issues for improvement. The work description states that the incumbent 'monitors and identifies performance gaps,' is responsible for 'recording and following up on deficiencies,' tracks and evaluates problems encountered, and conducts monitoring and quality assurance exercises. Those are evaluation inputs even if the role is not formally conducting enterprise evaluations. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity increase the importance of continuous feedback, adoption metrics, and staff-readiness evidence. This role is relevant because it sits close to the workforce capability layer and generates practical evidence on where staff struggle, what training needs exist, and how business-practice changes are being absorbed.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance because the role performs monitoring, quality assurance, and analysis of changes to business practices, which can contribute to evaluative thinking about training effectiveness and methodological compliance. The capability involved is analytical review and synthesis of observed issues rather than formal program evaluation. Evidence includes conducting 'research and analysis of changes,' monitoring and quality assurance exercises, tracking and evaluating problems encountered, and recommending solutions. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase pressure to assess whether training and coaching are effectively supporting modernization. However, the work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for producing evaluation reports or dashboards, so relevance remains low.

This subprocess is only weakly connected. The role identifies deficiencies, recommends coaching and training plans, and works with subject matter resources to adjust training products, which resembles localized action planning for learning improvements. The capability involved is recommending corrective actions and supporting follow-up on identified gaps. Evidence includes developing and recommending coaching and training plans, recording and following up on deficiencies, and working with subject matter resources in the design of new products to reflect changes to business practices. Future-state drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity may increase the need for disciplined prioritization of training responses and clearer ownership of workforce adaptation actions. Still, the work description does not indicate that the incumbent has formal decision-making authority to agree enterprise action plans, so relevance is low.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns identifying what statistics are needed and understanding user requirements and external developments. The position directly supports this through outreach, collaboration, and expert advice to understand user needs and economic trends. The work description states the incumbent is 'Responsible for outreach and collaboration with a variety of stakeholders ... to establish relationships to leverage new methods and data sources, understand user needs and keep abreast of economic trends and developments, and providing expert advice and analysis.' That is direct evidence of identifying emerging needs and scanning the environment. Future-state impacts are significant under Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment: with fewer staff, flatter structures, and stronger prioritization, this role will likely face greater pressure to triage needs, identify which demands can be met through lower-cost methods, and use AI, automation, machine learning, and new tools and methods to assess feasibility. Because the role already leads research/analysis and engages stakeholders to leverage new methods and data sources, it is materially connected to how needs will be identified and narrowed in the future.

This subprocess is about defining the statistical outputs required to meet confirmed user needs, including trade-offs among scope, quality, timeliness and resources. The position is materially connected because it manages and leads work that determines what analytical, dissemination and visualization products will be produced and how projects respond to user needs. Evidence includes: 'Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products,' and 'Leads complex projects ... to respond to user needs; develops mitigation strategies to address delays and briefs senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary.' This shows responsibility for shaping outputs and adjusting objectives when constraints arise. Future changes are driven by Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. Those drivers will increase explicit trade-offs, accountability, and prioritization of highest-value outputs under scarce resources and reduced staffing. The role's existing responsibility to brief senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary indicates direct involvement in transparent trade-offs and disciplined objective-setting.

This is one of the most directly implicated subprocesses. It concerns assessing whether existing data sources, including administrative, alternative and linked data, can meet user requirements and under what legal, technical and operational conditions. The position directly performs this kind of work. Evidence includes: 'Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs'; 'Participates in or leads data acquisition negotiations'; and stakeholder outreach 'to establish relationships to leverage new methods and data sources.' These are core source assessment, acquisition and suitability activities. The capability involved includes evaluating source fitness, negotiating access, understanding user needs, and managing integration feasibility. Future-state impacts are substantial and cumulative. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion is highly relevant because the role already works with alternative data sources, acquisition, integration and linkage. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase scrutiny of privacy, secure access, authorizations and legal conditions for source use. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will make platform fit, centralized repositories, secure ingestion and scalable infrastructure more central to source decisions. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the importance of metadata quality and interoperability in source assessment. Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will expand expectations around linked data environments, unstructured-source extraction, integrated pipelines and enterprise-scale reuse. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will further push this role toward lower-cost reusable sources and away from labour-intensive approaches. The work description provides direct evidence that this role fulfills the operational need for source evaluation and acquisition.

This subprocess concerns documenting options, costs, benefits, risks, timelines and resource implications for new or modified statistical processes and supporting go/no-go decisions. The work description does not explicitly say the incumbent prepares formal business cases, so relevance is not High. However, the role materially contributes to the substance that would feed such cases. Evidence includes: 'Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs; develops mitigation strategies to address delays and briefs senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary.' This indicates responsibility for project scope, risk, mitigation, schedule impacts and briefing senior management—key inputs to business-case style decisions. The role also 'Manages activities' involving implementation of tools/software and ensures quality and completeness of results, which supports option appraisal and implementation planning. Future-state drivers increase this connection: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will require clearer milestones, implementation readiness and risk management; Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline will raise approval thresholds and require explicit trade-offs; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will foreground savings, staffing assumptions and automation-enabled operating models; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make training, reskilling and readiness more central. The role is therefore a meaningful contributor to this subprocess even if not explicitly the approval owner.

This subprocess covers detailed design of statistical outputs, products and services to be disseminated. The position is directly connected because it manages preparation of dissemination and visualization products and authors analytical material supporting dissemination. Evidence includes: 'Manages activities related to ... the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products' and 'Authors analytical papers and other types of material supporting data development and dissemination.' The capability involved includes translating analytical results into usable outputs, designing products that meet user needs, and ensuring quality and completeness. Future-state impacts are meaningful. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will require outputs to be more metadata-rich, standardized and discoverable. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will push output design toward platform-based, digital-first and reusable dissemination patterns. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase attention to secure access and privacy-aware design where outputs may involve sensitive content. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will encourage standardization and lower-cost reusable products. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need for outputs and dissemination procedures that staff can operate and explain using modern digital and analytical tools. The work description directly supports this subprocess through both management and production of dissemination outputs.

This subprocess concerns defining collected and derived variables, classifications and metadata needed for downstream processing. The work description does not explicitly mention variable design, so relevance is not High. However, the role's responsibilities in data integration, manipulation, analytics, linkage and alternative data use imply meaningful involvement in shaping how variables from multiple sources are harmonized and used. Evidence includes managing 'data integration, data manipulation, data analytics' and leading projects involving 'integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources.' Those activities regularly require determining how source variables align, what derived variables are needed, and how data from different sources can be made analytically usable. Future-state drivers strengthen this connection: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increases the need to redefine variables around sourced, linked and derived data; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the importance of standardized variable metadata; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increases emphasis on variables designed for linkage, derivation and automated processing. The role is therefore materially affected by this subprocess even if not explicitly the formal designer of variables.

This subprocess concerns designing collection strategies and acquisition mechanisms, including administrative and alternative data transfer methods and agreements. The position is not described as designing survey instruments, but it is materially connected to non-survey collection and source acquisition design. Evidence includes leading projects involving 'data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources,' participating in or leading 'data acquisition negotiations,' and collaborating with stakeholders to leverage 'new methods and data sources.' These responsibilities align with designing or shaping acquisition approaches, agreements and source onboarding for non-survey data. Future-state impacts are important: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will further reorient collection toward administrative registers, linked data, alternative feeds and online-first residual collection; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase requirements around secure transfer, APIs, agreements and confidentiality; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will shape feasible acquisition modes and integration methods; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase hybrid acquisition and adaptive source use. The role is therefore a regular contributor to collection design for alternative and acquired data sources.

This subprocess designs the methodology for coding, editing, imputation, integration, validation and estimation used in processing and analysis. The position is directly implicated because it manages data integration, manipulation, analytics, processing and analysis activities, leads implementation of tools/software, and ensures quality and completeness of results. Evidence includes: 'Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis ... implementation of various tools or software, and ensuring overall quality and completeness of program results.' This is direct evidence of responsibility for how processing and analysis are operationalized. The role also leads complex projects involving acquisition, integration and linkage, which are central design considerations in this subprocess. Future-state impacts are extensive and cumulative. AI and Automation in Statistical Production will reshape coding, validation and analytical routines; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase the need for methodologies for integrating heterogeneous sources and linked data; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will require methods to be specified as automatable pipeline steps; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata an operational input to processing; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will expand advanced methods, linkage-based integration and automated workflows; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward automation and sustainable methods with fewer staff; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require stronger analytical expertise and training. This is a core subprocess for the role.

This subprocess determines the end-to-end workflow from collection through dissemination, reuse of systems and services, and how staff interact with systems and responsibilities. The position is materially connected because it manages integrated analytical and dissemination activities, leads implementation of tools/software, supervises teams, and ensures quality and completeness across projects. Evidence includes managing 'data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products,' leading 'implementation of various tools or software,' and 'Supervises directly or in a matrix environment to plan and coordinate teams responsible for statistical outputs or projects.' This shows responsibility for cross-step workflow coordination, staff interaction with systems, and operational delivery. Future-state impacts are especially strong from Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. These drivers collectively point to more automated, reusable, monitored, secure and lean workflows, with staff shifting toward supervision, exception handling, orchestration and cross-functional coordination. Because the role already manages integrated production activities and teams, it is highly relevant.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess covers reusing or building components needed for processing and analysis, including transformation functions, workflow tools, dashboards and metadata services. The position is directly connected because it manages processing, analytics and tool/software implementation. Evidence includes responsibility for 'data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis' and 'implementation of various tools or software.' That is direct evidence of building, adapting or deploying processing and analysis capabilities. Future-state impacts are strong: AI and Automation in Statistical Production will increase reusable AI-enabled coding, validation and analytical components; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will require linkage, harmonisation and geospatial services; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will shift components onto shared platforms and cloud environments; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will require modular pipeline-ready components; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase demand for metadata services; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will expand advanced analytical and linkage components; Modular Architecture and Operational Efficiency drivers will push reuse over bespoke builds. The role's current implementation and management responsibilities make this subprocess highly relevant.

This subprocess configures workflows, systems and transformations from collection through dissemination. The work description does not explicitly say the incumbent configures workflow systems, but the role materially contributes through implementation of tools/software, management of integrated processing and dissemination activities, and coordination of teams. Evidence includes 'implementation of various tools or software,' managing activities spanning integration through dissemination products, and supervising teams responsible for outputs or projects. These responsibilities imply regular involvement in configuring or adapting operational workflows even if not as a dedicated workflow specialist. Future-state drivers increase this connection: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will make workflow configuration more central; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will standardize orchestration across phases; AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push automation-first execution; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require clearer roles and exception handling. The role is therefore meaningfully affected by this subprocess.

This subprocess concerns testing assembled services and workflows, including integration, secure transmission and suitability of reused routines. The work description does not explicitly mention testing, but the role's responsibility for implementing tools/software and ensuring 'overall quality and completeness of program results' indicates meaningful involvement in validating whether systems and methods work as intended. Leading complex projects involving acquisition, integration and linkage also implies assessing whether integrated solutions are fit for use before operational delivery. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modular Architecture will increase the importance of integration testing, security testing, interoperability testing and end-to-end validation. The role is therefore regularly affected by this subprocess through quality assurance and implementation responsibilities.

This subprocess includes documentation, training users, and moving components into production. The role is not explicitly described as owning production deployment, but it materially contributes because it implements tools/software, supervises teams, and ensures quality and completeness of results. Evidence includes 'implementation of various tools or software' and supervising teams responsible for outputs or projects. As a senior specialist leading complex projects, the incumbent would likely contribute to operational readiness, user guidance and stabilization of new analytical/integration capabilities, without the work description explicitly assigning full deployment ownership. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the need for training, documentation, production hardening and user readiness. This makes the subprocess meaningfully relevant.

This subprocess ensures people, processes and technology are ready to collect data and metadata, including for non-survey sources. The role is materially connected for non-survey and acquired data because it leads data acquisition projects and negotiations and works with stakeholders to leverage new data sources. Evidence includes 'Leads complex projects involving data acquisition ... and use of alternative data sources' and 'Participates in or leads data acquisition negotiations.' These activities align with preparing source acquisition arrangements, systems and operational readiness for incoming data. Future-state impacts are strong from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production. These drivers will increase setup requirements for secure receipt, source management, digital tools, APIs, confidentiality procedures and workforce readiness. The role is therefore regularly involved in this subprocess for alternative and acquired data environments.

This subprocess implements collection, including supplier follow-up, monitoring and adjustments for administrative and non-statistical data. The role is not a survey operations role, but it is materially connected to running non-survey acquisition and supplier-based collection. Evidence includes leading projects involving 'data acquisition ... and use of alternative data sources,' participating in acquisition negotiations, and collaborating with stakeholders to establish relationships for new data sources. These responsibilities imply ongoing interaction with suppliers and operational management of incoming data streams. Future-state impacts from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase reliance on scheduled receipt, digital monitoring, adaptive adjustments and supplier coordination. The role is therefore meaningfully affected by this subprocess, especially for alternative and administrative data collection execution.

This subprocess loads collected data and metadata into environments for further processing, including conversion, versioning, metadata/paradata analysis and preparation for downstream integration. The role is materially connected because it manages data integration, manipulation and processing and leads projects involving acquired and alternative data sources. Evidence includes managing 'data integration, data manipulation ... processing' and leading projects involving 'data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources.' These responsibilities imply involvement in preparing incoming data for processing and integration. Future-state impacts from Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase automation, metadata handling, pseudonymisation, versioning and secure handoff requirements. The role is therefore regularly affected by this subprocess.

This is the most directly implicated subprocess. It concerns combining data from multiple sources, harmonising values, record linkage, data fusion, prioritisation across sources and producing consolidated datasets. The position title itself is 'Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration,' and the work description repeatedly centers on integration. Evidence includes: 'Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis'; 'Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources'; and responsibility for ensuring quality and completeness of results. This is direct performance of the subprocess. Future-state impacts are extensive and cumulative. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion makes integration, harmonisation and linkage central production activities. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access increases the importance of controlled linkage environments, de-identification and secure access. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure enables scalable integration through centralized repositories and cloud platforms. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration makes integration a backbone of automated production. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability improves interoperability and reuse across sources. Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production makes integrated reusable datasets central to modernization. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases reliance on integrated existing sources instead of labour-intensive collection. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity raises the need for advanced integration skills and disciplined sequencing. This subprocess is core to the role now and in the future.

This subprocess concerns assigning codes and classifications to input data, often using automated or clerical coding. The work description does not explicitly mention coding or classification responsibilities. However, because the role manages data manipulation, analytics, processing and alternative data integration, there is a plausible but limited connection where non-standard source data may need harmonisation to statistical classifications. Evidence is indirect: managing 'data manipulation' and leading projects involving alternative data sources could entail some coding or mapping work. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may increase exposure to automated coding and harmonisation of non-standard inputs, but the supplied work description does not directly assign this responsibility. Relevance is therefore Low.

This subprocess examines data to identify errors, discrepancies, duplicates and anomalies before and after integration. The role is directly connected because it manages processing and analysis activities and is explicitly responsible for ensuring 'overall quality and completeness of program results.' That is direct evidence of validation responsibility. The role's work in data integration, linkage and alternative data use also creates a strong operational need to validate heterogeneous and linked inputs. Future-state impacts are substantial. AI and Automation in Statistical Production will increase automated anomaly detection and monitoring; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will introduce more source heterogeneity, linkage errors and structural inconsistencies; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will embed validation checkpoints into automated flows; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata quality part of validation; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will require scalable validation for more complex and automated production; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase reliance on automated validation with fewer staff. The role's quality assurance responsibility makes this subprocess highly relevant.

This subprocess changes incorrect, missing or unreliable data and records metadata on those changes. The work description does not explicitly mention editing or imputation, so relevance is not High. However, the role's management of data manipulation, processing, integration and quality/completeness of results indicates regular involvement in the broader correction and treatment of data issues. Evidence includes managing 'data manipulation ... processing' and ensuring 'overall quality and completeness of program results.' In integrated and alternative-data environments, those responsibilities are meaningfully affected by editing and imputation choices even if not explicitly named. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward more automated, source-prioritized and metadata-documented correction methods. The role is therefore materially affected by this subprocess.

This subprocess derives variables and units not directly collected but needed for outputs. The role is materially connected because data analytics, integration, linkage and alternative data use often require deriving analytical variables from combined sources. Evidence includes managing 'data analytics' and 'data integration' and leading projects involving 'integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources.' These activities commonly depend on derived variables and units, even though the work description does not explicitly state formal derivation design. Future-state impacts are meaningful: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increases reliance on derived variables from linked and administrative records; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration requires explicit dependency management for derivations; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the need to document derivation logic; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production expands model-based and linked-source derivations; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment encourages deriving variables instead of collecting them directly. The role is therefore regularly affected by this subprocess.

This subprocess assembles the results of processing into datasets used as input to analysis. The role is materially connected because it manages processing, analysis and integration activities and prepares outputs from those results. Evidence includes managing 'processing, analysis' and ensuring quality and completeness of results. In practice, a senior specialist leading integration and analytics projects would be meaningfully involved in ensuring consolidated analytic datasets are ready for downstream use, even though the work description does not explicitly mention file finalization. Future-state impacts from Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will increase standardization, metadata-rich packaging, automated handoffs and pressure for timely preliminary/final datasets. The role is therefore meaningfully affected.

This subprocess transforms processed data into statistical outputs and prepares methodological notes and supporting materials. The role is directly connected because it manages preparation of dissemination and visualization products and authors analytical papers and supporting material. Evidence includes: 'Manages activities related to ... the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products' and 'Authors analytical papers and other types of material supporting data development and dissemination.' This is direct output-preparation work. The capability involved includes analytical interpretation, product preparation, and communicating methods and results. Future-state impacts are meaningful: AI and Automation in Statistical Production may accelerate draft production but increase the need for transparent explanation of AI-supported methods; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will require clearer explanation of mixed-source outputs and linkage methods; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will require richer contextual metadata; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will expand granular, geospatial and model-based outputs; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will encourage templating and automation. This subprocess is clearly relevant.

This subprocess validates outputs against expectations, prior cycles, auxiliary information and quality indicators. The role is materially connected because it provides expert analysis, keeps abreast of economic trends and developments, and ensures quality and completeness of program results. Evidence includes stakeholder collaboration 'to understand user needs and keep abreast of economic trends and developments, and providing expert advice and analysis,' plus responsibility for 'overall quality and completeness of program results.' Those are core capabilities for validating whether outputs make sense in context. Future-state impacts are strong: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will create methodological breaks and comparability issues requiring stronger validation; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase reliance on benchmarks, metadata, paradata and domain intelligence; AI and Automation in Statistical Production will require scrutiny of automated outputs; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward more risk-based validation with fewer staff. Because the role combines domain awareness, expert analysis and quality responsibility, this subprocess is highly relevant.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the role authors analytical papers, provides expert advice and analysis, and works with stakeholders to understand user needs and economic trends. Evidence includes: 'Authors analytical papers and other types of material supporting data development and dissemination' and stakeholder collaboration to 'understand user needs and keep abreast of economic trends and developments, and providing expert advice and analysis.' These are direct interpretation and explanation responsibilities. The capability involved includes analytical expertise, domain interpretation, and communication of findings. Future-state impacts are meaningful: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will require explaining outputs from mixed-source systems and any comparability changes; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will require interpretation of outputs shaped by advanced methods, linked data and AI-assisted processing; AI and Automation in Statistical Production may change analyst workflows through AI assistants while increasing transparency expectations; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need for strong analytical and communication skills using new tools. This subprocess is central to the role.

This subprocess ensures outputs and associated information are fit for purpose and ready for release, including commentary, technical notes, briefings and approval preparation. The role is directly connected because it prepares dissemination and visualization products, authors analytical and supporting materials, and briefs senior management when project scope or cost changes are necessary. Evidence includes managing 'the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products,' authoring 'analytical papers and other types of material supporting data development and dissemination,' and briefing senior management. These are core finalization activities. Future-state impacts are significant: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata a core part of release readiness; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will increase pressure for disciplined sign-off and timely caveat decisions; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will require more explicit caveats, technical notes and uncertainty communication; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will affect release levels and controlled use; Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline will clarify approval authority and trade-offs. The role is therefore highly relevant.

This subprocess manages formatting and loading data and metadata into dissemination systems. The work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for dissemination databases or system updates, so relevance is not High. However, the role materially contributes because it manages dissemination and visualization products and implements tools/software used in production. Evidence includes managing 'the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products' and implementation of 'various tools or software.' Future-state impacts from Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase the importance of standardized metadata linkage, automated loading and platform-based dissemination stores. The role is therefore meaningfully affected by this subprocess.

This subprocess produces publications, websites, tables, maps, downloadable files and other dissemination products. The role is directly implicated because it manages preparation of dissemination and data visualization products and authors analytical material supporting dissemination. Evidence includes: 'Manages activities related to ... the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products' and 'Authors analytical papers and other types of material supporting data development and dissemination.' This is direct product-production work. Future-state impacts are meaningful: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will require products to be metadata-rich and reusable; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will support more scalable and interactive digital products; AI and Automation in Statistical Production may automate assembly and drafting while increasing transparency requirements; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase mixed-source, linked and geospatial products; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push standardization and templating; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require digital product skills and accessible communication. This subprocess is clearly highly relevant.

This subprocess manages timing of release, embargoes, briefings, subscriber provision and controlled access to confidential data. The work description does not explicitly assign release management, embargo handling or subscriber/researcher access responsibilities. There is some plausible connection because the role prepares dissemination products and briefs senior management, but the supplied evidence does not show direct ownership of release operations. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure may affect the role indirectly through tighter release coordination and secure digital channels, but based on the supplied information the involvement is limited. Relevance is therefore Low.

This subprocess gathers feedback, process metadata, system metrics and staff suggestions for evaluation. The role is materially connected because it manages projects, develops mitigation strategies, ensures quality and completeness, collaborates with stakeholders, and supervises teams. These activities naturally generate evaluation inputs on quality, delays, scope changes, user needs and operational performance. Evidence includes developing 'mitigation strategies to address delays,' briefing senior management when 'cost or scope changes are necessary,' stakeholder outreach to understand user needs, and supervising teams. Future-state impacts are meaningful: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will generate richer monitoring data, paradata and system metrics; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the importance of evidence on productivity, workload, adoption and sustainability. The role is therefore a meaningful contributor to evaluation inputs.

This subprocess analyzes evaluation inputs and synthesizes findings into reports or dashboards with recommendations. The work description does not explicitly state that the incumbent conducts formal evaluations, but the role materially contributes through expert analysis, project leadership, quality oversight, mitigation planning and senior management briefings. Evidence includes leading complex projects, developing mitigation strategies for delays, briefing senior management on cost/scope changes, and ensuring quality and completeness of results. These are strong indicators of evaluative and performance-assessment responsibilities, even if not formal program evaluation ownership. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need for dashboard-based assessment of quality, timeliness, efficiency, workforce readiness and modernization outcomes. The role is therefore meaningfully connected.

This subprocess brings together decision-making power to agree actions based on evaluation findings and monitor their impact. The role is materially connected because it leads complex projects, develops mitigation strategies, briefs senior management on cost/scope changes, and supervises teams. Evidence includes: 'develops mitigation strategies to address delays and briefs senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary' and 'Supervises directly or in a matrix environment to plan and coordinate teams responsible for statistical outputs or projects.' This shows involvement in turning issues into concrete actions and coordinating implementation, even if the work description does not explicitly assign formal approval authority for enterprise action plans. Future-state impacts are meaningful from Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, and Modular Architecture/modernization drivers. These will require more explicit prioritization, ownership, sequencing, workforce support and monitoring of corrective actions. The role is therefore a meaningful contributor to this subprocess.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it covers collection strategy, fieldwork operations, respondent engagement, collection instruments, multi-mode collection, online-first approaches, adaptive collection, agreements, and respondent management systems. The work description shows the position actively shaping and adapting census collection operations rather than only executing a fixed script. Evidence includes: the incumbent 'contributes to the development of operational plans for census data collection activities,' 'develops collection strategies and contingency plans,' 'organizes, oversees and controls census field collection activities,' and makes decisions on 'objectives, content and approaches for census collection activities' and on 'development and implementation of collection applications, alternate work methods and models.' The capability involved is operational design and redesign of collection approaches for a geographic area, including prioritization, contingency planning, respondent relations, and adaptation of operational processes.
