Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability suggests more support around navigating metadata-rich repositories. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment implies more triaged, self-service and lower-touch support models. Evidence also includes managing the intranet and wiki, which are natural support and knowledge-sharing channels.

This subprocess is relevant because it gathers feedback, process metadata, system metrics, staff suggestions and quality indicators for evaluation. The work description shows several activities that generate or compile such inputs: 'participates in collection development activities, including planning, information audits, product evaluation and usage reports,' 'prepares reports (including financial and usage) for a range of clients,' 'prepares and delivers reports to library management for analysis and decision making,' and analyzes and organizes data from the integrated library system to develop and deliver reports. The capability involved is collecting operational evidence on usage, performance and service effectiveness to inform management decisions. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment all increase the importance of continuous metrics, monitoring, dashboards and evidence on efficiency and adoption. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is also relevant because the incumbent provides training and guidance, making staff feedback and adoption issues part of the operational picture. Evidence from the work description clearly supports involvement in usage reporting, audits and management reporting.

This subprocess is materially connected because it analyzes evaluation inputs, compares them to expectations, synthesizes findings into reports or dashboards, and recommends changes. The position does not own enterprise evaluation, but it contributes meaningfully through analysis and recommendations in the library-services domain. Evidence includes 'participates in collection development activities, including planning, information audits, product evaluation and usage reports,' 'prepares and delivers reports to library management for analysis and decision making,' 'recommends improvements to library services,' and 'interprets and applies divisional policies and procedures; analyzes them in order to revise or recommend changes.' The capability involved is service evaluation, operational analysis, and evidence-based recommendation-making. Future-state drivers such as Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity suggest stronger emphasis on performance evidence, prioritization, efficiency gains, adoption impacts and continuous improvement. The work description's repeated references to audits, evaluation, usage reports, analysis for decision making, and recommending changes are direct evidence.

This subprocess is plausibly relevant at a limited level because it concerns bringing together decision-making authority to agree actions based on evaluation findings and monitoring their impact. The position is not described as the approval authority, so relevance is limited. However, the work description shows contribution to the inputs and coordination that support action planning: the incumbent 'recommends and implements changes to procedures, guidelines and other administrative and technical material,' 'recommends improvements to library services to the supervisor or section head,' 'assists the unit head and/or section chief in the planning and establishment of goals, priorities and training plans,' and chairs or participates in working groups and project teams while monitoring and reporting on progress. The capability involved is contributing recommendations, implementation support, and project coordination rather than final governance authority. Future-state drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity suggest that recommendation-making, prioritization and monitored implementation will become more structured and consequential. Evidence supports contribution to action planning, but not ownership, so Low relevance is appropriate.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position coordinates and improves how data are collected, including both manual and automated collection operations. The work description explicitly states that the position 'coordinates and organizes the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'develops operational plans and procedures for the manual and automated collection,' and 'outlines proposals for changes and improvements to survey content and coverage, questionnaire design, collection and processing of data.' Those duties align closely with collection design responsibilities such as determining collection methods, instruments, respondent interactions, and operational arrangements. The capability involved is operational design expertise for survey collection, questionnaire and instrument changes, and coordination of field or collection activities. The position fulfills that need by planning collection procedures, proposing questionnaire and coverage changes, clarifying technical procedures to respondents and data suppliers, and leading work groups involved in data collection operations. Future-state drivers materially intensify this connection. Administrative, alternative and linked data expansion and modern statistical methods will shift collection design toward online-first, adaptive, mixed-source and supplier-based models; the position is already involved in explaining technical procedures to data suppliers/respondents and in proposing changes to collection approaches. AI and automation in statistical production, enterprise digital platforms and cloud infrastructure, and modular/reusable collection components will change the tools, interfaces, and workflows used in collection, especially because the position already works across 'manual and automated' operations and proposes use of 'new hardware and software options.' Cyber security, privacy and secure access are also relevant because the position prepares policies and guidelines to maintain integrity, security and backup systems, and must apply the Statistics Act and Privacy Act in collection activities. Workforce implications such as reduced manual effort, digital collection, evolving collection roles, and need for tools and training are directly applicable because this role leads work groups and provides operational guidance during collection.

This subprocess is materially connected because the position helps define and improve processing methods, testing approaches, data quality checks, and system requirements used in processing statistical data. Evidence includes: 'coordinates and organizes the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data'; 'reviews and documents operational processes and assesses the quality and application of data outputs in order to propose solutions or explain results'; 'determines the nature of the problem with respect to data inconsistency or integrity'; 'develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in revising existing systems or in developing new processing systems'; and 'specifies testing approaches, plans and environments' for acceptance testing. The capability involved is design and stewardship of processing rules, validation logic, coding and integration requirements, and operational quality assurance. The position fulfills that need by diagnosing integrity issues, reviewing test results, recommending implementation changes, and translating operational requirements into specifications for analysts and programmers. Future drivers strongly affect this work. AI and automation in statistical production, modern statistical methods and next-generation production, and operational efficiency/cost realignment all point toward more automated coding, validation, editing, integration and streamlined processing. That is highly relevant because the role already oversees manual and automated processing and recommends improvements to coding and processing activities. Metadata-driven data management and integrated data pipelines/process orchestration are also relevant because the role documents processes, writes specifications and guidelines, and supports repeatable operational workflows. Administrative and alternative data expansion will increase complexity of integration and validation across sources, which fits the role's responsibility to reconcile differences in source concepts and develop special adjustment methods. Workforce implications such as reduced manual intervention, need for workflow/orchestration skills, and upskilling in AI and modern tools are material because this role sits between operations, systems specialists, and working groups and is already responsible for operationalizing new procedures.

This is one of the strongest matches. The subprocess concerns end-to-end workflow design, reuse of systems and services, and defining how staff interact with systems and who is responsible for what and when. The work description directly reflects this: the position 'coordinates and organizes the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations'; 'reviews and documents operational processes'; 'develops operational plans and procedures'; 'writes specifications and guidelines to be used by others in developing or operating systems and processes'; 'develops and outlines system requirements'; and 'leads work groups established to coordinate and implement statistical production activities.' The capability involved is operational workflow design, systems/process coordination, role assignment, and production governance at the working level. The position fulfills that need by coordinating across stages of collection, coding and processing, documenting workflows, assigning work, monitoring progress, and identifying resource needs. Future-state drivers cumulatively make this subprocess even more central. Integrated data pipelines and process orchestration directly affect this role because work is shifting from manual step execution to pipeline supervision, exception handling, and coordinated execution across collection, processing, analysis and dissemination. AI and automation, enterprise digital platforms and cloud infrastructure, modular architecture/reusable components, and governance/prioritization drivers all reinforce a move toward standardized, reusable, monitored workflows with clearer handoffs and fewer redundancies. The work description already shows this role operating at those handoffs: meeting with subject matter and systems specialists to establish the framework and conditions for operations, resolving differences affecting efficiency and output quality, and participating on teams and working groups as the statistical operations representative. Workforce implications such as clarifying handoffs across programs, cross-functional coordination, reduced manual effort, and stronger role clarity are directly relevant because the position leads work groups and manages operational execution.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because the position contributes to specifying, testing, and implementing processing components, even if it is not described as a software developer. Evidence includes 'develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in revising existing systems or in developing new processing systems,' 'specifies testing approaches, plans and environments,' and 'reviews test results from new or revised procedures to determine the impact on existing program operations.' The capability involved is operational specification of processing components, acceptance criteria, and implementation readiness. The position fulfills that need by translating operational requirements into specifications, supporting testing, and recommending implementation of revised procedures. Future drivers such as AI and automation, enterprise platforms, modular architecture/reusable components, and integrated pipelines will increase reuse of shared processing services and reduce bespoke manual routines. That means this role is likely to be increasingly affected through more standardized components, stronger governance, and greater need to assess operational fit, validation, and sustainability. The work description's emphasis on generalized survey software packages, system analysis and design knowledge, and overseeing design/testing/operation/maintenance of processing systems supports this connection.

This subprocess is materially connected because the role operationalizes and adjusts workflows across collection, coding and processing. Evidence includes coordinating 'implementation, conduct and maintenance' of operations, developing operational plans and procedures, writing specifications and guidelines for systems and processes, specifying testing environments, and reviewing revised procedures for impact on operations. The capability involved is configuring and adapting operational workflows so that systems, procedures and staff activities work together in production. The position fulfills that need by coordinating work groups across stages of operations, monitoring progress against objectives, and resolving operational differences that affect efficiency and quality. Future-state drivers make this more important: integrated data pipelines and process orchestration, AI and automation, enterprise platforms, and operational efficiency/cost realignment all push toward standardized, automated, lower-touch workflows with explicit handoffs and exception handling. The role is already positioned at that interface because it leads work groups, documents processes, and acts as the operations representative on teams and working groups. Workforce implications such as shift from manual execution to supervision, need for orchestration skills, and clearer responsibilities are directly relevant to a coordinator role.

This subprocess is directly relevant because testing and sign-off activities are explicitly described in the work description. Evidence includes: 'specifies testing approaches, plans and environments for use by other project staff to set up and carry out acceptance testing of new or modified computer applications'; 'reviews test results from new or revised procedures to determine the impact on existing program operations'; and 'documents the results and prepares recommendations for implementation.' The capability involved is operational testing design, acceptance testing oversight, impact assessment, and readiness recommendation. The position fulfills that need by defining test approaches, reviewing results, and assessing operational impacts before implementation. Future-state drivers such as AI and automation, enterprise digital platforms/cloud, cyber security/privacy, modular architecture, and integrated pipelines all increase the complexity and importance of testing assembled services, secure channels, reusable components, and end-to-end workflows. This role is likely to be materially affected because it already bridges operational requirements and technical testing, and because future production environments will require more integration, security, and workflow testing with fewer staff and more automation.

This subprocess is relevant because the role helps move revised procedures and systems into operational use through recommendations, guidelines, and operational coordination. Evidence includes preparing and implementing policies and guidelines to maintain integrity, security and backup systems, writing specifications and guidelines for others, reviewing test results and preparing recommendations for implementation, and leading work groups to coordinate statistical production activities. The capability involved is operational readiness, user guidance, and controlled implementation of new or revised systems and procedures. The position fulfills that need by documenting processes, preparing guidance, and coordinating staff activities during implementation. Future drivers such as workforce skills transition and leadership capacity, enterprise platforms, AI adoption, and modular/reusable solutions increase the importance of documentation, training, role clarity, and sustainable operating procedures. While the work description does not explicitly mention formal training delivery, it clearly shows operational guidance and implementation support responsibilities, making this a meaningful but somewhat less direct connection than testing or workflow design.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role prepares and coordinates the people, processes and technology needed for collection operations. Evidence includes coordinating implementation and maintenance of collection operations, developing operational plans and procedures for manual and automated collection, leading work groups involved in different stages of data collection operations, contacting data suppliers/respondents to obtain collaboration and explain technical procedures, and meeting with clients, service providers and specialists to establish the framework and conditions for statistical operations. The capability involved is operational readiness for collection, including procedures, staff coordination, respondent/supplier interaction, and system/process setup. The position fulfills that need by organizing collection operations, clarifying requests and procedures, and coordinating resources and work groups. Future-state drivers such as administrative and alternative data expansion, online-first and adaptive collection, enterprise digital platforms, cyber security/privacy, and workforce skills transition will materially change collection setup toward digital tools, secure channels, supplier coordination, and mixed-source readiness. This role is already positioned to absorb those changes because it works across manual and automated collection and provides advice on methods and procedures related to statistical operations services.

This subprocess is directly implicated because the position leads and coordinates live collection operations. Evidence includes 'coordinates and organizes the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection... of data,' 'leads the activities of work groups involved in different stages of data collection operations,' and 'contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities, to explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format, or to clarify and explain statistical concepts.' The capability involved is operational execution of collection, respondent/supplier management, issue resolution, and monitoring of collection quality and progress. The position fulfills that need by leading work groups, interacting directly with respondents and suppliers, and resolving operational issues affecting efficiency and output quality. Future drivers such as AI and automation, administrative and alternative data expansion, agility/timelines, and online-first collection will change how collection is run through more digital channels, automated monitoring, supplier-based acquisition, and adaptive follow-up. Workforce implications such as workload shifts from traditional field collection to digital monitoring and supplier coordination are especially relevant because this role already spans those operational interfaces.

This subprocess is relevant because the role covers the transition from collection into processing, including handling data integrity, formats, and operational procedures. Evidence includes coordinating collection and processing operations together, determining problems with data inconsistency or integrity, reviewing operational processes, and knowledge of computer processing and databases to oversee operation and maintenance of processing systems. The capability involved is ensuring collected data and associated operational outputs are ready for downstream processing, including integrity, documentation, and procedural consistency. The position fulfills that need indirectly through oversight of both collection and processing operations and through diagnosing integrity issues. Future drivers such as integrated pipelines, metadata-driven management, cyber security/privacy, and automated loading from digital and external sources will make this handoff more automated and metadata-rich. Because the role already spans collection and processing and documents operational processes, it is meaningfully affected even if the work description does not explicitly mention loading or archiving activities.

This subprocess is relevant because the position works with multiple data sources, reconciles differences, and develops methods to adjust source data. Evidence includes 'reviews and compares the concepts and definitions of data sources with those of the statistical program. Reconciles differences and develops special methods of adjusting source data,' as well as knowledge of data sources within and external to Statistics Canada and identifying/evaluating possible data conflicts. The capability involved is source comparison, harmonisation, and operational integration of data inputs into statistical production. The position fulfills that need by reconciling source differences and assessing data conflicts and output quality. Future drivers such as administrative, alternative and linked data expansion, metadata-driven management, enterprise platforms, and integrated pipelines will make integration more central and more complex. This role is likely to be increasingly affected because it already performs source reconciliation and supports operational systems/processes that depend on integrated data.

This subprocess is directly relevant because coding is explicitly part of the position's operational scope. Evidence includes coordinating operations for 'collection, coding and processing of data,' knowledge of concepts and principles used in 'collection, coding and processing of statistical data,' and recommending and implementing improvements to coding activities. The capability involved is operational management and improvement of coding processes, including manual and automated coding. The position fulfills that need by coordinating coding operations, proposing improvements, and overseeing related systems and procedures. Future-state drivers strongly affect this work: AI-enabled automated coding, automation, machine learning, and operational efficiency pressures will reduce clerical coding and increase machine-assisted coding, monitoring, and exception handling. The work description already shows the role bridging manual and automated operations and supporting new hardware/software options, so the future impact is substantial. Workforce implications such as reduced manual effort and need for AI/digital upskilling are directly relevant.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role explicitly reviews processes, diagnoses data problems, and assesses output quality. Evidence includes 'reviews and documents operational processes and assesses the quality and application of data outputs in order to propose solutions or explain results,' 'determines the nature of the problem with respect to data inconsistency or integrity,' and 'reviews test results from new or revised procedures to determine the impact on existing program operations.' The capability involved is input and process validation, anomaly/problem identification, and quality assessment. The position fulfills that need by investigating inconsistencies, assessing outputs, and recommending corrective or explanatory actions. Future drivers such as AI and automation, administrative and linked data expansion, metadata-driven management, and operational efficiency will increase automated validation, exception routing, and multi-source quality assessment. This role is already centered on those validation and quality functions, making the connection strong.

There is a plausible but limited connection to this subprocess. The work description includes designing statistical tables, charts and graphs, reconciling source differences, and developing special methods of adjusting source data, which suggests some involvement with transformed or derived operational outputs. However, the description does not explicitly assign responsibility for deriving new variables or units. The relevance is therefore limited. Future drivers such as administrative and linked data expansion and modern statistical methods may increase the extent to which operational roles are affected by derivation logic embedded in processing systems, especially where direct collection is replaced by derived constructs, but the supplied work description does not provide strong direct evidence of responsibility for this subprocess.

This subprocess is relevant because the role spans collection, coding and processing and is responsible for operational integrity, documentation, and readiness of outputs for downstream use. Evidence includes coordinating implementation and maintenance of collection/coding/processing operations, maintaining databases, reviewing operational processes, and assessing quality and application of data outputs. The capability involved is bringing operational processing results into a coherent, usable state for subsequent analysis or use. The position fulfills that need through quality assessment, process documentation, and operational coordination across stages. Future drivers such as integrated pipelines, metadata-driven management, enterprise platforms, and agility/timelines will make standardized, traceable, analysis-ready outputs more important. This role is meaningfully affected because it already manages the operational continuity and quality of the upstream processes that produce those files.

This subprocess is relevant because the position prepares statistical presentation materials and explanatory content for clients. Evidence includes 'designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in statistical analysis by clients both inside and outside Statistics Canada' and 'assesses trends and developments in the program area by preparing tabulations and reviews outlining program results for use by program managers and general data users.' The capability involved is transforming processed results into usable draft analytical outputs and explanatory materials. The position fulfills that need by preparing tables, charts, graphs, explanatory text, and tabulations for internal and external users. Future drivers such as AI and automation, metadata-driven management, and modern statistical methods will affect how draft outputs are generated, documented, and explained, especially where outputs rely on automated or mixed-source methods. The role is therefore regularly involved and likely to experience meaningful change.

This subprocess is relevant because the role assesses the quality and application of outputs and explains results. Evidence includes 'assesses the quality and application of data outputs in order to propose solutions or explain results' and 'assesses trends and developments in the program area by preparing tabulations and reviews outlining program results.' The capability involved is checking whether outputs are credible, usable, and consistent enough to support users and managers. The position fulfills that need by reviewing outputs, investigating issues, and explaining results to clients and internal users. Future drivers such as administrative and linked data expansion, modern methods, and AI-enabled production will increase the need to validate outputs against expectations, prior results, and methodological changes. This role is materially affected because it already performs output quality assessment, though it is not described as the final statistical authority for release validation.

This subprocess is directly relevant because interpreting and explaining results is explicitly part of the job. Evidence includes 'reviews and documents operational processes and assesses the quality and application of data outputs in order to propose solutions or explain results,' 'interprets and clarifies client requests and inquiries for statistical data and information,' 'responds orally or in writing to enquiries... to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results,' and 'designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text.' The capability involved is operational and analytical interpretation of statistical outputs for clients, managers, and users. The position fulfills that need by explaining results, clarifying concepts and methods, and preparing explanatory materials. Future drivers such as modern statistical methods, administrative and linked data expansion, and AI/automation will increase the need to explain outputs produced through more complex, mixed-source, and automated methods. Workforce implications around analytical expertise, clear communication, and skills transition are highly relevant because this role is already a user-facing interpreter of operational results.

This subprocess is relevant because the position prepares dissemination-style components such as tables, charts, graphs, explanatory text, and has contextual knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices. Evidence includes 'designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in statistical analysis by clients both inside and outside Statistics Canada' and knowledge of 'departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices' to establish common divisional policies and practices in preparing statistical tables, charts and explanatory notes for dissemination. The capability involved is preparing statistical product components and ensuring they align with dissemination practices. The position fulfills that need by producing those components and advising users on methods and procedures related to statistical operations services. Future drivers such as metadata-driven dissemination, enterprise digital platforms, automation, and standardization will affect how such products are assembled and documented. The role is not a pure dissemination specialist, but it contributes regularly and will be meaningfully affected.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the role provides advice and responds to user and client requests about statistical operations services and results. Evidence includes 'provides advice to users on the methods and procedures related to statistical operations services,' 'interprets and clarifies client requests and inquiries for statistical data and information,' and 'responds orally or in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results.' The capability involved is user support, service response, clarification of methods/procedures, and support to clients and data users. The position fulfills that need directly through advisory and response functions. Future drivers such as AI chatbots, website search, self-service platforms, metadata-driven discoverability, and operational efficiency/cost realignment will change how support is delivered, likely shifting routine inquiries toward automated/self-service channels while increasing the value of this role for complex or methodological questions. Workforce implications around reduced manual effort, clearer communication, and support for users navigating modernized products are directly relevant.

This subprocess is relevant because the role generates and documents operational evidence about process performance, quality, and issues. Evidence includes reviewing and documenting operational processes, assessing quality and application of outputs, monitoring progress against objectives, tracking time and costs, reviewing test results, and preparing recommendations for implementation. The capability involved is producing operational documentation, quality indicators, test evidence, and performance information that can feed evaluation. The position fulfills that need by documenting processes and results, monitoring work groups, and identifying operational problems and resource needs. Future drivers such as AI/automation, integrated pipelines, enterprise platforms, and operational efficiency will increase the amount of process metadata, monitoring information, and performance evidence available and expected. This role is meaningfully connected because it already creates much of the operational evidence base used for evaluation.

This subprocess is relevant because the role analyzes operational results, compares processes and outputs, and recommends changes. Evidence includes assessing quality and application of outputs to propose solutions or explain results, researching options and requirements for divisional systems and processes, assessing trends and developments in the program area, reviewing test results and preparing recommendations for implementation, and reconciling differences in source concepts. The capability involved is operational evaluation and continuous improvement analysis rather than formal enterprise evaluation ownership. The position fulfills that need by synthesizing operational findings into recommendations for process and system improvements. Future drivers such as operational efficiency/cost realignment, AI and automation, governance/prioritization, and workforce transition will make evaluation more dashboard-driven and more focused on efficiency, quality, and sustainability. This role is materially affected because it already performs the analytical and recommendation functions that underpin evaluation.

There is a limited but plausible connection to this subprocess. The work description shows the position preparing recommendations, outlining proposals for changes and improvements, identifying financial and human resource needs, and leading work groups to implement statistical production activities. That indicates contribution to action planning and implementation discussions, but not clear authority to formally agree enterprise action plans. The capability involved is contributing operational recommendations and implementation considerations. Future drivers such as governance, prioritization, agility, and workforce transition may increase the need for clearer ownership and disciplined follow-through on operational improvements, and this role would likely contribute evidence and practical implementation input. However, the supplied information does not show formal decision-making power to agree action plans, so relevance remains low.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns setting output objectives within resource, quality, confidentiality and operational constraints. The work description shows the position helps shape operational objectives and trade-offs by developing operational plans and procedures, outlining proposals for changes to survey content and coverage, questionnaire design, collection and processing, and reviewing impacts of revised procedures on existing operations. That is evidence of contributing to decisions about what outputs can be delivered and under what conditions. The capability involved is operational planning, prioritization, and translating client and program needs into feasible production arrangements. The role fulfills this need by interpreting client requests, meeting with subject matter and systems specialists to establish the framework and conditions for statistical operations, and preparing recommendations for implementation. Future change is likely from Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment: stronger accountability, transparent trade-offs, and scarce resources focused on highest-value outcomes will make this role more involved in explicit scope, timeliness and quality trade-offs; fiscal pressure, fewer staff, and efficiency expectations will push tighter operational objective-setting and more standardized delivery models.

This subprocess is materially connected because it assesses whether available data sources and operational conditions can support statistical needs. The work description does not assign enterprise source-strategy authority, but it does show regular contribution to assessing source suitability and operational feasibility: the position 'reviews and compares the concepts and definitions of data sources with those of the statistical program,' 'reconciles differences and develops special methods of adjusting source data,' maintains knowledge of data sources and contacts within and external to Statistics Canada, and contacts data suppliers or respondents to clarify problems and obtain data in the appropriate format. The capability involved is evaluating source fit, resolving concept differences, and ensuring operational usability of incoming data. The role fulfills that need through source comparison, verification of data accuracy, and collaboration with suppliers and clients. Future-state drivers increase the importance of this work: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will expand the range of non-survey and linked sources that must be assessed; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will strengthen scrutiny of confidentiality, legal and secure-access conditions; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make platform fit, metadata quality, and interoperability more central. Evidence includes knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act, knowledge of data sources and contacts, and responsibility for explaining technical procedures for obtaining data in the appropriate format.

This subprocess is relevant at a limited level because the position contributes evidence and recommendations used in approval and change decisions, though the work description does not state formal responsibility for preparing business cases for governance approval. The capability involved is documenting current operations, identifying inefficiencies, estimating resource needs, and recommending implementation options. The role supports this by documenting operational processes, preparing recommendations for implementation, identifying financial and human resource needs, monitoring costs for cost recovery, preparing estimates for special requests, and outlining proposals for changes and improvements to systems, questionnaires, hardware and software. Future drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the value of this operational evidence because approvals will depend more on explicit trade-offs, milestones, affordability, staffing impacts, and implementation readiness. Evidence includes 'reviews test results... documents the results and prepares recommendations for implementation' and 'identifies financial and human resource needs.'

This is one of the most directly relevant subprocesses because the position coordinates and organizes implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for collection, and develops operational plans and procedures for collection activities. The capability involved is designing and refining collection strategies, instruments, procedures, respondent interactions, and operational conditions for statistical collection. The work description directly supports this through proposals for changes to survey content and coverage, questionnaire design, collection and processing of data, implementation of new hardware and software options, and contacts with respondents or data suppliers to explain procedures and obtain collaboration. The role also leads work groups involved in different stages of data collection operations, showing direct operational responsibility. Future-state drivers will materially reshape this work: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure point to more online-first, automated, API-based, and mixed-source collection models; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase secure-by-design requirements; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push lower-touch and more standardized collection. Evidence includes 'develops operational plans and procedures for the manual and automated collection... of statistical data,' 'outlines proposals for changes... questionnaire design, collection and processing of data,' and 'contacts data suppliers or respondents... to explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format.'

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position helps design how data will be coded, processed, validated, integrated and assessed. The capability involved is specifying processing rules, testing approaches, system requirements, and quality/integrity controls for statistical production. The work description directly supports this through developing operational plans for coding and processing, determining problems related to data inconsistency or integrity, assessing quality and application of data outputs, specifying testing approaches and environments for acceptance testing, preparing policies and guidelines to maintain integrity, security and backup systems, and developing system requirements for analysts and programmers. Future drivers will intensify this connection: AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase automation, AI-enabled coding, and integrated processing; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will shift work toward orchestrated, repeatable processing flows; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the importance of standardized rules and lineage; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push more automation and less manual intervention; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require stronger technical and oversight skills. Evidence includes 'knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to oversee the design, testing, operation and maintenance of processing systems' and 'develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers.'

This subprocess is directly implicated because the role coordinates manual and automated operations across collection, coding and processing, reviews operational processes, writes specifications and guidelines for systems and processes, and leads work groups across production stages. The capability involved is designing end-to-end workflows, clarifying responsibilities, integrating systems and procedures, and ensuring production activities fit together efficiently. The work description matches this closely: it includes coordinating implementation and maintenance of operations, reviewing and documenting operational processes, developing operational plans and procedures, specifying testing environments, writing specifications and guidelines, and leading work groups involved in different stages of data collection operations. Future-state drivers strongly affect this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment all point to more integrated, reusable, automated, monitored workflows with clearer handoffs, fewer redundancies, flatter structures, and stronger accountability. Workforce implications such as shift from manual step execution to pipeline supervision and greater need for orchestration skills are especially relevant to an operations coordinator role. Evidence includes 'coordinates and organizes the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations' and 'writes specifications and guidelines to be used by others in developing or operating systems and processes.'

This subprocess is relevant because the position helps operationalize designed workflows by specifying testing approaches, writing specifications and guidelines, reviewing revised procedures, and coordinating implementation of manual and automated operations. The capability involved is configuring and adapting workflows, systems and transformations for operational use. The role fulfills this need by documenting processes, preparing recommendations for implementation, and guiding work groups through production activities. Future drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase the need for standardized workflow configuration, automated handoffs, secure permissions, and reduced manual checkpoints. Evidence includes 'specifies testing approaches, plans and environments,' 'reviews test results from new or revised procedures to determine the impact on existing program operations,' and 'coordinates and organizes the implementation... of manual and automated operations.'

This subprocess is highly relevant because testing is explicitly part of the position's responsibilities. The capability involved is defining test approaches, reviewing results, assessing impacts on operations, and supporting sign-off for new or modified systems and procedures. The work description directly states that the position 'specifies testing approaches, plans and environments for use by other project staff to set up and carry out acceptance testing of new or modified computer applications' and 'reviews test results from new or revised procedures to determine the impact on existing program operations,' then documents results and prepares recommendations for implementation. This subprocess is relevant because the role generates and interprets operational evidence about efficiency, quality, respondent issues and data integrity problems.
