The capability involved is producing operational feedback and quality signals that can feed evaluation and continuous improvement. Future-state drivers make this more important: AI and automation, integrated pipelines, enterprise platforms, efficiency pressures and workforce transition all increase reliance on process metrics, paradata, staff suggestions and operational monitoring. Because this role sits close to live operations and operational redesign, it is well positioned to supply evaluation inputs on what is working, where quality issues arise, and how modernization is affecting workflows.

This subprocess is materially connected because the role evaluates operational trends, client needs, and production efficiency/quality, and recommends new approaches. That is evaluative work, even if not framed as formal enterprise evaluation reporting. Evidence includes "evaluates changes in statistical needs of clients, as well as trends and developments in data collection, capture, coding and processing" and "provides advisory and consultative services to users regarding collection and production efficiency and/or quality." The capability involved is operational assessment and synthesis of performance issues into recommendations for change. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all increase the importance of evidence-based evaluation of whether modernization is improving quality, timeliness, efficiency and sustainability. This role is therefore likely to be increasingly involved in assessing operational impacts and recommending adjustments.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance. The work description shows the position recommends new approaches, participates on teams and working groups, and leads project teams. That suggests some involvement in shaping improvement actions, though not necessarily formal approval authority. The capability involved is contributing operational recommendations and participating in implementation planning. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity suggest that action planning will become more disciplined, time-bound and resource-constrained. This role is likely to contribute operationally grounded recommendations and project-team input, but the supplied description does not support claiming formal decision-making power over action plans.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes designing outputs, products, services, and especially processes governing access to confidential outputs. A Research Data Centre Analyst works in a setting explicitly associated with researcher access to data, and the work description identifies the position title as "Research Data Centre Analyst" and branch/division as ": Research Data Centre," which materially connects the role to confidential-output access arrangements rather than general public dissemination alone. The capability involved is supporting or operating controlled access to statistical outputs and microdata for authorized users. Future-state drivers make this more important: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access directly affects confidential output access through privacy, authorizations, secure access, and safer innovation; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure affects platform-based controlled access and reusable dissemination tooling; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the need for metadata-rich, searchable, well-described outputs; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity implies staff will need stronger digital, accessibility, and communication capabilities to operate and explain modern access environments. Even though the supplied work description is sparse and does not list detailed technical duties, the position title and RDC organizational placement are direct evidence of meaningful involvement in this subprocess.

This subprocess covers building or reusing dissemination components, including access to microdata. It is plausibly relevant because Research Data Centres are a controlled dissemination environment for researcher access, and the position title "Research Data Centre Analyst" indicates likely proximity to those dissemination mechanisms. The capability involved would be use, support, or adaptation of controlled-access dissemination components rather than inventing software-development responsibilities. Future-state drivers suggest meaningful change even if direct build responsibility is not evidenced: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access strengthens secure publication channels and controlled microdata access; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure increases use of scalable platforms, secure access, and reusable dissemination tooling; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the need for metadata-linked dissemination components; and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development points toward standardized, governed dissemination services. Because the work description contains no explicit technical activities beyond the title and RDC placement, relevance is limited but plausible.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it ensures data and metadata to be disseminated or internally stored do not breach confidentiality rules, including for microdata sets for research purposes. That is directly aligned with a Research Data Centre context, where researcher access to confidential microdata is central. The capability involved is confidentiality protection, output checking, and ensuring that access or use conditions for research data do not violate disclosure rules. The strongest evidence is the position title "Research Data Centre Analyst" and branch/division ": Research Data Centre," which materially connect the role to research-use microdata environments specifically referenced in the subprocess description. Future-state drivers intensify this connection: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increases re-identification risk through richer linked records and geospatial outputs; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access directly strengthens privacy protection, secure handling, authorizations, and controlled access; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure expands data accessibility and self-serve possibilities while requiring stronger privacy and secure-access controls; and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development increases the need for embedded governance and standard controls in reusable or self-service environments. The cumulative effect is that RDC work is expected to face stronger disclosure assessment, more complex confidentiality scenarios, and tighter secure-access controls over time.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it includes managing access to confidential data by authorised user groups, such as researchers. That is one of the clearest direct matches in the supplied GSBPM set to a Research Data Centre Analyst role. The capability involved is operationalizing controlled release and access arrangements for confidential data, including authorized-user access, embargo or release controls where applicable, and handling restricted dissemination environments. The work description provides direct evidence through the position title "Research Data Centre Analyst" and branch/division ": Research Data Centre." Future-state drivers materially change this work: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline affects release readiness, deadlines, and authority for release or restriction decisions; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access directly governs researcher access, secure access, authorizations, and resilient release operations; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure changes release channels and controlled-access environments through cloud and platform-based services; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration can automate release readiness and controlled publication actions; and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability makes metadata completeness part of release readiness. The cumulative effect is that RDC analyst work tied to researcher access will likely become more platform-mediated, more tightly governed, and more dependent on secure authorization and metadata-linked release controls.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it explicitly includes responding to user queries and requests for services such as microdata access. A Research Data Centre Analyst is materially connected to this need because RDCs serve authorized researchers and related users of confidential microdata. The capability involved is recording and responding to user requests, supporting access processes, and helping users navigate products and services within agreed deadlines. The strongest evidence from the work description is the position title "Research Data Centre Analyst" and branch/division ": Research Data Centre," which strongly imply a user-facing support role in a research access environment. Future-state drivers indicate substantial change: AI and Automation in Statistical Production introduces AI chatbots, AI assistants, website search, automation, and knowledge-base generation that can reduce manual effort but require governance, transparency, and public trust safeguards; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access affects verification, authorization checks, and privacy-aware responses for restricted-data services; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure enables self-service support models, controlled access workflows, and platform-based case handling; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability changes support toward helping users navigate metadata-rich repositories and reusable assets; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases pressure for triaged support, FAQs, and self-service due to reduced staffing; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity implies stronger communication, digital-tool, and methodological explanation skills will be needed. The cumulative effect is that RDC analyst support work is likely to shift from purely manual case handling toward a mix of secure access support, digital self-service enablement, and more complex explanation of modernized data products and access conditions.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns identifying what statistics and collection approaches are needed in light of respondent feedback, operational constraints, and environmental change. The position contributes to that need by evaluating trends in data collection concepts, methods and techniques, including response patterns and respondent behaviour, and by soliciting participation from non-respondents and resolving complaints. Those activities provide direct evidence about user and respondent needs and operational feasibility. The work description states that the incumbent 'evaluates trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques including response patterns and respondent behaviour' and 'sollicits participation from non-respondents and resolves complaints.' Future-state drivers make this more important: under Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, need identification will be more constrained by scarce resources, fewer staff, and pressure to find efficiencies through automation, AI, machine learning and new tools and methods. Because this manager assesses costs, quality, efficiency and productivity and feeds respondent and operational evidence back into program decisions, the role will increasingly help determine which collection needs remain feasible and worthwhile.

This subprocess is relevant because output objectives must reflect quality, scope, timeliness, confidentiality and available resources, and the position regularly informs those trade-offs from the collection side. The work description shows responsibility for assessing 'cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security' of data collection, processing, editing and compilation, and for preparing summaries and evaluation reports used by senior management to shape program plans and assess objectives. The incumbent also 'provides advice to senior management and subject matter experts regarding proposed changes to questionnaire design, modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection systems and processes.' That means the role contributes evidence on what outputs can realistically be delivered through collection operations. Future changes are driven by Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment: stronger accountability, transparent trade-offs, and scarce resources focused on highest-value outcomes will tighten decisions on scope, timeliness and service levels. As management structures flatten and staffing declines, this role's operational evidence on collection feasibility and quality-service trade-offs will become more consequential.

This subprocess is relevant because it assesses whether available sources and collection approaches can meet requirements under legal, security, quality and operational conditions. The position does not own enterprise source strategy, but it materially contributes through operational assessment of collection and transmission requirements, technology suitability, respondent availability, quality control, and security. Evidence includes: 'Participates in the development of strategies and business solutions for data collection and transmission requirements'; 'Identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations to identify the availability of respondents and to ensure quality control of data, to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software'; and knowledge of 'data confidentiality and security.' This aligns with the subprocess need to assess suitability, ICT feasibility, access conditions and residual gaps. Future-state drivers intensify this connection. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will shift collection from survey-only approaches toward mixed-source models, online-first strategies, adaptive collection design, and linked data. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will make secure access, authorizations, privacy, platforms and tooling central suitability criteria. The manager's role in evaluating hardware/software, transmission requirements, respondent behaviour, and security means the work will increasingly be affected by these source and platform decisions even where enterprise ownership sits elsewhere.

This subprocess is relevant because business cases for new or modified statistical processes require evidence on current operations, costs, benefits, staffing, risks, timelines and implementation needs. The position contributes substantial operational planning and resource evidence even if it is not the formal approval authority. The work description shows that the incumbent 'develops operational plans and schedules,' 'establishes and monitors program budgets,' 'plans and budgets for the management and operation of the regional CATI or CAPI program,' and prepares reports used by senior management to assess program objectives, costs, efficiency and resource utilization. The role also identifies human resource needs, training plans, equipment costs, and impacts of new hardware and software. These are core business-case inputs. Future-state drivers strengthen this link: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline requires milestone-based, executable plans; Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline raises approval thresholds and explicit trade-offs; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment foregrounds savings, workforce reductions and automation-enabled models; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity makes training, sequencing and leadership readiness central feasibility factors. Because this manager supplies operational, budgetary, staffing and implementation evidence, the role is materially connected to business-case development and will be increasingly shaped by more disciplined approval processes.

This subprocess is relevant at a limited level because the position provides operational advice on questionnaire design, survey content and coverage, which can influence what variables are collected and how they are defined for collection. Evidence includes acting as a regional representative who 'provides advice on proposed questionnaire design and survey content and coverage' and possessing 'knowledge of questionnaire development to outline specifications and requirements for the collection and processing of statistical information and to provide feedback to subject matter experts.' However, the work description does not indicate primary responsibility for defining variables, classifications or metadata standards. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability may increase the operational importance of harmonized variables, prefill and derived-variable design, but this role's connection remains advisory rather than central.

This is one of the most directly relevant subprocesses. It concerns designing collection strategy, instruments, modes, fieldwork operations, respondent engagement and collection systems. The position is deeply connected through leadership of CATI/CAPI/PAPI operations, development of alternate work methods and models, proposals for changes to questionnaire design and collection systems, and participation in strategies for data collection and transmission requirements. Evidence includes: 'Leads and coordinates the 7-day statistical data collection activities for either telephone interviewing (CATI) or personal interviewing (CAPI or PAPI) programs'; 'Develops and implements alternate work methods and models and proposes changes and improvements to questionnaire design... revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software for use in data collection activities'; 'Discusses and negotiates... on the development of questionnaires, collection applications, and the framework and conditions within which statistical programs will occur'; and 'Provides advice... regarding proposed changes to questionnaire design... revisions to collection systems and processes.' The capability involved is operational collection design expertise, respondent management, field coordination, system/process design input, and secure collection operations. Future-state drivers strongly reshape this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure point to chatbot-assisted interaction, online-first strategy, adaptive collection design, APIs, machine-to-machine transfers, reusable tooling, cloud platforms and stronger workflow integration. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access adds secure-by-design requirements for channels, devices and respondent authentication. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases pressure to reduce interviewer-heavy methods and standardize collection. Workforce implications are direct: the role already manages interviewers, training and field activities, and will increasingly shift toward digital collection, source monitoring, workflow coordination, and staff transition support.

This subprocess has limited relevance. The position works in survey collection operations and has knowledge of household and business survey programs, respondent availability and response patterns, which can inform frame and sample considerations indirectly. Evidence includes assessing 'the availability of respondents' and evaluating response patterns and respondent behaviour. However, the work description does not assign responsibility for defining target populations, sampling frames, or sampling methodology. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and adaptive collection design may affect how collection operations receive and act on source-based frames, but the role remains only plausibly connected rather than directly responsible.

This subprocess is relevant because it covers design of coding, editing, validation, integration and estimation methods, and the position is materially involved in assessing and advising on the operational side of processing, editing and data quality. Evidence includes responsibility to 'assess the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of the functions and activities associated with the data collection, processing, editing, and compilation of statistical outputs'; to prepare evaluation reports on 'the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes and the quality and completeness of data'; and to review and modify operational techniques and methods, including integration of data from 'financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses.' The role does not design statistical methodology in a specialist sense, but it contributes operational expertise on how processing and editing methods perform in production. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase automation, linkage, metadata-driven processing and exception-based workflows. That means this manager's work will be increasingly affected through evaluation of new methods, operational readiness, quality control and staff adaptation, even if methodological ownership lies elsewhere.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it concerns end-to-end workflow design, reuse of systems and services, role clarity, and staff interaction with systems. The position directly contributes by developing operational plans, guidelines, procedures and alternate work methods; proposing revisions to collection systems and processes; evaluating new hardware and software; and leading multidisciplinary teams that implement programs. Evidence includes: 'Develops guidelines, instructions and procedures for the use and evaluation of statistical systems and processes'; 'Develops and implements alternate work methods and models'; 'proposes... revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software'; and 'Leads and coordinates multi-disciplinary project teams... engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs.' The capability involved is operational workflow design, systems/process stewardship, role assignment, and coordination across teams. Future-state drivers make this central: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all point to reusable enterprise workflows, automated handoffs, clearer accountabilities, fewer manual steps, flatter structures, and staff-system interaction redesign. The work description already emphasizes assigning responsibilities, monitoring progress, training plans, and safeguarding systems and data. This role will therefore be heavily affected as collection operations move toward orchestrated, platform-based, monitored workflows with more exception handling and less manual coordination.

This subprocess is relevant because the position influences the operational build and reuse of collection instruments through questionnaire and collection application development input, implementation of new hardware/software, and training for collection operations. Evidence includes negotiating 'the development of questionnaires, collection applications,' proposing changes to questionnaire design and collection systems, and knowledge of training methods 'to develop and present operational training modules.' The role does not appear to be the technical builder of instruments, but it materially contributes requirements, operational testing perspectives, and deployment readiness. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will increase use of web instruments, APIs, extraction routines, metadata-connected tools and reusable components. This will affect the role through greater involvement in operational readiness, training, and assessment of whether instruments support quality, respondent interaction and secure collection.

This subprocess is relevant because the position develops and implements operational methods, schedules, procedures and system/process changes that amount to configuring how collection workflows run in practice. Evidence includes developing 'operational plans and schedules to manage, organize and control the 7-day data collection activities,' developing 'guidelines, instructions and procedures for the use and evaluation of statistical systems and processes,' and revising collection systems and processes. The role is not described as a technical workflow configurator, but it is materially involved in operational configuration and adaptation of workflows. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push workflows toward automation-first execution, milestone-driven sequencing, fewer manual checkpoints and stronger monitoring. This will increase the role's emphasis on configuring operational routing, exception handling, staff responsibilities and deadlines in collection operations.

This subprocess is relevant because the position evaluates the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes, reviews completeness and integrity of manuals and data, and assesses suitability of new hardware and software. Evidence includes preparing 'evaluation reports outlining the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes and the quality and completeness of data,' ensuring 'completeness, accuracy, integrity and compliance,' and identifying and assessing 'the suitability of new hardware and software.' These are core testing and sign-off contributions from an operational perspective. Future-state drivers such as Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will expand testing needs to include secure transmission, interoperability, automated workflows and reusable components. The role will therefore be increasingly affected through operational validation, readiness assessment and issue escalation before production use.

This subprocess is relevant because the position manages live collection operations and evaluates methods, systems, respondent reactions and technology changes, which are all central to piloting and field-testing redesigned collection processes. Evidence includes evaluating 'questionnaire design, concepts, change in technology, respondent reaction and understanding,' leading 7-day collection activities, and preparing assessments for senior management and survey clients. While the work description does not explicitly mention pilots, the role's operational leadership and evaluation responsibilities make it materially connected to testing collection processes in realistic conditions. Future-state drivers such as Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need to test adaptive collection, online-first approaches, chatbot support, and staff readiness before scale-up. This manager would likely be heavily affected by such pilots through field coordination, training, monitoring and feedback.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes documentation, user manuals, training and moving systems into production, and the position has direct responsibilities for procedures, manuals, training plans and operational readiness. Evidence includes preparing and reviewing 'correspondence, manuals and data,' developing 'guidelines, instructions and procedures,' approving individual training plans, and knowledge of training methods to develop operational modules. The role also plans and manages ongoing CATI/CAPI operations, so production readiness is part of the job. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will increase the importance of training users on modern tools, documenting new workflows, and supporting deployment into secure enterprise environments. This will materially affect the role through greater emphasis on workforce enablement and operational stabilization.

This is a core subprocess for the position. It concerns ensuring people, processes and technology are ready to collect data, including training staff, configuring systems, preparing instruments, respondent communications, confidentiality procedures and readiness checks. The work description directly aligns: the incumbent 'leads and coordinates the 7-day statistical data collection activities,' manages interviewers and senior interviewers, develops operational plans and schedules, develops procedures for systems and safeguarding equipment/databases/files, identifies HR needs, approves training plans, and plans budgets for CATI/CAPI operations. The role also responds to inquiries, solicits participation from non-respondents, and negotiates collection applications and program conditions. Future-state drivers strongly intensify this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all point to digital readiness, online-first operations, APIs, adaptive collection, secure devices and channels, and major training needs. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access adds credentialing, confidentiality and secure setup requirements. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline increases pressure to complete readiness activities on fixed timelines. This role is therefore directly responsible for a subprocess that will undergo major transformation in technology, workforce skills and operating model.

This is the most directly relevant subprocess. It covers implementing collection, respondent contact and follow-up, managing respondent relationships and complaints, fieldwork management, monitoring collection and adjusting operations to improve quality. The work description is an exact match: the incumbent 'leads and coordinates the 7-day statistical data collection activities' for CATI/CAPI/PAPI; manages interviewers and interdisciplinary teams; 'sollicits participation from non-respondents and resolves complaints'; evaluates response patterns and respondent behaviour; prepares schedules and work plans for operation of collection systems; and assesses cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of collection activities. The capability involved is frontline operational management of live collection, respondent management, quality monitoring, staffing, scheduling and issue resolution. Future-state drivers cumulatively reshape this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production introduces chatbot-supported interactions, automated follow-up and real-time monitoring. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production shift operations toward online-first, adaptive collection, supplier-based receipt and mixed-source environments. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline makes deadline management and rapid intervention more central. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access adds secure channels and privacy controls during live operations. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases pressure to reduce manual follow-up and interviewer-heavy approaches. Workforce implications are direct: the role already manages interviewers and will increasingly need to lead staff through digital, automated and lower-touch collection models.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes loading collected data and metadata into processing environments, handling capture/conversion, analysing paradata, archiving instruments and versioning software-based collection tools. The work description shows responsibility for assessing functions associated with 'data collection, processing, editing, and compilation,' for safeguarding databases and files, and for evaluating quality and completeness of data and systems. The role is not explicitly described as performing ingestion or archiving, but it materially oversees the operational environment in which collection handoff occurs. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will make automated loading, metadata/paradata handling, pseudonymisation, versioning and secure handoff more important. This means the role will be increasingly affected through oversight of collection closure, quality evidence and readiness for downstream processing.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance. The work description notes that operational programs may involve 'the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses),' and the incumbent reviews and modifies operational techniques to meet such needs. That indicates awareness of and some contribution to integration-related operational issues. However, the role is primarily collection management rather than direct execution of data integration. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the extent to which collection operations are shaped by downstream integration requirements, but the connection remains indirect.

This subprocess is only weakly implicated. The work description includes assessment of processing and editing functions and evaluation of data quality, which may be affected by coding practices, but it does not assign direct responsibility for classification or coding routines. Future-state drivers around AI-enabled automated coding and efficiency may affect the broader collection-processing environment the manager oversees, especially where questionnaire design and collection applications influence coded responses, but the role is not materially responsible for coding operations.

This subprocess is relevant because the position assesses data quality, completeness, variances and comparability, and prepares evaluation reports on systems and data quality. Evidence includes: 'Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy'; 'Prepares evaluation reports outlining... the quality and completeness of data'; and assesses 'quality control of data.' The capability involved is operational quality assurance and validation-oriented analysis, especially from the collection and early processing perspective. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase automated validation, anomaly detection, mixed-source quality issues and exception-based review. This role will therefore be increasingly affected through monitoring quality indicators, interpreting anomalies, and advising on operational corrections even if formal data editing occurs elsewhere.

This subprocess has limited relevance. The work description explicitly includes assessment of editing functions and data quality, but not direct responsibility for changing data values or selecting imputation methods. The role may be affected by future automation and model-assisted editing because it assesses the efficiency and quality of editing activities and advises on systems and processes, but the responsibility described remains oversight and evaluation rather than direct edit/imputation execution.

This subprocess is only plausibly connected. The work description mentions integration of data from multiple sources and knowledge of questionnaire development and processing requirements, but it does not assign responsibility for deriving variables or units. Future-state shifts toward linked and administrative data may indirectly affect collection design and questionnaire content, yet the role remains peripheral to derivation work.

This subprocess has limited relevance. The position works in survey collection operations and evaluates response patterns and respondent behaviour, which can indirectly affect weighting and nonresponse adjustment, but there is no stated responsibility for weighting methodology or execution. Future adaptive collection and online-first strategies may make collection operations more influential on weighting assumptions, but the role remains indirect.

This subprocess is weakly relevant because the position oversees collection, processing and data quality and prepares reports on completeness and effectiveness, but the work description does not indicate direct responsibility for assembling final analytic datasets. The role may be affected by more automated handoffs and standardized outputs under integrated pipelines, yet the connection is mainly through upstream operational quality and readiness rather than direct file finalization.

This subprocess is only indirectly relevant. The position assesses the quality and completeness of data and compilation of statistical outputs and prepares summaries used by senior management, but does not appear to prepare analytical outputs for dissemination. The role may contribute operational context and quality evidence that informs draft outputs and methodological notes, especially as mixed-source and modernized methods require clearer explanation, but direct responsibility is not stated.

This subprocess has limited relevance. The incumbent interprets data quality, comparability over time and relevance, and prepares assessments for senior management and survey clients, which can support output validation. However, the work description does not assign responsibility for validating final statistical outputs against domain expectations. The role's connection is therefore supportive and operational rather than central.

This subprocess is weakly implicated because the position prepares reports and summaries that influence senior management decisions and provides advice on questionnaire and system changes affecting outputs, but there is no direct responsibility for release-ready statistical content, caveats or approval. Future governance and modernization pressures may increase demand for operational input into caveats and quality notes, but the role remains peripheral to final output approval.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it gathers feedback, paradata, system metrics, quality indicators and staff suggestions for evaluation. The position directly generates and uses such inputs through operational monitoring, respondent feedback, quality assessments and evaluation reports. Evidence includes evaluating 'response patterns and respondent behaviour,' soliciting participation from non-respondents and resolving complaints, preparing evaluation reports on systems and data quality, and assessing cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security. The role also prepares summaries used by senior management to assess objectives and resource utilization. These are classic evaluation inputs. Future-state drivers strongly increase this relevance. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will generate richer monitoring, telemetry, paradata and workflow metrics. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion adds source-quality and online-response indicators. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity adds staff feedback, training outcomes and adoption signals. This manager is therefore central to producing and interpreting evaluation evidence from collection operations.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position explicitly evaluates operational methods, systems, data quality, respondent behaviour, technology changes, costs and program effectiveness, and reports findings to senior management and clients. Evidence is extensive: 'Evaluates trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques'; 'Prepares assessments of questionnaire design, concepts, change in technology, respondent reaction and understanding'; 'Prepares evaluation reports outlining the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes and the quality and completeness of data'; and assesses 'cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security.' The capability involved is operational evaluation, synthesis of quality and performance evidence, and recommendation-oriented analysis. Future-state drivers make this even more central. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline adds milestone and schedule evaluation; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment requires evidence on savings, productivity and sustainability; AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production require evaluation of automation, quality, trust and workflow impacts; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity requires assessment of training, readiness and workforce sustainability. This role is therefore materially connected to formal and continuous evaluation of collection operations and modernization impacts.

This subprocess is relevant because the position has managerial authority, leads multidisciplinary teams, identifies HR needs, approves work plans and priorities, and proposes changes and improvements based on operational analysis. Evidence includes leading project teams and committees, approving work plans and priorities, recommending organizational structures and responsibilities, and proposing changes to questionnaire design, survey content, collection systems, processes, and hardware/software. That means the role participates in turning evaluation findings into operational actions. Future-state drivers strengthen this connection: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline requires milestone-based action plans; Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline requires explicit ownership and trade-offs; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment requires decisions on simplification, automation and staffing; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity requires leadership ownership, training actions and realistic sequencing. While the role may not be the final enterprise decision-maker, it clearly has the authority and expertise to shape and implement regional collection action plans based on evaluation findings.

This subprocess is the clearest material connection to the work description because it concerns responding to user queries, supporting access to services, maintaining knowledge resources such as FAQs/knowledge bases, and helping users navigate services. The work description is centered on employee-facing HR information and service navigation: the listed key activities are "HR A to Z index," "HR service standards," "Wellness at Statistics Canada," "HR committees," "HR contact list," and "Corporate service providers." Those activities align directly with the capability and operational need in 7.5 to record and respond to requests, provide guidance, and populate reusable support resources. An "HR A to Z index" is functionally similar to the subprocess's reference to a knowledge database or FAQ page; an "HR contact list" and "Corporate service providers" support routing users to the right service channels; and "HR service standards" aligns with the subprocess requirement to provide responses within agreed deadlines. Future-state drivers materially affect this work. Evidence includes: 'manipulates and processes data to generate tables, charts and data files'; 'Compiles data from a number of different but easily identifiable sources to produce statistical tables and charts'; 'Responds to requests from subject matter specialists and clients for custom tabulations'; and knowledge of 'marketing and dissemination of data.' The capability involved is assembling statistical content into usable dissemination products and responding to user-specific output needs. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push dissemination toward more standardized, metadata-rich, digital, and reusable products. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will also change product content and explanatory requirements. Because the work description directly includes producing tables/charts/files and custom tabulations for users, relevance is high.

This subprocess is strongly implicated because the role directly responds to user requests and inquiries, explains requirements and procedures, and liaises with clients, survey officers, respondents and data users. Evidence includes: 'Responds to requests from subject matter specialists and clients for custom tabulations'; 'liaises with survey officers, respondents and data users to understand and obtain clarifications'; 'Explains requirements and procedures for obtaining the information in the appropriate format'; and 'Responds to inquiries from managers, employees and the general public on the availability, consistency and application of statistical data and on the methods and techniques used.' The capability involved is front-line statistical user support, service response, clarification of methods and access, and communication with internal and external users. Future-state drivers are highly relevant. AI and Automation in Statistical Production will introduce AI assistants, chatbots, website search, and knowledge-base style support; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will enable self-service and controlled-access support models; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will change support toward helping users navigate metadata-rich assets; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase pressure for triaged and self-service support; and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will affect support for restricted access and confidentiality-related requests. The work description provides direct evidence of this responsibility, making relevance high.

Positions.Branch/Division: Communications and Information Services/ Communications and Library Services

implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess covers the detailed design of statistical outputs, products and services, including dissemination procedures and access arrangements. The capability involved is communications/dissemination design: shaping how outputs are presented, explained, accessed and supported. The work description places the position in "Communications and Information Services/ Communications and Library Services," which is direct evidence of a communications and dissemination-facing role, even though no task list is provided. That organizational placement makes this subprocess materially relevant because communications functions are regularly involved in how products are prepared for public-facing use and how dissemination approaches are supported. Future-state drivers increase the significance of this connection. AI and Automation in Statistical Production introduces AI chatbots, website search, enterprise platforms, documentation and transparency requirements, which change dissemination design toward more automated, searchable and interactive products while increasing public trust and quality expectations. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access is also relevant because dissemination design must increasingly account for privacy, secure access and authorization controls, especially where confidential outputs or differentiated access models exist. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure further shifts dissemination toward platform-based digital delivery, reusable tooling and secure access patterns. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is relevant because outputs increasingly need to be designed as searchable, metadata-rich assets. Workforce implications such as extensive coordination across communications, analysis and dissemination teams are especially pertinent to a position located in Communications and Library Services. Evidence is limited to branch/division only, so relevance is Medium rather than High.

This subprocess concerns building or reusing the components needed to disseminate statistical products, including web services, publications, open data outputs, maps and access channels. The capability involved is operational dissemination support: assembling or supporting the components through which products are delivered. The work description does not specify technical build duties, so no direct build responsibility can be inferred; however, the position sits in "Communications and Information Services/ Communications and Library Services," which is materially connected to dissemination components because communications and library services are part of the organizational environment that supports dissemination products and channels. Future-state drivers make this area more important. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure points to scalable web services, reusable dissemination tooling, secure access and platform-based delivery. AI and Automation in Statistical Production adds AI-enabled search, chatbot capabilities and reusable web/platform components, which will affect communications-facing dissemination environments. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is also relevant because dissemination components increasingly need to expose searchable metadata and standardized asset descriptions. Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development further pushes dissemination toward shared components, templates and governed reusable services. The work description provides only organizational evidence, not explicit responsibilities, so the position is best assessed as regularly contributing to or being affected by this subprocess rather than directly owning it.

This subprocess transforms processed data into draft statistical outputs and prepares accompanying methodological notes and explanatory material. The capability involved is preparing communications-ready output packages, including explanatory text and supporting context. The position's placement in "Communications and Information Services/ Communications and Library Services" is direct evidence that the role sits in the organizational area most plausibly connected to drafting, packaging, or supporting explanatory output materials, even though the work description does not list tasks. This makes the subprocess materially relevant because communications functions are regularly involved in preparing or refining draft outputs for user-facing release. Future-state drivers reinforce this connection. AI and Automation in Statistical Production affects draft output preparation through AI assistants, automation and stronger documentation/transparency requirements, meaning communications-related staff will increasingly work with AI-supported drafting and need to help ensure clear explanation of AI-supported methods. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production both increase the need for methodological explanation, quality notes, and clearer communication of mixed-source, linked-data, geospatial or model-based outputs. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability also matters because outputs increasingly need accompanying metadata and contextual information to be interpretable and reusable. Workforce implications such as extensive coordination across collection, communications, analysis and dissemination teams directly align with the branch context in the work description. Because no explicit drafting responsibility is stated, relevance remains Medium.

This subprocess is about understanding outputs and explaining their meaning using appropriate tools, media and analysis. The capability involved is explanatory communication: translating statistical results and methodological context into understandable messages for users. The strongest evidence in the work description is the organizational location in "Communications and Information Services/ Communications and Library Services," which makes this subprocess materially relevant because communications functions are regularly involved in explaining outputs, supporting interpretation, and helping users understand results. The role may not itself perform statistical interpretation, but it is meaningfully connected to the communication of interpreted outputs. Future-state drivers increase this relevance. AI and Automation in Statistical Production means analysts and communications staff may use AI assistants in daily work, but transparency and public trust require clearer explanation of outputs influenced by automated or AI-assisted methods. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the complexity of outputs by introducing linked, administrative, alternative, geospatial and model-based sources, which in turn raises the need for stronger explanatory capability and clearer communication of comparability issues, methodological changes and limitations. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is also relevant because it emphasizes analytical expertise, clear communication and training in new tools and methods. The evidence is organizational rather than task-specific, so Medium is the appropriate relevance.

This subprocess ensures outputs and associated information are fit for purpose and ready for release, including commentary, technical notes, briefings, metadata and approval support. The capability involved is final release preparation from a communications perspective: assembling supporting information, coordinating briefings and ensuring outputs are ready for use. The work description's branch/division, "Communications and Information Services/ Communications and Library Services," is direct evidence that the position is situated in the organizational area most likely to contribute to final output packaging and release support. Even without explicit duties, this makes the subprocess materially relevant. Future-state drivers strengthen the connection. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline is especially important because finalisation sits at the point where deadlines, approvals, caveats and release readiness must be reconciled; communications functions are often affected by fixed timelines, milestone discipline and rapid turnaround for final materials. AI and Automation in Statistical Production increases the need for caveats, technical notes and transparency where automated methods influence outputs. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is relevant because final outputs must include complete metadata as part of release readiness. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access also matters because release levels and supporting materials increasingly need to reflect privacy and controlled-access constraints. The branch evidence supports regular contribution or meaningful impact, but not direct approval authority, so relevance is Medium.

This subprocess produces dissemination products such as publications, press releases, websites, interactive graphics, tables, maps and downloadable files. The capability involved is core communications and dissemination production: preparing explanatory texts, assembling product components, editing products and checking publication standards. This is the most directly implicated subprocess based on the work description because the position is located in "Communications and Information Services/ Communications and Library Services," which is explicit organizational evidence of direct connection to communications and dissemination product work. Even though the work description lacks listed activities, the branch/division itself strongly indicates that the role operates in the area responsible for communications products and services. Future-state drivers materially reshape this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production introduces AI assistants, automation, chatbots and website search, which can automate parts of drafting and product assembly while increasing the need for transparency, quality statements and public trust safeguards. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure pushes dissemination products toward scalable, reusable, interactive digital formats supported by platforms, tooling and secure digital infrastructure. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is highly relevant because dissemination products increasingly need to be metadata-rich, searchable and reusable. Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development points toward standard templates, reusable publishing components and governed product assembly. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment adds pressure to standardize and automate recurring products as staffing tightens. Workforce implications such as extensive coordination across analysis, communications and dissemination teams directly match the branch context. Because the organizational evidence aligns directly with the subprocess purpose, relevance is High.

This subprocess manages release timing, briefings, embargoes, subscriber provision, controlled access for authorized users and possible retractions. The capability involved is release coordination and communications support around publication. The work description places the role in "Communications and Information Services/ Communications and Library Services," which is strong evidence of direct connection to release-related communications activities such as coordinating release materials, supporting briefings, and managing dissemination readiness from a communications standpoint. While the description does not explicitly state release authority, the branch placement makes this subprocess highly relevant because release of dissemination products is a core communications-facing function. Future-state drivers intensify this relevance. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline is especially important because release management is explicitly governed by fixed timelines, milestone discipline, clear authorities and contingency handling; communications roles are heavily affected by these timing and coordination pressures. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access is also highly relevant because release increasingly includes secure access for authorized users, embargo handling and controlled provision of confidential products. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure changes release channels through cloud-based dissemination platforms and controlled-access environments. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration adds more automated release sequencing and readiness gates, which changes how release-day coordination occurs. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability also matters because metadata completeness is increasingly part of release readiness. The branch/division evidence is sufficiently direct to support High relevance.

This subprocess records and responds to user queries and requests, supports services such as microdata access, maintains FAQs/knowledge bases, and supports partner organizations involved in dissemination. The capability involved is direct user-facing support and information service delivery. The work description's placement in "Communications and Information Services/ Communications and Library Services" is strong evidence that the role is in an organizational area directly connected to responding to users, supporting access to information products, and maintaining communications or library service channels. Among all subprocesses, this is one of the clearest matches to the branch/division named in the work description. Future-state drivers make this work likely to change substantially. AI and Automation in Statistical Production is highly relevant because AI chatbots, AI assistants and website search can automate responses, triage requests and populate knowledge bases, reducing manual effort but requiring governance, transparency and public trust safeguards. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure supports self-service platforms, case-routing tooling and controlled access workflows, changing how support is delivered. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access is relevant where support involves restricted services or microdata access, requiring authorization checks and privacy-aware responses. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability also matters because better metadata and searchable repositories shift some support toward helping users navigate standardized assets and interpret metadata. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases pressure for self-service, triage and FAQ reuse under reduced staffing. The branch/division evidence directly supports this subprocess, so relevance is High.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the work description explicitly involves designing and improving collection methods and operational approaches. The role 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' and 'provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding.' These are core collection-design and collection-method responsibilities. The capability involved is operational design of collection strategies, instruments, procedures, respondent/data-supplier interaction practices, and supporting operational specifications. The work description also states the position 'prepares and distributes procedures, operational specifications and training for the manual and automated collection, coding and processing of statistical data' and 'evaluates and recommends appropriate procedures, software and hardware for the collection, coding and processing of data,' which aligns strongly with designing collection modes and methods. Future-state drivers materially affect this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will shift collection design toward chatbot-assisted interaction, automation, and more workflow-integrated collection. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will push collection away from survey-only approaches toward online-first, adaptive collection, administrative inputs, and mixed-source acquisition. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will change the technical and security constraints under which collection methods are designed. Workforce implications are direct: the role already supports training and operational guidance, and future changes will require more digital collection, source-monitoring, and tool adoption skills. Impact mechanisms such as process streamlining, production workflow integration, reduced manual effort, online-first strategy, adaptive collection design, secure access, and modern tooling are all relevant because this position helps define procedures, specifications, and training for collection operations.

This subprocess is materially connected because the position helps define how data are coded, processed, tested, validated, and operationally handled after collection. The work description states the role participates in 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' evaluates 'methods, procedures and results of statistical collection, coding and processing operations and recommends alternatives,' and has knowledge of 'methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.' It also says the position 'develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems' and 'develops test cases and data from functional specifications and specifies testing approaches.' These are direct contributions to the design of processing rules, coding approaches, validation logic, and operational processing specifications. The capability involved is translating statistical and operational requirements into processing methods, system requirements, validation approaches, and quality controls. Future-state drivers will significantly reshape this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase use of AI-enabled automated coding, automated validation, and more advanced processing methods. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase the need for integration, source-specific validation, and harmonization rules. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make standardized metadata and lineage more central to processing design. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will shift work toward modular, orchestrated, repeatable processing steps. Workforce implications include reduced manual effort, greater need for workflow configuration and exception handling, and developing skills to support AI and modern technologies. Evidence from the work description includes preparing operational specifications, assessing system requirements, evaluating software and hardware, analyzing reported data and work results, and reporting on problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and instructions.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role contributes to how collection, coding, and processing activities fit together operationally across manual and automated environments. The work description shows direct involvement in end-to-end operational design through participation in 'implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations,' preparation of 'procedures, operational specifications and training,' development of 'system requirements' for analysts and programmers, and specification of 'testing approaches' to ensure applications meet requirements. The capability involved is workflow and production-system design: defining how staff, systems, procedures, and controls interact across operational stages. The role also 'participates in project teams, work groups, meetings and conferences in order to develop and improve work methods and practices,' which aligns with workflow redesign and operational integration. Future-state drivers are especially important here. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development all point to more integrated, reusable, automated workflows with clearer handoffs and stronger monitoring. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward leaner workflows, reuse, and fewer redundant manual steps. Workforce implications are substantial because this subprocess explicitly concerns staff interaction with systems and responsibilities; the work description already includes training, operational guidance, and collaboration across teams. Evidence includes the role's responsibility for operational specifications, system requirements, testing approaches, improving work methods, and understanding 'the conditions within which statistical operations will occur' to resolve issues affecting efficiency and quality.

This subprocess is relevant because the position contributes to the operational specification, testing, and training associated with collection instruments, even though the work description does not explicitly say the role builds instruments end-to-end. Evidence includes preparing and distributing 'procedures, operational specifications and training for the manual and automated collection' of data, developing 'system requirements' for analysts and programmers, and developing 'test cases and data from functional specifications' with specified testing approaches. Those activities materially support reuse or build of collection instruments and their readiness for production. The capability involved is operational translation of collection needs into specifications, test cases, and user guidance. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will change collection instruments toward digital, online-first, metadata-connected, and more reusable tools. Workforce implications include the need to provide employees with tools and training, reduce manual effort, and support digital readiness. The role's training and specification responsibilities indicate meaningful involvement, but because the work description does not explicitly assign instrument build ownership, relevance is medium rather than high.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because the role helps define and test processing components used in coding and data processing. The work description states the position 'develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems,' 'evaluates and recommends appropriate procedures, software and hardware for the collection, coding and processing of data,' and 'develops test cases and data from functional specifications and specifies testing approaches.' These are clear contributions to building or reusing processing components, even if the role is not described as the primary software builder. The capability involved is requirements definition, operational testing, and quality assurance for processing components. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will increase reuse of shared processing services, AI-enabled coding, and modular validation/transformation components. Workforce implications include upskilling in modern tools, more exception handling, and reduced manual effort. The work description provides strong evidence of contribution, but not sole ownership of component development, so medium relevance is appropriate.

This subprocess is relevant because the role contributes to configuring and operationalizing workflows through specifications, testing, and procedural guidance. Evidence includes preparing 'procedures, operational specifications and training' for manual and automated collection, coding and processing; developing system requirements; and specifying testing approaches to ensure applications meet requirements. The role also participates in teams to 'develop and improve work methods and practices,' which supports workflow configuration and refinement. The capability involved is translating designed workflows into configured operational procedures and tested system behavior. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase the importance of standardized, automated, secure workflow configuration with fewer manual handoffs. Workforce implications include a shift from manual execution to supervision and exception handling, plus greater need for orchestration skills. The work description supports regular contribution to this subprocess, though not explicit ownership of enterprise workflow tools, so medium relevance fits.

This subprocess is directly relevant because testing is explicitly part of the role. The work description states the position 'develops test cases and data from functional specifications and specifies testing approaches for own use and use by other program staff to ensure that computer applications meet requirements.' It also notes knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows, and responsibility for assessing system requirements for new processing systems. The capability involved is production-system testing, validation of assembled applications against requirements, and support for operational readiness. Future-state drivers intensify this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development all increase the complexity of testing interactions across automated, secure, reusable, and cloud-based services. Workforce implications include greater need for workflow/orchestration skills, more monitoring of automated runs, and upskilling in modern tools. The evidence is explicit and strong, making this a high-relevance subprocess.

This subprocess is relevant because the role contributes to documentation, training, and operational readiness for production systems. The work description states the position 'provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery,' writes 'survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports,' and prepares and distributes 'procedures, operational specifications and training.' These are core activities in finalizing systems for operational use. The capability involved is preparing users and operational documentation so systems can be used consistently and effectively. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the importance of user guidance, training, and production-readiness support as systems become more digital, automated, and platform-based. Workforce implications are especially relevant because the role already supports training and knowledge transfer, and future transformation will require more upskilling and transition support. Relevance is medium because the work description supports production readiness but does not explicitly assign deployment authority.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the role supports operational readiness for collection through procedures, training, user advice, and participation in collection operations teams. The work description says the position 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection,' 'provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding,' 'participates on data collection and operations teams,' and 'provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery.' The capability involved is preparing people, procedures, and operational supports so collection can run effectively. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will materially change collection setup toward digital tools, online response, secure channels, APIs, and more complex staff training needs. Workforce implications are central: the role already trains staff and advises users, and future-state changes will increase the need for digital readiness, technical support, and adaptable workforce capability. The evidence is direct and operational, supporting high relevance.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role directly participates in live collection operations. The work description explicitly states the position 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'participates on data collection and operations teams,' and 'contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities.' It also notes responding to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public about divisional systems and processes. The capability involved is operational execution of collection, respondent/data-supplier interaction, issue resolution, and monitoring of collection practices. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will change how collection is run through online-first channels, automated follow-up, supplier-based acquisition, real-time monitoring, and secure digital operations. Workforce implications include reduced manual effort in some areas but greater need for digital operations, exception handling, and communication skills.
