The work description provides direct evidence of collection execution responsibilities, making this high relevance.

This subprocess is relevant because the role works across collection, coding, and processing and evaluates the results of those operations, which implies involvement in the handoff from collection into processing. Evidence includes participation in 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' evaluation of 'methods, procedures and results,' and knowledge of verification methods to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications. The capability involved is ensuring collected data and associated operational outputs are ready for downstream processing and that procedures/results are assessed. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will make collection finalization more automated, metadata-rich, and security-sensitive. The role's operational and evaluative responsibilities suggest meaningful involvement, though the work description does not explicitly mention loading, archiving, or pseudonymisation, so medium relevance is appropriate.

This subprocess is relevant because the role works across collection, coding, and processing and has contextual knowledge of 'computer processing and data flows,' 'the application and conversion of databases,' and 'maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.' The work description also includes analyzing changes to data sources and outputs to determine impacts on integrity and completeness, and assessing system requirements for new processing systems. The capability involved is supporting operational integration of data sources and flows into coherent processing environments. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will increase the importance of integrating multiple sources, linked data, and metadata-rich assets. Workforce implications include the need for tools and training to handle more complex multi-source environments. Because the work description supports integration-related operational knowledge and analysis but does not explicitly assign record linkage or integration ownership, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is directly relevant because coding is explicitly central to the role. The work description repeatedly refers to 'collection, coding and processing of data,' including participation in manual and automated coding operations, evaluation of coding methods and results, advice to users on coding practices, and knowledge of coding-related methods and controls. The capability involved is operational coding, coding-method evaluation, and support for coding quality and consistency. Future-state drivers are highly material. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production directly point to AI-enabled automated coding, reduced clerical effort, and more machine-assisted classification. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase the need to harmonize non-standard source-system codes. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will strengthen use of common classifications and coding definitions. Workforce implications include reduced manual effort, increased need for AI and analytical tool skills, and more oversight of automated coding outputs. Evidence includes the role's direct participation in coding operations, evaluation of coding methods, and advice/training on coding practices.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role explicitly evaluates methods, procedures and results, verifies data reliability and consistency, analyzes reported data and work results, and reports on problems encountered in survey implementation. The work description includes 'knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications' and states the role 'analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists, presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered... and recommending alternatives.' The capability involved is input-data review, validation, quality assessment, and identification of operational or data issues. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase automated validation, anomaly detection, and multi-source quality assessment while reducing capacity for exhaustive manual review. Workforce implications include more exception handling, stronger analytical skills, and use of modern validation tools. The evidence is explicit and substantial, supporting high relevance.

This subprocess is relevant because the role evaluates data-processing results, verifies reliability and consistency, and works in coding and processing operations where correction-oriented decisions are often operationally adjacent. The work description does not explicitly mention editing or imputation, so responsibilities cannot be overstated. However, the role's knowledge of verification methods, analysis of reported data and work results, and recommendations of alternatives indicate meaningful contribution to identifying where data correction approaches may be needed. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment suggest that editing and imputation will become more automated and model-assisted, which will affect staff involved in processing quality and exception review. Workforce implications include reduced manual effort and increased need for oversight of automated correction methods. Because the work description supports adjacent contribution rather than explicit ownership, relevance is medium.

This subprocess has plausible but limited relevance. The work description includes knowledge of statistical and economic principles, systems analysis, data flows, database application and ad hoc manipulations/retrievals, and analysis of changes to data sources and outputs. These capabilities could support derivation activities in some operational contexts. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase reliance on derived variables from linked and administrative sources, which may indirectly affect this role's processing and operational support work. However, the work description does not explicitly state responsibility for deriving variables or units. Therefore, relevance is low and based on likely operational adjacency rather than direct assignment.

This subprocess is relevant because the role works across collection, coding, and processing and contributes to the procedures, specifications, testing, and analysis needed to produce reliable processed outputs. Evidence includes participation in manual and automated collection/coding/processing operations, preparation of operational specifications, development of test cases, and analysis of reported data and work results. The capability involved is helping ensure processed datasets are coherent, tested, and ready for downstream use. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will make finalization of data files more standardized, metadata-rich, and automated. Workforce implications include more monitoring of readiness and less manual packaging. The work description supports meaningful contribution to this subprocess, though not explicit ownership of final dataset assembly, so medium relevance is appropriate.

This subprocess is relevant because the role prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs, explanatory text, reports, and management reports. The work description explicitly states the position 'designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications' and 'writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports.' The capability involved is transforming operational and statistical results into draft analytical and publication-ready materials. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will affect how draft outputs are prepared through more automation, richer metadata, and greater need to explain modern methods. Workforce implications include use of AI assistants, stronger communication skills, and efficient standardized output preparation. Because the role clearly prepares output materials but is not described as the primary analytical authority for release products, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is relevant because the role analyzes outputs and data-source changes to determine impacts on integrity, completeness, consistency, and reliability. The work description states the position 'analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results' and has knowledge of locating, analyzing and comparing statistical output 'to ensure consistency and reliability.' The capability involved is checking outputs against expectations, consistency standards, and operational knowledge. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and AI and Automation in Statistical Production will increase the need to validate outputs affected by source substitution, linkage, automation, and methodological change. Workforce implications include stronger analytical judgment and more targeted validation under constrained staffing. The role contributes materially to output validation, though the work description does not frame it as a senior statistical sign-off role, so medium relevance fits.

This subprocess is relevant because the role prepares explanatory text, responds to enquiries about program results, and reports findings on survey conduct and implementation issues. Evidence includes responding orally and in writing to enquiries 'to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results,' preparing explanatory text for publications, and analyzing reported data/work results to present findings and recommend alternatives. The capability involved is explaining outputs, their operational context, and issues affecting interpretation. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need to explain outputs produced through mixed-source, automated, and modernized methods. Workforce implications include stronger communication and analytical expertise. Because the role clearly explains and contextualizes outputs but is not described as leading advanced domain interpretation, relevance is medium.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance. The role prepares supporting materials such as tables, charts, explanatory text, reports, manuals, and recommendations, all of which can feed final output packages. The work description also shows interaction with managers, subject matter specialists, and users, which supports pre-release coordination. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the importance of caveats, technical notes, and supporting documentation. However, the work description does not explicitly assign approval of statistical content, release-level decisions, or final output sign-off. Therefore relevance is low.

This subprocess is relevant because the role directly prepares components used in dissemination products. The work description states the position 'designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications' and writes reports and manuals. The capability involved is assembling core dissemination components such as tables, charts, explanatory text, and quality-related materials. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push dissemination product production toward more standardized, metadata-rich, digital, and reusable formats. Workforce implications include stronger digital-tool use, communication capability, and more templated production. Because the role clearly contributes to product content but is not described as owning dissemination channels or release management, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is relevant because the role responds to enquiries, advises users on methods and practices, and explains systems, processes, and results. The work description explicitly states the position 'provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding' and 'responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results.' The capability involved is user support, operational guidance, and explanation of methods and outputs. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will change this work through more self-service support, AI-assisted responses, knowledge-base use, and triaged support models. Workforce implications include the need for clear communication, digital support tools, and efficient service under staffing pressure. The evidence is direct, making this a solid medium-relevance subprocess.

This subprocess is relevant because the role evaluates methods, procedures, results, and operational changes, and prepares reports that can serve as evaluation inputs. The work description states the position evaluates collection, coding and processing methods/results, analyzes changes to data sources and outputs for impacts on integrity and completeness, and prepares reports for managers or subject matter specialists on how surveys were conducted, problems encountered, and alternatives. The capability involved is generating operational evidence, quality observations, and recommendations that feed evaluation. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase the amount of process metadata, system metrics, and workforce feedback relevant to evaluation. Workforce implications include more use of monitoring outputs and more structured evidence gathering. Because the role clearly produces evaluation-relevant inputs but is not described as leading formal evaluation, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is relevant because the role performs evaluative analysis of operational methods, results, and impacts, and recommends alternatives. Evidence includes evaluating 'methods, procedures and results of statistical collection, coding and processing operations and recommends alternatives,' analyzing changes to data sources and outputs to determine impacts on integrity and completeness, and preparing findings on survey conduct and implementation problems for managers and subject matter specialists. The capability involved is operational evaluation and synthesis of findings into recommendations for improvement. Future-state drivers such as Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make evaluation more focused on efficiency, automation outcomes, quality, timeliness, and workforce readiness. The role's analytical and reporting responsibilities align well with this subprocess, though not at enterprise governance level, so medium relevance is appropriate.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns identifying what statistics and services users need, including needs triggered by user requests and changing environments. The work description shows direct involvement in interpreting and responding to user demand: the position 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users,' and 'liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development.' That means the role contributes evidence about user needs and feasible responses, even if it does not formally approve program priorities. The capability involved is translating user demand into statistical products and operational implications. Future-state drivers make this more consequential: under Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, need identification will be more constrained by prioritization, fewer staff, and pressure to find efficient ways to meet requests. The position's existing role in assessing feasibility, interpreting requests, and evaluating impacts of changes in 'procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services' suggests it will increasingly need to help distinguish high-value requests from lower-priority or less feasible ones.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns defining the outputs required to meet confirmed user needs, including quality, scope, confidentiality and resource considerations. The position contributes to this through custom tabulations, dissemination, and advisory work: it 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' and 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users.' The role also applies legal and policy constraints, including 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.' That means the position helps operationalize what outputs can be produced and under what conditions. Future changes are driven by Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment: output objectives will be narrowed toward highest-value outcomes, with more explicit trade-offs among scope, timeliness and service levels. Because this role already evaluates feasibility, adapts data to new presentation formats, and resolves dissemination problems, it is likely to be increasingly affected by tighter output standardization and more explicit limits on bespoke products.

This is one of the most directly connected subprocesses. It covers detailed design of statistical outputs, products, services and dissemination procedures. The work description is centered on dissemination and output preparation: the position 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' 'drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data,' and 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats.' It also drafts manuals and training packages, which supports dissemination procedures and user understanding. The capability involved is designing and shaping usable statistical outputs, explanatory materials, and dissemination-ready products while respecting standards and confidentiality. Future-state drivers will materially change this work. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase the importance of secure-by-design dissemination and confidentiality-aware output choices, which aligns with the role's explicit requirement to apply the Statistics Act and Privacy Act. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will push outputs toward more standardized, searchable, metadata-rich assets. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will likely reduce bespoke dissemination and increase reusable, platform-based products. The role's current responsibility for modifying presentation formats, drafting explanatory material, and resolving dissemination problems is strong evidence of direct relevance.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it covers design of coding, editing, validation, integration and related analytical methods used in processing. The work description directly includes responsibilities in these areas: the position 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' 'evaluates problems related to the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical information,' 'implements enhancements or modifications to computer systems and applications used to edit, validate, market and disseminate statistical data,' and 'modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches to improve existing surveys or to meet specific new needs.' It also 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications' and analyzes effects on integration and coordination of data capture and processing functions. The capability involved is operational method design and refinement for validation, processing quality, and system-supported statistical production. Future-state drivers are cumulative here: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment all point toward more automated, reusable, metadata-driven, and integrated processing methods with less manual intervention. The role is already positioned at the intersection of methods, systems, validation and operational change, so these drivers are likely to materially reshape how the work is done.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it concerns end-to-end workflow design, reuse of systems and databases, and how staff interact with systems across production. The work description shows direct involvement in workflow and system change: the position 'implements enhancements or modifications to computer systems and applications used to edit, validate, market and disseminate statistical data,' 'liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' and 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' The role also participates on production and dissemination teams and project teams to improve work methods and practices. The capability involved is contributing operational expertise to production-system design, workflow integration, and staff-facing process improvements. Future-state drivers strongly intensify this relevance: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all affect how workflows are standardized, automated, monitored and staffed. Because the role already bridges subject-matter requirements, systems, processing, dissemination and training, it is materially connected to this subprocess now and in the future.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it covers reusing or building components needed for processing and analysis, including transformation and workflow-related services. The work description does not indicate software development ownership, but it does show operational contribution to component enhancement and suitability: the position 'implements enhancements or modifications to computer systems and applications used to edit, validate, market and disseminate statistical data,' 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' and examines revised processing specifications and their effects on integration. The capability involved is specifying, testing, and operationally validating processing components rather than building them from scratch. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development suggest more reusable and automated processing components, with stronger emphasis on validation, interoperability and supportability. This role is likely to be meaningfully affected because its current work already depends on assessing and implementing changes to processing applications and methods.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns building or reusing components needed for dissemination products. The position is not described as a technical builder of dissemination platforms, but it is materially connected through operational use, enhancement and quality assessment of dissemination-related systems. Evidence includes 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'implements enhancements or modifications to computer systems and applications used to edit, validate, market and disseminate statistical data,' and drafting reports, articles and manuals used in publications and dissemination. The capability involved is operational dissemination expertise, product assembly support, and input into dissemination tooling and content. Future-state drivers such as Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will likely shift dissemination toward reusable digital components, stronger metadata linkage, and more secure controlled release. The role will therefore be affected through changing dissemination tools, standards and workflows.

This subprocess is relevant because it covers testing assembled services, workflows, and system interactions to ensure production readiness. The work description provides direct evidence of system-quality assessment: the position 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' 'evaluates problems related to the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical information,' and 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications' to determine effects on integration and coordination. The capability involved is operational testing, quality assessment, and identifying impacts of system changes on statistical outputs and workflows. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will increase the complexity of testing interactions, automation, metadata flows and secure operations. This role is therefore materially connected as a user-side assessor of whether changed systems and workflows produce valid, reliable dissemination-ready outputs.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes documentation, user manuals, training and preparing systems for production use. The work description directly includes training and documentation responsibilities: the position 'provides input to training material and assists in the delivery,' 'drafts program information manuals and training packages for use by colleagues, operational staff and management, and assists in the delivery of training,' and participates in teams to improve methods and share knowledge. It also implements system enhancements, which links the role to operational readiness. The capability involved is helping operationalize new or modified systems through user-facing documentation, training and adoption support. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development make this increasingly important because modernized systems require more training, clearer procedures, and stronger workforce readiness. The evidence strongly supports relevance, especially on the workforce-enablement side.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance because it concerns loading collected data and metadata into environments for further processing, including format conversion and metadata/paradata handling. The work description is not collection-focused, but it does include reviewing outputs from computer applications and databases, assessing validity of processed data, and examining effects of revised processing specifications on data capture and processing integration. That suggests some downstream involvement with the handoff from collection into processing. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure may increase the extent to which downstream production staff need to understand automated ingestion, metadata linkage and standardized handoffs. However, the work description does not directly assign collection-finalization responsibility, so relevance remains low.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns combining data from multiple sources, harmonising outputs, and producing consolidated datasets. The work description does not explicitly assign record linkage or enterprise integration ownership, but it does show related responsibilities: the position 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output,' 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, depending on the complexity of the subject matter or the number of different sources,' and examines effects of revised processing specifications on 'integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' The capability involved is operational integration and harmonisation of source data for output production and consistency. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will make integration more central, more automated, and more metadata-dependent. This role is likely to experience meaningful change because its current work already depends on combining and adapting data from multiple sources for dissemination.

This subprocess has limited relevance. The work description does not explicitly mention coding text responses or applying classifications after collection. There is some indirect connection through 'modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches,' knowledge of socio-economic concepts and methods, and use of analytical software, which could affect classification consistency in outputs. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may indirectly affect the role if coding becomes more automated and embedded in production workflows that feed dissemination products. However, because coding responsibilities are not stated in the work description, relevance remains low.

This is a core subprocess for the position. The work description explicitly states that the role 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' 'analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' and has knowledge 'to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.' It also evaluates problems related to editing and validation and provides solutions or recommendations. The capability involved is detecting errors, inconsistencies and quality issues in data and systems before dissemination. Future-state drivers strongly reinforce this relevance: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all point toward more automated validation, more heterogeneous sources, stronger metadata checks, and greater emphasis on exception handling rather than routine manual review. This role is directly in scope for those changes.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description explicitly includes editing and problem resolution, though it does not explicitly mention imputation. Evidence includes 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'evaluates problems related to the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical information,' and knowledge used 'to assess the validity of collected and processed data.' The capability involved is correcting or improving data quality through editing-related decisions and method adjustments. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment suggest more automated, rule-based and model-assisted correction processes with stronger metadata and audit requirements. Because imputation is not explicitly assigned, relevance is medium rather than high, but the editing component is clearly material.

This subprocess is relevant because the role adapts and transforms data into new forms needed for outputs. Evidence includes 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output,' and 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, depending on the complexity of the subject matter or the number of different sources.' The capability involved is deriving output-ready variables, classifications or presentation structures from existing data, even if the role is not described as a formal methodologist for derived units. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase reliance on derived variables from integrated and administrative sources and on reusable derivation logic. The role's current adaptation and custom-tabulation work makes this a meaningful connection.

This subprocess is relevant because the position produces tables, charts and custom tabulations from compiled data. Evidence includes 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations' and 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output.' The capability involved is transforming microdata or source data into aggregated statistical outputs for users and dissemination. Future-state drivers such as Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration suggest more automated aggregate generation, more granular outputs, and faster recurring production. The role is not described as designing weighting or estimation methods, but it clearly contributes to aggregate production and will likely be affected by increased automation and standardization of those outputs.

This subprocess is relevant because it assembles the results of processing into datasets used for analysis and downstream output production. The work description shows involvement in preparing and validating output-ready data: the position compiles data from diverse sources, adapts data to new definitions or formats, assesses validity of processed data and database contents, and examines effects of changes in procedures and technology on 'data output, products and services.' The capability involved is preparing coherent, reliable, analysis- and dissemination-ready data outputs. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will make final datasets more standardized, metadata-rich and automatically handed off. This role is likely to be affected because its current work already depends on reliable final data structures for tabulation and dissemination.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it transforms processed data into statistical outputs and accompanying explanatory material. The work description directly matches this: the position 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output,' 'summarizes and describes meaning of data,' and 'drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used.' The capability involved is preparing draft statistical products and methodological explanation for publication and user use. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will change how draft outputs are assembled, documented and explained, with more automation, more metadata packaging, and greater need to explain modern methods clearly. This is central to the role.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it concerns validating outputs against expectations, metadata, quality indicators and domain knowledge. The work description provides strong evidence: the position 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' 'assesses trends and developments in the subject area,' and uses knowledge of current economic and social issues 'to identify and assess trends and issues represented by statistical data series.' It also compares related statistical output to ensure 'consistency and reliability.' The capability involved is subject-matter-informed validation of outputs before release or client delivery. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase the need for risk-based, metadata-aware, method-aware validation of outputs produced from more complex and automated pipelines. The role is directly implicated.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role explicitly interprets and explains statistical outputs. Evidence includes 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users,' 'summarizes and describes meaning of data,' 'drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used,' and knowledge of current economic and social issues to assess trends represented by data series. The capability involved is analytical interpretation, explanation of meaning, and communication of statistical results to users and colleagues. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need to explain outputs produced from mixed sources, automated methods and changing methodologies in clear, trustworthy ways. This is a direct and enduring part of the role.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it includes consistency checks, caveats, supporting information, technical notes, internal documents and approval-ready statistical content. The work description aligns strongly: the position edits, validates and disseminates data; drafts reports and articles included in publications; summarizes and describes meaning of data; and drafts manuals and training packages. It also applies legal and confidentiality requirements under the Statistics Act and Privacy Act. The capability involved is preparing outputs and supporting materials so they are fit for use and ready for release or client delivery. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase demands for stronger metadata, clearer caveats, faster but disciplined finalization, and more explicit explanation of methods and confidentiality constraints. The role's current publication and dissemination responsibilities make this highly relevant.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns formatting, loading and linking data and metadata into dissemination systems. The work description does not explicitly assign database loading responsibility, but it does show close operational involvement with dissemination systems: the position 'implements enhancements or modifications to computer systems and applications used to edit, validate, market and disseminate statistical data,' reviews data quality from systems and databases, and works with outputs and presentation formats. The capability involved is ensuring dissemination systems and their outputs are operationally usable and quality-assured. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will make metadata linkage, automated loading and secure dissemination-system updates more central. The role is therefore meaningfully affected even if not the primary technical owner.

This is a core subprocess for the position. It covers preparing explanatory texts, tables, charts, maps, quality statements and assembling them into dissemination products. The work description directly matches this: the position 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output,' 'drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data,' and those reports are 'included in publications.' The capability involved is producing dissemination-ready statistical products and explanatory content. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will push this work toward more standardized, metadata-rich, digitally assembled products with stronger accessibility, quality and explanatory requirements. The evidence is direct and substantial.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns ensuring all elements for release are in place, including timing, briefings, subscriber provision and controlled access. The work description clearly includes dissemination and client service, though not formal release authority: the position 'disseminates data,' 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users,' and drafts publication content reviewed by managers. The capability involved is operational support to release readiness and delivery of products to users. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will affect release timing, secure access, metadata completeness and digital release channels. Because the role disseminates products and serves users but is not described as owning embargoes or release approvals, relevance is medium.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role directly supports users and responds to requests. Evidence is explicit: the position 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users,' and drafts explanatory reports and articles on interpretation and use of statistical data. The capability involved is responding to user queries, tailoring outputs, explaining methods and supporting access to statistical information. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will change how support is delivered: more self-service, AI-assisted responses, searchable knowledge resources, and stronger controls around secure or confidential access. The role is already directly engaged in user-facing support, so this subprocess is materially connected now and in the future.

This subprocess is relevant because it gathers feedback, process metadata, system metrics and staff suggestions for evaluation. The work description shows the role generates and uses several such inputs: it reviews and assesses data quality from systems and databases, analyzes effects of changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services on outputs, participates in project teams to improve methods and practices, and liaises with users whose requests and feedback can indicate changing needs. The capability involved is producing operational evidence about quality, system performance, user demand and process impacts. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the amount of process telemetry, quality indicators and workforce feedback available and needed. The role is not an evaluator by title, but it clearly contributes important evaluation inputs.

This subprocess is relevant because it analyzes evaluation inputs, compares performance to expectations and recommends changes. The work description does not assign formal evaluation-report ownership, but it does show evaluative responsibilities: the position 'assesses trends and developments,' 'reviews the potential impact on program subject-matter content,' 'evaluates problems related to the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical information,' 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services,' and examines effects of revised processing specifications on integration and coordination. The capability involved is operational assessment of quality, methods, systems and service impacts, which is a core input to evaluation. Future-state drivers such as Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make evidence-based evaluation of efficiency, quality, automation and workforce readiness more important. The role is therefore materially connected, though not as the final decision-maker.

Positions.Branch/Division: Strategic Analysis, Publication, and Training (SAPT) Division

implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it covers the design of statistical methodology, validation, coding, editing, integration and analysis approaches, and the work description is explicitly centred on teaching and coaching staff on the interpretation and application of Statistics Canada survey, subject matter and statistical learning business practices and methodologies. The capability involved is methodological subject-matter expertise, quality assurance awareness, troubleshooting of interpretation problems, and the ability to translate evolving business practices into training materials and tools. The position fulfills this need by 'provid[ing] technical subject matter expertise and coaching support to course participants,' by 'continually studying changes to business practices of Statistics Canada survey, subject matter, and statistical learning programs,' and by ensuring trainees comply with methodologies and receive guidance on 'live case scenarios.' Future-state drivers make this work more affected over time even if the position is not itself designing production methods: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all increase the pace of methodological change and the need for staff to understand new tools, validation logic, metadata-rich processes, and more automated production methods. Workforce implications such as 'provide employees with the tools and training they need,' 'support a skilled and adaptable workforce,' and 'developing skills to support the adoption of modern, open-source technologies and AI' align directly with this role's training mandate. The impact mechanism is mainly indirect but material: as processing and analysis methods modernize, this role must update training content, coach staff on new practices, and help close performance gaps. Evidence includes 'Knowledge of the theories and principles of Business and Economic development, Survey development is required,' 'Knowledge of training delivery methods and practices,' and 'Conducts research and analysis of changes to Survey, Subject Matter and Statistical learning programs-related business practices.'

This subprocess is relevant because it explicitly includes how staff interact with systems and who is responsible for what and when across the production process. The work description is not responsible for designing enterprise workflows, but it is materially connected through workforce preparation, role clarification, and training adaptation to changing business practices. The capability involved is translating evolving operational workflows and responsibilities into usable learning content, coaching, and performance support. The position fulfills this need by monitoring changes to Statistics Canada business practices, adapting learning sessions to different levels of knowledge, identifying performance gaps, and ensuring training materials 'reflect current business policies and practices.' Future-state drivers make this increasingly important: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all imply changing staff-system interactions, clearer handoffs, more automation, and new role expectations. Relevant capability themes and workforce implications include 'clarifying handoffs across programs,' 'production workflow integration,' 'shift from manual step execution to pipeline supervision,' 'greater emphasis on exception handling,' 'clarity of roles, responsibilities, and priorities,' and 'training.' The impact mechanism on this role is that workflow redesign and platform modernization will require continual revision of training text, simulation exercises, and coaching approaches so staff can operate in new environments. Evidence includes 'Contributes to new skill development by providing day-to-day technical guidance and direction to course participants,' 'monitors and identifies performance gaps and develops and recommends coaching and training plans,' and 'Ensures that training text, handouts, simulation exercises and testing tools reflect current business policies and practices.'

This is one of the most directly implicated subprocesses because it explicitly includes producing documentation, user manuals, and training users on how to operate the process. The work description aligns strongly with that responsibility: the position develops, adapts and drafts training materials and tools; mentors and coaches participants; ensures training products reflect current business policies and practices; and works with learning specialists to transpose technical subject-matter knowledge into adult learning methodologies. The capability involved is operational training, documentation upkeep, user readiness, and translation of technical business practices into learnable content. The position fulfills this need directly through day-to-day coaching, technical guidance, training-plan development, and maintenance of training text, handouts, simulation exercises and testing tools. Future-state drivers intensify this connection. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is especially relevant because training is explicitly central to the subprocess and to the role; AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline all increase the need for updated user guidance, faster rollout training, and support for staff transitions. Relevant workforce implications include 'provide employees with the tools and training they need,' 'support a skilled and adaptable workforce,' 'agency staff will integrate AI assistants into their daily work to increase efficiency,' 'transition programs to modern corporate platforms,' and 'training, mentorship, and realistic sequencing of work.' Impact mechanisms include increased documentation requirements, production-readiness training, and support for adoption of modern tools and workflows. Evidence from the work description is explicit: 'Writing skills are required to develop, adapt and draft training materials and tools,' 'mentor and coach throughout the duration of the course,' 'provide day-to-day coaching,' and 'work in close cooperation with Learning Specialist and transpose technical subject matter knowledge into adult learning methodologies.'

This subprocess is relevant because it includes training staff and preparing people, processes and technology for collection operations. The work description does not state that the position sets up collection systems directly, but it does show responsibility for training staff on survey and subject-matter business practices and for keeping that training current as practices change. The capability involved is workforce readiness for operational statistical activities, especially where survey and collection-related business practices are part of the curriculum. The position fulfills this need by studying changes to 'Statistics Canada survey, subject matter, and statistical learning programs,' identifying coaching and training needs, and adapting learning sessions to individual performance requirements. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will change collection operations toward online-first, mixed-source, digital and automated environments. That means training roles like this one will need to update materials and coaching to prepare staff for new collection tools, source-management practices, and digital workflows. Relevant workforce implications include 'provide employees with the tools and training they need,' 'support a skilled and adaptable workforce,' 'recruitment of thousands of employees,' and 'skills transition in data, methods, and digital tools.' Evidence includes the requirement for 'Knowledge of Stats Can’s mandate, and business practices in order to ensure that the training programs accurately reflects Stats Can business practices' and the responsibility to ensure training materials reflect 'current business policies and practices.'

This subprocess is relevant because the role is fundamentally support-oriented in a learning environment: it responds to participant questions, provides guidance, troubleshoots interpretation issues, and adapts explanations to user needs. While the users here are internal course participants rather than external dissemination users, the subprocess's core capability of recording and responding to queries, supporting service delivery, and building reusable guidance is materially analogous to the work described. The capability involved is responsive support, explanation of methods and practices, and creation of reusable support materials. The position fulfills this need by mentoring and coaching participants, responding to concerns and information requests, researching atypical issues, and adapting communication style, tone and terminology to varying knowledge levels. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity suggest support models will become more digital, more self-serve, and more dependent on clear, reusable guidance and FAQs. Even if the work description does not mention chatbots or formal service desks, the cumulative effect is that internal training/support roles will likely need to provide more scalable support content and help staff navigate modernized tools and methods. Relevant impact mechanisms include automation reducing manual effort, knowledge-base style reuse of responses, and increased need for clear communication under workforce adjustment. Evidence includes 'respond to concerns and information request from course participants,' 'respond to questions on methodologies accordingly,' and 'research, analyze and resolve interpretation problems.'

This subprocess is relevant because the work description includes monitoring trainee performance, tracking deficiencies, evaluating problems encountered, and preparing reports and correspondence. Those activities are forms of gathering evaluation inputs about training effectiveness, performance gaps, and operational issues. The capability involved is collecting evidence on learner needs, deficiencies, and changing business-practice impacts so that training and related processes can be improved. The position fulfills this need by identifying and analyzing coaching and training needs, tracking and evaluating problems encountered, recording and following up on deficiencies, and conducting monitoring and quality assurance exercises. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the importance of continuous feedback, performance indicators, and staff-readiness evidence. Relevant workforce implications include monitoring adoption of new tools, assessing training effectiveness, and supporting a skilled and adaptable workforce under modernization and staffing pressure. The impact mechanism is that as business practices change faster, this role's monitoring and reporting functions become more important inputs to future training adjustments and broader workforce transformation decisions. Evidence includes 'track and evaluate problems encountered,' 'recording and following up on deficiencies,' 'conduct monitoring and quality assurance exercises,' and 'prepare reports and correspondence.'

This subprocess is relevant because the role does more than collect issues; it analyzes them and recommends changes. The work description shows evaluative responsibilities tied to training performance, methodological compliance, and changing business practices. The capability involved is synthesizing observed deficiencies, performance gaps, and business-practice changes into recommendations for improved training products and approaches. The position fulfills this need by identifying and analyzing coaching and training needs, assessing content, recommending and initiating changes, and conducting research and analysis of changes to business practices. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production make evaluation more important because training programs must quickly assess whether staff are ready for new tools, methods, and workflows. Relevant impact mechanisms include dashboard-like monitoring of readiness, evaluation of adoption success, and recommendations for continuous improvement under constrained resources. Evidence includes 'monitors and identifies performance gaps and develops and recommends coaching and training plans,' 'assess the content of training case study materials and tools and recommend and initiate changes,' and 'Conducts research and analysis of changes to Survey, Subject Matter and Statistical learning programs-related business practices.'

This subprocess has a plausible but limited connection. The work description does not indicate formal decision-making authority to approve enterprise action plans, but it does show that the position develops and recommends coaching and training plans and recommends solutions to resolve methodological or performance issues. The capability involved is translating evaluation findings into practical improvement actions within the training context. The position fulfills this need at a local level by recommending coaching and training plans, following up on deficiencies, and working with subject-matter resources to design new products reflecting changes to business practices. Future-state drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity may increase pressure for clearer prioritization of training interventions, faster implementation of updates, and stronger accountability for workforce-readiness actions. However, because the work description does not show formal governance or approval authority, relevance remains low. Evidence includes 'develops and recommends coaching and training plans,' 'recommend solutions to resolve these issues,' and 'working with subject matter resources in the design of new products to reflect changes to business practices.'

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns identifying what information is needed, often using environmental scanning, periodic review, and lessons from prior evaluations. The work description directly supports that need through evaluation, strategic review, and analysis of emerging issues affecting programs and operations. The position 'prepares program evaluation reports and documents on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of existing programs, operations and initiatives,' 'collects and analyzes foundation data' to create new information about programs and their effectiveness, and 'reviews emerging issues, trends and developments impacting government operations' to recommend strategies. Those responsibilities align with identifying information needs and reassessing them in light of changing operating conditions. The capability involved is analytical evaluation of program relevance, effectiveness, and future information requirements for management decision-making. Future-state drivers make this more important: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will intensify prioritization of needs under fiscal constraint, requiring sharper triage of what programs and information demands can be sustained. The work description already shows this role advising on 'scope, structure, redefinition or termination of major programs, initiatives, operations or activities,' which is exactly the kind of evidence-based need identification that becomes more consequential as resources tighten and efficiencies are sought.

This subprocess is implicated because it is about defining objectives, quality expectations, and trade-offs for outputs within governance and resource constraints. The work description shows direct involvement in planning, priority setting, performance measurement, monitoring and reporting, and in advising managers on integrating evaluation methodologies into program and policy design. Evidence includes providing consultative services related to 'strategic, annual and long-term evaluation plans, priority setting, strategic planning, policy development, performance measurement, monitoring and reporting,' and preparing information used by management to make decisions on 'scope, structure, redefinition or termination' of major activities. The capability involved is setting and advising on performance and accountability objectives, including what should be measured and reported. Future changes are driven by Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. Those drivers increase the need for explicit trade-offs, accountability, and focus on highest-value outcomes. This role is likely to be increasingly affected because it already supports management accountability frameworks, evaluation plans, and recommendations on improving policies, programs and operations under constrained resources.

This subprocess is materially connected because it involves documenting options, costs, benefits, risks, resource needs, and recommendations for approval. The work description does not use the term business case explicitly, but it clearly describes closely related responsibilities: developing strategic recommendations and proposals; writing reports, working papers, background and briefing material for senior officials; planning and budgeting for studies and projects; negotiating contracts; and providing critical information for system applications such as the LTP database, Risk Profile and Management Accountability Framework. The capability involved is assembling evidence for decision-making, including operational analysis, risk, resource implications, and recommendations for senior management and governance bodies. Evidence includes 'develops strategic recommendations and proposals,' 'writes reports, working papers, background and briefing material for the direct use of analysts and senior officials,' and 'plans and budgets for on-going studies and/or special projects.' Future-state drivers strengthen this connection. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline mean approval processes will demand clearer prioritization, explicit trade-offs, milestone discipline, and stronger accountability. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase emphasis on affordability, savings, and workforce implications. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is also relevant because the role already develops training plans, coordinates teams, and supports methodological evolution, all of which are likely to become more prominent in approval-oriented planning and change proposals.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns designing outputs, products, services, and associated explanatory material. The work description is not a dissemination production role, but it contributes materially through design of reporting and accountability frameworks and performance reporting approaches. Evidence includes providing advice and guidance regarding 'the development and implementation of reporting and performance review frameworks, processes and tools,' and strengthening 'performance reporting to Parliament and the public.' The capability involved is designing what information products and accountability outputs should look like, including standards, frameworks, and explanatory structures. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will affect this work by increasing the need for standardized, metadata-rich, accessible, and well-explained outputs. Because the role develops methodologies, tools and techniques and communicates with senior management, central agencies, and other organizations, it is meaningfully connected to how outputs are structured and explained, even if not directly building dissemination systems.

This subprocess is implicated because it covers design of analytical methods, validation, integration, and methodological rules used in processing and analysis. The work description shows strong methodological and analytical responsibilities: 'develops methodologies, tools and techniques,' uses statistical methods and techniques to conduct research and analysis, develops new tools for statistical analysis in response to unique problems, and works with performance indicators, monitoring and reporting procedures. The capability involved is methodological design for analysis and evaluation, including selecting data sources, developing tools, and structuring analytical approaches for complex, sensitive issues. Evidence includes 'knowledge of concepts, methods and techniques to develop evaluation standards and performance indicators,' 'knowledge of statistical methods and techniques,' and 'develops new tools for statistical analysis in response to unique problems.' Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity suggest this role will be increasingly affected as analytical design becomes more automated, metadata-dependent, and integrated with enterprise platforms. The role is not a production-methods designer for official statistics broadly, so relevance is medium rather than high.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns end-to-end workflow design, reuse of systems, and defining staff interaction with systems and responsibilities. The work description shows involvement in system-related planning and accountability infrastructure rather than technical workflow engineering. Evidence includes providing the manager with 'critical information for the development, use and maintenance of various system applications such as the LTP database, Risk Profile and the Management Accountability Framework,' and planning, organizing and coordinating project teams with goals, priorities, milestones, schedules, and human resource needs. The capability involved is designing or informing governance and operational workflows around planning, evaluation, accountability, and system use. Future-state drivers make this more important: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all point toward clearer handoffs, leaner workflows, stronger role clarity, and more platform-enabled operations. The role is materially affected because it already works at the intersection of systems, accountability frameworks, project coordination, and management processes.

This subprocess is relevant because it involves combining information from multiple sources and harmonizing it for analysis. The work description does not describe operational data integration pipelines, but it does describe selecting data sources, collecting and analyzing foundation data, synthesizing information from diverse disciplines, and defending analyses drawn from 'a wide variety of sources with varying degrees of technical complexity.' The capability involved is analytical integration of evidence across sources for evaluation, accountability, and strategic recommendations. Evidence includes 'selects data sources to be used,' 'collects and analyzes foundation data,' and 'skill in synthesising information from diverse disciplines.' Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment suggest this role will increasingly need to assess and use more heterogeneous sources in evaluation and planning work. The role is not directly responsible for production integration routines, so relevance is medium.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role directly prepares analytical and evaluative outputs for management and stakeholders. Evidence is explicit: the position 'prepares program evaluation reports and documents,' 'writes reports, working papers, background and briefing material,' and prepares briefing notes, memoranda, reports, and analytical documents. It also presents findings and recommendations to senior officials and stakeholders. The capability involved is transforming analysis into usable outputs, including reports, briefings, and methodological documentation. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will affect how these outputs are produced, standardized, documented, and accelerated. The work description also notes the need to adapt large volumes of information and specialized terminology to improve departmental policies, programs and operations, which is central to draft output preparation.

This subprocess is materially connected because the role validates findings against expectations, evidence, and accountability requirements before they are used by management. The work description emphasizes assessing economy, efficiency and effectiveness; monitoring and assessing management accountability; defending results of analysis; integrating conflicting stakeholder views; and working in highly sensitive areas requiring solid proof of findings. The capability involved is analytical validation of outputs, conclusions, and performance information. Evidence includes 'monitors and assesses management accountability for departmental programs,' 'the areas under evaluation are highly sensitive and require solid proof of findings,' and 'defends the results of analysis of complex issues.' Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase the complexity of validating outputs as methods, sources, and automation change. This role is already responsible for ensuring findings are credible enough for senior management, central agencies, and stakeholders.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the role interprets complex analytical results and explains them to decision-makers and stakeholders. Evidence includes researching and analyzing 'complex, multi-dimensional and interrelated variables and issues,' assessing socio-economic impacts, presenting options and recommendations, and using oral and written skills to explain and clarify issues, present arguments, and report findings and recommendations to senior officials and stakeholders. The capability involved is substantive interpretation of analytical outputs in policy, accountability, and evaluation contexts. The work description also highlights knowledge of economics, public policy administration, management science, and social science research methods, which supports interpretation from multiple perspectives. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need to explain outputs produced from more complex methods, mixed sources, and modern tools. This is a core function of the position.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role prepares final reports, recommendations, briefings, and supporting documentation for senior management and external stakeholders.
