Evidence includes preparing program evaluation reports and documents, writing briefing material for direct use by analysts and senior officials, presenting findings and recommendations, and adapting specialized information to improve policies, programs and operations. The capability involved is ensuring outputs are complete, decision-ready, and appropriately documented for release or internal use. The role also liaises with Treasury Board Secretariat and the Industry Portfolio Office to ensure compliance to established standards, which supports final quality and approval discipline. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase pressure for timely, well-governed, clearly caveated, and well-documented outputs. The work description's emphasis on politically sensitive issues, urgent high-profile evaluations, and short deadlines further supports strong relevance.

This subprocess is directly implicated because the role gathers and analyzes evidence used for evaluation. Evidence includes collecting and analyzing foundation data, selecting data sources, monitoring and assessing management accountability, maintaining project working files containing evidence, findings, conclusions and recommendations, and using sensitive documentation to undertake evaluations and reviews. The capability involved is assembling evaluation evidence, indicators, and supporting records for assessment and reporting. The work description explicitly states that project files contain 'evidence (specimens, analysis-documentation, project findings, conclusions and recommendations) gathered during the course of evaluations and reviews.' Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will expand the kinds of inputs available and expected, including system metrics, metadata, and staff feedback. This role is already central to gathering and organizing evaluation evidence.

This is one of the most directly connected subprocesses. The work description is fundamentally an evaluation and research role: it prepares program evaluation reports on economy, efficiency and effectiveness; monitors and assesses management accountability; recommends improvements to policies, programs and operations; develops analytical reviews and strategic recommendations; and develops methodologies, tools and techniques for evaluation and review activities. The capability involved is conducting formal evaluation, synthesizing evidence, benchmarking performance, and producing recommendations for future action. Evidence is extensive throughout the description, including consultative services related to strategic and long-term evaluation plans, performance measurement, monitoring and reporting. Future-state drivers such as Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all intensify the importance of evaluation as a mechanism for prioritization, modernization assessment, workforce adaptation, and continuous improvement. This role is directly responsible for that work.

This subprocess is relevant because the role develops recommendations and supports decision-makers who would agree and monitor action plans, even if the work description does not explicitly state final approval authority. Evidence includes recommending ways to improve departmental policies, programs and operations; developing strategic recommendations and proposals; reviewing emerging issues to recommend strategies; and providing critical information to management frameworks and system applications. The capability involved is translating evaluation findings into actionable recommendations and supporting governance decisions. The role also plans and coordinates project teams, sets objectives and milestones, and liaises with central agencies to ensure compliance, which supports implementation-oriented follow-through. Future-state drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make action planning more disciplined, time-bound, and resource-constrained. Because the description supports but does not clearly own final action-plan approval, relevance is medium rather than high.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns the initial investigation of what statistical information users need. The work description directly states that the position "investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used," which is a direct match to identifying needs. The capability involved is user-needs assessment, scoping of statistical requests, and determining feasible approaches for meeting those needs. The position fulfills this need through client-facing requirement analysis, defining special studies, and adapting or developing approaches for specific requests. Future-state change is likely to come from the driver Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment: under fiscal constraint, need identification will become more selective and triaged, with stronger pressure to prioritize high-value requests and use AI, automation, machine learning, and new tools and methods to meet needs more efficiently. This is especially relevant because the role already modifies techniques and develops new approaches, so future changes will likely shift that work toward lower-cost, more standardized or automated ways of satisfying user demand.

This subprocess is implicated because the role helps define what outputs will be produced, their scope, and the constraints under which they will be delivered. Evidence includes: "Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources" and knowledge of "departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination." The capability involved is setting output objectives, balancing scope, quality, timeliness, confidentiality, and resources, and aligning outputs with user and organizational requirements. The position fulfills this through project definition, prioritization, and dissemination policy application. Future changes are driven by Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. These drivers imply more explicit trade-offs, stronger accountability, and tighter limits on scope, frequency, granularity, and service levels. Because the role already defines priorities and prepares plans, it is likely to face more disciplined governance, clearer approval expectations, and stronger pressure to standardize outputs and focus scarce resources on highest-value outcomes.

This subprocess is materially connected because the position determines data sources and assesses whether they can support special requests, studies, and integrated outputs. Evidence includes: "determines the sources of data for special requests," "Some studies may involve ... the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses)," and "Knowledge of data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements." The capability involved is assessing source suitability, continuity, compatibility, legal/policy constraints, and operational feasibility. The role fulfills this by selecting sources, integrating conceptually different data, discussing reporting agreements, and ensuring continuity and compatibility of data. Future-state impacts are substantial from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. These drivers mean the role will increasingly assess administrative, linked, alternative, and metadata-rich sources; consider secure access, privacy, and cyber requirements; and use enterprise platforms and centralized repositories to operationalize source reuse. The work description already shows strong source-integration and policy knowledge, so this role is likely to be heavily affected by the shift from survey-first to mixed-source, platform-enabled, security-conscious source strategies.

This subprocess is relevant because the role leads and plans new or modified processing systems and projects, including objectives, work plans, budgets, resources, contracts, and implementation costs, even though the work description does not explicitly mention preparing formal business cases for governance approval. Evidence includes: "Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems," "Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources," and "Plans and budgets for on-going studies and/or special projects." The capability involved is articulating options, resource needs, timelines, and implementation implications for change initiatives. The position fulfills part of this need by developing plans, budgets, and recommendations for modified systems and procedures. Future changes from Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure suggest that project justification and approval expectations will become more disciplined, milestone-driven, and explicit about trade-offs, workforce readiness, reuse, automation, and platform alignment. The role is therefore meaningfully affected, even if not the formal approval owner.

This is one of the most directly implicated subprocesses. The work description explicitly centers on dissemination products and output preparation: the position has knowledge of "departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients." It also "develops data bases for the provision of time-series information" and provides expert advice on program results. The capability involved is designing outputs, dissemination-ready products, explanatory materials, and associated standards and procedures. The role fulfills this through database development for time-series outputs, interpretation of results, preparation of dissemination materials, and application of publication and dissemination policies. Future changes are driven by Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity. These drivers imply more digital-first, metadata-rich, reusable, secure, and standardized dissemination products, with stronger privacy-by-design and platform-based delivery. Because the role already works at the intersection of production and dissemination, it is likely to be materially reshaped by these cumulative drivers.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role develops guidelines, specifications, parameters, and methods for processing systems and integrated statistical outputs. Evidence includes: "Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications," "Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters," "develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs," and "Research and analysis are required to evaluate the effectiveness of processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications, to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria." The capability involved is designing processing rules, integration methods, validation logic, coding/classification/report formats, and analysis-supporting system specifications. The position fulfills this directly through system design guidance, parameter approval, and technical specification work. Future changes are expected from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity. These drivers point to more automated coding, validation, integration, metadata-driven processing, reusable components, and pipeline-based production, with staff shifting from manual processing toward exception handling, orchestration, and governed method design. The work description already aligns strongly with these future-state changes.

This subprocess is directly implicated because the role leads development and implementation of statistical processing systems and coordinates staff involved in manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data. Evidence includes: "Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data," "Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems," and "Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs." The capability involved is end-to-end workflow and system design, role assignment, reuse, compatibility, and operational fit across production stages. The position fulfills this through workflow coordination, system redesign, compatibility assessment, and leadership of implementation teams. Future changes are especially strong from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity. These cumulative drivers imply more integrated pipelines, reusable enterprise services, clearer handoffs, flatter structures, stronger governance, secure-by-design workflows, and a workforce shift toward supervision of automated flows. This role is central to that transformation.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is materially connected because the role develops and improves processing systems, data compilation programs, and related specifications. Evidence includes: "develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs," "Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures," and "Leads project teams ... in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems." The capability involved is building or reusing processing components, transformation functions, workflow tools, and analysis-supporting services. The role fulfills this through technical specification, system review, and implementation leadership. Future changes from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity indicate that component development will increasingly emphasize reusable enterprise services, AI-enabled processing, metadata services, secure deployment, and open-source or modular approaches. The role's current responsibilities strongly position it within this shift.

This subprocess is relevant because the role not only designs and leads implementation of processing systems, but also coordinates operational activities and approves detailed processing parameters. Evidence includes: "Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data," "Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters," and leadership of implementation of new or modified systems. The capability involved is configuring operational workflows, sequencing processing steps, and aligning systems and staff responsibilities. The role fulfills this need through operational coordination and parameter-setting, though the description emphasizes design and oversight more than hands-on workflow configuration. Future changes from Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment suggest more standardized, automated, monitored workflows with clearer role assignments and fewer manual handoffs. This means the role will likely experience meaningful change in how workflows are configured and governed.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the work description explicitly includes testing, evaluation, and acceptance criteria for processing systems. Evidence includes: "Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications," "interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations and feasibility studies," and "design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria to ensure that processing systems yield the desired outputs." The capability involved is technical and operational testing of assembled systems, validation of interactions, and sign-off on whether systems produce expected outputs. The role fulfills this directly through test design, interpretation of results, and approval of processing parameters. Future changes from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the complexity of testing by adding automated components, secure environments, reusable services, and end-to-end pipeline interactions. The role's testing responsibilities are therefore likely to become more integration-focused, security-aware, and automation-intensive.

This subprocess is relevant because the role leads implementation of new or modified processing systems and manages staff, training plans, and operational readiness, although the description does not explicitly mention final production deployment documentation or user manuals. Evidence includes: "Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems" and in leadership responsibilities, "develops training plans." The capability involved is moving systems into production, preparing users, and ensuring operational readiness. The role fulfills part of this need through implementation leadership, staff coordination, and training planning. Future changes from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity suggest stronger emphasis on documentation, training, controlled deployment, and workforce readiness for modernized systems. The role is therefore meaningfully affected even if not solely responsible for all finalization tasks.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance because the role works with manipulation, storage, retrieval, and continuity of statistical data after receipt from multiple sources. Evidence includes coordination of staff involved in "manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data" and review of processing parameters to ensure "continuity and compatibility of data." The capability involved is preparing collected data and metadata for downstream processing, including loading, conversion, and ensuring compatibility. The role appears more downstream than collection-focused, but it is affected where incoming data from surveys, administrative files, or other sources must be standardized and made usable for production. Future changes from Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment may increase automation of handoffs and metadata-rich ingestion, which could affect this role's data handling and compatibility responsibilities.

This is one of the most directly implicated subprocesses. The work description explicitly states that studies may involve "the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses)" and that data collected for other purposes "must be translated into common concepts." It also notes the need "to integrate conceptually different data from other programs." This subprocess is relevant because the role provides feedback and recommendations for improvement on established statistical programs, researches gaps and inconsistencies in collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods, and interprets quality and variance issues. The capability involved is generating evidence about process performance, quality issues, and user or operational needs that can feed evaluation. The position fulfills this need by identifying methodological and program weaknesses and by interacting with users, suppliers and stakeholders whose feedback informs improvement. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Agility and Execution Discipline, Enterprise Platforms, Integrated Pipelines, Metadata-Driven Management, Modern Statistical Methods, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition will increase the volume of process metrics, paradata, staff feedback and modernization evidence relevant to evaluation. Evidence includes explicit responsibility for feedback and recommendations for improvement and for researching gaps and inconsistencies across the statistical process.

This subprocess is relevant because the role not only identifies issues but synthesizes analytical findings into recommendations for program improvement and new or modified surveys/projects. The capability involved is assessing whether methods, outputs and processes are meeting expectations and recommending changes. The position fulfills this need through analytical review of quality, comparability, relevance and methodological adequacy, and through proposals to improve existing surveys or initiate new projects. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation, Agility and Execution Discipline, Governance and Prioritization, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Modern Statistical Methods and Workforce Skills Transition will make evaluation more dashboard-driven, more focused on efficiency and modernization outcomes, and more explicit about trade-offs and sustainability. Evidence includes developing guidelines, proposals and recommendations for management to improve surveys or initiate new projects, and researching inconsistencies and enhancements across methods and procedures.

This subprocess is plausibly connected because the role develops proposals and recommendations for divisional management, leads project teams, and represents the division on development projects, task forces and committees. The capability involved is contributing expert evidence and recommendations that inform action planning, though the work description does not explicitly assign final decision-making authority for enterprise action plans. The position fulfills this need by supplying the analytical basis for improvement actions and participating in forums where consensus is developed. Future-state impacts from Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition may increase the importance of clear ownership, prioritization and executable recommendations, which would affect how this role frames advice to management. Evidence includes developing recommendations for management, leading teams, and participating in committees to develop consensus.

This subprocess concerns identifying what statistics are needed and how needs change in response to users, environmental change, and practice elsewhere. The position is relevant because it explicitly investigates client and policy needs and researches emerging developments that shape future statistical requirements. The work description states that the incumbent 'investigates client requirements for statistical information,' has 'knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments ... to determine their information requirements,' and has 'knowledge of data users ... to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies.' It also states that the incumbent 'identifies and researches trends and developments in mass data processing concepts, methods and techniques' and has 'extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues ... to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data.' This is not just passive awareness; it supports strategic identification of future program needs. Future-state drivers make this more consequential: under Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, need identification will be more constrained by prioritization, fewer staff, and pressure to find lower-cost ways to meet needs using automation, AI, machine learning and new tools and methods. Because the role plans long-term strategies and prepares options for new or modified programs, it will increasingly need to triage needs and align them with feasible, efficient production models.

This subprocess establishes the statistical output objectives needed to meet confirmed user needs, including quality, confidentiality and resource considerations. The position is highly relevant because it sets strategic direction for statistical programs and determines production and dissemination approaches. Evidence includes: 'Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs'; 'Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs'; 'Determines the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied in the development and operation of statistical programs regarding the acquisition, production and dissemination of data'; and 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results.' These duties align directly with defining what outputs will be produced, at what quality level, and under what constraints. Future changes are strongly shaped by Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. The role already makes trade-offs among framework, strategy, resources and impact; those trade-offs will become more explicit as scarce resources are focused on highest-value outcomes, accountability for decisions is strengthened, and output scope, timeliness, granularity and service levels are tightened under fiscal pressure and workforce reduction. The work description's emphasis on proposals, options, recommendations, quality certification and resource implications is direct evidence of this subprocess responsibility.

This subprocess assesses whether existing data sources can meet requirements, including administrative and alternative sources, legal constraints, ICT feasibility, security, continuity and agreements. The position is highly relevant because the work description explicitly requires assessing source availability, reliability, integration feasibility, legal constraints and technology suitability. Evidence includes: 'Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve ... the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses)'; 'Assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations and identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources'; 'Investigates client requirements ... and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified systems to meet these requirements'; and 'Knowledge of the Statistics Act ... and the Privacy Act is also required to ensure ... confidentiality.' The role also 'establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data' and reviews technology options for mass data capture, conversion and dissemination. Future-state drivers intensify this work substantially. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the importance of assessing administrative data, linked data, gridded data and non-survey sources. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure make secure access, authorizations, privacy, cyber security, platforms and scalable infrastructure core suitability criteria. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the importance of metadata quality and reuse potential. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment pushes stronger preference toward lower-cost reusable sources. The position's combination of source assessment, systems capacity analysis, confidentiality responsibility and technology evaluation makes this subprocess central.

This subprocess documents options, costs, benefits, risks, resources and recommendations for new or modified statistical business processes. The position is highly relevant because the work description explicitly includes preparing proposals, defining costs, managing budgets, contracting, and recommending strategic options for program change. Evidence includes: 'Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs'; 'Defines, coordinates and evaluates the cost of statistical system development work'; 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes'; and 'Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit.' The role also negotiates contracts and selects contractors, which aligns with documenting required technical and human resources and implementation approaches. Future-state drivers make this subprocess even more important. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline means business cases must be more implementation-ready, milestone-based and time-bound. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline raises approval thresholds and requires clearer trade-offs and accountability. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment means proposals must foreground savings, automation, reuse and affordability under reduced staffing. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity means business cases must increasingly account for training, sequencing, leadership capacity and workforce readiness. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will also reshape the 'To-Be' solutions the role proposes, pushing enterprise platforms, reusable components, automation and governed modernization rather than bespoke builds.

This subprocess covers detailed design of statistical outputs, products, services and dissemination procedures, including confidential access processes. The position is highly relevant because dissemination is explicitly part of the role title and core responsibilities. Evidence includes the title 'Head, Production and Dissemination'; the duty to 'determine the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied in the development and operation of statistical programs regarding the acquisition, production and dissemination of data'; the responsibility to 'provide expert advisory and consultative services' explaining findings and their interpretation; and the need to maintain the department's reputation for 'producing high quality data.' The role also participates in task forces and committees 'as an expert in statistical production and dissemination systems,' which directly supports design of dissemination approaches and products. Future-state drivers indicate that output design will increasingly be shaped by Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. This means more digital-first, metadata-rich, reusable and secure dissemination products, with stronger privacy-by-design and platform-based delivery. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity also matters because staff will need to operate and explain modern digital dissemination products. The work description's explicit dissemination leadership and communication responsibilities make this subprocess central.

This subprocess designs collection strategy, instruments, methods, agreements and respondent management. The position is relevant because the work description covers determining acquisition methods and establishing mass statistical data collection environments, though it is more strategic and systems-oriented than hands-on collection operations. Evidence includes: 'Determines the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied ... regarding the acquisition, production and dissemination of data'; 'Advanced knowledge of systems analysis and design ... in order to establish and manage mass statistical data collection, production and dissemination environments'; and 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes.' The role also defines specifications for contracted development work and researches new technology for 'mass data capture.' Future-state drivers suggest meaningful change: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production shift collection design toward online-first, adaptive, administrative and alternative-source acquisition; AI and Automation in Statistical Production introduces chatbot-assisted and automated collection patterns; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access make secure digital collection infrastructure and APIs more central; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment pushes lower-touch collection models. The position is implicated because it governs systems and methods that enable these collection designs, even if the description does not show direct operational management of field collection.

This subprocess designs methodologies for coding, editing, imputation, integration, validation, estimation and disclosure control. The position is highly relevant because the work description repeatedly emphasizes systems analysis and design, integration of multiple sources, quality review, methodological assessment and production specifications. Evidence includes: 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes'; 'Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes'; 'Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs ... Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources'; 'Assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations'; and 'Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs.' The role also 'reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results,' which depends on sound processing and analysis design. Future-state impacts are substantial. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production directly affect coding, validation, editing, imputation and integration design. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increases the need for linkage, source prioritization and heterogeneous-source validation methods. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration pushes methods to be modular, orchestrated and automated. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development increase the need for reusable, metadata-aware, governed processing components. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity matters because staff will need stronger analytical and technical capability to design and oversee these methods. The work description provides direct evidence of this methodological and systems-design responsibility.

This subprocess designs the end-to-end workflow from collection to dissemination, reusing existing systems where possible and defining staff-system interactions and responsibilities. The position is highly relevant because the work description is fundamentally about planning, designing, managing and improving statistical production and dissemination systems. Evidence includes: 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes'; 'Manages a unit and project teams involved in systems design'; 'Advanced knowledge of systems analysis and design ... in order to establish and manage mass statistical data collection, production and dissemination environments'; and 'Participates in or leads task forces or committees as an expert in statistical production and dissemination systems.' The role also develops policies, procedures and specifications, and manages resources and contractors, all of which are core to workflow and production-system design. Future-state drivers make this one of the most affected subprocesses. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development all point toward integrated, reusable, automated, cloud-enabled workflows with clearer handoffs and fewer redundancies. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will require clearer accountabilities, leaner workflows and milestone-driven implementation. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will push redesign toward fewer manual steps, flatter structures, role clarity, exception handling and sustainable staffing models. The work description aligns directly with this subprocess.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess builds or reuses components needed for processing and analysis. The position is relevant because it manages systems design and development specifications rather than coding components directly. Evidence includes: 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes'; 'Defines processing and production specifications and guidelines for the contracting of development work to internal service areas, outside agencies and contractors'; 'Manages a unit and project teams involved in systems design'; and 'Negotiates cost reductions and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services.' This shows responsibility for directing and governing component build/reuse decisions. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will increase pressure to adopt reusable enterprise processing components, AI-enabled coding and validation services, and modular open-source or shared solutions. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will further favour reuse over bespoke development. The role is materially connected because it specifies, governs, resources and evaluates such development work, even if it does not itself build components.

This subprocess builds or reuses dissemination components such as web services, open data outputs, maps and access mechanisms. The position is relevant because dissemination systems are explicitly within scope and the role leads systems design and development for production and dissemination. Evidence includes the title 'Head, Production and Dissemination'; participation in committees 'as an expert in statistical production and dissemination systems'; responsibility to 'plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes'; and management of project teams involved in systems design. Future-state drivers indicate that dissemination components will increasingly be platform-based, metadata-rich, secure and reusable, shaped by Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development. AI and Automation in Statistical Production may also introduce chatbot and search-enabled dissemination features. The role is implicated because it governs and directs dissemination-system development, though the description does not show direct hands-on component construction.

This subprocess configures workflows, systems and transformations based on the production workflow design. The position is relevant because it oversees implementation and operation of systems and processes and manages teams and contractors responsible for systems design. Evidence includes: 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes'; 'Manages a unit and project teams involved in systems design'; and 'Defines processing and production specifications.' This indicates responsibility for ensuring workflows are operationalized, even if not personally configuring them. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will make workflow configuration more automated, standardized and enterprise-based. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will also constrain customization and require clearer approvals, milestones and exception paths. The role is materially connected because it directs the implementation environment and operational model for configured workflows.

This subprocess tests assembled services, workflows, secure channels and supplier files to ensure coherent end-to-end operation. The position is relevant because it reviews and certifies quality and completeness of results and manages development and implementation of systems and processes. Evidence includes: 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results'; 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes'; and responsibility for security and confidentiality policies for systems, databases and files. These duties imply accountability for ensuring systems are fit for production use. Future-state drivers increase the importance of testing integrated, automated, secure and cloud-based systems: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development all expand testing scope and sign-off complexity. The role is implicated as a manager and certifier of production quality, though the description does not explicitly mention hands-on testing management.

This subprocess puts processes and services into production, including documentation, training and deployment readiness. The position is relevant because it manages implementation and operation of systems and processes, approves training plans, and leads units and projects through operationalization. Evidence includes: 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes'; 'Plans and schedules the work ... evaluates employee performance ... and approves training plans'; and 'Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes.' These responsibilities align with production readiness, user guidance and operational deployment. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase the importance of training, documentation, role clarity and sustainable operation in leaner, more automated environments. The role is materially connected because it manages the organizational and operational conditions needed for production launch.

This subprocess prepares people, processes and technology for collection. The position has limited but plausible involvement because it establishes and manages mass data collection environments and approves training plans, but the work description is not focused on operational collection setup. Evidence includes 'Advanced knowledge of systems analysis and design ... to establish and manage mass statistical data collection, production and dissemination environments' and management duties that include determining human resource needs and approving training plans. Future-state drivers such as Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will affect collection readiness through digital tools, secure access, source acquisition and staff training. However, the description supports only indirect managerial involvement rather than direct collection setup responsibility.

This subprocess executes collection operations. The position has only limited connection because the work description focuses on strategic program management, systems design and dissemination rather than live collection operations. There is some indirect relevance through responsibility for acquisition methods and mass data collection environments: the incumbent 'determines the methods ... regarding the acquisition, production and dissemination of data' and has knowledge needed 'to establish and manage mass statistical data collection, production and dissemination environments.' Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will change collection execution toward digital, automated and source-based models, which may affect the systems and methods the role oversees. But the supplied evidence does not support direct operational responsibility for running collection.

This subprocess loads collected data and metadata into processing environments and manages capture, versioning, archiving and pseudonymisation. The position is only indirectly relevant because it oversees systems and processes that support acquisition and production, but the work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for collection finalization. Evidence for indirect relevance includes responsibility for methods regarding 'acquisition, production and dissemination of data,' systems design expertise, and policies for 'security and confidentiality of data and the maintenance and protection of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.' Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will make this handoff more automated and controlled, which may affect systems under the role's oversight. Still, the connection remains limited based on the supplied duties.

This subprocess integrates data from multiple sources, including administrative, geospatial and linked data, and harmonises conflicting values into consolidated datasets. The position is highly relevant because the work description explicitly centers on integrating conceptually different data from multiple sources and assessing impacts across programs. Evidence includes: 'Programs involve ... the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses)'; 'Knowledge of other statistical programs ... to integrate conceptually different data from other programs'; 'Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts'; and 'Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the production and dissemination methods and procedures ... Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.' This is direct evidence of integration responsibility and expertise. Future-state drivers make this subprocess even more central. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production make integration, linkage and harmonisation core production capabilities. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access increases the importance of controlled linkage and de-identification. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration support scalable, reusable integration environments. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability strengthens interoperability and source comparison. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases reliance on integrated existing sources instead of direct collection. The role's explicit integration and cross-program stewardship responsibilities make this subprocess one of the strongest matches.

This subprocess classifies and codes input data, increasingly using automated and AI-enabled methods. The position is relevant because it determines methods and practices for production systems and researches new data processing techniques, but the work description does not explicitly assign operational coding responsibility. Evidence includes: 'Determines the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied in the development and operation of statistical programs'; 'Reviews trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and techniques ... on the use and application of new technology to mass data capture, conversion and dissemination applications'; and 'Assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices.' These duties support governance of coding approaches and technology adoption. Future-state drivers are significant: AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production directly affect automated coding; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases pressure to reduce clerical coding; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability strengthens standard classifications; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity increases the need for staff oversight of AI-enabled coding. The role is materially connected through methodological and systems leadership rather than direct coding operations.

This subprocess identifies errors, anomalies, duplicates and inconsistencies in input data before and after integration. The position is highly relevant because quality review and analysis of variances are explicit core duties. Evidence includes: 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results'; 'Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions'; and 'Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the production and dissemination methods and procedures.' The role also develops policies and procedures for systems evaluation and has knowledge of Statistics Canada policies on data quality. Future-state drivers intensify this work. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increases heterogeneity, linkage errors and source drift risks. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment push more automated validation and exception handling. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration embeds validation checkpoints into automated flows. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the need to validate metadata as well as data. Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production raises the complexity of validation across integrated, automated and model-based processes. The work description provides direct evidence of responsibility for quality assessment and variance analysis, making this subprocess highly relevant.

This subprocess corrects, replaces or imputes incorrect, missing or unreliable data and records metadata about those changes. The position is relevant because it determines methods and practices for statistical production, assesses new methods, and oversees quality and systems design, though the description does not explicitly mention editing or imputation operations. Evidence includes: 'Determines the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied in the development and operation of statistical programs'; 'Assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices'; and 'Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs.' These duties imply influence over editing and imputation approaches as part of broader processing methodology. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push more automated and model-assisted editing and imputation. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase source-prioritized correction using administrative values and linked-source logic. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the importance of documenting edits and imputations. The role is materially connected through methodological governance and quality oversight rather than direct execution.

This subprocess derives variables and units not directly collected, often from linked or integrated data. The position is relevant because the work description explicitly addresses translating source data collected for other purposes into common concepts and integrating conceptually different data from multiple programs. Evidence includes: 'Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts'; 'Knowledge of other statistical programs ... to integrate conceptually different data from other programs'; and the role's responsibility for determining methods and practices for acquisition, production and dissemination. These duties support derivation logic and conceptual transformation, even if derivation is not named directly. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase reliance on derived variables and units from administrative, linked and geospatial data. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will require derivations to be sequenced, documented and reusable. The role is materially connected through conceptual integration and methodological stewardship.

This subprocess creates aggregate data and totals from microdata. The position has plausible but limited involvement because it reviews program outputs, explains findings and maintains quality, but the work description does not explicitly mention aggregate calculation. Evidence includes 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results' and communication duties explaining 'statistical program findings' and defending 'the validity of statistical methods and approaches used.' Future-state drivers such as Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may affect aggregate production through small area estimation, geospatial outputs and faster automated pipelines, but the supplied duties point more to oversight of results than direct responsibility for aggregate calculation.

This subprocess assembles the results of processing into datasets ready for analysis. The position is relevant because it oversees production systems and processes end-to-end and certifies quality and completeness of results. Evidence includes: 'Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes'; 'Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes'; and 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results.' These duties imply accountability for the readiness and integrity of processed outputs handed to analysis and dissemination. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will make final datasets more standardized, metadata-rich, automated and reusable. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will also increase pressure for timely preliminary and final files. The role is materially connected through production oversight and quality certification.

This subprocess transforms processed data into draft statistical outputs and methodological notes. The position is highly relevant because it is responsible for production and dissemination, explains findings to users, and writes and presents technical and subject-matter concepts in accessible language. Evidence includes: 'Provides expert advisory and consultative services ... Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information'; 'Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify ... program results'; and the title 'Head, Production and Dissemination.' The role also participates in defending findings and maintaining the department's reputation for high-quality data, which is closely tied to draft output preparation and supporting notes. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the need for methodological explanation, metadata-rich outputs, and communication about AI-assisted or model-based methods. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will require clearer explanation of mixed-source outputs and geospatial products. The work description directly supports this subprocess.

This subprocess validates outputs against quality frameworks, prior cycles, metadata, auxiliary information and domain expectations. The position is highly relevant because validating and defending outputs is a central stated responsibility. Evidence includes: 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results'; 'Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions'; and communication duties requiring the incumbent to 'present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used.' The role also has extensive contextual and subject-matter knowledge needed to assess outputs against expectations and external developments. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production make output validation more complex because source substitution, linkage and advanced methods can create methodological breaks and new quality risks. AI and Automation in Statistical Production increases the need to validate automated outputs and associated metadata. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push more risk-based validation under leaner staffing. The work description provides direct evidence of output validation responsibility.

This subprocess interprets outputs, explains their meaning and assesses them against expectations using domain knowledge and analytical tools. The position is highly relevant because interpretation and explanation of results to internal and external users are explicit core duties. Evidence includes: 'Provides expert advisory and consultative services ... Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information'; 'Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts ... to explain and clarify ... program results'; and the need to defend findings when challenged or misinterpreted. The role also requires 'knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory' and 'extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues' to analyze outputs and assess impacts. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will make interpretation more complex because outputs will increasingly reflect linked, administrative, geospatial and model-based methods. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will change analyst workflows and increase the need to explain AI-assisted methods transparently. This subprocess is directly reflected in the work description.

This subprocess ensures outputs and stored data do not breach confidentiality rules. The position is relevant because confidentiality, privacy and security are explicit responsibilities in the work description, though disclosure control methods are not described in detail. Evidence includes: 'Establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data'; 'Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, (e.g. confidentiality of data, security ... data quality) ... to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of production and dissemination activities'; and knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act 'to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information ... and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.' These are direct confidentiality governance responsibilities relevant to disclosure control. Future-state drivers such as Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will strengthen privacy, secure access and controlled-use requirements, especially for linked and geospatial outputs under Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion. The role is materially connected through policy, governance and dissemination accountability.

This subprocess ensures outputs, commentary, caveats, technical notes and approvals are complete and ready for release. The position is highly relevant because it certifies quality, explains results, prepares technical explanations, and participates in consensus-building and expert review. Evidence includes: 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results'; 'Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts ... to explain and clarify ... program results'; 'Provides expert advisory and consultative services'; and 'Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings ... to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge.' The role also defends findings and methods when challenged, which aligns with final release readiness and caveat-setting. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase pressure for disciplined sign-off, stronger metadata packaging, clearer caveats and uncertainty communication, and faster but controlled finalization. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will also affect release-level decisions. The work description strongly supports this subprocess.

This subprocess updates dissemination systems with data and metadata ready for release. The position is relevant because it leads production and dissemination systems and manages their development and operation. Evidence includes the title 'Head, Production and Dissemination'; responsibility to 'plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes'; and expertise in 'statistical production and dissemination systems.' The role also has responsibility for security, confidentiality and protection of databases and files, which is relevant to controlled updates of output systems. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will make output-system updates more automated, metadata-centric, platform-based and controlled. The role is materially connected through dissemination-system oversight rather than direct operational loading.

This subprocess assembles dissemination products such as publications, websites, tables, maps and explanatory texts. This aligns directly with designing coding, validation, integration, estimation and analytical methods. Future-state drivers will materially reshape this work: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will push methods toward automated, reusable, metadata-driven and pipeline-ready designs; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will require methods for integrating heterogeneous sources and linked data; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will strengthen confidentiality and disclosure-control considerations; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require upskilling and leadership oversight for methodological change. The role's authority to review proposals for new methods and assess implications is direct evidence of high relevance.

This subprocess is relevant because the role directs multidisciplinary and interdepartmental teams, allocates resources, and determines broad study parameters and reviews. Although the work description does not explicitly assign technical workflow architecture design, it clearly places the incumbent in a leadership role over how complex research activities are organized and coordinated. Evidence includes directing "the work of multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project teams, working groups and committees involved in significant research and analytical activities" and developing plans and objectives while allocating human and financial resources. The capability involved is operational leadership, coordination, and assignment of responsibilities across teams. Future-state drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will materially affect how such teams and workflows are structured, with clearer handoffs, more automation, flatter structures, and stronger role clarity. The role is therefore meaningfully affected by this subprocess even if not the technical builder of systems.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is implicated because the role reviews and approves methodological innovations and directs analytical activities that depend on processing and analysis components. The work description does not say the incumbent personally builds components, but it does say they "review proposals to develop new methods and techniques," "assess the implications of new approaches," and direct significant research and analytical activities. The capability involved is methodological oversight and approval of analytical tooling and approaches. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increasingly convert methods into reusable enterprise components and automated services. This means the role's current responsibility for approving and steering methodological approaches will increasingly extend to judging reusable analytical components, workforce readiness, and sustainability of modernized analytical production.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance because the role is a senior manager who directs staff, recruitment, performance, and resource allocation for major research activities. The work description includes directing recruitment activities, identifying knowledge requirements, preparing performance appraisals, and managing staff and contractors. That indicates responsibility for workforce readiness and operational support, though not explicit responsibility for final technical deployment. The capability involved is managerial readiness and enabling staff to operate approved methods and studies. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will affect this work by increasing training, change leadership, and sustainable operating-model demands as new methods move into production. Relevance remains low because the description does not explicitly mention production deployment, documentation, or system training.

This subprocess is relevant because the role conducts and directs complex studies spanning multiple subject-matter areas and develops methods and concepts for unique studies. The work description emphasizes wide-ranging reviews across subject matter areas, expert interpretation of results, and analysis of impacts on major policy and regulatory issues. While it does not explicitly mention record linkage or operational data integration, the breadth of studies and methodological leadership imply meaningful involvement in combining evidence across domains. The capability involved is cross-domain analytical integration and methodological judgment. Future-state drivers make this more material: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase reliance on integrating survey, administrative, alternative and linked data; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Enterprise Digital Platforms will make interoperability and reusable integrated assets more central; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will heighten confidentiality constraints. The role's advisory and methodological authority means it will be materially affected by how integrated data are produced and interpreted.

This subprocess has limited relevance because the work description does not assign direct coding responsibilities. However, the role does review and approve analytical methods and research outputs, and develops new methods and concepts for unique studies. That creates a plausible connection where coding approaches may fall within broader methodological oversight. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increasingly automate coding and may affect the methodological environment in which this role operates. Still, because no explicit coding or classification responsibility is stated, relevance remains low.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role provides expert analysis and interpretation of results, reviews analytical material, and assesses implications of methods and study findings. The work description states that the incumbent "provides expert analysis and interpretation of results," "reviews strategic directions for the management of significant research studies," and "approves analytical material and research papers for publication." These are direct indicators of validating whether outputs and analyses are sound, credible and fit for use. The capability involved is senior analytical quality assurance, methodological scrutiny, and domain-informed judgment. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase the need for automated validation, exception review, and scrutiny of heterogeneous and AI-assisted outputs. The role's authoritative advice to senior officials on study results and impacts is strong evidence that it performs high-level validation of analytical outputs.

This subprocess has only limited relevance. The work description does not mention editing or imputation directly. Its connection is indirect through the incumbent's responsibility for methodological issues, development of new methods, and oversight of analytical quality. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment may affect the methodological context of correction and imputation, but the supplied work description does not provide evidence that this role directly performs or manages those functions. Therefore relevance is low.

This subprocess is relevant because the role develops new concepts and definitions and directs unique studies that may require derived analytical constructs. The work description explicitly states that the incumbent "develops new methods, concepts and definitions to meet the needs of the most unique studies." That is strong evidence of conceptual derivation work, even if not framed in operational processing terms. The capability involved is advanced conceptual modeling and methodological design. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase reliance on derived variables and units from linked and administrative data, while Metadata-Driven Data Management will require clearer lineage and documentation. Because the role is responsible for conceptual innovation in complex studies, it is materially connected to this subprocess.

This subprocess has plausible but limited relevance. The role interprets results, develops conclusions, and advises on impacts of studies, which may involve use of aggregates, but the work description does not explicitly mention producing aggregates or population totals. Future-state drivers such as Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may affect the kinds of aggregates available for analysis, especially more granular or model-based outputs, but the evidence supports only indirect involvement.

This subprocess is only weakly connected. The work description focuses on directing studies, methods, teams, and publication-ready analytical outputs rather than assembling analysis-ready datasets. Future-state drivers around integrated pipelines and metadata-rich assets may affect the analytical environment in which the role works, but there is no explicit evidence that the incumbent finalizes data files. Relevance is therefore low.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the role prepares, reviews and approves research papers, reports and analytical material for publication, and develops overall conclusions and recommendations.
