The work description explicitly states that the incumbent "develops the overall conclusions and recommendations," "reviews and approves analytical material and research papers for publication," and has writing skills to prepare and review widely disseminated reports. The capability involved is transforming analytical results into authoritative draft outputs with supporting interpretation. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will change how draft outputs are assembled, documented and explained, especially where AI-assisted methods or mixed-source data require stronger methodological notes and reusable metadata. This role is central to that work.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role validates analytical outputs through expert interpretation, review, and approval before publication and executive advice. Evidence includes reviewing and approving analytical material and research papers, providing authoritative recommendations based on study results, and analyzing the impact of results on major program, policy and regulatory issues. The capability involved is senior domain validation, quality assurance, and judgment against expectations and policy context. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need to validate outputs produced from linked, administrative, alternative and AI-assisted methods against historical expectations and domain intelligence. The role's authoritative advisory function makes this a high-relevance subprocess.

This is one of the most directly connected subprocesses. The work description centers on interpreting complex study results, developing conclusions, and explaining implications to senior officials and external stakeholders. It states that the incumbent provides "authoritative analysis and advice," "expert analysis and interpretation of results," and represents the federal government while presenting options and strategies on complex policy issues. The capability involved is high-level interpretation, explanation, and contextualization of outputs for decision-makers. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will make interpretation more complex because outputs will increasingly reflect linked, administrative, alternative and model-based methods. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will also affect how analysts explain AI-assisted methods and use new tools. The work description provides extensive direct evidence of this responsibility.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description explicitly emphasizes legal and policy responsibilities related to confidentiality and privacy. It states that knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act is "particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided" and to ensure that neither the incumbent nor subordinates release identifying information without prior consent. The capability involved is stewardship of confidentiality and lawful release practices. While the description does not explicitly mention applying suppression or perturbation methods, it clearly assigns responsibility for protecting confidential information in outputs and communications. Future-state drivers such as Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase disclosure risks, especially with linked and richer data environments, making this responsibility more consequential for the role.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the role finalizes analytical outputs for publication and executive use. The work description states that the incumbent reviews and approves analytical material and research papers for publication, develops overall conclusions and recommendations, and provides authoritative advice to senior officials within and outside Statistics Canada. The capability involved is final quality judgment, preparation of supporting interpretation, and approval of release-ready analytical content. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase pressure for disciplined sign-off, stronger caveats and technical notes, and clearer communication of uncertainty and methodological change. The role's publication approval authority and executive advisory responsibilities are direct evidence of high relevance.

This subprocess is relevant because the role prepares and reviews research papers, reports and articles that are disseminated widely or published. The work description explicitly mentions writing and editing skills for studies, articles and reports that will be "disseminated widely or published" and responsibility for approving analytical material for publication. The capability involved is producing and quality-assuring substantive dissemination content. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will affect how such products are assembled, standardized, explained and delivered digitally. The role is not described as managing dissemination platforms, so relevance is medium rather than high.

This subprocess is implicated because the role represents the department and federal government in sensitive discussions, provides advice to senior officials, and approves analytical material for publication. That indicates meaningful involvement in release readiness, briefing content, and communication of published findings, even if not explicit operational control of release logistics. Evidence includes representing the department where consensus must be achieved on major issues and dealing with sensitive and political issues that could embarrass the department. The capability involved is executive-facing communication, release sensitivity judgment, and stewardship of public-facing analytical content. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will increase the importance of disciplined release timing, secure access, and controlled communication. The role's sensitivity to political and reputational issues makes this materially relevant.

This subprocess has limited relevance because the role provides authoritative advice to senior officials, governments, industry, academia and other institutions, which is a form of high-level stakeholder support and explanation. However, the work description does not describe routine handling of user queries, service requests, or microdata access support. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Metadata-Driven Data Management may change how users seek explanations of outputs, but the evidence supports only limited involvement at a senior advisory level rather than operational user support.

This subprocess is relevant because the role reviews strategic directions, assesses implications of new approaches, and directs significant studies whose results and methods would generate evaluation evidence. The work description also shows strong engagement with current and emerging socio-economic trends and with reviewing proposals and strategic directions. The capability involved is gathering and interpreting evidence on study performance, methodological implications and emerging needs. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the importance of collecting evidence on quality, efficiency, staffing impacts and modernization readiness. While the description does not explicitly mention formal evaluation metrics, the role's strategic review and methodological assessment functions make this materially relevant.

This subprocess is implicated because the role evaluates strategic directions, assesses implications of new methods and approaches, and recommends innovative solutions and priorities to senior management. The work description states that the incumbent "reviews strategic directions for the management of significant research studies," "assesses the implications of new approaches," and recommends priorities and initiatives. The capability involved is synthesizing evidence into judgments and recommendations for future action. Future-state drivers such as Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make formal evaluation of quality, efficiency, workforce readiness and modernization outcomes more central. The role's strategic and methodological review responsibilities provide clear evidence of meaningful involvement.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role has clear decision-making authority, recommends priorities and initiatives, allocates resources, and advises senior management on strategic directions and innovative solutions. The work description states that the incumbent recommends new research priorities and initiatives to senior management, reviews strategic directions, recommends innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives, develops plans and objectives, and allocates human and financial resources. The capability involved is senior decision-making, prioritization, and translating evaluation or strategic findings into concrete actions. Future-state drivers strongly reinforce this relevance: Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline will require explicit ownership and trade-offs; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will require milestone-based, executable action plans; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will force action plans to address staffing reductions, training, sequencing and sustainable operating models. The work description provides direct evidence that this role already performs this kind of action-planning function.

This subprocess is relevant because it assesses whether existing data sources are suitable for statistical use, including quality, timeliness, legal constraints, and feasibility of use. The work description directly connects to this need through responsibilities to "review and verify data sources," assess the "timeliness, completeness, accuracy and validity of data compiled for publication," and maintain "knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability." It also states that the position evaluates problems and proposes solutions across "collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation" and has knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act, which aligns with source suitability, confidentiality, and legal-use considerations. Future-state drivers make this even more central: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increases the need to assess administrative and linked sources rather than relying only on surveys; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the importance of searchable, standardized source metadata; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure make secure access, privacy, authorizations, and platform fit core suitability criteria; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production expands assessment to linked, alternative, geospatial, and unstructured sources. The work description's emphasis on analyzing effects of "computer technology," assessing validity of database contents, and proposing changes to methods shows the position materially contributes to present and future source assessment.

This subprocess concerns defining collected and derived variables, classifications, and metadata. The work description is relevant because the position "develops and outlines new statistical methods, concepts and procedures," "develops or modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches," and has "knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data." It also includes reviewing questionnaires and subject-matter concepts, which implies involvement in how variables are defined and interpreted. The role is not framed as the lead designer of variables, so relevance is medium rather than high. Future-state drivers increase the importance of this connection: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production shift variable design toward harmonized, linked, derived, and geospatially enabled variables; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability makes standardized variable metadata more important. Evidence includes the requirement to modify "concepts, definitions and approaches," review questionnaires, and assess validity of data and database contents.

This subprocess is relevant because it covers collection strategy, instruments, questionnaires, and agreements for obtaining data. The work description shows direct contribution through responsibilities to "review and design questionnaires for the collection of data," provide feedback on "collection... methods and procedures," and assist in recommendations for improvements to "survey methods and activities." The position also evaluates problems in collection and develops procedures for collection and presentation of data. This is regular contribution under guidance rather than full ownership, so medium relevance fits. Future-state drivers indicate meaningful change: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will shift collection toward online-first, adaptive, administrative, and alternative-source models; AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will embed digital tools, APIs, automation, and platform-based collection; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase secure-by-design requirements. The work description's references to questionnaire design, collection-method feedback, and analysis of changes in procedures and computer technology support this linkage.

This subprocess designs coding, editing, imputation, integration, validation, estimation, and analysis methods. It is one of the strongest matches to the work description. The position directly "evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information," "develops and implements procedures for the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data," "implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications," and "develops or modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches." The role also analyzes current methods and procedures to propose changes or alternative systems, and assesses impacts of concepts, definitions, and conditions under which data were collected, processed, and stored. These are core design-processing responsibilities. Future-state drivers intensify this connection: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment all push processing and analysis toward automated, metadata-driven, reusable, integrated, and lower-touch methods. Workforce implications such as reduced manual effort and increased need for new analytical and digital skills are directly relevant because the work description already requires analysis of changes in methodology and computer technology in a computerized environment.

This subprocess concerns end-to-end workflow design, reuse of systems, and how staff interact with systems. The work description is relevant because the position analyzes changes in "procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services," implements enhancements to processing systems and applications, writes manuals and monitoring procedures, and participates in project teams to improve work methods and practices. These duties show contribution to workflow and system improvement, though not explicit enterprise-level ownership. Future-state drivers make this more important: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all reshape workflows toward integrated, reusable, automated production with clearer handoffs and changed staff-system interaction. Evidence includes writing "program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures," implementing system enhancements, and analyzing alternative systems.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess covers building or reusing components for processing and analysis. The work description supports medium relevance because the position "implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications," develops procedures for processing, editing, compilation and presentation, and writes technical and operational documentation for systems and applications. This indicates contribution to component implementation and adaptation, though the description does not clearly assign primary build responsibility. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production suggest that such work will increasingly involve reusable enterprise components, automated services, and modern tools. Evidence comes from the explicit responsibility to implement system enhancements and to explain divisional systems and applications in common terminology.

This subprocess is relevant because it configures workflows, systems, and transformations from collection through dissemination. The work description indicates contribution through implementing modifications to processing systems and applications, analyzing current methods and procedures to propose alternative systems, and writing monitoring procedures and manuals used in implementation and assessment of statistical programs. The role also participates in project teams to improve work methods and practices. This is meaningful involvement but not explicit ownership of workflow orchestration, so medium relevance is appropriate. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the importance of configuring standardized, automated, lower-touch workflows. Evidence includes system enhancement work, monitoring procedures, and analysis of procedural and technological changes.

This subprocess is plausibly connected because the work description includes reviewing and designing questionnaires, developing collection procedures, and analyzing collection methods. However, the description does not explicitly assign operational setup responsibilities such as training collection staff, provisioning devices, or configuring live collection environments. Relevance is therefore low. It remains relevant because future-state drivers—especially Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity—will make collection setup more digital, secure, and tool-dependent, which may affect positions that design questionnaires and collection procedures. Evidence is limited to questionnaire design, collection-method feedback, and knowledge of collection practices.

This subprocess integrates data from multiple sources and harmonizes them into consolidated datasets. The work description strongly aligns because the position analyzes data, reviews and verifies data sources and methods of data compilation, assesses validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data, and ensures consistency and reliability by locating, analyzing and comparing related statistical output. It also evaluates problems in compilation and presentation and develops procedures for processing and compilation. These are core integration-adjacent responsibilities. Future-state drivers make this even more material: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production all increase the scale and complexity of multi-source integration, linkage, harmonization, and controlled access. Evidence includes "reviews and verifies data sources and methods of data compilation," "knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada," and assessing validity of database contents and alternative manipulations.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description includes processing, editing, and compilation responsibilities and developing procedures and methods in those areas. While coding is not named explicitly, the role evaluates problems in processing and editing, develops and implements procedures, and works in a computerized statistical environment. That supports medium relevance rather than high. Future-state drivers make this more important: AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production directly affect coding through AI-enabled automated coding; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases pressure to reduce clerical effort; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability strengthens standardized classifications. Evidence includes responsibilities for processing and editing procedures, system enhancements, and knowledge of data gathering and statistical estimation methods.

This subprocess is a strong match because the work description repeatedly emphasizes assessing data quality and validity. The position "assesses the timeliness, completeness, accuracy and validity of data compiled for publication," evaluates problems in processing and editing, assesses the impact and constraints of concepts and conditions under which data were collected and stored, and analyzes methods and procedures to propose changes. It also has knowledge needed to assess the validity of collected and processed data, computer application outputs, database contents, and alternative manipulations of data. These are direct validation responsibilities. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will shift validation toward more automated, metadata-aware, multi-source, exception-based quality control. Evidence is explicit and extensive in the work description.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description directly includes editing among the areas where the position evaluates problems, develops procedures, and proposes improvements. However, imputation is not explicitly mentioned, so the connection is material but partial. The role's responsibilities in processing, editing, compilation, and method development support medium relevance. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment suggest editing work will become more automated, model-assisted, and metadata-documented, increasing the impact on this role's method and procedure work. Evidence includes repeated references to "editing" in key activities and decision-making responsibilities.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description includes developing and modifying statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches, and assessing results from alternative manipulations of data. Those responsibilities support derivation of new analytical variables or transformed outputs, even though the description does not explicitly mention deriving units. The role also participates in analysis of statistical program data and subject-matter studies, which often depend on derived concepts. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase reliance on derived variables from linked, administrative, and alternative data. Evidence includes method development, concept and definition modification, and analysis of alternative manipulations of data.

This subprocess has plausible but limited relevance. The work description includes knowledge of statistical estimation and survey methods and participation in analysis of data and survey improvements, which could place the role near weighting-related work. However, there is no explicit responsibility for creating weights or calibration. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may increase exposure to hybrid estimation and weighting changes, but the supplied work description does not support a stronger classification. Evidence is limited to knowledge of statistical estimation and survey methods.

This subprocess is relevant because the position participates in analysis of statistical program data, identifies statistical trends and developments, prepares analytical material for publication, and works with compilation and presentation of data. These duties imply regular use of aggregated outputs even if the description does not explicitly say the position computes aggregates itself. Future-state drivers such as Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will increasingly automate aggregate production and expand granular and geospatial outputs, affecting how this role analyzes and prepares outputs. Evidence includes preparation of analytical material for publication, identification of trends, and responsibilities in compilation and presentation.

This subprocess is relevant because it assembles the results of processing into datasets ready for analysis. The work description connects through responsibilities for processing, compilation, presentation, reviewing data sources and compilation methods, implementing system enhancements, and analyzing effects of procedural and technological changes on data output, products and services. The role appears to contribute to readiness of processed data for analysis and publication, though not necessarily as the final owner of file finalization. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will make standardized, metadata-rich, automated handoff datasets more important. Evidence includes work on compilation methods, data output effects, and system/application enhancements.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the work description explicitly states that, under guidance, the position "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes." It also identifies statistical trends and developments, writes and presents subject-matter and technical concepts in common terminology, and writes management reports, manuals, and training packages. These are direct output-preparation activities. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will change how draft outputs are assembled, documented, and explained, especially where AI-assisted methods and mixed-source data require stronger methodological notes and metadata. Evidence is explicit in the key activities and communication responsibilities.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role assesses whether outputs are valid, consistent, and publication-ready. The work description explicitly includes assessing the "timeliness, completeness, accuracy and validity of data compiled for publication," identifying trends and developments, locating and comparing related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability, and analyzing the impact of concepts and collection conditions on results. These are core output-validation functions. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase the need for validating outputs produced from mixed sources, automated methods, and tighter timelines. Evidence is direct and substantial.

This subprocess is a strong match. The work description states that the position participates in analysis of statistical program data, identifies statistical trends and developments, assists users inside and outside Statistics Canada, and writes and presents detailed subject-matter and technical concepts in common terminology. It also requires knowledge of current and emerging economic and social issues to identify and assess trends represented by statistical data series. These are direct interpretation and explanation responsibilities. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need to explain outputs derived from linked, administrative, automated, and modernized methods in clear terms. Evidence includes trend identification, user assistance, communication duties, and subject-matter knowledge requirements.

This subprocess is relevant because the role contributes to preparing publication-ready analytical material and assessing validity for publication. The work description includes preparing analytical material for publication, assessing data validity for publication, writing reports and explanatory materials, and participating in subject-matter studies and reviews. It does not explicitly assign release approval authority, so medium relevance is appropriate. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and AI and Automation in Statistical Production will increase the importance of caveats, technical notes, metadata, and disciplined final review. Evidence includes preparation of analytical material for publication and assessment of publication validity.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description explicitly states that the position "provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada." It also writes and presents technical concepts in common terminology, which supports responding to user questions and explaining outputs or systems. The role is not described as a dedicated service-support function, so medium relevance is appropriate. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment suggest user support will shift toward self-service, AI-assisted responses, knowledge bases, and more questions about methods, metadata, and access. Evidence is direct in the key activities and communication section.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description includes analyzing changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine effects on outputs, products and services; participating in subject-matter studies and reviews; and suggesting feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures. These activities generate evaluation inputs about process performance and improvement opportunities. The role is not explicitly responsible for formal evaluation governance, so medium relevance fits. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the amount of process metadata, system metrics, and staff feedback available and needed for evaluation. Evidence includes analysis of procedural and technological changes and participation in studies and reviews.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description shows the position analyzing methods, procedures, technology changes, and their effects on outputs and services; participating in subject-matter studies and reviews; and assisting in development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities. That is substantive evaluative work, even if not framed as producing formal evaluation reports. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make evaluation more dashboard-driven, comparative, and focused on quality, timeliness, efficiency, and workforce readiness. Evidence includes determining effects on outputs, proposing changes, and participating in reviews to support project teams or senior officers.

This subprocess concerns identifying what statistics are needed and how needs change based on user demand, environmental change, and feedback. The work description is relevant because the position "provides data, assistance and advice to users within and outside Statistics Canada," "assists in subject matter studies and reviews," and "identifies statistical trends and developments," all of which contribute evidence about emerging information needs and changing subject-matter requirements. The capability involved is subject-matter analysis and user-facing interpretation of statistical needs, not final approval authority. Future-state change is driven by Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment: with fewer staff and stronger prioritization pressures, this role's trend analysis, user advice, and subject-matter review work will increasingly feed sharper triage of which needs are pursued. The work description also shows awareness of changing program content and implications through duties such as identifying trends and determining implications for statistical methods and procedures.

This subprocess sets statistical output objectives, including quality, scope, timeliness and resource trade-offs. The position is relevant because it participates in preparing analytical material "for internal use and publication purposes," reviews survey and production results, and provides advice to users and specialists, which contributes to shaping what outputs are suitable and useful. The capability involved is analytical support to output definition, including explaining concepts, definitions and technical implications to users and colleagues. Evidence includes writing and presenting subject-matter and technical concepts, providing advice to data users and clients, and writing manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports. Future changes are likely from Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment: scarce resources, transparent trade-offs, and tighter scope decisions will make this role's analytical input more focused on highest-value outputs, acceptable quality-service trade-offs, and clearer articulation of what can be sustained with fewer resources.

This subprocess assesses whether existing data sources can meet requirements, including suitability, comparability, legal constraints, ICT feasibility and gaps. It is directly relevant to the work description. The position "specifies sources of data to be used in the preparation of subject-matter statistics and forecasts, verifies the consistency and comparability of the various sets of data obtained and modifies the data to permit comparison." It also "researches and compiles data from diverse sources," "assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored," and has contextual knowledge of related statistical programs, legislation, privacy and confidentiality. These are core source-assessment capabilities. Future-state impacts are substantial. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase the need to assess administrative, alternative, linked and possibly geospatial sources rather than relying mainly on survey inputs. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make source discovery and interoperability more systematic, increasing the importance of metadata quality. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will add stronger scrutiny of privacy, secure access, authorizations, platforms and storage environments before sources are considered viable. Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will expand source assessment to linked environments, integrated pipelines and nontraditional formats. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will further push this role toward identifying lower-cost reusable sources. The work description provides strong evidence through source specification, comparability checks, data adaptation, and legal/privacy awareness.

This subprocess designs statistical outputs, products and dissemination approaches. The position is relevant because it participates in analysis and preparation of analytical material for publication, assists in presentation methods and procedures, and writes program information manuals and management reports. The capability involved is helping shape how outputs are presented and explained, especially from a subject-matter and analytical perspective. Evidence includes assisting in recommendations for improvements to "presentation methods and procedures" and preparing analytical material for publication purposes. Future changes are likely through Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity. Outputs will increasingly need richer metadata, more standardized digital formats, and clearer explanatory material that staff can operate and explain using modern tools. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment may also push toward more standardized, reusable dissemination products rather than bespoke outputs.

This subprocess defines collected and derived variables, units and classifications. The work description is relevant because the position develops or modifies statistical methods, concepts and procedures to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions, and has knowledge of concepts, methods and techniques used in collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data to resolve subject-matter concept and definition issues. The capability involved is subject-matter conceptualization and methodological support for variable definitions rather than sole ownership of variable design. Evidence includes "develops new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques and approaches to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions" and knowledge of current or emerging issues to identify concept and definition requirements. Future changes are driven by Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production: variables will increasingly need to align across linked and administrative sources, support derivation, and be documented in richer standardized metadata.

This subprocess designs collection strategy, instruments and methods. The position is relevant because it assists in analysis and feedback on "collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," identifies problems in collection and provides recommendations, and liaises with specialists and users to translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development and procedural modifications. The capability involved is subject-matter and methodological input to collection design, not direct field operations ownership. Evidence includes suggesting feedback on collection methods, reviewing current collection methods for relevancy, and knowledge of collection concepts and techniques. Future-state impacts are meaningful. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will shift collection design toward online-first, mixed-source and administrative-data-supported models. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase use of automated, digital and lower-touch collection approaches. Workforce implications include the need for digital skills and adaptation to changing collection-support roles.

This subprocess designs coding, editing, imputation, integration, validation and estimation methods. It is strongly connected to the work description. The position develops and modifies statistical methods and procedures; determines the need for and implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to collect, capture, process, edit, compile and present statistical data; identifies and evaluates problems in collection, capture, processing, editing, compilation and presentation; reviews current processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods; and examines revised processing specifications for their effect on integration and coordination. The capability involved is methodological and operational design expertise spanning processing and analysis. Evidence is extensive in the decision-making, knowledge, and research sections. Future changes are substantial and cumulative. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will reshape coding, validation, editing, imputation and estimation toward AI-enabled, automated and advanced methods. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase the need for integration and validation methods across heterogeneous sources. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will require methods to be expressed as orchestrated, repeatable pipeline steps. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata operational inputs to processing design. Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will push toward reusable validation and processing modules. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity mean the role will increasingly shift from manual analytical handling toward designing, supervising and improving automated, sustainable methods.

This subprocess designs end-to-end workflows, systems, databases, reuse of existing solutions, and staff-system interactions. The work description is highly relevant because the position determines enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications; liaises with specialists and users to translate requirements into system-development specifications; examines operational system concepts and revised processing specifications to determine effects on integration and coordination with other divisional systems; and coordinates work groups implementing program activities. The capability involved is analytical and subject-matter contribution to workflow and system design, including integration and operational coordination. Evidence includes knowledge of system analysis and design, generalized survey software packages, databases, and system development liaison responsibilities. Future-state impacts are major. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will redesign workflows around enterprise platforms, automation, integrated pipelines and reusable services. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push leaner workflows, clearer accountabilities and reuse-first designs. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is especially relevant because this subprocess explicitly concerns how staff interact with systems and who is responsible for what and when; the work description already shows coordination, guidance and system-facing expertise that will be reshaped by digital and automation-driven workflows.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess builds or reuses components for processing and analysis. The position is relevant because it determines enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications, has knowledge of system analysis and design and generalized survey software packages, and uses programming languages or statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data. The capability involved is contributing specifications, testing expectations and operational requirements for processing components rather than acting as a dedicated software builder. Evidence includes designing, developing, testing, maintaining and implementing processing systems, and examining revised processing specifications. Future changes are likely through AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development. These drivers will increase reuse of enterprise components, AI-enabled coding and validation services, and open-source or modular tools, meaning this role's subject-matter and methodological input to component design and reuse will become more important.

This subprocess configures workflows, systems and transformations across the business process. The position is relevant because it examines operational system concepts and revised processing specifications for effects on integration and coordination, determines modifications to processing systems and applications, and coordinates work groups implementing program activities. The capability involved is helping operationalize designed workflows through specifications, coordination and system understanding. Evidence includes monitoring progress against objectives, providing guidance, and liaising to establish project plans, priorities and target dates. Future changes are driven by Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. Workflow configuration will become more automation-first, standardized and exception-based, increasing the importance of this role's ability to understand handoffs, integration effects and operational implications.

This subprocess prepares people, processes and technology for collection. The work description does not show direct responsibility for operational collection setup, but it does show meaningful indirect relevance through advice on collection methods, knowledge of collection concepts and techniques, liaison with users and specialists, and writing training packages, manuals and monitoring procedures. The capability involved is analytical and documentation support to collection readiness rather than direct setup management. Future changes from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity may increase the need for subject-matter staff to support digital collection readiness, training materials and mixed-source operational guidance. Evidence is limited but present in the communication and knowledge sections.

This subprocess executes collection operations. The work description does not indicate direct responsibility for running collection, respondent management or fieldwork. Relevance is limited to being affected by collection outcomes and providing feedback on collection methods and procedures. Evidence includes assisting in analysis of data and suggesting feedback on collection methods, and identifying problems in collection to provide solutions or recommendations. Future changes from adaptive, online-first and mixed-source collection may affect the role indirectly because collection processes will shape the quality and structure of data the position analyzes, but the work description does not support a stronger classification.

This subprocess loads collected data and metadata into processing environments and handles capture, conversion, archiving and pseudonymisation. The position is only indirectly relevant through its involvement with processing systems, data manipulation, and awareness of metadata, privacy and data handling. Evidence includes determining modifications to systems used to collect, capture and process data, and knowledge of databases, processing systems, and privacy/confidentiality obligations. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access may increase the downstream impact of this subprocess on the role, but the work description does not show direct operational responsibility.

This subprocess integrates data from multiple sources, including harmonisation, linkage, prioritisation and creation of consolidated datasets. It is directly relevant to the work description. The position specifies sources of data, verifies consistency and comparability across datasets, modifies data to permit comparison, researches and compiles data from diverse sources, and assesses the impact of concepts, definitions and collection conditions on results. It also examines effects of revised processing specifications on integration and coordination of data capture and processing functions. The capability involved is multi-source analytical integration and harmonisation. Future-state impacts are strong and cumulative. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production make integration of administrative, alternative, linked and geospatial data central. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will improve interoperability but also require stronger metadata use. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will operationalize integration in scalable, automated environments. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase controls around linkage and de-identification. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will further push substitution of direct collection with integrated source use. The work description provides direct evidence of source comparison, data modification for comparability, and integration-related system analysis.

This subprocess classifies and codes input data, increasingly through automated or AI-enabled methods. The position is relevant because it has knowledge of collection, processing, editing and compilation methods; knowledge of programming languages and statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data; and responsibility for developing or modifying statistical methods and processing systems. While the work description does not explicitly state that the position performs coding routines, it does show involvement in the methods and systems that support such work. Future changes are meaningful: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase automated coding and reduce clerical effort, shifting work toward oversight, validation and methodological support. Administrative and alternative sources may also require more harmonisation to statistical classifications. Evidence is strongest in the knowledge and decision-making sections.

This subprocess detects errors, discrepancies, outliers, duplicates and other quality issues before correction. It is strongly connected to the work description. The position reviews statistical survey and production results, identifies and evaluates problems in collection, capture, processing, editing, compilation and presentation, reviews current methods and procedures to propose changes, and assesses impacts and constraints arising from concepts, definitions and collection conditions. The capability involved is analytical quality review and methodological validation across the production chain. Evidence includes reviewing results, evaluating technical and conceptual problems, and examining system concepts and specifications for integration effects. Future-state impacts are substantial. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase validation complexity across heterogeneous and linked sources. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will expand automated anomaly detection and rule-based validation. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will embed validation checkpoints in automated flows. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata completeness part of validation. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase reliance on automated validation because manual review capacity will be tighter. The role is therefore both directly involved now and likely to be materially reshaped.

This subprocess corrects, replaces or imputes missing, incorrect or unreliable data and records metadata on those actions. The work description is relevant because the position assists in analysis of data and suggests feedback on editing methods and procedures, identifies and evaluates problems in editing and processing, and develops or modifies statistical methods and procedures. The capability involved is methodological support to editing and correction processes rather than explicit ownership of imputation operations. Evidence includes feedback on "editing" methods and knowledge of concepts, methods and techniques used in editing statistical data. Future changes from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push editing and imputation toward more automated and model-assisted approaches, increasing the need for methodological oversight, transparency and metadata. Administrative and linked data expansion will also change source-prioritised correction logic.

This subprocess derives variables and units not directly collected. The position is relevant because it develops new statistical methods, concepts and procedures; conducts special studies requiring econometrics, regression, mathematical programming and modeling; adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats; and assesses impacts of concepts and definitions on results. The capability involved is analytical and methodological derivation of subject-matter measures, though the work description does not explicitly use the GSBPM term 'derive variables.' Evidence includes econometric and modeling knowledge and adapting data to new definitions. Future changes are driven by Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, which will increase reliance on derived variables and units from linked and administrative sources, as well as model-based derivations. Integrated Data Pipelines and Metadata-Driven Data Management will also require clearer sequencing and documentation of derivations.

This subprocess creates weights for records according to designed methodology. The work description shows econometric and statistical expertise and review of survey results, but it does not explicitly mention weighting responsibilities. Relevance is therefore limited and indirect, based on the position's analytical role in survey methods and statistical methodology. Future changes in adaptive collection, administrative auxiliaries and modern survey redesign may affect the role's surrounding analytical context, but the supplied work description does not provide enough evidence to claim direct weighting responsibility.

This subprocess creates aggregate data and totals from microdata or lower-level aggregates. The position is relevant because it participates in analysis of statistical program data, researches and compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts and tables, and prepares analytical material for internal use and publication. The capability involved is transforming processed data into analytical summaries and statistical outputs. Evidence includes producing charts, tables and other output, and reviewing survey and production results. Future changes from Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may expand granular, geospatial and model-based aggregates, while automation and integrated pipelines may standardize routine aggregate production. The role appears to contribute regularly, though not necessarily own the full aggregation process.

This subprocess assembles the results of processing into datasets ready for analysis. The position is relevant because it works across source specification, comparability checks, data manipulation, processing-system modification, and production-result review. The capability involved is helping ensure processed data are coherent and usable for analysis and publication. Evidence includes retrieving and manipulating data, examining integration effects across systems, and preparing analytical material from processed data. Future changes from Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will make final datasets more standardized, metadata-rich and automatically handed off, increasing the importance of this role's understanding of data readiness, comparability and downstream analytical use.

This subprocess transforms processed data into draft statistical outputs and methodological notes. It is directly relevant to the work description. The position "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes," researches and compiles data to produce charts, tables and other output, and writes technical and subject-matter material for colleagues, operational staff and management. The capability involved is analytical drafting, interpretation support and preparation of explanatory material. Future changes are meaningful. AI and Automation in Statistical Production may support drafting and routine output preparation but will increase the need for transparent methodological explanation. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will require clearer notes on mixed-source methods, linkage, geospatial outputs and advanced methods. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the need to package outputs with richer metadata. Evidence from the work description is direct and strong.

This subprocess validates outputs against expectations, prior cycles, auxiliary information and quality indicators. The position is strongly relevant because it identifies statistical trends and developments, reviews survey and production results, assesses impacts of concepts and definitions on results, and conducts special studies requiring econometric and analytical expertise. The capability involved is domain-informed validation and interpretation of whether outputs make sense. Evidence includes identifying and assessing trends and developments, reviewing potential impacts on subject-matter content, and reviewing statistical survey and production results. Future changes are substantial. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the need to validate outputs affected by source substitution, linkage and advanced methods. AI and Automation in Statistical Production will require stronger scrutiny of automated outputs. Metadata-Driven Data Management will make metadata and quality indicators more central to validation. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment may push more risk-based validation. This aligns closely with the role's analytical and subject-matter responsibilities.

This subprocess interprets outputs and explains their meaning using analytical techniques and domain understanding. It is one of the clearest matches to the work description. The position participates in analysis of statistical program data, identifies trends and developments, prepares analytical material for publication, provides advice to users, and has specialized knowledge in econometrics, regression, mathematical programming and modeling. The capability involved is substantive interpretation, explanation and communication of statistical results. Evidence includes providing data, assistance and advice to users within and outside Statistics Canada, writing and presenting detailed subject-matter and technical concepts in common terminology, and conducting special economic, demographic and technological studies. Future changes are driven by AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity. Analysts will increasingly need to explain outputs produced from mixed-source, linked and AI-assisted methods, using new tools while preserving transparency and public trust. This is central to the role now and in the future.

This subprocess ensures outputs and associated information are fit for purpose and ready for release, including commentary, technical notes and internal review. The position is relevant because it prepares analytical material for publication, writes manuals and reports, provides advice to users, and translates technical concepts into common terminology. The capability involved is contributing analytical content, explanatory notes and subject-matter review rather than final release approval. Evidence includes preparing analytical material for publication purposes and writing management reports and technical concepts. Future changes from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will increase the need for caveats, technical notes, metadata completeness and timely internal review. The role contributes materially to these outputs even if it does not appear to hold final approval authority.

This subprocess assembles dissemination products such as tables, charts, maps, publications and explanatory texts. The position is relevant because it prepares analytical material for publication, researches and compiles data to produce charts, tables and other output, and writes explanatory and technical materials. The capability involved is analytical content production and explanatory support for dissemination products. Evidence includes producing statistical charts, tables and other output and writing program information manuals and reports. Future changes are likely through Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. Dissemination products will become more metadata-rich, digital, reusable and standardized, while staff may use AI and automation to assemble recurring products more efficiently.

This subprocess records and responds to user queries and service requests. It is directly relevant because the work description explicitly states that the position "provides data, assistance and advice to users within and outside Statistics Canada." It also liaises with users, explains subject-matter and technical concepts in common terminology, and provides advice to data users and clients on concepts, methods, techniques and results. The capability involved is user-facing analytical support and interpretation of statistical information. Evidence is explicit in both key activities and communication responsibilities. Future changes are meaningful. AI and Automation in Statistical Production may introduce AI assistants, chatbots and knowledge-base support that change how routine queries are handled. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will shift support toward helping users navigate richer digital assets and self-service environments. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment may increase triaging and self-service expectations. Administrative and linked data expansion may also increase methodological questions from users. This subprocess is therefore materially connected now and likely to change significantly.

This subprocess gathers feedback, paradata, system metrics, quality indicators and staff suggestions for evaluation. The position is relevant because it writes monitoring procedures and management reports, reviews survey and production results, provides user advice that can surface changing needs, and assists in studies and reviews supporting project teams or senior officers. The capability involved is generating and interpreting operational and analytical evidence that can feed evaluation, though not necessarily leading formal evaluation. Evidence includes writing monitoring procedures and management reports and reviewing current methods and procedures to propose changes. Future changes from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the amount of process metadata, monitoring information and staff adaptation evidence available. This role's analytical and reporting functions make it a regular contributor to such inputs.

This subprocess analyzes evaluation inputs, compares them to targets and recommends changes. The position is relevant because it reviews methods and procedures to ascertain relevancy and propose changes, identifies and evaluates problems across collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation, assists in subject-matter studies and reviews, and develops recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities. The capability involved is analytical review and continuous-improvement support. Evidence includes proposing changes or alternative systems and providing solutions or recommendations to management. Future changes are likely from Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity. Evaluation will increasingly focus on efficiency, automation benefits, quality, timeliness, workforce readiness and sustainability, all areas this role already touches through analytical review and recommendations.

This subprocess brings together decision-making authority to agree an action plan based on evaluation findings. The work description does not show formal approval authority for enterprise action plans, so relevance is limited. However, the position does contribute recommendations for improvements, coordinates work groups implementing program activities, establishes project plans, priorities and target dates, and provides guidance to working group members. The capability involved is contributing to implementation planning and operational follow-through rather than final governance decisions. Future changes from Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity may increase the importance of disciplined prioritization and clearer ownership in work groups this role supports, but the supplied evidence supports only low relevance.

This subprocess concerns identifying what statistics are needed and how needs change in response to user demand, environmental change, and program review. The work description is relevant because the position directly participates in identifying emerging subject-matter needs and changes in the socio-economic environment: it 'participates in the analysis of socio-economic trends and developments to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs,' 'identifies and assesses changes and developments in the subject area,' and provides advice to managers, data users and clients. That is substantive needs-identification work rather than only downstream analysis. The capability involved is subject-matter analysis, user-need interpretation, and early assessment of implications for program content and methods. Future-state change is driven especially by Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment: under fiscal constraint, need identification becomes more selective and triaged, with stronger pressure to prioritize highest-value needs and consider lower-cost ways of meeting them using automation, AI, machine learning and new tools and methods. Because this position already assesses feasibility and impact of new or modified programs and advises users and managers, it is likely to be increasingly affected by sharper prioritization and reduced capacity.

This subprocess establishes the statistical outputs required to meet confirmed user needs, including trade-offs among quality, scope, timeliness and resources. The position is relevant because it helps translate user and program needs into concrete analytical and statistical outputs: it 'undertakes the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes,' 'interprets program and user needs for statistical information, assesses the suitability of existing data products and services and translates them into a concrete, timely and affordable product,' and liaises with users and specialists to develop requirements and project plans. The capability involved is analytical product definition, subject-matter interpretation, and balancing user requirements with methodological and operational constraints. Future changes are shaped by Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. These drivers mean output objectives will be set with more explicit transparent trade-offs, accountability, and prioritization under scarce resources and fewer staff. For this role, that likely means more pressure to narrow objectives to highest-value outputs, justify scope and timeliness choices, and support managers with evidence on what is feasible and affordable.

This subprocess assesses whether existing data sources can meet requirements, including suitability, legal constraints, ICT feasibility, metadata, continuity and residual gaps. It is highly relevant because the work description explicitly states that the position 'reviews data collection and information systems to determine the usefulness of the existing data sources, to propose changes to the system and to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.' It also 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modification or replacement with alternative systems, methods and procedures,' and has knowledge of legislative and privacy requirements governing manipulation, storage and retrieval of data. The capability involved is source assessment, methodological feasibility analysis, subject-matter alignment, and advising on whether existing or alternative sources can support program needs. Future-state impacts are substantial and cumulative. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will shift this work from traditional survey-source review toward systematic assessment of administrative data, alternative data, SDLE-enabled linkages, gridded data and online-first residual collection. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase scrutiny of privacy, secure access, authorizations and legal conditions. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will make platform fit, centralized repositories, secure ingestion and scalable infrastructure part of source suitability assessment. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the importance of metadata completeness and interoperability. Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production and AI and Automation in Statistical Production will expand the range of usable sources, including unstructured sources, while requiring stronger quality, transparency and governance checks. The work description's repeated emphasis on reviewing sources, systems, feasibility, privacy/confidentiality and recommending changes is direct evidence of strong relevance.

This subprocess documents options, costs, benefits, risks, resources and recommendations for new or modified statistical processes. The position is relevant because it contributes core analytical and operational inputs used in business-case style decisions even if it is not described as the formal approval authority. Evidence includes: assessing 'the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs,' developing 'recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities,' planning and budgeting for special projects, providing cost estimates, developing operational plans and project priorities, and leading project teams involved in special studies. The capability involved is analytical option assessment, feasibility analysis, project planning, and translating subject-matter and operational evidence into recommendations for management. Future changes are driven by Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, and modernization drivers. These will make proposals more disciplined, milestone-based, resource-constrained and explicit about trade-offs, workforce readiness, automation, platform reuse and modernization risks. For this role, that means stronger expectation to provide evidence on costs, benefits, staffing, methods, risks and implementation feasibility when supporting changes to programs or methods.

This subprocess designs statistical outputs, products, services and dissemination arrangements. The position is relevant because it contributes directly to analytical material for publication and to presentation methods: it 'assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes,' 'suggests feedback on ... presentation methods and procedures,' 'writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts,' and 'writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports.' The capability involved is shaping how outputs are framed, explained and presented so they are usable and aligned with subject-matter requirements. Future-state impacts come from Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity. Outputs will increasingly need richer metadata, digital-first and reusable dissemination patterns, secure handling of confidential outputs, and clearer explanatory material for modernized methods. This role's communication and analytical responsibilities suggest meaningful involvement in defining and explaining outputs, though not necessarily building dissemination systems.

This subprocess defines collected and derived variables, classifications and units. The position is relevant because the work description includes developing subject-matter concepts and definitions, modifying techniques and approaches, and reviewing methods, concepts and definitions to improve surveys and data.
