It specifically states the incumbent 'modifies existing techniques and approaches ... and develops subject-matter concepts and definitions' and 'reviews the development of new subject-matter methods, concepts and definitions.' The capability involved is subject-matter conceptualization and ensuring variables and definitions reflect analytical and program needs. Future changes are driven by Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production. Variables will increasingly need to be harmonized across administrative, linked, alternative and geospatial sources, with stronger metadata and derivation logic. Because this role already develops concepts and definitions and reviews methods, it is likely to be materially affected by the shift toward derived, linked and metadata-rich variable design.

This subprocess designs collection strategy, instruments, modes, agreements and respondent management. The position is relevant because it provides analytical feedback on collection methods and procedures and recommends improvements to survey methods and activities. Evidence includes: 'suggests feedback on collection processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures following data analysis and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities,' plus knowledge of survey design and collection methods. The capability involved is using analytical evidence and subject-matter expertise to influence collection design choices rather than directly operating collection systems. Future-state impacts are meaningful: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will shift collection toward online-first, adaptive, mixed-source and administrative-data-supported models; AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will embed digital tools, APIs and automated workflows; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push lower-touch, standardized collection. This role will likely increasingly assess and recommend changes to collection approaches as those models evolve.

This subprocess defines populations, frames and sampling methodology. The work description shows relevant methodological knowledge—'sampling theory,' 'survey design,' and analysis of program coverage—but does not explicitly assign responsibility for frame or sample design. The strongest evidence is that the incumbent modifies techniques to improve 'program coverage' and has knowledge of sampling theory and survey design. The capability connection is therefore plausible but limited: the role may contribute subject-matter and analytical input to coverage and population considerations without being the primary designer of frames and samples. Future changes from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may increase indirect involvement as administrative registers, linked data and geospatial sources reshape coverage and target-population design, but the work description does not support a stronger classification.

This subprocess designs coding, editing, imputation, integration, validation, estimation and disclosure-related methods for processing and analysis. It is highly relevant because the position directly analyzes and evaluates collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods; identifies and evaluates problems in those areas; proposes solutions; and reviews survey methods, statistical applications and techniques used. Evidence includes: 'identifies and evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information,' 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures,' and 'reviews the results of projects and surveys in order to provide interpretation and analysis on subject-matter concepts and definitions, survey methods, statistical applications and techniques used.' The capability involved is methodological analysis and redesign of processing and analytical approaches. Future-state impacts are extensive and cumulative. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all point toward more automated, metadata-driven, reusable, pipeline-based and AI-assisted processing methods with fewer manual interventions and stronger governance, transparency and validation. Because this role already diagnoses and recommends changes to processing and analytical methods, it is one of the most directly affected subprocesses.

This subprocess designs end-to-end workflows, systems, databases, reuse patterns and staff-system interactions. The position is relevant because it reviews information systems, liaises with systems specialists, translates subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, and has knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software and databases. Evidence includes: 'reviews data collection and information systems,' 'liaises ... to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' and possesses 'knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing ... to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems.' The capability involved is subject-matter and methodological input into workflow and system design, especially where analytical and operational requirements must be translated into system specifications. Future changes are significant because Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Governance and Prioritization, Modular Architecture and Operational Efficiency will push reuse-first, automated, platform-based workflows with clearer handoffs and more exception-based work. This role is likely to be materially affected as staff-system interaction and workflow design become more standardized and digitally integrated.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess builds or reuses processing and analysis components needed for Process and Analyse phases. The work description does not state that the incumbent is a software builder, but it does show meaningful involvement in specifying, testing, maintaining and developing processing systems and databases, and in using programming languages and statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data. Evidence includes knowledge 'to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and develop databases,' plus 'knowledge of high level programming languages, utility programs or statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data.' The capability involved is analytical-method and subject-matter contribution to component development and reuse, and possibly hands-on technical work with data and databases. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines, Modern Statistical Methods, Modular Architecture and Workforce Skills Transition suggest more reusable, automated, open-source and enterprise components, with staff shifting toward configuring, validating and sustaining shared analytical services. This role is therefore regularly connected, though not clearly the primary software engineering authority.

This subprocess configures workflows, systems and transformations across the business process. The position is relevant because it helps translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications and project plans, and has knowledge of system analysis, design and processing systems. Evidence includes liaising 'to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' discussing requirements with systems specialists and operations managers, and knowledge to manage design, development, testing and implementation of processing systems. The capability involved is configuring or shaping operational workflows from a subject-matter and methodological perspective, especially where transformations and handoffs must reflect analytical requirements. Future-state impacts from Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation, Modular Architecture, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition mean workflows will become more automated, standardized and exception-driven. This role is likely to be affected through increased need to define, monitor and adapt workflow logic and handoffs.

This subprocess tests assembled services, workflows, secure channels and data exchanges. The position is relevant because the work description includes knowledge to manage testing of processing systems and to design specifications for testing data, and because it reviews systems and methods for usefulness and feasibility. Evidence includes knowledge of system analysis and design 'to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data,' and reviewing collection and information systems to propose changes. The capability involved is methodological and subject-matter testing support, especially validating whether systems and data behave as required for statistical use. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation, Cyber Security, Enterprise Digital Platforms, Integrated Data Pipelines, Modern Statistical Methods and Modular Architecture will increase the complexity of testing automated, secure, integrated and reusable systems. This role is therefore meaningfully connected through testing specifications and assessment of system suitability.

This subprocess covers documentation, user manuals, training and moving systems into production. The work description provides some evidence through writing manuals, training packages and monitoring procedures, and leading project teams, but it does not clearly assign responsibility for production deployment. Evidence includes 'writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports' and leadership of special projects. The capability connection is therefore limited to supporting documentation and training rather than full production finalization. Future-state drivers around Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, Enterprise Digital Platforms and AI adoption may increase the importance of this support role, but the work description does not justify a stronger relevance level.

This subprocess prepares people, processes and technology for collection. The work description does not indicate direct operational responsibility for collection setup, but it does show indirect relevance through recommendations on survey methods, knowledge of collection methods, and writing training packages and manuals. The capability involved is advisory support to collection readiness rather than direct setup. Future-state changes in digital collection, online-first strategy and workforce training may increase indirect effects on the role, especially where analytical feedback informs setup decisions, but evidence remains limited.

This subprocess executes collection and manages respondent or supplier interactions. The work description does not show direct responsibility for running collection, but it does indicate some indirect connection through feedback on collection methods, advice to clients and respondents, and resolving collection-related problems referred by staff. Evidence includes identifying and evaluating problems in collection and encountering resistance from external clients or respondents. The capability involved is analytical and advisory support to collection operations rather than direct operational management. Future-state digital and automated collection may affect the role indirectly through increased need to interpret collection performance and recommend changes, but the work description does not support stronger relevance.

This subprocess loads collected data and metadata for further processing and handles versioning, archiving and pseudonymisation. The work description does not explicitly assign these operational tasks, though it does include knowledge of data manipulation, storage, retrieval, confidentiality and databases. The capability connection is therefore limited and indirect. Future-state metadata-driven and automated collection finalization may affect the role through downstream analytical dependence on better metadata and source handling, but there is insufficient evidence of direct responsibility.

This subprocess combines data from multiple sources, including linkage, harmonisation and prioritisation. The position is relevant because it reviews usefulness of existing data sources, analyzes statistical program data, assesses suitability of data products and services, and has knowledge of databases, data retrieval and manipulation. It also interprets user needs and reviews methods to improve surveys and data. The capability involved is analytical integration from a subject-matter and methodological perspective, especially assessing how multiple sources can support coherent outputs. Future-state impacts are substantial: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security, Enterprise Digital Platforms, Integrated Data Pipelines, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Modern Statistical Methods and Operational Efficiency all make integration more central, more automated and more dependent on linkage, harmonisation and secure access. While the work description does not explicitly say the incumbent performs record linkage, it strongly supports regular contribution to multi-source assessment and integration-related methodological work.

This subprocess classifies and codes input data, increasingly through automated methods. The position is relevant because it has knowledge of subject-matter concepts, definitions and classifications, uses programming/statistical packages to manipulate data, and analyzes processing and editing methods. The work description also emphasizes resolving conceptual and technical problems and reviewing statistical applications and techniques. The capability involved is ensuring coding and classification align with subject-matter standards and analytical needs, and likely using or assessing coding outputs in analysis. Future-state impacts are meaningful: AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production directly increase automated coding; Administrative and Alternative Data Expansion increases non-standard source coding needs; Metadata-Driven Data Management strengthens standard classifications; Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition push automation and reskilling. The role is not described as a dedicated coder, but it is materially connected through methodological oversight and use of coded data.

This subprocess identifies errors, discrepancies, outliers, duplicates and other quality issues before or after integration. It is highly relevant because the work description repeatedly emphasizes analyzing data, comparing versions, identifying and evaluating problems in collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation, and reviewing survey results to provide interpretation and analysis. Evidence includes 'identifies and evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information,' 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods,' 'reviews the results of projects and surveys,' and there is even 'an occasional requirement for sensory observation when comparing old and new versions of data.' The capability involved is statistical quality review, methodological validation and analytical diagnosis of anomalies and issues. Future-state impacts are strong: AI and Automation, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Modern Statistical Methods, Modular Architecture and Operational Efficiency all increase automated validation, exception handling, metadata checks and multi-source quality assessment. This role is directly aligned with those needs.

This subprocess corrects, replaces or imputes missing, incorrect or unreliable data and records metadata on those changes. The position is relevant because it analyzes and evaluates editing methods and procedures, identifies problems in editing and processing, and recommends methodological improvements. Evidence includes feedback on 'editing' methods and procedures, identifying problems in 'processing, editing, compilation and presentation,' and knowledge of concepts, methods and techniques used in collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data. The capability involved is methodological oversight and analytical assessment of editing and imputation approaches rather than necessarily performing all edits directly. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Modern Statistical Methods, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition point toward more automated, source-prioritized and metadata-documented editing/imputation. This role is meaningfully affected because it already evaluates and recommends changes to those methods.

This subprocess derives variables and units not directly collected. The position is relevant because it develops subject-matter concepts and definitions, analyzes and synthesizes socio-economic characteristics, prepares profiles and forecasts, and uses statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data. These are core capabilities for deriving analytical variables and constructs from existing data. Evidence includes 'analyzes and synthesizes geographic, demographic, social, economic and/or labour market characteristics and prepares profiles and forecasts' and develops subject-matter concepts and definitions. Future-state impacts are meaningful: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods will increase reliance on derived variables from linked and administrative sources; Integrated Data Pipelines and Metadata-Driven Data Management will require more explicit sequencing and documentation of derivations; Operational Efficiency will encourage derivation instead of direct collection where feasible. The role is therefore regularly connected through analytical derivation and conceptual work.

This subprocess creates weights for records according to methodology. The work description includes knowledge of sampling theory and survey design, which makes involvement plausible, but it does not explicitly assign weighting responsibilities. The capability connection is therefore limited to methodological literacy that may support weighting discussions or interpretation. Future changes in hybrid survey-administrative estimation may increase indirect exposure, but the supplied work description does not justify medium or high relevance.

This subprocess creates aggregate data and totals from microdata. The position is relevant because it undertakes analysis of statistical program data, prepares analytical material for publication, analyzes socio-economic characteristics, prepares profiles and forecasts, and reviews survey results for interpretation. Those activities depend on and often involve aggregate production and interpretation. The capability involved is transforming analyzed data into summary statistical outputs and interpreting aggregate patterns. Future-state impacts from Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production include more granular, geospatial and model-based aggregates, while automation and integrated pipelines will standardize recurring aggregate production. The work description supports regular contribution to aggregate-based analysis even if not explicit ownership of aggregation routines.

This subprocess assembles the processed dataset used as input to analysis. The position is relevant because it works at the boundary between processing and analysis: it analyzes statistical program data, uses programming/statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data, maintains and develops databases, and reviews processing methods and systems. The capability involved is ensuring processed data are analytically usable and aligned with subject-matter needs. Future-state impacts from Integrated Data Pipelines, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Enterprise Digital Platforms, Agility and Modern Statistical Methods will make final analytic datasets more standardized, metadata-rich and pipeline-driven, with stronger versioning and handoff discipline. This role is materially connected because its analytical work depends on and likely helps assess readiness of those files for analysis.

This subprocess transforms processed data into draft statistical outputs and methodological notes. It is highly relevant because the work description explicitly states the incumbent 'undertakes the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.' It also writes and presents detailed subject-matter and technical concepts, writes manuals and reports, and reviews survey results to provide interpretation and analysis. The capability involved is converting statistical analysis into publishable analytical outputs with supporting explanation. Future-state impacts are significant: AI and Automation may support drafting and standard output generation; Administrative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods will require more explanation of mixed-source, model-based and geospatial outputs; Metadata-Driven Data Management will increase the need for richer contextual metadata; Operational Efficiency will push templating and automation; Workforce Skills Transition will increase demands on analytical expertise and communication. This is one of the clearest direct matches in the work description.

This subprocess validates outputs against expectations, prior cycles, auxiliary information, metadata and quality indicators. It is highly relevant because the position undertakes substantive analytical review and interpretation of survey and project results, identifies changes and developments in the subject area, and assesses impacts on program content. Evidence includes 'reviews the results of projects and surveys in order to provide interpretation and analysis,' 'analyzes and synthesizes ... characteristics and prepares profiles and forecasts,' and 'identifies and assesses changes and developments in the subject area.' The capability involved is domain-informed validation: checking whether outputs make sense in light of subject-matter knowledge, prior evidence and methodological context. Future-state impacts are strong because Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods, AI and Automation, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Operational Efficiency all increase the need for faster but more sophisticated validation of outputs produced from new sources and methods. This role's subject-matter expertise and analytical review responsibilities make it directly relevant.

This subprocess interprets outputs, explains their meaning and assesses them against expectations using analytical tools such as time series and econometric analysis. It is highly relevant because the work description is centered on exactly this kind of work: analyzing statistical program data, preparing analytical material for publication, analyzing socio-economic trends, preparing profiles and forecasts, and possessing 'a thorough knowledge of the theories and principles of economics, econometric methods and techniques,' plus working knowledge of time series, special analysis and forecasting. The capability involved is substantive interpretation of socio-economic statistics and explanation of results to internal and external users. Evidence also includes providing subject-matter advice to data users and writing/presenting technical concepts in common terminology. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Workforce Skills Transition mean analysts will increasingly need to explain outputs produced from mixed-source, model-based and AI-assisted processes while using new tools themselves. This is a core subprocess for the role.

This subprocess applies confidentiality protections to outputs and stored data. The work description does not assign direct disclosure-control duties, but it does show strong awareness of confidentiality obligations under the Statistics Act and Privacy Act, including ensuring no identifying information is released. The capability connection is therefore limited but real: the incumbent must work within confidentiality rules and understand security and privacy constraints on outputs and data handling. Future-state impacts from Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and linked-data expansion may increase the practical importance of these constraints for the role, but the supplied evidence does not support direct operational responsibility for disclosure control methods.

This subprocess completes consistency checks, caveats, commentary, technical notes, internal briefings and approval preparation for release. The position is relevant because it prepares analytical material for publication, writes reports and explanatory material, provides advice to managers and users, and writes detailed subject-matter and technical concepts in common terminology. The capability involved is preparing the substantive analytical and explanatory content that supports release readiness. Future-state impacts from Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods, Governance and Workforce Skills Transition will increase the need for timely caveats, technical notes, uncertainty communication and disciplined approval support. The role appears to contribute materially to final content and supporting explanation, though not necessarily to final release authority.

This subprocess assembles dissemination products such as publications, tables, maps, websites and explanatory texts. The position is relevant because it assists in preparing analytical material for publication, writes explanatory and technical material, and provides subject-matter advice to users. Evidence includes preparation of analytical material for publication, writing detailed concepts in common terminology, and writing manuals and reports. The capability involved is producing the analytical and explanatory components of dissemination products rather than building dissemination platforms. Future-state impacts from Metadata-Driven Data Management, Enterprise Digital Platforms, AI and Automation, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition will push more digital, metadata-rich, reusable and standardized products with stronger quality statements and methodological explanation. This role is therefore regularly connected to product content creation.

This subprocess records and responds to user queries and service requests, including support for microdata access and partner dissemination. The position is relevant because the work description explicitly states it 'provides assistance and subject matter advice to data users within and outside STC' and maintains liaison with client departments to understand needs and provide advice and guidance on concepts, methods, techniques and results. It also notes encounters with external clients, respondents, media and the public. The capability involved is subject-matter user support, explanation of methods and results, and responding to client needs. Future-state impacts are meaningful: AI and Automation may introduce chatbots, AI assistants and knowledge-base support; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Metadata-Driven Data Management will shift support toward self-service and metadata-rich discovery; Cyber Security and Secure Access will affect support for restricted services; Operational Efficiency will increase triage and reuse of support content. Because user advice is explicitly part of the role, this subprocess is materially connected.

This subprocess gathers feedback, paradata, system metrics, staff suggestions and quality indicators for evaluation. The position is relevant because it undertakes subject-matter studies and reviews, analyzes methods and procedures to determine relevance and need for modification, reviews project and survey results, and leads special studies. Those activities generate evaluation evidence and recommendations. The capability involved is collecting and synthesizing analytical findings about program performance, methods and outputs. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Agility, Enterprise Platforms, Integrated Pipelines, Metadata-Driven Management, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition will increase the volume and importance of process metrics, staff feedback, source-quality indicators and modernization evidence. This role is likely to contribute materially to gathering and interpreting such inputs through its review and study functions.

This subprocess analyzes evaluation inputs, compares them to expectations and produces evaluation reports or dashboards with recommendations. The position is relevant because it conducts studies and analytical projects to improve surveys and data, assesses feasibility and impact of new or modified programs, reviews methods and procedures for relevance, and develops recommendations for improvements. Evidence includes 'conducts studies and analytical projects to improve existing surveys and data,' 'assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities,' and assesses feasibility and impact of program changes. The capability involved is evaluative analysis of program performance, methods and outputs, leading to recommendations for future changes. Future-state impacts are strong from AI and Automation, Agility, Governance, Operational Efficiency, Workforce Skills Transition and modernization drivers, which will make evaluation more dashboard-driven, more focused on efficiency, quality, workforce readiness and modernization outcomes. The role is materially connected as an evaluator and recommender, though not necessarily the final governance authority.

This subprocess brings together decision-making authority to agree an action plan and monitoring mechanism based on evaluation findings. The work description supports some involvement because the position develops recommendations, leads project teams, sets goals and priorities for special studies, and plans operational work. However, it does not clearly state that the incumbent has the authority to agree enterprise or program action plans arising from evaluation. The capability connection is therefore limited to contributing recommendations and project-level planning input. Future-state drivers around Governance, Prioritization, Agility, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition may increase the importance of disciplined action planning around the role's recommendations, but the supplied evidence does not support a stronger relevance level.

This subprocess concerns the initial investigation of what statistics are needed and what users require from them. The position is directly relevant because it explicitly investigates client requirements and determines the nature and scope of studies: the work description states the incumbent 'Investigates client requirements for statistical information, determines the nature and scope of studies' and 'Conducts analysis of socio-economic trends and developments to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.' The capability involved is subject-matter analysis, user-need interpretation, and early program scoping. The role fulfills that need by translating uncertain client demands into concrete statistical studies and by assessing feasibility and impact for new or modified programs. Future-state change is driven especially by Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment: under fewer resources and stronger prioritization, this need-identification work will become more selective and triage-oriented. The driver’s technology themes—artificial intelligence, automation, machine learning, and new tools and methods—may change how needs are assessed and what is considered feasible, while workforce implications such as a decrease of approximately 900 FTEs and prioritization of services increase pressure to focus only on highest-value needs.

This subprocess establishes the statistical output objectives needed to meet confirmed user needs, including quality, scope, and resource considerations. The position is materially connected because it determines study scope, methods, outputs, and recommends changes to survey content, coverage, and presentation. Evidence includes: 'determines the nature and scope of studies,' 'Interprets preliminary results, reviews study format and modifies approaches and techniques as necessary,' and 'recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage.' The capability involved is defining fit-for-purpose outputs and balancing user needs with methodological, legal, and operational constraints. The role fulfills this by shaping what studies will produce and by advising on presentation and dissemination practices. Future changes will be influenced by Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. Capability themes such as accountability, prioritization, transparent trade-offs, and cross-field decision-making will make output-setting more explicit and constrained. With scarce resources and workforce reductions, the incumbent’s current discretion in shaping outputs will increasingly need to account for tighter trade-offs among scope, timeliness, granularity, and quality.

This subprocess assesses whether existing data sources can meet requirements and under what legal, technical, and operational conditions. The work description is strongly relevant because the position works across collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods, integrates data from multiple sources, and knows data suppliers, users, legislation, confidentiality, and related programs. Evidence includes: 'Modifies existing techniques or develops new methods of collecting, processing, editing, compiling and presenting statistical data'; 'Some studies may involve ... the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses)'; 'Knowledge of data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements'; and knowledge of the Statistics Act, Privacy Act, confidentiality, security, and data quality. The capability involved is assessing source suitability, comparability, access conditions, and legal/policy constraints. The role fulfills this need by reviewing source gaps and inconsistencies, translating different concepts into common concepts, and recommending changes to collection or production systems. Future-state impacts are substantial. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase reliance on administrative, alternative, linked, and geospatial sources; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will intensify scrutiny of privacy, authorizations, and secure access; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will make platform fit, centralized repositories, and secure ingestion more central; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the importance of metadata quality in source assessment; and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push stronger use of lower-cost reusable sources. The position is already aligned with these needs through its source integration, legal knowledge, and recommendations on systems and methods.

This subprocess documents options, costs, benefits, risks, resources, and recommendations for approval of new or modified statistical processes. The position is relevant because it assesses feasibility studies and project proposals, makes recommendations to senior management, defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries, plans budgets, negotiates contracts, and recommends implementation of new hardware and software. Evidence includes: 'evaluates feasibility studies and project proposals submitted by stakeholders and makes recommendations to senior management'; 'Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources'; 'Plans and budgets for on-going studies and/or special projects'; and 'Develops proposals for further study ... and the implementation of new hardware and software.' The capability involved is assembling the analytical, methodological, operational, and resource rationale that underpins approval decisions. The role fulfills this need through feasibility assessment, option development, budgeting, and project planning, though the description does not explicitly say the incumbent submits formal business cases. Future changes will be shaped by Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity. These drivers will make approval packages more milestone-driven, more explicit about trade-offs, more focused on savings and reuse, and more attentive to workforce readiness, training, and reduced staffing capacity.

This subprocess designs statistical outputs, products, services, and dissemination procedures. The position is relevant because it writes and edits analytical material for publication, provides feedback on presentation methods, and has knowledge of publication, marketing, and dissemination policies and practices. Evidence includes: 'writes and edits analytical material for internal use and publication purposes'; 'Provides feedback on ... presentation methods and procedures'; and 'Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination.' The capability involved is shaping how outputs are structured, explained, and prepared for users. The role fulfills this by influencing presentation methods and preparing analytical content and explanatory materials. Future-state impacts include stronger metadata-rich and digital-first dissemination expectations, secure-access requirements for confidential outputs, and more standardized reusable dissemination patterns. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the need for outputs to be metadata-rich and discoverable; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will strengthen confidentiality-by-design; and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push standardization over bespoke products.

This subprocess defines variables, derived variables, units, and classifications. The position is relevant because it recommends changes to questionnaire design, survey content and coverage, integrates conceptually different data into common concepts, and works with statistical concepts and classification systems. Evidence includes: 'recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage'; 'Often, the data have been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts'; and 'Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies ... and classification systems.' The capability involved is conceptual and methodological design of what is measured and how variables align across sources. The role fulfills this need by improving concepts, extending application of divisional statistics, and harmonizing definitions across programs and sources. Future changes will come from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, which will increase emphasis on harmonized variables, derived variables from linked and non-survey sources, and richer variable metadata.

This subprocess prepares collection strategy, instruments, methods, agreements, and respondent management approaches. The position is strongly relevant because it develops new methods of collecting data, recommends questionnaire and survey-content changes, recommends revisions to collection systems and processes, negotiates with service providers, and resolves issues affecting collection efficiency and data quality. Evidence includes: 'develops new methods of collecting ... statistical data'; 'recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design ... revisions to collection or production systems and processes'; 'Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources, timeframes and costs with service providers ... regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors'; and 'resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the collection and compilation of data and the quality of outputs.' The capability involved is designing collection approaches that meet subject-matter needs while fitting operational realities. The role fulfills this through methodological recommendations, service-provider negotiation, and subject-matter leadership on development projects. Future-state impacts are major: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will shift collection toward online-first, adaptive, and mixed-source models; AI and Automation in Statistical Production will introduce more automated and workflow-integrated collection; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will strengthen secure-by-design collection; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will push reusable digital collection tooling; and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will reduce tolerance for labour-intensive collection modes.

This subprocess defines populations, frames, and sampling methodology. The work description does not explicitly assign sampling design responsibility, so relevance is limited. However, there is plausible involvement because the incumbent recommends changes to survey content and coverage, understands other statistical programs and databases, and integrates data from administrative and survey sources. Evidence includes 'enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage' and knowledge of 'other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise.' The capability involved would be subject-matter input into target populations or coverage implications rather than formal sample design. Future changes from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods may increase indirect involvement where source-based frames and coverage issues affect subject-matter interpretation, but the description does not support a stronger classification.

This subprocess designs methodologies for coding, editing, imputation, integration, validation, estimation, and disclosure control where process-specific. The position is directly relevant because it modifies or develops methods for processing, editing, compiling and presenting data; reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods; integrates data from multiple sources; and provides feedback and recommendations after analysis. Evidence includes: 'Modifies existing techniques or develops new methods of collecting, processing, editing, compiling and presenting statistical data'; 'Reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures used'; and 'Some studies may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources.' The capability involved is methodological design for downstream processing and analytical quality. The role fulfills this by redesigning methods, resolving technical and conceptual problems, and recommending system and process changes. Future-state impacts are extensive. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all point to more automated, modular, metadata-driven, and reusable processing methods, with staff shifting toward oversight, exception handling, and advanced methodological stewardship.

This subprocess designs the end-to-end workflow, systems, databases, reuse of existing solutions, and staff responsibilities across production. The position is strongly relevant because it recommends revisions to collection or production systems and processes, implementation of new hardware and software, leads multidisciplinary project teams, negotiates with system specialists and service providers, and represents subject-matter divisions on development projects. Evidence includes: 'revisions to collection or production systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software'; 'Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees'; 'Supervises project teams'; and negotiation with 'system specialists.' The capability involved is translating subject-matter and methodological requirements into operational workflow and system changes, including role clarity and cross-functional coordination. The role fulfills this by shaping production redesign and leading projects that affect how processes fit together. Future-state impacts are especially strong from Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity. These drivers collectively imply more standardized enterprise workflows, clearer handoffs, fewer manual interventions, stronger governance, and greater emphasis on staff-system interaction, training, and role redesign.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess builds or reuses components needed for processing and analysis. The position is relevant because it recommends new hardware and software, revises production systems and processes, and develops or modifies methods that would drive component requirements. Evidence includes recommendations for 'implementation of new hardware and software' and 'revisions to collection or production systems and processes.' The capability involved is specifying and shaping the analytical and methodological functionality that components must support, rather than hands-on technical build. The role fulfills this need by defining requirements through methodological redesign and project leadership. Future changes from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will increase reliance on reusable enterprise components and may make the role more involved in specifying standardized analytical services and workflow tools.

This subprocess configures workflows, systems, and transformations based on designed production workflows. The position is relevant because it leads projects affecting production systems and processes, negotiates with system specialists, and resolves technical and conceptual problems affecting collection, processing, and output quality. Evidence includes negotiation with 'system specialists,' recommendations on 'production systems and processes,' and leadership on development projects. The capability involved is operationalizing methodological and subject-matter requirements into configured workflows, though the description does not explicitly assign direct configuration duties. The role fulfills this need indirectly through project leadership, requirement-setting, and issue resolution. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will make workflow standardization and automation more central, increasing the practical impact of this role’s decisions even if technical configuration remains elsewhere.

This subprocess prepares people, processes, systems, and materials for a collection instance. The position has limited but plausible relevance because it leads projects, negotiates with service providers, and recommends collection-system changes, but the description does not explicitly assign operational collection setup responsibilities such as staff training, device preparation, or respondent communications. Evidence is indirect: negotiation with regional office staff and survey methodologists, and recommendations on collection systems and questionnaire design. Future-state drivers around digital collection, secure setup, and workforce transition may increase the downstream effect of the role’s design decisions on setup activities, but the work description supports only low relevance.

This subprocess executes collection operations. The position is only indirectly connected. The work description shows the incumbent provides feedback on collection methods after analysis and resolves issues affecting collection efficiency and output quality, but does not state that the incumbent runs collection operations. Evidence includes 'Provides feedback on collection ... methods and procedures following data analysis' and participation in resolving issues affecting 'the efficiency of the collection and compilation of data.' The capability involved is analytical feedback into collection performance rather than operational execution. Future changes in adaptive and digital collection may increase the importance of analytical monitoring and feedback, but the description does not support medium or high relevance.

This subprocess combines data from multiple sources, harmonises concepts, prioritises conflicting values, and may include linkage and geospatial integration. The position is directly relevant because the work description explicitly states that studies often involve integrating data from financial statements, tax files, administrative sources, surveys, and censuses, and translating different definitions into common concepts. Evidence includes: 'integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses)' and 'must be translated into common concepts.' The capability involved is multi-source integration, harmonisation, and conceptual reconciliation. The role fulfills this need through advanced analysis, methodological adaptation, and knowledge of related programs and databases. Future-state impacts are very strong from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity. These drivers will make integration more central, more automated, more metadata-dependent, and more privacy-sensitive, increasing the complexity and strategic importance of work already present in the role.

This subprocess applies classifications and coding routines to input data. The work description shows knowledge of classification systems and processing methods, but does not explicitly assign coding responsibilities. Evidence includes 'Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies ... and classification systems' and broad knowledge of processing and editing methods. The capability involved would be understanding and advising on classification use rather than performing coding operations. Future-state drivers such as AI-enabled automated coding and metadata standardization may affect the role indirectly through methodological oversight and interpretation of coded outputs, but the supplied description does not justify stronger relevance.

This subprocess identifies errors, discrepancies, outliers, duplicates, and other quality issues before and after integration. The position is strongly relevant because it interprets study results, determines reasons for variances, reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in collection and processing methods, and resolves technical and conceptual problems. Evidence includes: 'Interprets study results, determines reasons for variances'; 'Reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures used'; and 'reviews and resolves technical and conceptual problems.' The capability involved is analytical validation, quality assessment, and diagnosis of anomalies in data and methods. The role fulfills this need through substantive and methodological review of outputs and processes. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will shift validation toward more automated, exception-based, metadata-aware, and multi-source quality control, increasing the need for expert oversight and interpretation.

This subprocess corrects, replaces, or imputes missing, unreliable, or duplicated data and records metadata on those changes. The position is relevant because it works on editing methods, resolves inconsistencies, and develops or modifies processing approaches. Evidence includes 'develops new methods of ... editing' and 'Reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, editing ... methods and procedures used.' The capability involved is methodological oversight of correction and editing approaches rather than explicit operational imputation. The role fulfills this need by redesigning methods and recommending improvements after analysis. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability suggest more automated and model-assisted editing and stronger metadata traceability, which would increase the methodological complexity of work this role already influences.

This subprocess derives variables and units not directly collected. The position is relevant because it integrates conceptually different data, improves concepts, and develops new approaches to extend divisional statistics. Evidence includes: 'improve existing concepts or develop new approaches to extend the application of divisional statistics' and translating source data 'into common concepts.' The capability involved is conceptual derivation and analytical transformation of source data into usable statistical constructs. The role fulfills this through subject-matter expertise and methodological development, though the description does not explicitly mention derivation routines. Future-state impacts from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase reliance on derived variables from linked and administrative sources and require clearer lineage and sequencing of derivations.

This subprocess creates survey or calibration weights. The work description does not explicitly mention weighting, calibration, or nonresponse adjustment. There is only indirect relevance through broad statistical-method knowledge and survey-method improvement responsibilities. Future modernization of hybrid survey and administrative models may affect the role’s broader methodological environment, but the supplied information does not support a stronger connection.

This subprocess creates aggregate data and totals from microdata or lower-level aggregates. The position is relevant because it plans and conducts analysis of statistical program data, reviews survey findings, writes analytical material for publication, and interprets results and variances over time. Evidence includes 'Plans and conducts the analysis of statistical program data' and 'analyze, review and present survey findings.' The capability involved is transforming processed data into analytical summaries and interpretable statistical results. The role fulfills this through substantive analysis and preparation of outputs, though the description does not explicitly mention aggregate calculation mechanics. Future-state impacts from Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may increase use of granular geospatial and model-based aggregates, affecting the analytical context of this work.

This subprocess assembles final datasets for analysis. The position is indirectly affected because it depends on finalized data for analysis and interprets results from them, but the description does not assign responsibility for assembling or packaging final data files. Future automation and integrated pipelines may change how analysis-ready files are delivered to the role, but the work description does not support direct operational responsibility.

This subprocess transforms processed data into draft statistical outputs and methodological notes. The position is directly relevant because it analyzes statistical program data, writes and edits analytical material for internal use and publication, writes technical concepts in common terminology, and presents study results and recommendations. Evidence includes: 'Plans and conducts the analysis of statistical program data; writes and edits analytical material for internal use and publication purposes'; 'Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology'; and attendance at meetings with senior officials to explain results. The capability involved is converting analytical findings into usable draft outputs and explanatory material. The role fulfills this directly through analysis, writing, editing, and explanation. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase use of templating, AI-assisted drafting, richer metadata, and stronger methodological explanation for outputs based on advanced methods and mixed sources.

This subprocess validates outputs against expectations, prior cycles, auxiliary information, metadata, and domain intelligence. The position is strongly relevant because it interprets study results, determines reasons for variances and comparability over time, analyzes socio-economic trends and developments, and explains variances using knowledge of related programs and databases. Evidence includes: 'determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions' and knowledge of other programs 'to explain variances.' The capability involved is domain-informed validation of outputs and assessment of whether results make sense. The role fulfills this directly through substantive expertise, trend analysis, and comparison across sources and time. Future-state impacts from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will make validation more complex because outputs will increasingly reflect linked, administrative, geospatial, and model-based methods, requiring stronger benchmark comparison and faster but robust assurance.

This subprocess interprets outputs, explains their meaning, and assesses them against expectations using domain knowledge and analytical tools. The position is directly aligned: it conducts analysis of socio-economic trends, interprets study results, explains results to senior officials and external users, and writes technical and subject-matter concepts in common language. Evidence includes: 'Conducts analysis of socio-economic trends and developments'; 'Interprets study results'; 'Attends meetings with senior officials to interpret or explain study results and recommendations'; and 'Provides subject-matter expertise and advice' to governments, business, agencies, and academics. The capability involved is substantive interpretation, explanation, and communication of statistical meaning. The role fulfills this core need directly. Future-state impacts from Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require the incumbent to explain outputs produced from more complex mixed-source and AI-assisted methods, increasing demands for methodological literacy, clear communication, and trust-building.

This subprocess applies confidentiality protections to outputs and stored data. The position has limited relevance because the work description emphasizes knowledge of confidentiality, security, the Statistics Act, and the Privacy Act, and responsibility to ensure no identifying information is released improperly. Evidence includes knowledge of 'confidentiality of data, security' and ensuring they 'do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.' The capability involved is compliance awareness and confidentiality stewardship rather than explicit application of disclosure-control techniques. Future-state drivers around privacy, secure access, linked data, and geospatial outputs may increase the importance of this awareness, but the description does not indicate direct responsibility for suppression, perturbation, or output checking.

This subprocess ensures outputs are fit for purpose, collates commentary and technical notes, conducts internal review, and approves content for release. The position is strongly relevant because it writes and edits publication material, presents and explains results, has knowledge of dissemination policies and explanatory notes, and provides advice that is accepted by senior management and informs policy or action. Evidence includes writing for publication, preparing 'statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination,' and attending meetings with senior officials to explain results and recommendations. The capability involved is final analytical packaging of outputs, including commentary, caveats, and internal briefing. The role fulfills this through substantive review, communication, and preparation of dissemination-ready analytical content. Future-state impacts from Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase pressure for timely sign-off, stronger metadata and technical notes, clearer caveats for advanced methods, and disciplined approval under constrained resources.

This subprocess assembles dissemination products such as publications, tables, charts, maps, and explanatory texts. The position is relevant because it writes and edits analytical material for publication, writes technical concepts in common terminology, and has knowledge of dissemination practices for tables, charts, and explanatory notes. Evidence includes 'writes and edits analytical material for internal use and publication purposes' and knowledge needed for 'preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination.' The capability involved is producing substantive content and explanatory components of dissemination products. The role fulfills this by preparing analytical text and influencing presentation methods. Future-state impacts from Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push more standardized, metadata-rich, digital, and reusable dissemination products, affecting how this analytical content is assembled and delivered.

This subprocess records and responds to user queries and service requests and supports partner organizations. The position is relevant because it provides advisory and consultative services to data users within and outside Statistics Canada, offers subject-matter expertise to governments, business, agencies, and academics, and negotiates with clients inside and outside the department. Evidence includes: 'Provides advisory and consultative services as well as subject matter advice to data users within and outside STC' and 'Provides subject-matter expertise and advice to all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics.' The capability involved is user-facing interpretation, advisory support, and response to complex information needs. The role fulfills this directly through consultation and explanation of survey results and developments. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment suggest more self-service, chatbot-supported, and metadata-enabled support models, while the role may increasingly focus on higher-complexity interpretive requests rather than routine inquiries.

This subprocess gathers feedback, process metadata, system metrics, and staff suggestions for evaluation. The position is relevant because it provides feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods following data analysis, investigates client requirements, and works closely enough with users and projects to generate evaluative evidence. Evidence includes: 'Provides feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures following data analysis' and ongoing advisory interactions with users and stakeholders. The capability involved is generating analytical feedback and identifying quality or process issues from substantive analysis and user interaction. The role fulfills this by surfacing variances, inconsistencies, client needs, and recommendations for improvement. Future-state impacts from AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the amount of process evidence available and the importance of staff and user feedback on modernization impacts.

This subprocess analyzes evaluation inputs, compares them to targets, and produces evaluation findings and recommendations. The position is relevant because it assesses feasibility and impact of new or modified programs, evaluates project proposals, interprets results against changing requirements and socio-economic conditions, and makes recommendations to senior management. Evidence includes: 'assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs'; 'evaluates feasibility studies and project proposals ... and makes recommendations to senior management'; and interpretation of relevance in light of 'changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.' The capability involved is evaluative analysis of program performance, relevance, and methodological adequacy. The role fulfills this through analytical review and recommendation-making, though the description does not explicitly mention formal evaluation reports or dashboards. Future-state impacts from Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make evaluation more dashboard-driven, more focused on efficiency and sustainability, and more attentive to workforce readiness and modernization outcomes.

This subprocess brings together decision-making authority to agree improvement actions and monitoring mechanisms. The position is relevant because it makes recommendations to senior management, defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans, leads project teams, and participates in development projects, task forces, and committees. Evidence includes: 'makes recommendations to senior management'; 'Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans'; 'Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees'; and 'Leads project teams involved in the conduct of subject matter studies/reviews.' The capability involved is turning analytical findings into prioritized actions, plans, and coordinated implementation steps. The role fulfills this by shaping recommendations, planning work, and leading teams, though final enterprise action-plan approval may sit above the role. Future-state impacts from Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make action planning more disciplined, more resource-constrained, more explicit about trade-offs, and more dependent on leadership capacity, training, and realistic sequencing.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns identifying what statistics are needed and what is needed of those statistics. The work description directly states that the position 'assesses the policies and programs of key client departments to determine their requirements for statistical information,' 'investigates client requirements for statistical information,' and uses knowledge of 'current and emerging socio-economic issues' to 'anticipate and understand needs for new data.' That is direct evidence of identifying statistical needs and scanning changing user and environmental requirements. The capability involved is senior program and client-facing judgment: understanding policy demand, translating it into statistical requirements, and determining whether existing or new approaches are needed. The role fulfills this need by advising users, assessing requirements, and defining program objectives and options for senior management. Future-state drivers strengthen this connection. Under Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, need identification will be more constrained by prioritization pressures, fewer staff, and the search for lower-cost approaches using AI, automation, machine learning and new tools and methods. Because the position already determines client requirements and recommends modifications or new approaches, it is likely to face sharper triage of which needs can be pursued and how they can be met efficiently.

This subprocess is implicated because the role helps define what outputs statistical programs should produce, under what scope and constraints. The work description says the incumbent 'defines the objectives, content and approaches of statistical programs,' 'develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures,' and 'determines program priorities and milestones.' It also notes responsibility for recommending survey content and design and for presenting recommendations to senior management to improve and expand existing programs and elaborate new options. The capability involved is setting program direction, balancing user needs, quality, scope, methods and resources, and making explicit trade-offs. The role fulfills this need by shaping program objectives and recommending content, coverage, methods and priorities. Future-state drivers make this more consequential. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline will require clearer accountability, cross-field decision-making and transparent trade-offs. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will tighten constraints on scope, frequency, granularity and timeliness because of scarce resources and workforce reduction pressures. Since this position already allocates resources and sets priorities, it will be materially affected by stronger enterprise discipline around what outputs are approved and sustained.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the work description repeatedly emphasizes assessing data sources, integrating multiple source types, and determining whether existing sources can meet requirements. Evidence includes: 'identify the most appropriate sources of data'; 'new or modified data sources'; 'integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses)'; and 'investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet these requirements.' The role also requires knowledge of the Statistics Act, Privacy Act, confidentiality, security, respondent relations and data quality, all of which align with source suitability, legal conditions and access restrictions. The capability involved is evaluating source fitness, comparability, continuity, legal usability and operational feasibility. The role fulfills this need by reviewing conceptual frameworks, assessing source integration methods, and recommending source changes. Future-state impacts are substantial and cumulative. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will shift source strategy toward administrative data, alternative data, SDLE-enabled linkage and reduced direct collection. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase scrutiny of privacy, authorizations, secure access and cyber risk in source use. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will make platform fit, centralized repositories and secure ingestion part of source feasibility. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata quality and reuse more central. Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will expand use of linked, unstructured and geospatial sources. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase pressure to replace labour-intensive collection with reusable sources. This role is already deeply engaged in source assessment and integration, so these drivers materially reshape its work.

This subprocess is relevant because the role develops and recommends program changes, new options, priorities, budgets and resource allocations, even though the work description does not explicitly mention preparing formal business cases. Evidence includes 'defines the objectives, content and approaches of statistical programs and presents recommendations to senior management,' 'develops enhancements and recommends modifications,' 'determines program priorities and milestones,' and 'allocates and manages the human and financial resources of the program.' The capability involved is framing options, assessing implications, and supporting approval decisions with operational, methodological and resource considerations. The role fulfills this need by recommending program modifications, elaborating new program options, managing budgets, negotiating contracts and assessing impacts on divisional programs. Future-state drivers increase the likelihood that this work becomes more formalized and disciplined. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will require clearer approval ownership, milestone-based implementation logic and explicit trade-offs. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will foreground savings, staffing assumptions and automation-enabled redesign. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make training, sequencing and readiness part of feasibility. The role is therefore materially connected, though somewhat less directly than to source, collection and processing design.

This subprocess is relevant because the role determines concepts, definitions, standards and techniques and recommends survey content and design. The work description explicitly states that the incumbent 'determines the concepts, definitions, standards and techniques to be applied,' and 'recommends survey content and design.' It also emphasizes integrating conceptually different data from other programs and translating source data collected for other purposes into common concepts. The capability involved is defining what variables and classifications are needed and ensuring conceptual coherence across sources and programs. The role fulfills this need through methodological leadership over concepts, definitions and standards rather than through narrow technical drafting alone.
