Future-state drivers increase the importance of harmonized variables across administrative, alternative, linked and geospatial sources. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will require variables to be designed for linkage, derivation and cross-source harmonization. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the need for standardized variable metadata. The role's conceptual and standards-setting responsibilities make this a meaningful, though not primary, connection.

This is one of the most directly implicated subprocesses. The work description explicitly states that the position 'reviews the survey collection framework for existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaptation,' 'coordinates and reviews collection, coding, processing and client-relation activities,' 'provides expert advisory and consultative services to users on the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data,' and participates in task forces 'as an expert in data collection operations.' It also recommends survey content and design and manages units responsible for statistical program operations. The capability involved is designing and governing collection strategy, instruments, operational methods and respondent or supplier-facing arrangements. The role fulfills this need directly through operational leadership over collection frameworks and collection operations. Future-state drivers will materially transform this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production introduces chatbot-assisted interaction, automated extraction and monitoring-heavy workflows. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion shifts collection toward online-first, adaptive, mixed-source acquisition and supplier coordination. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access makes secure channels, credentials and confidentiality procedures central. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure changes feasible collection modes and tooling. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration embeds collection into end-to-end automated flows. Modular Architecture and reusable components will push standard collection services over bespoke approaches. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will intensify movement away from labour-intensive collection. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require training, role redesign and change leadership. The work description provides strong direct evidence that this role leads exactly the area most affected by these drivers.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description states that the incumbent 'recommends survey content and design, sample estimation and imputation methods, data integration from different sources, sample sizes and allocations to maximize efficiency within resource constraints.' That is direct evidence of involvement in sampling methodology and allocation decisions. The capability involved is determining how target populations are represented operationally and how sample design supports quality and efficiency. The role fulfills this need by recommending sample sizes, allocations and related methods as part of program design. Future-state drivers suggest meaningful change. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase use of administrative registers, linked files and geospatial inputs in frame construction and more targeted or adaptive sampling. This role's existing responsibility for sample estimation and efficiency-oriented design means it will be affected, though the work description does not indicate sole ownership of frame construction.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the role determines methods and techniques used in coding, processing, integration, estimation and analysis. Evidence includes: 'determines the concepts, definitions, standards and techniques to be applied'; 'recommends ... imputation methods, data integration from different sources'; 'assesses and reviews techniques and methods used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data'; 'researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures used'; and 'provides guidance on ... statistical techniques and systems.' The capability involved is methodological and operational design of processing, validation, integration and analytical routines. The role fulfills this need by reviewing and improving processing methods and by advising on coding and processing operations. Future-state drivers are extensive. AI and Automation in Statistical Production will redesign coding, validation, editing and imputation around automated methods with stronger governance and transparency. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will require more complex integration and validation methods across heterogeneous sources. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will strengthen secure handling and disclosure-control design. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will require methods to be modular, sequenced and automatable. Metadata-Driven Data Management will make metadata operational inputs to processing. Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will expand advanced methods, linkage-based integration and automated workflows. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase pressure to substitute automation for manual effort. Workforce Skills Transition will require upskilling and leadership oversight. The work description strongly supports this as a core area of responsibility.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role plans and leads statistical operations across collection, coding, processing and client relations, and manages units and project teams responsible for statistical program operations. Evidence includes: 'plans and leads the development of statistical operations'; 'coordinates and reviews collection, coding, processing and client-relation activities'; 'manages a unit involved in statistical operations and leads project teams'; and determines priorities, milestones, staffing and budgets. The capability involved is end-to-end operational design: ensuring processes fit together, assigning responsibilities, and organizing staff-system interactions. The role fulfills this need by overseeing operational workflows across multiple stages and by resolving conflicting priorities in multidisciplinary teams. Future-state drivers make this especially important. AI and Automation, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modular Architecture, Governance and Prioritization, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition all directly affect workflow design, handoffs, reuse, role clarity, automation, monitoring and flatter operating models. The work description's emphasis on concurrent activities, multidisciplinary coordination and operational management aligns closely with this subprocess and its future transformation.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because the role is responsible for the methods and operational requirements that drive processing and analysis components, although the work description does not explicitly describe hands-on software build activity. Evidence includes responsibility for collection, coding and processing operations; recommending imputation and integration methods; assessing techniques used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data; and providing guidance on statistical techniques and systems. The capability involved is specifying and governing reusable operational components and ensuring they support program needs. The role fulfills this need indirectly through methodological and operational leadership over what components must do and how they should support production. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation, Administrative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Platforms, Integrated Pipelines, Modular Architecture and Operational Efficiency will increase reuse of shared processing services and reduce bespoke manual workflows. This role is therefore meaningfully connected as an operational and methodological leader affected by those changes, even if not the primary builder.

This subprocess is relevant because the role coordinates and manages operational activities across collection, coding and processing and determines priorities, milestones and resource allocation. That indicates responsibility for how workflows are operationalized, even if the work description does not explicitly mention configuring workflow systems. The capability involved is translating designed processes into workable operational flows with clear sequencing, responsibilities and escalation. The role fulfills this need by managing concurrent activities, resolving conflicting priorities and leading multidisciplinary teams in statistical operations. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation, Enterprise Platforms, Agility and Execution Discipline, Governance and Operational Efficiency will make workflow configuration more standardized, automated and tightly governed. The role is materially affected because its operational management responsibilities will increasingly depend on configured enterprise workflows rather than manual coordination.

This subprocess is relevant because the role manages units and project teams, approves training plans, determines human resource needs, and oversees operational readiness. Evidence includes recruiting staff, evaluating performance, approving training plans, and managing operational budgets and contractors. The capability involved is preparing staff and operations for production use, including readiness, training and operational support. The role fulfills this need through management of staff capability and operational deployment rather than technical release management alone. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation, Agility and Execution Discipline, and Modular Architecture will increase the importance of training users, documenting new ways of working, and ensuring staff can operate modernized systems. This is a meaningful but secondary connection.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the role manages collection operations and the people and resources needed to run them. Evidence includes 'reviews the survey collection framework,' 'coordinates and reviews collection ... activities,' 'manages a unit involved in statistical operations,' determines human resource needs, recruits staff, approves training plans, and manages budgets and contracts. The capability involved is operational readiness for collection: ensuring staff, processes, systems and supporting arrangements are in place. The role fulfills this need through staffing, planning, training approval, operational coordination and resource management. Future-state drivers will materially change this work. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will add source acquisition, online-first setup and supplier coordination. AI and Automation will require setup of digital tools, APIs and automated channels. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will make secure devices, credentials and confidentiality procedures central. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will increase dependence on scalable digital infrastructure. Agility and Execution Discipline will tighten readiness timelines. Workforce Skills Transition will increase training and change-management demands. The work description strongly supports this as a core operational responsibility.

This subprocess is one of the clearest matches. The work description explicitly says the role 'coordinates and reviews collection, coding, processing and client-relation activities,' provides expert advice on collection and capture, participates as an expert in data collection operations, and manages units responsible for statistical program operations. The capability involved is live operational execution of collection, including monitoring, adjustment, respondent or client relations, and ensuring collection meets program needs. The role fulfills this need directly through operational oversight of collection activities and client relations. Future-state drivers will significantly reshape this work. AI and Automation will introduce automated follow-up, chatbot support and real-time monitoring. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will shift execution toward supplier-based receipt, digital channels and adaptive collection. Agility and Execution Discipline will intensify deadline-driven monitoring and intervention. Cyber Security and Enterprise Platforms will make secure digital operations and resilient infrastructure central. Operational Efficiency will reduce tolerance for labour-intensive collection. Workforce Skills Transition will require staff to operate new tools while maintaining quality and relationships. The evidence in the work description is direct and strong.

This subprocess is directly implicated because the work description repeatedly emphasizes integrating data from multiple sources into common conceptual frameworks. Evidence includes 'data integration from different sources,' 'integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses),' 'integrate data into a common conceptual framework,' and 'integrate conceptually different data from other programs.' The capability involved is harmonisation, source prioritisation, linkage-aware interpretation and production of coherent statistical information from heterogeneous inputs. The role fulfills this need by reviewing conceptual frameworks, assessing integration techniques, and recommending methods and source changes. Future-state drivers make this one of the most transformed areas. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Enterprise Platforms, Cyber Security and Integrated Pipelines all intensify the importance of secure, metadata-rich, reusable multi-source integration. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation, Administrative/Alternative/Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Management, Modern Statistical Methods, Operational Efficiency, and Workforce Skills Transition will affect how draft outputs are produced, documented, and explained, especially where AI-assisted methods or mixed-source outputs require stronger methodological notes and transparency. This is a core responsibility of the role, so relevance is high.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position interprets findings, evaluates analytical material, defends validity of methods and results, and advises senior management on trends and conclusions. The capability involved is validating whether outputs are credible, consistent, and fit for use in light of domain knowledge and methodological understanding. Evidence includes 'interprets study findings and conclusions,' 'analyzes the results and findings of studies conducted by in-house analysts and consultants,' 'prepares recommendations and advice to senior management,' and communication duties requiring defense of 'the validity of statistical methods and approaches used.' The role also comments on written material to be published and provides expert advice on program findings and their application. Future-state drivers such as Administrative/Alternative/Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods, AI and Automation, Metadata-Driven Management, Integrated Pipelines, Operational Efficiency, and Workforce Skills Transition will increase the need to validate outputs against historical expectations, auxiliary sources, metadata, and methodological changes. The work description strongly supports high relevance.

This subprocess is one of the most directly connected to the role. The capability involved is interpreting statistical results, explaining their meaning, and communicating implications to varied audiences including senior management, policy makers, academics, media, and other professionals. Evidence is extensive: the incumbent 'interprets study findings and conclusions and prepares recommendations and advice to senior management'; 'provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers ... academics'; 'writes and presents analytical material'; and must 'present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used.' The role also provides guidance on study results and socio-economic analysis. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation, Administrative/Alternative/Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods, and Workforce Skills Transition will materially affect this work because outputs will increasingly reflect linked data, alternative sources, advanced methods, and AI-assisted production, all of which require clearer explanation and stronger analytical judgment. This is a core function of the position, so relevance is high.

This subprocess is relevant because the position is explicitly responsible for confidentiality, security, and legislative compliance in statistical programs. The capability involved is ensuring outputs and information handling comply with confidentiality rules and legal requirements. Evidence includes knowledge of 'Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality),' and especially knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act 'to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.' The incumbent also develops initiatives concerning 'dissemination and confidentiality of information.' This is direct evidence of responsibility for confidentiality controls, though not necessarily hands-on disclosure-control method application. Future-state drivers such as Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure; Administrative and Linked Data Expansion; and Modular Architecture increase the importance of disclosure control because linked, administrative, and geospatial data raise re-identification risks and secure-access requirements. Relevance is medium because confidentiality governance is explicit, even if technical suppression methods are not.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position prepares and evaluates analytical material for publication, comments on written material, advises on dissemination, and represents the program in pre-release and publication contexts. The capability involved is ensuring outputs, commentary, caveats, and supporting information are ready for release and meet quality and communication standards. Evidence includes 'prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material for publication purposes,' 'writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated,' 'comments on written material to be published by STC,' and provides guidance on dissemination. The role also advises senior management and external users on findings and methods, which aligns with final release readiness and supporting documentation. Future-state drivers such as Agility and Execution Discipline, Metadata-Driven Management, Modern Statistical Methods, AI and Automation, Governance and Prioritization, Cyber Security and Privacy, Operational Efficiency, and Workforce Skills Transition will increase pressure for disciplined approvals, stronger caveats, richer metadata, and clearer explanation of modernized methods. Because publication readiness and analytical release quality are central to the role, relevance is high.

This subprocess has limited relevance. The position is strongly involved in dissemination and publication, but the work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for loading data and metadata into dissemination systems or updating databases. Evidence for indirect relevance comes from coordinating dissemination and evaluating analytical material for publication. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Management, Enterprise Platforms and Cloud, and Integrated Pipelines may affect the role indirectly because dissemination increasingly depends on metadata-linked systems and standardized digital platforms. However, absent explicit system-update duties, relevance remains low.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position produces and oversees analytical and dissemination products for varied audiences. The capability involved is assembling explanatory texts, analytical content, and publication materials into dissemination products that meet standards and user needs. Evidence includes: 'coordinates and reviews the ... marketing and dissemination of statistical data'; 'prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material for publication purposes'; 'writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience'; and provides expert advice on dissemination. The role also comments on written material to be published and chairs meetings to build understanding and consensus. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Management, Enterprise Platforms and Cloud, AI and Automation, Administrative/Alternative/Linked Data Expansion, Operational Efficiency, and Workforce Skills Transition will affect product formats, metadata packaging, digital delivery, accessibility, and standardization. Because dissemination product creation is explicitly part of the role, relevance is high.

This subprocess is relevant because the position is involved in publication, dissemination, external communication, and defending results publicly, though the work description does not explicitly mention embargo management or release scheduling. The capability involved is preparing and supporting release of statistical products, including communication with media, policy makers, academics, and other users. Evidence includes writing and presenting analytical material for dissemination, defending findings when challenged by media, and providing expert advisory services to external users. The role also represents subject-matter divisions and participates in interdepartmental meetings and conferences. Future-state drivers such as Agility and Execution Discipline, Cyber Security and Secure Access, Enterprise Platforms and Cloud, and Metadata-Driven Management will affect release timing, controlled access, and release governance. Relevance is medium because the role clearly supports release content and stakeholder communication, even if operational release management is not explicit.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position provides expert advisory and consultative services to data users and responds to interpretation and methodological questions from a wide range of stakeholders. The capability involved is supporting users, explaining outputs and methods, and maintaining trust in Statistics Canada products. Evidence includes: 'provides expert advisory and consultative services to data users (e.g. academics, policy makers, international bodies, etc.) on the results of surveys and studies, survey concepts and methods'; 'provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics'; 'provides expert advice to STC and other professionals'; and responds when 'media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings.' This is direct user-support work. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Cyber Security and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Management, Operational Efficiency, and Workforce Skills Transition will change how support is delivered through chatbots, self-service, secure-access workflows, and metadata-rich knowledge resources. The role’s communication and advisory responsibilities make this a high-relevance subprocess.

This subprocess is relevant because the position reviews program results, assesses methods and procedures, investigates client requirements, and uses feedback and analytical findings to recommend changes. The capability involved is gathering evidence on program performance, quality issues, user needs, and methodological gaps to inform improvement. Evidence includes 'determines changes in the statistical needs of clients,' 'assesses the impact on divisional programs,' 'researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures used,' and analyzes findings from studies conducted by staff and consultants. The role also chairs meetings and participates in groups to share knowledge and build understanding, which supports gathering evaluative input. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation, Administrative/Alternative/Linked Data Expansion, Agility and Execution Discipline, Enterprise Platforms, Integrated Pipelines, Metadata-Driven Management, Operational Efficiency, and Workforce Skills Transition will increase the volume and importance of process metrics, staff feedback, and user signals. Relevance is medium because the role clearly gathers and interprets evaluative evidence, though not necessarily through a formal evaluation office function.

This subprocess is relevant because the position analyzes program results, assesses methods and procedures, interprets findings for management, and recommends changes to programs and operations. The capability involved is evaluating whether statistical programs and methods are performing as intended and synthesizing findings into recommendations. Evidence includes 'plans, develops and directs the analysis, review and presentation of program results,' 'assesses and reviews statistical techniques, methods and approaches,' 'researches gaps and inconsistencies,' 'analyzes the results and findings of studies conducted by in-house analysts and consultants,' and 'prepares recommendations and advice to senior management.' These are evaluation-like responsibilities. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation, Agility and Execution Discipline, Governance and Prioritization, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Modern Statistical Methods, and Workforce Skills Transition will make evaluation more dashboard-driven, more focused on efficiency, modernization outcomes, workforce readiness, and trade-offs. The role’s advisory and analytical responsibilities support medium relevance.

This subprocess is relevant because the position develops options and strategies, recommends program changes, advises management, and manages units and projects through change. The capability involved is turning findings into actionable improvements with clear priorities and operational follow-through. Evidence includes 'develops options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations,' 'develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures,' 'provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental policies and develops new program initiatives,' and leadership responsibilities for units, projects, budgets, staffing, and priorities. These are strong indicators of action-planning responsibility. Future-state drivers such as Governance and Prioritization, Agility and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, and AI/modernization drivers will make action planning more disciplined, prioritized, and constrained by staffing, timelines, and enterprise governance. Because the role has managerial authority and strategic advisory responsibilities, relevance is medium.

Positions.Branch/Division: Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division

implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is directly relevant because it concerns gathering evaluation material such as user feedback, process metadata, system metrics, staff suggestions, progress reports and quality indicators for later evaluation. The position title is "Junior Evaluation Officer" in the "Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division," which is explicit evidence that the role sits within an evaluation function and is therefore materially connected to collecting and organizing inputs used in evaluation work. Although the work description is sparse, the listed key activities include corporate and HR information resources such as "HR service standards," "HR committees," "HR contact list," and "Corporate service providers." These items are consistent with locating organizational contacts, standards, governance touchpoints and service information that can support gathering evaluation evidence, coordinating with stakeholders, and assembling inputs. Future-state drivers further increase the importance of this subprocess for such a role. AI and Automation in Statistical Production increases the volume of monitoring outputs, documentation, paradata and system metrics available for evaluation, meaning evaluation staff will increasingly need to work with richer automated evidence. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion adds new indicators on source quality, linkage performance, online response behaviour and workload shifts, broadening the range of inputs an evaluation role may need to gather. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline increases the need to collect milestone, schedule and execution evidence for rapid assessment. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability makes metadata-related evidence more central. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity also matters because staff feedback, training outcomes, readiness signals and well-being indicators become evaluation inputs. The cumulative effect is that an evaluation role, even junior, is likely to be increasingly affected by more automated, continuous, metadata-rich and workforce-related evidence gathering.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it covers analysing evaluation inputs, comparing them to expected results, synthesising findings into an evaluation report or dashboard, identifying quality issues and deviations, and recommending changes. The strongest evidence is the work description itself: the position is titled "Junior Evaluation Officer" and is located in the "Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division." That is a direct organizational and functional match to conducting evaluations. Even though no detailed technical duties are provided, the classification context and branch placement indicate material involvement in evaluation activity rather than only peripheral support. The listed key activities—"HR service standards," "HR committees," "HR contact list," and "Corporate service providers"—suggest the role may rely on internal service standards, governance forums and organizational contacts when conducting or supporting evaluations, especially in a corporate environment. Future-state drivers make this subprocess even more central. AI and Automation in Statistical Production reshapes evaluation toward continuous dashboards, monitoring-based assessment, and explicit review of transparency, trust and governance of automated processes. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment makes evaluation more consequential because processes may need to be redesigned, scaled back or stopped based on evidence of productivity, savings and sustainability under reduced staffing. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline makes schedule adherence, milestone attainment and implementation effectiveness core evaluation criteria. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline increases the need for evidence-based assessment tied to enterprise priorities and transparent trade-offs. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity means evaluations increasingly need to assess readiness, training uptake, leadership effectiveness and workforce sustainability. Because the role is explicitly an evaluation role, these drivers imply meaningful present and future change in the methods, evidence base and expectations associated with the work.

This subprocess is relevant because it brings together decision-making authority to agree an action plan based on evaluation findings and includes monitoring mechanisms for future iterations. A Junior Evaluation Officer would not necessarily hold final decision-making authority, and the work description does not state that the position approves or owns action plans. However, the role is plausibly and materially connected through supporting evaluation outputs that feed action planning, given the explicit evidence that the position is a "Junior Evaluation Officer" in the "Evaluation Division." The listed key activities such as "HR committees," "HR service standards," and "Corporate service providers" also suggest exposure to governance structures, service expectations and organizational coordination mechanisms that can support action-plan discussions or follow-up. The relevance is therefore medium rather than high because the description supports contribution to, but not ownership of, this subprocess. Future-state drivers increase the importance of this connection. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline makes action planning more explicit, accountable and trade-off driven. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline pushes action plans toward time-bound, monitored commitments with clear authorities. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment means action plans will increasingly focus on simplification, automation, prioritization and workforce impacts. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is especially relevant because action plans for modernization depend on leadership ownership, realistic sequencing, training and support through transition. For a junior evaluation role, this means future work may increasingly involve producing evidence and recommendations in forms that are directly usable for governance decisions and monitored improvement actions, even if the final approval rests elsewhere.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes assessing whether data sources and their accompanying metadata are suitable for statistical use, including conditions of access, quality, interoperability and downstream usability. The work description is materially connected through its core responsibility to assess corporate and client metadata requirements, evaluate metadata quality, and determine impacts of changes in methods, procedures and systems on metadata production, storage and dissemination. Evidence includes: 'Assesses corporate and client metadata requirements'; 'Interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata'; and 'Evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs.' The strongest future-state driver is Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, which makes standardized, searchable, metadata-rich assets central to source discovery and suitability assessment. This increases the importance of the position's expertise in metadata concepts, frameworks, standards and quality evaluation. Additional drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the need for metadata that can describe administrative, linked, geospatial and other non-traditional sources consistently. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure also matter because the position explicitly works under the Statistics Act and Privacy Act context and must ensure compliance, while metadata increasingly need to support secure access, interoperability and platform-based reuse. The cumulative effect is that this role will be increasingly affected by the need to ensure metadata are sufficiently standardized, complete and quality-assured to support source assessment and reuse across programs.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it concerns the detailed design of outputs, products and dissemination arrangements, including use of standards, metadata and dissemination procedures. The position is explicitly responsible for preparing, editing, validating, storing and disseminating statistical metadata and for contributing to documentation and training that explain dissemination-related methods and systems. Evidence includes: 'Prepares statistical metadata for storage and dissemination, reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata'; 'Assesses the need to update statistical metadata in response to modifications in client, policy or systems requirements'; and 'Contributes written information to be used as input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals which explain and clarify the policy requirements, methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate statistical metadata.' The capability involved is metadata design and stewardship for dissemination-ready outputs, including standards application, quality assurance, and communication of dissemination rules and methods. The Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability driver is especially important because it shifts dissemination design toward discoverable, standardized, metadata-rich assets; this aligns directly with the role's metadata production and validation mandate. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access also contribute to future change because dissemination increasingly occurs through platform-based, secure digital environments, and the work description explicitly references awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts and compliance with security and confidentiality requirements. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will likely push this work toward more standardized and reusable dissemination metadata products, while Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity implies growing need for training and explanatory materials, which the position already supports through manuals and training assistance.

This subprocess is relevant because preparation of metadata for collected and derived variables, classifications and units is a necessary precondition for later phases, and the position's work is centered on statistical metadata concepts, frameworks, standards and quality evaluation. The work description does not state that the position defines variables itself, but it does show direct involvement in the metadata structures that describe variables and classifications across programs. Evidence includes: 'Knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally'; 'Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data'; and 'Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to understand program statistical metadata requirements and ensure consistency.' The capability involved is maintaining standardized metadata that support variable definition, interpretation, reuse and quality assessment. The Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability driver increases the importance of formal, reusable variable-level metadata, while Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production and Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increase pressure to document variables derived from linked, administrative, alternative and geospatial sources. The position fulfills this need by preparing, validating and updating metadata in accordance with standards and by advising clients on metadata requirements. Future change is likely to increase the complexity and importance of variable metadata, even if the role remains more metadata-focused than method-design-focused.

This subprocess is materially connected because it includes design specifications for validation, integration, coding, transformation and disclosure-related methods, and the position contributes to the metadata, documentation, testing and quality evaluation that support those processing methods. Evidence includes: 'Implements and tests modifications to methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata'; 'Analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives'; and 'Knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata.' The capability involved is metadata support for processing and analysis design: documenting methods, ensuring metadata quality, and assessing impacts of method or system changes on downstream production. The Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability driver is highly relevant because processing increasingly relies on standardized metadata as operational inputs, not just documentation. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production also increase the importance of metadata that support automated, reusable processing flows. The work description shows the position contributes written input to procedures manuals, training manuals and quality reports, and participates in testing and feedback on current and proposed methods. Future-state impacts therefore include greater involvement in metadata needed for automated validation, lineage, and reusable processing components.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it covers end-to-end workflow design, reuse of systems and databases, and how staff interact with systems and responsibilities. The position is directly involved in methods, procedures and systems used in metadata production, storage, dissemination and evaluation, and in analyzing and testing changes to those systems. Evidence includes: 'Implements and tests modifications to methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata'; 'Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata'; 'Participates in project teams, work groups and meetings in order to develop and improve work methods and practices'; and 'Liaises ... to develop and translate requirements into specifications.' The capability involved is operational metadata workflow expertise: translating requirements into specifications, improving methods and practices, and ensuring metadata processes fit across programs. This aligns strongly with drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development. These drivers collectively point to more integrated, reusable, metadata-centric production workflows and stronger platform alignment. The work description also shows awareness of divisional mandate, priorities and consistency across programs, which supports enterprise workflow design. Future changes are likely to shift the role further toward metadata stewardship within integrated enterprise workflows, with more emphasis on standardized handoffs, reusable metadata services, and system-supported quality monitoring.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it concerns reuse or build of components such as metadata management services, transformation functions and workflow tools, and the position contributes to testing, feedback and documentation for metadata-related methods and systems. Evidence includes: 'Implements and tests modifications to methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata'; 'Knowledge of software used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata'; and 'to participate in testing and to provide feedback on current and proposed methods for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating metadata.' The capability involved is not software development per se, but operational and subject-matter expertise needed to validate, refine and support metadata-related components. The Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability driver is especially relevant because metadata management services become core reusable components. Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure also increase the importance of reusable metadata services and governed component reuse. The work description supports relevance through testing, analysis of system changes, and contribution to manuals and training. Future-state impacts are likely to increase the role's involvement in validating and operationalizing reusable metadata components even if the position does not directly build them.

This subprocess is relevant because it configures workflows, systems and transformations from collection through dissemination, and the position works on methods, procedures and systems for metadata production, storage, dissemination and evaluation, including testing modifications and analyzing impacts of changes. Evidence includes: 'Implements and tests modifications to methods, procedures and systems'; 'Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems ... to determine where updates are required to existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals'; and 'Liaises ... to negotiate procedural modifications, priorities and target dates.' The capability involved is configuring and adapting metadata-related operational workflows through specifications, procedural changes, testing and documentation updates. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration is relevant because metadata handoffs increasingly need to be configured across automated workflows. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability also matters because metadata handling becomes part of operational orchestration rather than separate documentation. The role fulfills this need by identifying impacts of system changes, updating metadata and supporting procedural documentation and training. Future changes are likely to increase the need for metadata-aware workflow configuration and exception handling as production becomes more automated and integrated.

This subprocess is materially connected because it includes testing assembled and configured services, checking metadata with suppliers, and ensuring coherent end-to-end operation. The work description explicitly includes implementing and testing modifications to methods, procedures and systems used in metadata production, storage, dissemination and evaluation. Evidence includes: 'Implements and tests modifications to methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata'; 'Knowledge of methods, procedures and systems ... to participate in testing and to provide feedback'; and 'Contributes written information ... to reports which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations.' The capability involved is metadata-focused testing, quality evaluation and feedback on system suitability. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the importance of testing metadata completeness, linkage and standards compliance. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure also matter because metadata systems increasingly operate in secure, platform-based environments, and the work description explicitly references compliance with the Statistics Act and Privacy Act. Future-state impacts include more rigorous testing of metadata flows, interoperability and quality indicators across integrated systems.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes producing documentation, user manuals and training users on how to operate the process. The work description directly states that the position contributes written information to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals and assists with delivery of training. Evidence includes: 'Suggests which information should be included in reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training materials'; 'Contributes written information to be used as input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals'; and 'assists with the delivery of training.' The capability involved is operationalization of metadata systems through documentation, training and user support. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is especially relevant because training and user readiness are central to this subprocess and already part of the role. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability also matters because metadata-centric processes require clear documentation and stewardship guidance. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will likely increase the need for updated manuals and training as metadata systems move onto modern platforms and become more integrated into production. The role is therefore materially affected by future-state demands for clearer operational guidance and broader metadata literacy across users and clients.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes loading collected data and metadata into suitable environments, analyzing metadata and paradata, versioning instruments and preparing assets for further processing. The position's work is directly concerned with preparing metadata for storage and dissemination, validating metadata, and evaluating metadata quality across programs. Evidence includes: 'Prepares statistical metadata for storage and dissemination, reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata'; 'Compiles information from diverse sources in order to prepare, edit, validate and evaluate statistical metadata'; and 'Evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs.' The capability involved is ensuring metadata are complete, standardized and quality-assured at the point they are finalized for downstream use. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is highly relevant because this subprocess explicitly handles loading, analyzing and preserving metadata. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration also matters because collection finalization becomes an automated handoff point into downstream processing, increasing the importance of metadata readiness. The role fulfills this need through metadata validation, quality evaluation and consistency work across programs. Future-state impacts include greater emphasis on metadata lineage, versioning and structured handoff into enterprise environments.

This subprocess is relevant because data integration increasingly depends on standardized metadata for matching, harmonisation, prioritisation and reuse across sources. While the position does not perform record linkage or integration itself, it supports the metadata frameworks, standards, quality evaluation and consistency needed for integration across survey and statistical programs. Evidence includes: 'Knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks ... and how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures'; 'Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to understand program statistical metadata requirements and ensure consistency'; and 'Evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs.' The capability involved is metadata standardization and quality stewardship that enables interoperable integrated data assets. The Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability driver is especially relevant because interoperability depends on standardized metadata. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production further increase the need for metadata that support integration of administrative, linked, geospatial and alternative sources. Future-state impacts on the role include greater demand for metadata consistency, source comparability and enterprise reuse to support integration-heavy production.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it concerns identifying problems, errors and discrepancies and validating data and metadata against predefined rules and expectations. The position's core duties include reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata, undertaking quality evaluations, and evaluating indicators of metadata quality across programs. Evidence includes: 'reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata and undertaking quality evaluations in accordance with documented standards'; 'Evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs in accordance with pre-defined quality guidelines'; and 'Contributes written information ... to reports which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations.' The capability involved is metadata validation, quality assessment, standards application and reporting. This aligns strongly with Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, which makes metadata quality itself a critical validation object. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production all increase the need for standardized, automated and repeatable validation of metadata-rich assets. The work description also shows the position analyzes methods and systems and proposes enhancements, which supports iterative validation improvement. Future-state impacts are likely to intensify this role's importance as metadata validation becomes more embedded in automated production and enterprise quality frameworks.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance because it includes changing values and producing metadata on editing and imputation processes. The work description does not state that the position edits statistical data values or performs imputation, so direct operational responsibility should not be inferred. However, the role is connected through its responsibility for preparing, editing and validating statistical metadata and documenting methods, procedures and quality results. Evidence includes: 'prepare, edit and validate statistical metadata'; 'Contributes written information ... to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals'; and 'Contributes written information ... to reports which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations.' The capability involved is metadata support and documentation for quality-related processing activities rather than editing data itself. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is the main relevant driver because standardized metadata on transformations, edits and quality processes become more important for transparency and reuse. Future-state impact on this role is likely indirect: greater need to capture and maintain metadata describing editing and imputation processes performed elsewhere.

This subprocess is only indirectly relevant. The work description does not indicate that the position derives statistical variables or units, so no direct methodological responsibility should be assigned. Relevance arises because derived variables and units require metadata, documentation and standards support, and the position is responsible for metadata preparation, validation, consistency and advice across programs. Evidence includes: 'Knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks'; 'Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data'; and 'ensure consistency in the methods of processing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of metadata across programs.' The capability involved is metadata stewardship for derived constructs rather than derivation itself. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the importance of documenting derivation logic and lineage. Future-state effects are therefore indirect but real: the role may increasingly need to support metadata for derived variables created from linked, administrative and model-based processes.

This subprocess is relevant because it assembles the results of processing into datasets used as inputs to analysis, and increasingly depends on metadata linkage, versioning and standardized handoff. The position's work directly supports preparation, storage, dissemination and validation of metadata and analysis of system changes affecting documentation and training. Evidence includes: 'Prepares statistical metadata for storage and dissemination'; 'Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems ... to determine where updates are required to existing documentation'; and 'Contributes written information ... to reports' and manuals. The capability involved is ensuring that finalized datasets are accompanied by complete, quality-assured metadata and that metadata-related procedures remain current. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is especially relevant because final datasets must be packaged as metadata-rich assets. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration also matters because finalised files become standardized handoff points. Future-state impacts include more structured metadata packaging, lineage requirements and enterprise-standard handoffs to analysis environments.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes preparing methodological notes and explanatory material to accompany outputs, especially when modern methods are used. The position contributes written information to documentation, procedures manuals, training materials and reports on metadata quality, and works directly on metadata dissemination. Evidence includes: 'Contributes written information to be used as input to reports which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations'; 'Contributes written information ... to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals'; and 'Suggests which information should be included in reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training materials.' The capability involved is preparing metadata and explanatory content that support interpretation and use of outputs. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is relevant because outputs increasingly need accompanying metadata and methodological context. Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production and Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increase the need for clearer explanation of source, method and quality changes. The role fulfills this need through metadata expertise, quality reporting and documentation support. Future-state impacts likely include more demand for metadata-rich explanatory materials and standardized quality statements.

This subprocess is relevant because it explicitly includes checking associated metadata, paradata and quality indicators and validating outputs against expectations. The position's work directly includes metadata quality evaluation, reporting and consistency assessment across programs. Evidence includes: 'Evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs'; 'Contributes written information ... to reports which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations'; and 'Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs ... to understand program statistical metadata requirements and ensure consistency.' The capability involved is metadata quality assurance as part of output validation. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is especially relevant because metadata completeness and consistency become part of release readiness. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production also increase the need to validate outputs with richer methodological and source metadata. Future-state impacts include stronger reliance on metadata quality indicators and more explicit validation of metadata accompanying outputs.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it includes collating supporting information, technical notes, uncertainty measures and necessary metadata, and approving content for release. The position title and duties are directly centered on metadata production and dissemination, including preparation, validation, updating, reporting and documentation. Evidence includes: 'Prepares statistical metadata for storage and dissemination'; 'Assesses the need to update statistical metadata in response to modifications in client, policy or systems requirements'; 'Contributes written information ... to reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals'; and 'Knowledge of policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' The capability involved is ensuring outputs are accompanied by accurate, standards-compliant metadata and supporting documentation fit for release and use. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is the strongest driver because metadata becomes a core part of release readiness. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access is also relevant because the work description explicitly requires awareness of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act and compliance with security and confidentiality requirements. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline and Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline may also affect the role through tighter release timelines, clearer approval expectations and prioritization of supporting materials. Future-state impacts point to more standardized metadata packaging, stronger release controls and greater demand for clear caveats and technical notes.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it manages formatting, loading and linking data and metadata into output systems ready for dissemination. The position's core work is to prepare statistical metadata for storage and dissemination, review and validate it, and assess updates required due to system or policy changes. Evidence includes: 'Prepares statistical metadata for storage and dissemination'; 'Assesses the need to update statistical metadata in response to modifications in client, policy or systems requirements'; and 'Knowledge of software used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' The capability involved is operational metadata management for dissemination systems, including metadata formatting, linkage, quality assurance and system adaptation. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is especially relevant because this subprocess depends on metadata-rich, searchable, standardized assets. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure also matter because dissemination systems increasingly receive automated loads in enterprise environments. The role fulfills this need directly through metadata preparation, validation and system-related analysis. Future-state impacts include more automated metadata loading, stronger metadata linkage requirements and greater platform standardization.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it produces dissemination products and includes preparing explanatory texts, quality statements and other components. The position is explicitly responsible for metadata production and dissemination and for contributing written information to reports, manuals and training materials that explain metadata methods, systems and quality. Evidence includes: 'Prepares statistical metadata for storage and dissemination'; 'Contributes written information to be used as input to reports which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations'; and 'Contributes written information ... to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals which explain and clarify the policy requirements, methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate statistical metadata.' The capability involved is producing and quality-assuring metadata and explanatory content that accompany dissemination products. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is highly relevant because dissemination products increasingly need to be metadata-rich and discoverable. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment suggest more standardized, reusable digital dissemination products, increasing the importance of consistent metadata packaging. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is also relevant because the role already assists with training and explanatory materials. Future-state impacts include more metadata-enabled digital products, stronger quality statements and more standardized dissemination packaging.

This subprocess is relevant because release requires all elements to be in place, including management of access to confidential data by authorized users, and because metadata and supporting information must be ready for release. The position is not described as managing release schedules or embargoes, but it is materially connected through metadata dissemination responsibilities and explicit compliance obligations under the Statistics Act and Privacy Act. Evidence includes: 'Prepares statistical metadata for storage and dissemination'; 'The position must have an awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information to ensure that actions are in compliance'; and knowledge of policies, directives and guidelines related to dissemination and quality evaluation. The capability involved is ensuring metadata and related dissemination content are release-ready and compliant. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access is particularly relevant because release increasingly depends on secure access and confidentiality controls. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability also matters because metadata completeness and linkage are part of successful release. Future-state impacts are likely to increase the role's exposure to secure release requirements, controlled-access dissemination contexts and metadata corrections or updates associated with release management.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes responding to user queries, supporting access requests, and populating knowledge bases and FAQs. The work description shows the position provides advice and assistance to clients, liaises with specialists and survey managers, contributes to training, and maintains knowledge of contacts within key client divisions. Evidence includes: 'provide advice and assistance to clients'; 'Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management'; 'Knowledge of contacts within key client Divisions in order to establish a liaison and provide assistance and advice'; and 'assists with the delivery of training.' The capability involved is client-facing metadata expertise: explaining metadata requirements, methods, procedures and quality results. AI and Automation in Statistical Production is relevant because user support is expected to shift toward AI assistants, chatbots, website search and knowledge-base reuse, which may change how metadata support is delivered. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability also matters because better metadata and searchable repositories change the nature of user questions and self-service support. Future-state impacts include more emphasis on reusable support content, metadata literacy support, and possibly more digital self-service channels, while the role's liaison and advisory functions remain important for complex metadata questions.

This subprocess is relevant because it gathers quality indicators, process metadata, system metrics and staff suggestions for evaluation. The position directly evaluates metadata quality indicators across programs, compiles information from diverse sources, and contributes reports describing metadata quality evaluation results. Evidence includes: 'Evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs'; 'Compiles information from diverse sources in order to prepare, edit, validate and evaluate statistical metadata'; and 'Contributes written information ... to reports which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations.' The capability involved is generating and compiling metadata quality evidence for continuous improvement. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is relevant because metadata-related indicators become more central to evaluation. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure also increase the volume and usefulness of metadata and system metrics. The role fulfills this need directly through quality evaluation and reporting. Future-state impacts include more continuous, automated collection of metadata quality indicators and stronger use of those indicators in enterprise evaluation.

This subprocess is relevant because it analyses evaluation inputs, synthesizes them into reports or dashboards, identifies quality issues and recommends changes. The position contributes to metadata quality reports, evaluates indicators across programs, analyzes methods, procedures and systems, and proposes enhancements or alternatives. Evidence includes: 'Contributes written information to be used as input to reports which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations'; 'Analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives'; and 'Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems ... to determine the need to update statistical metadata.' The capability involved is evaluation of metadata quality and metadata-related production performance, plus analysis of improvement options. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and AI and Automation in Statistical Production are especially relevant because evaluation increasingly focuses on quality, reuse, efficiency, automation impacts and sustainability. The role is materially connected through evidence generation and analytical input rather than enterprise-level decision authority. Future-state impacts include more dashboard-based metadata quality evaluation and stronger expectation to identify metadata-related improvement opportunities across programs.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance. The work description does not indicate that the position has formal decision-making authority to approve enterprise action plans, so direct governance responsibility should not be inferred. However, the role contributes analytical input, recommendations and evidence that can inform action planning. Evidence includes: 'provide recommendations to clients and management with respect to approaches and considerations'; 'Analyzes current ... methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives'; and participation in project teams, work groups and meetings to improve methods and practices. The capability involved is advisory and evidence-based contribution to improvement planning for metadata processes. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity may affect how such recommendations are prioritized and implemented, but the role's connection remains indirect. Future-state impacts are therefore limited to increased expectation that metadata quality findings, system analyses and client requirement assessments feed into broader action plans decided by management.

Positions.Branch/Division: Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division

implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is directly relevant because it concerns gathering evaluation material, including user feedback, process metadata, system metrics, staff suggestions, and reports against prior action plans for use in evaluation. The position title is explicitly "Evaluation Officer" in the "Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division," which is strong evidence that the role is materially connected to evaluation activity rather than to statistical collection, processing, or dissemination operations. Even though the work description is sparse, the organizational placement in an evaluation division aligns most closely with assembling inputs for evaluation. Future-state drivers reinforce that this work will increasingly rely on richer and more continuous evidence streams. Under AI and Automation in Statistical Production, technology themes such as monitoring, documentation, enterprise platforms, and statistical workflows increase the volume of automated evaluation inputs available; the impact mechanism is that automation and monitoring enable continuous capture of process metadata and quality indicators. Under Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, centralized repositories, data platforms, cloud, and tooling make evaluation evidence easier to consolidate and access. Under Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, end-to-end automation and workflow logs create more operational telemetry for evaluators. Under Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, staff feedback, training outcomes, and workforce sustainability indicators become more important evaluation inputs. The work description provides limited task detail, but the evidence of role and branch placement supports a high connection to gathering and compiling evaluation evidence.

This is the most directly implicated subprocess. It covers analysing evaluation inputs, comparing them to expected results, synthesising findings into evaluation reports or dashboards, identifying quality issues and performance deviations, and recommending changes. The role is explicitly titled "Evaluation Officer," and it sits in the "Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division," which is direct evidence that the position performs or materially contributes to evaluation work. No supplied evidence indicates responsibility for production, collection, or dissemination operations themselves; instead, the role identity points to the evaluation function. Future-state transformation drivers make this subprocess even more central. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline increases the importance of evidence-based assessment, explicit trade-offs, accountability, and recommendations about what should be improved, scaled, deferred, or stopped. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline makes schedule performance, milestone attainment, and implementation effectiveness core evaluation criteria, shifting evaluation toward more operational dashboards and rapid corrective action. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment makes evaluation critical for assessing productivity, savings, automation benefits, service impacts, and sustainability under reduced staffing. AI and Automation in Statistical Production adds the need to evaluate trust, transparency, governance effectiveness, and quality impacts of automated methods, while Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration provide richer telemetry and dashboard evidence for continuous evaluation. Workforce implications such as reduced staffing, leadership capacity, training uptake, and workforce sustainability also become evaluation dimensions. The supplied work description does not list detailed technical duties, but the position title and branch/division are sufficient evidence that conducting evaluation is a core responsibility.

This subprocess is relevant because it uses evaluation findings to form and agree an action plan and establish mechanisms to monitor the impact of those actions in future iterations. An Evaluation Officer in the Evaluation Division would regularly contribute to this subprocess by providing the evaluation evidence, findings, and recommendations that inform action planning, even if the final decision-making authority may sit with management or governance bodies. The work description does not explicitly state approval authority, so the relevance is medium rather than high; however, the role is still materially connected because action plans are a direct downstream use of evaluation outputs. Future-state drivers strengthen this connection. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline makes action planning more explicit about accountability, prioritization, cross-field decision-making, and transparent trade-offs. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline pushes action plans toward executable, milestone-based commitments with clear authorities and monitoring. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment means action plans will increasingly focus on process simplification, automation adoption, service prioritization, and workforce reallocation. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity adds emphasis on leadership ownership, disciplined decision-making, training, mentorship, and realistic sequencing of corrective actions. AI and Automation in Statistical Production also affects action planning by requiring decisions on workflow redesign, governance controls, shared solutions, and workforce upskilling. Evidence from the work description is limited, but the role title "Evaluation Officer" and placement in the Evaluation Division support regular contribution to action-plan formation based on evaluation reports and recommendations.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes assessing whether existing sources and their accompanying metadata are suitable for statistical use, including restrictions, quality, interoperability and downstream usability. The work description is materially connected through its responsibility to identify metadata requirements, analyze diverse metadata sources, and assess feasibility and options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating metadata consistently across programs.
