Evidence includes: 'Identifies diverse sources from which statistical metadata can be extracted', 'Analyses client requirements in order to determine the feasibility of, and options for, producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata consistently within and across survey and statistical programs', and 'Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter... relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data'. The capability involved is metadata assessment and source suitability from a metadata perspective rather than direct source acquisition. Future-state drivers strengthen this connection: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is especially relevant because standardized metadata-rich repositories make source discovery and suitability assessment more systematic, increasing demand for staff who can evaluate metadata completeness, concepts, formats and interoperability. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production also increase the importance of metadata quality for administrative, linked, geospatial and alternative sources. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access is relevant because the position explicitly requires awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts and security/confidentiality compliance, which affects metadata handling and advice to clients. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure further increase the need to assess metadata readiness for enterprise repositories and reusable platforms.

This subprocess is directly implicated because it concerns detailed design of outputs, products and dissemination arrangements, including use of standards and metadata from prior collections. The position's core mandate is to coordinate the preparation, storage and dissemination of statistical metadata and to write procedures and training materials used in metadata management programs. Evidence includes: 'Prepares, and coordinates the preparation of, statistical metadata for storage and dissemination', 'reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata', 'Writes and presents detailed documents, procedures manuals and training manuals which explain and clarify the methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate statistical metadata', and 'liaises with... survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications'. The capability involved is designing dissemination-ready metadata outputs and the procedures, standards and supporting documentation that make those outputs usable and consistent. Future-state drivers materially intensify this work. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is central because outputs increasingly must be structured as discoverable, standardized, metadata-rich assets. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development push dissemination toward reusable platform-based components and interoperable metadata services, increasing the need for standard metadata structures and reusable dissemination patterns. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access matters because dissemination design must account for confidentiality and secure access, and the work description explicitly references the Statistics Act, Privacy Act awareness, and compliance with security and confidentiality requirements. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment also pushes toward standardized, reusable dissemination products, which aligns with the position's role in recommending and testing modifications to methods, procedures and systems.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes preparation of metadata for collected and derived variables, classifications and units as a precondition for later phases. The position does not define survey variables directly, but it is materially connected through responsibility for statistical metadata concepts, frameworks, standards and consistency across programs. Evidence includes: 'Knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally', 'Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical metadata and to identify, evaluate and ensure consistency', and 'Writes reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training materials... related to the production, storage dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata'. The capability involved is variable- and classification-related metadata stewardship, standardization and documentation rather than substantive variable design ownership. Future-state drivers increase this relevance. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability strongly affects this subprocess because variable-level metadata must be standardized and reusable. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the need for harmonized metadata for linked, derived, geospatial and non-survey variables. The position's role in advising clients, identifying update needs when standards or systems change, and ensuring consistency across survey and statistical programs directly supports this future need.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes design of coding, validation, integration and disclosure-related methods, all of which increasingly depend on standardized metadata and metadata-aware processing rules. The position does not design statistical methods themselves, but it materially supports this subprocess by maintaining the metadata standards, procedures, documentation and quality evaluations that processing and analysis depend on. Evidence includes: 'Knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata', 'Reviews current production, storage, dissemination and evaluation methods, procedures and systems to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes', and 'Analyzes and evaluates statistical metadata with respect to policy and procedural requirements, consistency across survey and statistical programs and other pre-defined quality measures'. The capability involved is metadata method stewardship: ensuring processing and analysis environments have consistent, documented metadata structures and quality controls. Future-state drivers make this more important. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is highly relevant because processing design increasingly relies on metadata as an operational input. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the need for metadata-driven, reusable processing components and lineage. AI and Automation in Statistical Production also raises the importance of documentation, transparency, quality and repeatability, all of which the position supports through manuals, reports, validation and training. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access is relevant insofar as metadata and documentation must support secure handling and controlled processing.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it determines end-to-end workflows, systems, databases, reuse of existing solutions, and staff interaction with systems. The work description shows substantial responsibility for recommending, implementing and testing modifications to methods, procedures and systems used in metadata production, storage, dissemination and evaluation, and for coordinating work groups and advising clients on impacts. Evidence includes: 'Determines the need for, recommends, implements and tests modifications to methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata', 'Coordinates the activities of work groups established to conduct and implement program activities', 'liaises... to suggest improvements to methods, procedures and systems', and 'advising clients and management of potential impacts and results'. The capability involved is metadata workflow and system design coordination: ensuring metadata-related processes fit together efficiently, are documented, and are understood by users. Future-state drivers strongly amplify this connection. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is central because workflows must treat metadata as a core enterprise asset. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development all point toward reusable, metadata-driven enterprise workflows and stronger interoperability. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline is also relevant because the position sets priorities, timelines and advises management on impacts. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity matters because the position writes training materials, provides specialized training, and coordinates staff/client adoption of changed systems and procedures.

This subprocess has a limited but plausible connection because it recommends direct connection of collection instruments to metadata systems and emphasizes metadata capture at source. The position does not build collection instruments, but it is affected by and contributes to the metadata standards, procedures and training that support metadata capture and later reuse. Evidence includes repeated responsibility for 'production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata', writing training manuals, and knowledge of systems used in metadata production and dissemination. The capability involved is metadata-system integration guidance rather than instrument development. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the importance of capturing metadata at source, which may increase demand for this role's expertise in standards, documentation and client guidance. Relevance remains low because the work description does not state responsibility for building or testing collection instruments.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it covers reuse or build of metadata management services, transformation functions and workflow tools needed for processing and analysis. The position does not build software components as a primary responsibility, but it materially contributes by recommending, implementing and testing modifications to metadata-related methods, procedures and systems, and by producing the documentation and training needed for their use. Evidence includes: 'Determines the need for, recommends, implements and tests modifications to methods, procedures and systems', 'Writes reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training materials', and 'Knowledge of software, statistical packages and programming languages used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata'. The capability involved is operational metadata component stewardship and user enablement rather than software engineering ownership. Future-state drivers increase this relevance: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability makes metadata management services core reusable components; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development increase reuse of shared services; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration increases the need for metadata-aware components; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity increases the importance of training and support for adoption.

This subprocess is relevant because it configures workflows, systems and transformations based on designed workflows. The position is materially connected through its role in implementing and testing modifications to metadata systems and procedures, coordinating work groups, and advising on impacts, priorities and timelines. Evidence includes: 'recommends, implements and tests modifications to methods, procedures and systems', 'determining priorities and target dates', and 'coordinates the activities of work groups... assigns work... monitors progress against objectives and provides guidance'. The capability involved is configuring and operationalizing metadata-related workflows and ensuring users understand and follow them. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment all increase the need for standardized, automated, metadata-aware workflow configuration. The role's training and documentation responsibilities also align with Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity as workflows become more digital and reusable.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes testing assembled services and workflows, checking metadata with suppliers, and ensuring coherent end-to-end operation. The work description explicitly states that the position recommends, implements and tests modifications to metadata methods, procedures and systems, and evaluates metadata quality against standards and policies. Evidence includes: 'implements and tests modifications to methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata' and 'Analyzes and evaluates statistical metadata with respect to policy and procedural requirements... and other pre-defined quality measures'. The capability involved is testing and quality assurance of metadata-related systems and workflows. Future-state drivers strengthen this connection: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the need to validate metadata completeness and linkage; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration increase integration and workflow testing demands; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access matters because metadata and systems must operate securely; and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development increases validation and interoperability testing expectations.

This subprocess is directly implicated because it includes producing technical documentation and user manuals, training users, and moving components into production. These are explicit responsibilities in the work description. Evidence includes: 'Writes reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training materials', 'Writes and presents detailed documents, procedures manuals and training manuals', 'Provides assistance, advice and specialized training to subordinates and clients', and 'advising clients of changes to methods and procedures and advising clients and management of potential impacts and results'. The capability involved is production-readiness enablement for metadata systems and workflows: documentation, training, operational guidance and controlled rollout of changes. Future-state drivers strongly increase this relevance. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is especially important because training and user readiness are central to the subprocess and to the position. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production all increase the need for updated documentation, user guidance, and adoption support as metadata systems become more automated, platform-based and reusable. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access also matters because production deployment and user procedures must reflect secure and compliant operation.

This subprocess has limited relevance because it includes loading collected data and metadata into electronic environments, analyzing metadata and paradata, and versioning/archiving software-based instruments. The position does not finalize collection operations, but it is plausibly connected through expertise in metadata storage, quality evaluation, documentation and system changes. Evidence includes responsibilities for 'storage and dissemination' of metadata, evaluating metadata quality, and analyzing changes in methods, procedures and systems to determine documentation and training updates. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration increase the importance of metadata loading, versioning and linkage at handoff points. Relevance remains low because the work description does not assign collection-finalization duties.

This subprocess is relevant because integration of multiple sources depends heavily on harmonized metadata, source comparison, consistency assessment and documentation. The position does not perform data integration directly, but it materially supports it by identifying metadata requirements, analyzing metadata across programs, and ensuring consistency in methods of processing, storing and disseminating metadata. Evidence includes: 'Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs... to locate, analyze and compare related statistical metadata and to identify, evaluate and ensure consistency', 'Analyses client requirements... consistently within and across survey and statistical programs', and 'Identifies diverse sources from which statistical metadata can be extracted'. The capability involved is metadata harmonization and interoperability support for integrated production. Future-state drivers make this more important: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production make multi-source integration central; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability improves interoperability through standardized metadata; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration increase the need for reusable metadata-driven integration patterns; and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access matters because integrated environments require controlled metadata and confidentiality-aware practices.

This subprocess is directly implicated because the position's core work includes reviewing, editing, validating and quality-evaluating statistical metadata against standards, policies and predefined measures. Evidence is explicit: 'reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata', 'undertaking quality evaluations in accordance with documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines', and 'Analyzes and evaluates statistical metadata with respect to policy and procedural requirements, consistency across survey and statistical programs and other pre-defined quality measures'. The capability involved is metadata validation, quality assurance, anomaly detection from a metadata perspective, and reporting of results to clients and management. Future-state drivers strongly intensify this work. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the importance of validating metadata completeness, consistency and standards compliance. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the need for automated, repeatable, metadata-aware validation in production workflows. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases pressure for standardized validation with fewer staff. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is relevant because the position provides training and guidance to clients and colleagues on methods, procedures and systems used to evaluate metadata quality.

This subprocess has limited relevance because the work description includes editing metadata and changing metadata values when standards, methods, procedures or systems change, but it does not describe statistical data editing or imputation. Evidence includes 'reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata' and 'Identifies the need to update statistical metadata... Determines priorities and timelines for making required updates'. The capability involved is metadata correction and update management rather than statistical imputation. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability makes standardized recording of metadata changes more important, and AI/automation may increase structured metadata update workflows, but the work description does not support a stronger connection to imputation responsibilities.

This subprocess is only indirectly relevant. The position does not derive statistical variables or units, but it supports the metadata needed to document derived variables, classifications and transformations across programs. Evidence includes knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks, writing procedures and training materials, and ensuring consistency across survey and statistical programs. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the importance of documenting derivations and lineage, which may increase demand for this role's metadata expertise. Relevance remains low because the work description does not assign responsibility for deriving variables or units.

This subprocess is relevant because it assembles final datasets and requires versioning, traceability and handoff metadata for downstream analysis. The position is materially connected through responsibility for metadata storage, dissemination, documentation, quality evaluation and system/procedure changes that support standardized handoff and reuse. Evidence includes: 'production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata', 'Writes reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training materials', and 'advising clients and management of potential impacts and results'. The capability involved is ensuring final analytical assets are accompanied by complete, standardized metadata and supporting documentation. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production all increase the importance of metadata-rich, reusable, analysis-ready outputs. The role's cross-program consistency work and documentation responsibilities directly support this need.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes preparing methodological notes and explanatory material to accompany outputs, especially when modern methods are used. The position is materially connected through preparing and disseminating metadata, writing reports on metadata policy requirements and quality evaluations, and producing manuals and training materials used by clients and management. Evidence includes: 'Writes reports which describe statistical metadata policy requirements and the results of metadata quality evaluations', and 'Writes and presents detailed documents... used by other statistical metadata specialists, clients, and management in the maintenance and enhancement of statistical metadata management programs'. The capability involved is preparing metadata and explanatory documentation that supports interpretation and use of outputs. Future-state drivers increase this relevance: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability requires outputs to be metadata-rich and interpretable; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production and AI and Automation in Statistical Production increase the need for methodological explanation and transparency; and Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increases the need to explain source composition and quality implications.

This subprocess is relevant because it explicitly includes checking associated metadata, paradata and quality indicators, and validating outputs against expectations and auxiliary information. The position is materially connected through metadata quality evaluation, reporting, and consistency assessment across programs. Evidence includes: 'Analyzes and evaluates statistical metadata with respect to policy and procedural requirements, consistency across survey and statistical programs and other pre-defined quality measures' and 'Writes reports which describe... the results of metadata quality evaluations'. The capability involved is validating the metadata and quality context that support output validation, rather than validating substantive estimates themselves. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production make metadata completeness and methodological transparency more central to output validation. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion also increases the need for metadata that explains comparability and source changes. The role's liaison and advisory functions support clients and management in understanding these validation results.

This subprocess is directly implicated because it includes collating supporting information, technical notes and necessary metadata so outputs are fit for purpose and ready for release. The position's core work is to prepare, validate, store and disseminate statistical metadata and to produce reports, procedures and training materials used in maintenance and enhancement of metadata management programs. Evidence includes: 'Prepares, and coordinates the preparation of, statistical metadata for storage and dissemination', 'Writes reports which describe statistical metadata policy requirements and the results of metadata quality evaluations', and 'Writes and presents detailed documents... used by... clients, and management'. The capability involved is finalizing the metadata and supporting documentation that make outputs usable, interpretable and compliant with standards. Future-state drivers strongly reinforce this relevance. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is central because metadata becomes a core part of release readiness. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the need for caveats, technical notes and transparency about methods. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access matters because release-level decisions and metadata must reflect confidentiality and secure-access constraints, which aligns with the position's contextual knowledge of the Statistics Act, policies, and privacy/security awareness. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline is also relevant because the role advises management, sets priorities and timelines, and reports quality results used in release readiness decisions.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it manages formatting, loading and linking data and metadata into dissemination systems and includes a final check that necessary metadata are in place. This aligns closely with the position's mandate. Evidence includes: 'Prepares, and coordinates the preparation of, statistical metadata for storage and dissemination', 'reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata', and 'Determines the need for, recommends, implements and tests modifications to methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata'. The capability involved is operational metadata loading, linkage, quality assurance and system readiness for dissemination. Future-state drivers strongly increase this relevance. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is central because dissemination systems must hold searchable, standardized, metadata-rich assets. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration increases automated handoffs into dissemination systems. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure increases reliance on enterprise repositories, secure access and standardized loading patterns. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access matters because metadata and output systems must be updated in controlled, compliant ways. The position's role in documentation, training and advising clients on system changes further supports this subprocess.

This subprocess is directly implicated because dissemination products require explanatory texts, quality statements and metadata-rich packaging, and the position is specifically responsible for metadata production and dissemination coordination. Evidence includes the title 'Metadata Production and Dissemination Coordinator' and responsibilities to 'prepare... statistical metadata for storage and dissemination', 'write reports... on metadata policy requirements and the results of metadata quality evaluations', and 'write and present detailed documents, procedures manuals and training manuals'. The capability involved is producing and maintaining the metadata components and supporting documentation that accompany dissemination products and ensure they meet standards. Future-state drivers strongly reinforce this connection. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is central because dissemination products increasingly need standardized metadata for searchability, interoperability and reuse. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development push toward reusable digital dissemination components and metadata services. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increase templating and automation of recurring products, making standardized metadata even more important. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is relevant because the role supports clients and colleagues through training and documentation as dissemination products become more digital and metadata-rich.

This subprocess is relevant because release requires all elements to be in place, including access arrangements for confidential data and management of release content. The position is materially connected through ensuring metadata are prepared and disseminated, advising on impacts of system and procedure changes, and maintaining compliance with Statistics Act and privacy/security requirements. Evidence includes: 'Prepares... statistical metadata for storage and dissemination', 'advising clients and management of potential impacts and results', and contextual knowledge requirements concerning the Statistics Act, policies, and awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to security and confidentiality. The capability involved is ensuring release-ready metadata and supporting compliance context, rather than managing embargoes or press briefings. Future-state drivers such as Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increase the importance of accurate metadata, controlled access conditions and correction/retraction traceability. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline is also relevant because the position determines priorities and target dates and coordinates work groups, which can affect release readiness.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes responding to user queries, maintaining FAQs/knowledge bases, and supporting partner organizations involved in dissemination. The work description shows substantial client-facing advisory, liaison and training responsibilities related to metadata methods, systems, policy requirements and quality results. Evidence includes: 'Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management', 'Provides assistance, advice and specialized training to subordinates and clients', and 'Writes and presents detailed documents... used by other statistical metadata specialists, clients, and management'. The capability involved is metadata-related client support, guidance and knowledge transfer. Future-state drivers increase this relevance. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure point toward more self-service, searchable and chatbot-enabled support environments, increasing the value of standardized metadata documentation and knowledge materials. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability also matters because better metadata changes how users find and understand products. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases pressure for reusable support content and lower-touch service models, which aligns with the role's documentation and training functions.

This subprocess is relevant because it gathers process metadata, system metrics, staff suggestions and quality indicators for evaluation. The position is materially connected through metadata quality evaluation, reporting, tracking work activity for management reporting, and documenting impacts of changes to methods, procedures and systems. Evidence includes: 'Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of reporting to management and informing planning activities', 'Writes reports which describe statistical metadata policy requirements and the results of metadata quality evaluations', and 'Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems... to determine potential impacts on clients'. The capability involved is generating and organizing metadata-related quality evidence and operational reporting inputs. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure all increase the volume and importance of process metadata and system metrics. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is also relevant because the role provides training and guidance, making staff/client feedback and adoption impacts meaningful evaluation inputs.

This subprocess is relevant because it synthesizes evaluation inputs into reports or dashboards, identifies quality issues and deviations from expected performance, and recommends changes. The position is materially connected through conducting metadata quality evaluations, writing reports on policy requirements and evaluation results, reviewing current methods and systems for relevance, and proposing changes that improve efficiency or quality. Evidence includes: 'undertaking quality evaluations in accordance with documented standards', 'Writes reports which describe statistical metadata policy requirements and the results of metadata quality evaluations', and 'Reviews current production, storage, dissemination and evaluation methods, procedures and systems to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes'. The capability involved is evaluation of metadata management performance and recommendation of improvements. Future-state drivers such as Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production all increase the need for evidence-based evaluation of metadata workflows, quality, reuse and efficiency. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline is also relevant because evaluation findings increasingly support enterprise decisions on what to improve, standardize or stop.

This subprocess is relevant because it turns evaluation findings into agreed improvement actions with monitoring mechanisms. The position is materially connected through identifying the need to update metadata in response to changing requirements, determining priorities and timelines, recommending and implementing modifications to methods, procedures and systems, coordinating work groups, and advising management and clients on impacts. Evidence includes: 'Identifies the need to update statistical metadata in response to modifications in client, policy or systems requirements', 'Determines priorities and timelines for making required updates', 'Determines the need for, recommends, implements and tests modifications', and 'Coordinates the activities of work groups established to conduct and implement program activities'. The capability involved is translating metadata quality findings and changing requirements into concrete operational improvements. Future-state drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment all strengthen this connection by increasing the need for explicit prioritization, accountable implementation, training and sustainable change management. The role's combination of evaluation, coordination, documentation, training and advisory responsibilities makes it materially relevant to action planning for metadata-related improvements.

Positions.Position Title: Regional Geographer and Management Information Systems Analyst

implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it covers design of collection strategy, fieldwork operations, respondent management, geospatial collection mechanisms, and monitoring arrangements for census collection. The work description directly supports these needs through regional census geography and operational design work: it includes 'verification of collection maps prior to distribution to the field', 'resolution of geo-coding, boundary issues and CU types', 'validation of CU boundaries including CU refine', and 'delineation of assignments for CLs, FOSs, FOMs and Area Managers for all collection activities including L/L, NRFU, E-NRFU, Collectives, Early Enumeration, Canvasser and Reserves.' These are concrete collection-design and fieldwork-design responsibilities, not merely downstream use. The capability involved is operational design expertise in geospatially enabled census collection, assignment planning, and targeted collection strategies for difficult or special populations such as collective dwellings and reserves. The work description also shows direct contribution to collection strategy through advice on 'collective dwelling enumeration strategies and requirements', assistance to CFOs with 'assignment planning', and tactical decisions to 'organize and coordinate Collective dwelling collection activities.' Future-state drivers indicate this work will change materially. Under Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, collection design shifts toward adaptive collection design, online-first strategy, geospatial inputs, and more targeted residual collection. Even though the current duties are field- and map-intensive, the same regional geography and assignment-planning expertise will increasingly be shaped by adaptive collection design, digital routing, and mixed-source collection models. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will also affect how maps, collection systems, and assignment tools are configured and accessed securely. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will intensify pressure to optimize assignments, reduce labour-intensive approaches, and standardize collection operations. Evidence from the work description that managers rely on the incumbent's recommendations because actions 'impact the capability of managers to monitor and track key performance indicators, report on operations and to manage resources' further supports high relevance.

This subprocess is materially connected because, for census and census-like operations, it includes defining the population frame, using geospatial data and classifications, assessing coverage, and supporting complete enumeration or filtered operational frames. The work description directly addresses these responsibilities through regional geography and collection unit design: 'resolution of geo-coding, boundary issues and CU types', 'validation of CU boundaries including CU refine', 'identification of operationally mailable areas', and delineation of assignments across collection units and management roles. These activities are core to defining and validating the operational frame for census collection and ensuring spatial coverage is appropriate. The capability involved is geospatial frame expertise: understanding boundaries, collection unit types, mailable areas, and assignment geography so that the target population is correctly represented operationally. The work description is especially relevant because the incumbent's decisions affect 'efficient and effective operations of Census Field Offices located throughout the region,' which depends on sound frame and boundary design. Future-state drivers reinforce this relevance. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the role of administrative registers, linked files, and geospatial/gridded sources in frame construction and coverage assessment. That means regional geographers and GIS analysts will increasingly need to reconcile traditional collection geography with source-based and linked frames. The geospatial emphasis in the current role positions it squarely in this transition. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will also push stronger use of source-based frames and more selective direct collection, increasing the importance of accurate mailable-area identification and boundary validation. The evidence is explicit that the incumbent validates boundaries, resolves geocoding issues, and supports assignment delineation across all collection activities.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes design of validation, integration, and analysis methods used in processing and analysis, especially where management information, geospatial information, and operational data must be reconciled and interpreted. The work description shows recurring analytical responsibility for MIS reporting: the incumbent must 'structure searches and identify sources of information in order to prepare regular and ad hoc MIS reports,' 'select/apply methodologies to extract/consolidate, manipulate data,' and 'apply/adapt techniques and procedures to reconcile, validate, verify, analyze and present data, identify trends or anomalies.' That is direct evidence of methodological work around extraction, consolidation, reconciliation, validation, and analysis, even if focused on operational MIS rather than statistical estimation. The capability involved is analytical and methodological expertise in transforming operational data into reliable management information for monitoring costs, progress, and anomalies. The work description further states that the incumbent performs 'daily analysis of management information reports to monitor costs and field collection progress and make recommendations to management to resolve anomalies.' Future-state drivers suggest this work will become more automated, metadata-driven, and pipeline-based. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability point toward more standardized validation rules, automated monitoring, and reusable processing components. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase pressure to reduce manual reconciliation and anomaly detection. Workforce implications such as reduced manual effort and greater emphasis on exception handling are especially relevant because the current role already centers on identifying anomalies and advising management. Relevance is medium rather than high because the work description supports and applies these methods operationally, but does not explicitly state responsibility for enterprise-level statistical methodology design.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it concerns end-to-end workflow design, role assignment, system interaction, reuse of production solutions, and ensuring processes fit together without gaps or redundancies. The work description directly reflects workflow and operational design responsibilities: the incumbent makes recommendations on 'the need for and content of training courses and/or information sessions to managers,' supports 'delineation of assignments for CLs, FOSs, FOMs and Area Managers for all collection activities,' clarifies directives and provides guidelines on collection systems, procedures and concepts, and organizes working groups and committees 'to review and recommend work methods, procedures and training to support collection activities.' These are explicit workflow, role, and operating-model design functions. The capability involved is operational architecture for census collection: defining who does what, where, and when; aligning geography, assignments, procedures, and management information; and ensuring field operations can be monitored and controlled. The work description also shows the incumbent provides direct support to CFO and RCC managers in developing 'specific strategies for collective dwelling enumeration,' which is a workflow design and coordination function for a specialized collection stream. Future-state drivers make this even more significant. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all point to redesigned workflows with clearer handoffs, more automation, stronger monitoring, and changed staff-system interactions. The current role already sits at the intersection of geography, operations, MIS, and management guidance, so it is likely to be materially affected by shifts toward pipeline supervision, standardized reusable production flows, and flatter, more disciplined operating models. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will further pressure this role to simplify workflows and optimize assignments. The evidence that the incumbent's decisions affect 'efficient and cost-effective collection services and CFOs compliance to departmental directives' strongly supports high relevance.

This subprocess is directly implicated because it covers preparing people, processes, systems, communications, and training for live collection. The work description contains multiple setup-related responsibilities: verifying maps 'prior to distribution to the field'; deciding on 'the need for and content of training courses and/or information sessions to managers'; responding to queries from managers and staff; clarifying directives and providing guidelines and expertise to CFOs; and assisting with assignment planning for collective dwelling enumeration. These are concrete collection-readiness activities. The capability involved is operational readiness for census field collection, especially ensuring that geography, assignments, directives, and management understanding are in place before and during collection. The work description also notes direct support to CFO and RCC managers through meetings, written material, telephone calls, and strategy development, which aligns with preparing collection operations and staff. Future-state drivers indicate that collection setup will increasingly involve digital tools, secure access, online-first operations, and more standardized setup processes. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will affect how collection systems, maps, and staff access are provisioned. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is especially relevant because this role already determines training content and provides guidance to managers; future modernization will increase training and change-support demands. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline also matters because census setup is deadline-driven, and the work description shows operational decisions with direct impact on field office effectiveness. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will likely increase pressure for leaner setup and more standardized support.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the work description directly supports live collection operations, monitoring, tactical adjustment, and management of difficult collection areas. Evidence includes providing interpretation and technical expertise on collection systems and procedures to CFOs, facilitating 'resolution strategies to address collection requirements in difficult areas and apply targeted strategies,' organizing and coordinating collective dwelling collection activities, and performing 'daily analysis of management information reports to monitor costs and field collection progress and make recommendations to management to resolve anomalies.' These are core run-collection functions. The capability involved is operational control of census collection: monitoring progress, costs, and anomalies; supporting field offices; adjusting tactics; and ensuring compliance with directives. The work description also states that decisions affect 'the efficient and effective operations of Census Field Offices located throughout the region' and 'the provision of efficient and cost-effective collection services,' which is direct evidence of live operational impact. Future-state drivers suggest this work will evolve toward more automated monitoring, adaptive collection, and digital operations. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase real-time monitoring, automated reporting, and targeted intervention. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion may shift some collection burden away from direct enumeration, but will increase the need to manage mixed-source operations and residual targeted collection. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline is especially relevant because the role already manages progress against operational targets and resolves issues quickly. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will intensify the need for lower-touch, more optimized collection management.

This subprocess is relevant because the work description includes integrating and consolidating information from multiple sources for management and operational use. The incumbent must 'structure searches and identify sources of information' and 'extract/consolidate, manipulate data' to prepare MIS reports, then 'reconcile, validate, verify, analyze and present data.' While this is framed as MIS rather than statistical integration, it is still direct evidence of combining and harmonizing multiple operational inputs into consolidated information for decision-making. The capability involved is data integration for operational intelligence: bringing together management, geographic, and collection information to support monitoring and resource management. The work description further notes that these actions affect managers' ability to 'monitor and track key performance indicators, report on operations and to manage resources.' Future-state drivers indicate that integration work will become more central and more automated as administrative, alternative, linked, and geospatial data expand and as enterprise platforms and integrated pipelines mature. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will likely standardize source discovery and integration. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase reliance on reusable integrated data rather than manual compilation. Relevance is medium because the work description clearly shows integration-like activity, but in an operational MIS context rather than explicit statistical record linkage or enterprise data integration.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the work description repeatedly emphasizes validation, verification, anomaly detection, and quality checking. Evidence includes 'verification of collection maps prior to distribution to the field,' 'validation of CU boundaries including CU refine,' and MIS responsibilities to 'reconcile, validate, verify, analyze and present data, identify trends or anomalies.' The incumbent also performs 'daily analysis of management information reports to monitor costs and field collection progress and make recommendations to management to resolve anomalies.' These are explicit review-and-validate functions. The capability involved is quality assurance of both geospatial and operational data: checking boundaries, coding and geography issues, validating management information, and identifying discrepancies that affect field operations. The work description shows that these validation activities materially affect field office efficiency and compliance. Future-state drivers indicate this work will increasingly use automated monitoring, metadata-driven validation, and exception-based workflows. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development all point toward more standardized validation rules and stronger monitoring. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase heterogeneity of inputs and therefore complexity of validation. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will reduce tolerance for manual review and increase reliance on automated anomaly detection, making the incumbent's current validation expertise highly relevant to future change.

This subprocess is relevant because the incumbent prepares regular and ad hoc MIS reports and determines the most appropriate format for presenting data. The work description states that effort is required to 'prepare regular and ad hoc MIS reports' and to 'analyze and present data, identify trends or anomalies and to determine the most appropriate format for presentation of data.' That is direct evidence of transforming processed operational data into usable outputs for managers. The capability involved is analytical reporting and production of management-facing outputs that support operational oversight, KPI tracking, and resource management. The work description explicitly notes that these outputs affect managers' capability to 'monitor and track key performance indicators, report on operations and to manage resources.' Future-state drivers suggest these outputs will become more automated, metadata-rich, and potentially more standardized through enterprise platforms and integrated pipelines. AI and Automation in Statistical Production may support draft reporting and anomaly summaries; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase expectations for contextual metadata; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push templated and lower-touch reporting. Relevance is medium because the outputs are MIS and operational rather than public statistical products, but the subprocess remains materially connected.

This subprocess is relevant because the incumbent does not only produce MIS outputs but also checks them for trends, anomalies, and operational plausibility before management use. The work description states that the incumbent must 'reconcile, validate, verify, analyze and present data, identify trends or anomalies' and perform 'daily analysis of management information reports to monitor costs and field collection progress.' This is output validation in an operational management-information context. The capability involved is validating whether reported indicators and operational summaries are credible and useful for management decisions. The work description also shows use of domain intelligence: recommendations are made to management to resolve anomalies, and feedback is provided on successes and challenges 'throughout the planning and collection phase in order to assist in the overall evaluation of the Census Program.' Future-state drivers indicate that as outputs become more automated and sourced from more complex pipelines, validation will rely more on quality indicators, metadata, and exception-based review. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment all increase the need for targeted, risk-based validation. Relevance is medium because the outputs are internal operational reports rather than official statistical releases, but the validation function is clearly present.

This subprocess is materially connected because the incumbent interprets management information and explains it to managers and staff to support operational decisions. Evidence includes preparing MIS reports, identifying 'trends or anomalies,' responding to queries from managers and staff, providing written material and advice, and giving feedback on 'the success and/or challenges experienced throughout the planning and collection phase in order to assist in the overall evaluation of the Census Program.' The capability involved is interpretation of operational indicators and explanation of what they mean for census collection performance, costs, and tactical response. The work description also shows the incumbent clarifies directives and provides expertise on collection systems, procedures and concepts, which requires translating data and operational evidence into understandable guidance. Future-state drivers suggest this interpretive work will increasingly involve explaining outputs generated through more automated, integrated, and digitally enabled systems. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is relevant because communication and analytical expertise become more important as tools and methods change. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may alter how outputs are generated and therefore how they must be explained. Relevance is medium because the interpretation is operational rather than public-facing statistical analysis, but it is clearly part of the role.

This subprocess is relevant because the role generates and analyzes operational evidence that feeds evaluation of the census program. The work description explicitly states that the incumbent performs daily analysis of MIS reports and provides feedback on 'the success and/or challenges experienced throughout the planning and collection phase in order to assist in the overall evaluation of the Census Program.' That is direct evidence of gathering and synthesizing evaluation inputs. The capability involved is compiling operational indicators, anomalies, and field experience into evidence for program assessment. The role's MIS reporting, KPI tracking, and anomaly detection functions also align with gathering process metadata and performance indicators. Future-state drivers indicate this work will become richer and more continuous as monitoring, automation, and integrated pipelines generate more telemetry and paradata. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration all increase the volume and usefulness of evaluation inputs. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase demand for evidence on productivity, service trade-offs, and sustainability. Relevance is medium because the work description supports evaluation inputs rather than owning the full evaluation process.

This subprocess is materially connected because the work description includes analytical feedback intended to support evaluation of census operations. The clearest evidence is that the incumbent provides feedback on successes and challenges 'throughout the planning and collection phase in order to assist in the overall evaluation of the Census Program.' In addition, the incumbent analyzes management reports, monitors costs and progress, identifies anomalies, and makes recommendations to management. These are core evaluative activities, even if not framed as authorship of a formal evaluation report. The capability involved is operational performance assessment: comparing observed field performance against expectations, identifying issues, and informing future improvements. Future-state drivers suggest evaluation will become more dashboard-driven, more focused on efficiency, and more dependent on automated metrics and governance discipline. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment are especially relevant because the role already monitors progress, costs, and anomalies in real time. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will likely increase the amount of evaluative evidence available and shift work toward interpreting exceptions and performance trends. Relevance is medium because the role contributes materially to evaluation but does not explicitly own enterprise evaluation reporting.

Positions.Branch/Division: Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division

implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is directly relevant because it concerns gathering evaluation material from across the statistical business process, including user feedback, process metadata, system metrics, staff suggestions, and reports against prior action plans. The position title is explicitly "Evaluation Analyst," and the organizational placement is "Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division," which strongly indicates direct involvement in evaluation work rather than incidental exposure. The work description is sparse, but the listed key activities provide evidence of maintaining or using organizational reference and support information such as "HR service standards," "HR committees," "HR contact list," and "Corporate service providers." Those kinds of materials are consistent with assembling contextual inputs, service information, stakeholder references, and organizational evidence that can support evaluation work. Future-state drivers make this subprocess even more important: AI and Automation in Statistical Production increases the volume of monitoring outputs, documentation, and system metrics available for evaluation; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure increases centralized access to operational evidence and tooling; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration increases the availability of end-to-end process metadata and workflow telemetry; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity increases the importance of gathering staff feedback, training outcomes, and workforce-readiness evidence; and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases demand for evidence on productivity, service impacts, and sustainability under reduced staffing. The cumulative effect is that evaluation input gathering becomes more continuous, metadata-rich, and operationally important. The work description evidence is limited, but the role title and branch/division are strong direct evidence, while the HR-oriented key activities suggest interaction with service standards, committees, contacts, wellness, and providers that could serve as evaluation inputs or stakeholder/context sources.

This subprocess is materially connected because it is the core activity of analyzing evaluation inputs, comparing them to expectations or benchmarks, synthesizing findings into reports or dashboards, identifying quality or performance issues, and making recommendations. An "Evaluation Analyst" in the "Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division" is directly aligned with this responsibility. Even though the detailed technical responsibilities are not provided, the supplied work description identifies the role and organizational context clearly enough to establish direct relevance. The listed key activities such as "HR service standards," "Wellness at Statistics Canada," "HR committees," and "Corporate service providers" suggest subject matter areas or organizational domains that may be examined, monitored, or assessed in evaluation work. This aligns with the subprocess requirement to analyze evidence and assess performance against expectations. Future-state drivers intensify the importance of this subprocess: AI and Automation in Statistical Production supports continuous dashboards and richer evidence but also requires evaluation of transparency, governance, and trust; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline makes milestone attainment, schedule adherence, and implementation effectiveness central evaluation criteria; Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline increases the need for evidence-based recommendations and explicit trade-offs; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment makes evaluation central to judging productivity, savings, service impacts, and whether activities should be redesigned or stopped; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity adds evaluation dimensions related to training, adoption, leadership effectiveness, employee well-being, and workforce sustainability. The cumulative effect is that evaluation work becomes broader and more strategic, extending beyond traditional quality review into transformation assessment. Evidence from the work description is strongest in the explicit role title and branch/division, with the HR-related activity list indicating plausible evaluation subject areas without inventing additional duties.

This subprocess is relevant because evaluation work commonly feeds decision-making on corrective actions, improvement priorities, and monitoring mechanisms for future iterations. The subprocess is about bringing together decision-making authority to agree an action plan based on evaluation findings. An EC-04 Evaluation Analyst would not necessarily own final approval authority, and the work description does not state that this position approves plans, so relevance is not High. However, the role is still materially connected because evaluation analysts typically contribute the evidence, analysis, and recommendations that inform action plans. The work description supports this connection through the explicit role title "Evaluation Analyst" and placement in the "Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division." The listed key activities such as "HR service standards," "HR committees," and "Corporate service providers" also suggest involvement with organizational service environments where evaluation findings could lead to improvement actions, governance discussions, or follow-up mechanisms. Future-state drivers increase the significance of this subprocess: Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline strengthens the need for explicit prioritization, accountability, and transparent trade-offs in action planning; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline pushes action plans toward milestone-based, time-bound commitments; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity emphasizes leadership ownership, realistic sequencing, training, and support through change; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases pressure for action plans focused on simplification, automation, service prioritization, and workforce adjustment; AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure add action-planning needs around governance controls, shared solutions, monitoring, and workforce upskilling. The cumulative effect is that evaluation outputs are more likely to feed structured transformation action plans. The evidence is indirect but sufficient for Medium relevance: the role and branch clearly connect to evaluation, while the work description does not explicitly assign decision authority.

Positions.Position Title: Metadata Development, Dissemination and Evaluation Coordinator

implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it includes assessing whether data sources are suitable for statistical use and whether accompanying metadata are sufficient for access, interoperability, reuse and downstream processing. The work description is materially connected through its core responsibility for evaluating 'corporate and client metadata requirements' and for assessing issues related to the 'production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' The position also analyzes client requirements, evaluates consistency across surveys and programs, and advises on impacts of changes to methods, procedures and systems. That aligns with the metadata-driven aspect of source suitability assessment, especially under the driver 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' which makes standardized, searchable, metadata-rich assets more central to judging source suitability. Future-state changes are likely to increase the importance of this role because standardized metadata will be increasingly needed to assess source concepts, formats, quality, timeliness, access conditions and interoperability. Relevant evidence includes: 'Evaluates corporate and client metadata requirements'; 'Analyzes client requirements... relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata'; and knowledge of 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata.'

This subprocess is directly implicated because it covers the detailed design of outputs, products and dissemination arrangements, including metadata structures and dissemination procedures. The position title itself—'Metadata Development, Dissemination and Evaluation Coordinator'—and the duties around preparing metadata for storage and dissemination show direct responsibility. The work description states that the incumbent 'plans, prioritizes, coordinates and undertakes the development and preparation of statistical metadata for storage and dissemination,' and 'writes and presents detailed documents, procedures manuals and training manuals' explaining methods and systems used to 'produce, store and disseminate statistical metadata.' This is a direct fit with designing dissemination-ready outputs and related procedures. Future-state drivers make this even more central. Under 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' outputs must be structured as discoverable, standardized, metadata-rich assets. Under 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure' and 'Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access,' dissemination design increasingly assumes platform-based delivery, secure access patterns, and stronger metadata linkage. The role's responsibility to advise clients on methods, procedures, systems, and impacts of changes means it will be materially affected by these technology and capability themes, especially discoverability, interoperability, data accessibility and usability, and secure dissemination. Evidence includes repeated references to 'storage and dissemination,' producing internal documentation and training materials on dissemination methods, and reports used 'to ensure the quality and consistency of statistical metadata disseminated by Statistics Canada.'

This subprocess is highly relevant because it explicitly includes preparation of metadata for collected and derived variables, classifications and units as a precondition for later phases. The position is centered on statistical metadata concepts, frameworks, standards, and quality evaluation across programs. The work description states that the incumbent has 'knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks' and uses that knowledge 'to plan, prioritize, coordinate and undertake the preparation, editing, validation and quality evaluation of statistical metadata.' It also notes knowledge of survey and program subject matter 'to evaluate client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination' and to ensure consistency across programs. This is materially connected to variable-level metadata design and standardization, even though the role does not define survey variables themselves. The strongest future-state driver is 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' which makes variable-level metadata more standardized, reusable and discoverable across programs. 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' also increases the importance of richer metadata for derived variables, harmonization and reuse. The role fulfills this need by reviewing, editing, validating and evaluating metadata quality, and by advising clients on policy requirements, methods and procedures. Evidence includes: 'preparation, editing, validation and quality evaluation of statistical metadata'; 'knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts... to evaluate client requirements'; and identifying 'consistency in the methods of processing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of metadata across programs.'

This subprocess is relevant because collection design increasingly requires metadata capture at source, metadata exchange with suppliers, and monitoring of metadata impacts when collection methods or third-party sources change. The work description does not assign direct responsibility for designing collection instruments, but it does assign responsibility for advising on and evaluating metadata methods, procedures and systems used across production and dissemination, and for analyzing changes in methods and systems to determine impacts on metadata and documentation. The role 'analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats,' which is materially connected to collection redesign where metadata structures and formats change. Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion,' and 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' increase the need for metadata-aware collection design, especially for online-first, administrative, alternative and linked data environments. The position is likely to be meaningfully affected because clients will need advice, training, and updated procedures when collection changes alter metadata requirements. Evidence includes advising clients on 'methods, procedures and systems,' analyzing impacts of changes on 'existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals,' and liaising with survey managers to translate requirements into specifications for metadata production, storage, dissemination and evaluation.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it includes design of validation, integration and methodological rules, and the position is heavily engaged in evaluating and improving methods, procedures and systems for metadata production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation. The work description states that the incumbent 'evaluates the methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, determining the need for, recommending, implementing and testing modifications; participates in the development of new specifications.' It also states that the incumbent 'analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and evaluation methods, procedures and systems to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for changes or alternative methods, procedures and systems which would result in operational efficiencies and/or improvements in the quality of statistical metadata.' This is a strong fit with design of processing and analysis components for metadata-related workflows. Future-state drivers intensify this connection. 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' makes metadata an operational input to processing, not just documentation. 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration' and 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' increase the need for standardized, reusable, metadata-driven processing rules and lineage. 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' also pushes redesign toward more efficient methods. The role fulfills this need through specification development, testing modifications, quality evaluation, and advising clients and management on impacts. Evidence includes participation in 'development of new specifications,' recommending and testing modifications, and writing reports recommending 'procedures and tools that could be developed to evaluate the quality of statistical metadata.'

This subprocess is highly implicated because it concerns end-to-end workflow design, reuse of systems and databases, and staff interaction with systems and responsibilities. The work description repeatedly emphasizes evaluating and improving 'methods, procedures and systems' for metadata production, storage, dissemination and evaluation; advising clients on changes; and assessing impacts on workloads, outputs and clients. The incumbent also liaises with specialists, survey managers and management 'to develop and translate requirements into specifications' and to 'establish project plans, priorities and target dates.' This is directly relevant to workflow and system design for metadata management. Future-state drivers make this especially important. 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' requires workflows that treat metadata as a core enterprise asset. 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure,' 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration,' and 'Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development' all point toward reusable, interoperable, metadata-enabled workflows and clearer staff-system interactions. The work description also includes leadership responsibilities—leading project teams, setting goals and milestones, determining training requirements—which aligns with the workforce implications of redesigned workflows and role clarity. Evidence includes evaluating systems and impacts of modifications, participating in new specifications, advising on methods and procedures, and knowledge of 'the potential impacts of new or modified methods, procedures and systems on workloads, outputs and clients.'

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it covers reuse or build of processing, transformation, workflow and metadata management services. The work description does not say the incumbent programs or builds software components directly, so relevance is not high. However, the position materially contributes through specification development, testing modifications, evaluating systems, and producing procedures and training materials for metadata-related systems. The incumbent 'participates in the development of new specifications' and 'recommends, implements and tests modifications' to methods, procedures and systems used in metadata production, storage, dissemination and evaluation. That is a meaningful contribution to component reuse/build activities for metadata management and quality evaluation.
