Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure,' and 'Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development' increase the importance of reusable metadata services and standardized components. The role is likely to be increasingly affected because metadata management services, lineage, and quality controls will need clearer specifications, validation and documentation. Evidence includes testing modifications, developing specifications, writing procedures manuals and training manuals, and knowledge of software, statistical packages and programming languages used in metadata production, dissemination and evaluation.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns configuring workflows, systems and transformations based on designed production workflows. The work description does not explicitly assign workflow configuration authority, but it does show regular involvement in translating requirements into specifications, advising on methods and systems, negotiating procedural modifications, and assessing impacts of changes to metadata processes. The incumbent liaises with specialists and managers 'to develop and translate requirements into specifications' and 'to negotiate modifications to methods, procedures and timelines.' This indicates meaningful contribution to workflow configuration for metadata-related processes. Future-state drivers such as 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration,' 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' and 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' suggest that metadata workflows will become more automated, standardized and tightly integrated, increasing the importance of this role's advisory and specification work. The role will likely shift further toward ensuring metadata handoffs, documentation and quality controls are embedded in configured workflows. Evidence includes translating requirements into specifications, advising clients of changes to methods and procedures, and analyzing changes to determine updates needed to metadata, documentation and training materials.

This subprocess is materially connected because the work description explicitly includes testing modifications and undertaking quality evaluations against documented standards. The incumbent 'determines the need for, recommends, implements and tests modifications' to metadata methods, procedures and systems, and 'undertakes quality evaluations in accordance with documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines.' This aligns with testing assembled/configured services and confirming that routines are suitable for use. The role is especially relevant for metadata-related system testing, quality assurance and sign-off support, though not necessarily for all technical system testing. Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure,' 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration,' and 'Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development' increase the need to test metadata linkage, interoperability, validation and end-to-end coherence. The role's emphasis on standards, policies, documentation and reporting means it will be increasingly affected by stronger validation and testing expectations. Evidence includes 'testing modifications,' 'reviews and verifies the results of quality evaluations,' and writing reports on metadata quality evaluation results for clients and management.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it includes documentation and training for production-ready systems, and those are explicit core duties of the position. The work description states that the incumbent 'compiles, writes, edits and approves reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training materials' related to metadata production, storage, dissemination and evaluation, and 'provides advice and training' on policies, directives, methods, procedures and systems to subordinates, specialists, clients and managers. This is a direct fit with finalizing production systems through user manuals, technical documentation and training. Future-state drivers strongly reinforce this connection. 'Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity' is especially relevant because the role already identifies training needs, recommends training plans, and provides training. 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production,' 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure,' and 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' will increase the need for updated documentation, user guidance and workforce enablement as metadata systems modernize. Evidence includes writing and approving documentation and training materials, advising and training clients and staff, and assessing training needs related to metadata methods, procedures and systems.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes loading collected data and metadata into suitable environments, analyzing metadata and paradata, versioning and archiving collection instruments, and preparing metadata for downstream processing. The work description is not about collection operations directly, but it is strongly about metadata storage, formats, quality evaluation and adaptation to new formats. The incumbent 'analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems... to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats' and has responsibility for metadata production, storage and evaluation. That creates a meaningful connection to collection finalization where metadata are loaded, standardized and prepared for later phases. Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration,' and 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion' increase the importance of structured metadata loading, versioning and linkage at handoff points. The role is likely to be increasingly affected because metadata completeness and standardization at ingestion/finalization become more critical. Evidence includes responsibilities for metadata storage, adaptation to new formats, and evaluation of metadata quality across systems and programs.

This subprocess is relevant because integration increasingly depends on harmonized, standardized metadata across multiple sources, and the position is responsible for ensuring consistency, quality and comparability of metadata across surveys and programs. The work description states that the incumbent analyzes metadata requirements and ensures 'approaches and results are consistent within and across surveys and statistical programs,' and identifies 'conflicts, gaps or duplication of effort' across programs. While the role does not directly perform record linkage or data integration, it materially supports the metadata capability that makes integration possible and reliable. Future-state drivers make this more important. 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion,' 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' and 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' all increase reliance on metadata for interoperability, source comparison, harmonization and reuse. The role fulfills this need by evaluating metadata quality, advising on standards and procedures, and comparing metadata across programs. Evidence includes analyzing and comparing related statistical metadata across programs, ensuring consistency, and evaluating metadata with respect to policy and procedural requirements.

This subprocess is directly implicated because the work description repeatedly emphasizes validation and quality evaluation of statistical metadata. The incumbent 'plans, prioritizes, coordinates and undertakes the development and preparation of statistical metadata for storage and dissemination, reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata' and 'undertakes quality evaluations in accordance with documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines.' This is a direct match to review and validation activities, albeit focused on metadata rather than survey response data. The role also reviews and verifies quality evaluations done by others and writes reports on results and recommendations. Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production,' 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration,' and 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' all increase the need for standardized, automated, metadata-aware validation and exception handling. The role will likely become even more central as metadata quality becomes a prerequisite for reuse, interoperability and automated production. Evidence includes explicit references to 'reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata,' 'quality evaluations,' and evaluating metadata consistency across surveys and programs.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance because it includes changing data values and producing metadata on editing and imputation processes. The work description does not assign responsibility for editing or imputing statistical data. However, the position is responsible for metadata preparation, validation, quality evaluation and documentation, which could be affected by the need to document editing/imputation processes and resulting metadata. The strongest connection is indirect through metadata stewardship rather than direct execution of edit/imputation methods. Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' and 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' increase the importance of standardized metadata about transformations, but the work description does not show direct responsibility for those transformations themselves. Evidence is limited to the broader responsibility for metadata quality, documentation and evaluation rather than editing/imputation operations.

This subprocess is only indirectly relevant. The work description does not state that the incumbent derives variables or units. However, because the role is responsible for preparing, validating and evaluating metadata, and because derived variables and units require metadata and lineage, the position may be affected by this subprocess through documentation, standards and quality evaluation of derived metadata. Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' and 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' increase the importance of documenting derivation logic and semantic meaning, but the work description does not assign derivation responsibility itself. Evidence is limited to the incumbent's role in metadata concepts, frameworks, validation and consistency across programs.

This subprocess is relevant because it brings together processed results into datasets used for analysis, and increasingly requires standardized metadata, versioning, traceability and handoff information. The work description is materially connected through responsibilities for metadata storage, dissemination, evaluation, documentation and adaptation to new formats. The incumbent writes procedures and training materials, evaluates systems and methods, and analyzes changes to determine where metadata and documentation updates are required. Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration,' and 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure' make metadata-rich final datasets more important as governed enterprise assets. The role fulfills this need by ensuring metadata quality and consistency and by advising on impacts of system and procedure changes. Evidence includes responsibilities for metadata storage and dissemination, adapting metadata to new formats, and writing documentation used in the operation and enhancement of metadata management programs.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes preparing methodological notes and explanatory material to accompany outputs, especially when modern methods are used. The work description shows strong responsibility for writing reports, procedures manuals and training manuals, and for producing reports that describe policy requirements related to development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of high-quality metadata. The role is not responsible for drafting statistical commentary broadly, but it is directly responsible for metadata and methodological documentation that supports outputs. Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production,' and 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' increase the need for explanatory metadata and methodological transparency. The role fulfills this need by writing detailed documents and reports used by clients and management to ensure quality and consistency of disseminated metadata. Evidence includes writing reports on policy requirements and metadata quality evaluation results, and preparing documentation and training materials related to dissemination and evaluation of metadata.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes checking associated metadata, paradata and quality indicators and validating outputs against expectations. The work description is materially connected through metadata quality evaluation, consistency assessment across programs, and reporting on metadata quality results. The incumbent 'analyzes and evaluates statistical metadata with respect to policy and procedural requirements and consistency across survey and statistical programs' and writes reports used by clients and management 'to ensure the quality and consistency of statistical metadata disseminated by Statistics Canada.' This is a meaningful contribution to output validation from the metadata perspective. Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion,' and 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' increase the importance of validating metadata completeness, comparability and methodological context. Evidence includes quality evaluations, consistency checks across programs, and reports describing policy requirements and evaluation results for high-quality metadata.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it includes collating supporting information, technical notes, metadata and internal documents, and approving content for release readiness. The work description strongly matches these responsibilities from the metadata side. The incumbent 'compiles, writes, edits and approves reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training materials' and writes reports describing policy requirements and metadata quality evaluation results used by clients and management 'to ensure the quality and consistency of statistical metadata disseminated by Statistics Canada.' The role also advises clients and management on impacts of changes to methods and procedures. Future-state drivers make this even more central. 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' makes metadata a core part of release readiness. 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production' and 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' increase the need for caveats, technical notes and transparent metadata. 'Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline' also strengthens approval and accountability expectations. Evidence includes producing internal reports and documentation, approving materials, and ensuring quality and consistency of disseminated metadata.

This subprocess is directly implicated because it is about formatting, loading and linking data and metadata into output systems, and ensuring metadata are in place for dissemination. The work description is centered on metadata for 'storage and dissemination' and on evaluating methods, procedures and systems used for those purposes. The incumbent plans and coordinates metadata preparation for storage and dissemination, evaluates metadata requirements, and analyzes changes to determine where metadata must be updated or adapted to new formats. This is a strong fit with updating dissemination/output systems from the metadata perspective. Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration,' and 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure' make standardized metadata loading, linkage and final readiness checks more central. The role fulfills this need through metadata validation, system evaluation, documentation and client advice. Evidence includes 'development and preparation of statistical metadata for storage and dissemination,' adaptation to new formats, and writing procedures manuals explaining systems used to produce, store and disseminate metadata.

This subprocess is directly relevant because dissemination products require explanatory texts, quality statements, metadata and publication-standard assembly, and the position is explicitly responsible for metadata dissemination and quality reporting. The work description states that the incumbent writes reports describing policy requirements for 'high quality metadata,' writes recommendations for procedures and tools to evaluate metadata quality, and produces documentation and training materials used in the operation and enhancement of metadata management programs. The position title explicitly includes 'Dissemination.' Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure,' and 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' push dissemination products toward standardized, metadata-rich, reusable digital assets. The role fulfills this need by ensuring metadata quality, consistency, explanatory documentation and training. Evidence includes repeated references to dissemination, reports used to ensure quality and consistency of metadata disseminated by Statistics Canada, and writing detailed documents used by clients, systems specialists and management.

This subprocess has limited relevance. The work description does not indicate responsibility for managing release timing, embargoes, subscriber delivery, or researcher access. However, the role is plausibly involved indirectly because release readiness depends on complete, high-quality metadata and supporting documentation, and the position is responsible for ensuring the quality and consistency of metadata disseminated by Statistics Canada. Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' and 'Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access' may increase the importance of metadata completeness and controlled metadata handling at release, but the work description does not show direct release-management duties. Evidence is limited to dissemination-related metadata responsibilities rather than release operations.

This subprocess is plausibly relevant but only to a limited extent. The work description shows that the incumbent provides 'advice and training' to subordinates, specialists, clients and managers regarding metadata policies, directives, methods, procedures and systems. That indicates internal client support and guidance, but not explicit responsibility for external user support, query management, or microdata access services. Future-state drivers such as 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' and 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production' may increase demand for metadata-related support and knowledge materials, and the role already writes training and procedural documentation that could support self-service understanding. Evidence includes providing advice and training to clients and managers and writing training manuals, but there is no direct statement about managing user queries or support services.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position is explicitly responsible for metadata evaluation and quality reporting, and for compiling results for clients and management. The work description states that the incumbent 'undertakes quality evaluations,' 'reviews and verifies the results of quality evaluations undertaken by subordinates and colleagues,' 'compiles results and writes reports for clients and management,' and analyzes impacts of changes on clients in both the short and long term. This is a strong fit with gathering evaluation inputs, compiling quality indicators and making them available for evaluation. Future-state drivers such as 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production,' 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' and 'Conduct evaluation' related drivers increase the importance of continuous metrics, metadata quality indicators, and evidence on workflow and system performance. The role fulfills this need through systematic quality evaluation, reporting and analysis of metadata-related impacts. Evidence includes compiling results, writing reports, and evaluating metadata quality in accordance with standards and policies.

This subprocess is one of the most directly implicated. The position title includes 'Evaluation Coordinator,' and the work description repeatedly emphasizes evaluating metadata requirements, methods, procedures, systems and quality. The incumbent 'evaluates corporate and client metadata requirements,' 'evaluates the methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata,' and 'analyzes and evaluates statistical metadata with respect to policy and procedural requirements and consistency across survey and statistical programs.' The role also writes reports describing results of metadata quality evaluations and recommending improvements. This is a direct match to conducting evaluation, synthesizing findings and making recommendations for future changes. Future-state drivers such as 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production,' 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment,' 'Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline,' and 'Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity' all intensify the need for evidence-based evaluation of quality, efficiency, sustainability, training needs and process changes. Evidence includes explicit evaluation duties, recommendation writing, impact analysis, and reporting to clients and management.

This subprocess is relevant because the role provides input to management decisions and recommendations, identifies training needs, recommends improvements to methods and procedures, and leads project teams with goals, priorities and milestones. The work description states that the incumbent 'provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve divisional and program initiatives,' evaluates issues to provide direction on 'possible approaches, priorities, target dates and training needs,' and recommends and tests modifications to methods, procedures and systems. While the role does not appear to hold final enterprise decision authority, it materially contributes to action planning based on evaluation findings. Future-state drivers such as 'Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline,' 'Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline,' and 'Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity' increase the importance of clear ownership, prioritization, training actions and monitored improvement plans. The role fulfills this need by supplying evidence, recommendations, priorities and training implications to management. Evidence includes recommending improvements, identifying priorities and target dates, leading project teams, and providing input to management decisions and program initiatives.

Positions.Branch/Division: Field 7 – Census, Regional Services and Operations / Collection and Regional Services / Collection Support Unit (CSU)

implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it covers preparing the people, processes and technology needed for collection operations, including training collection staff, ensuring resources are available, configuring systems and communication channels, and supporting readiness for collection activities. The work description places the position in the Collection Support Unit within Collection and Regional Services, which materially connects it to collection-readiness support functions. Evidence is limited, but the listed activities are strongly workforce- and support-oriented: "HR A to Z index," "HR service standards," "Wellness at Statistics Canada," "HR committees," "HR contact list," and "Corporate service providers." These indicate responsibility for helping staff navigate HR services, standards, contacts, wellness supports, and corporate service interfaces rather than direct statistical processing. That aligns with the people-and-readiness dimension of 4.2, especially where collection operations depend on staff preparation, support access, and coordination with service providers. Future-state drivers increase this relevance. The Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity driver is particularly pertinent because 4.2 explicitly includes training staff and preparing people and technology; the work description's HR and wellness focus suggests the role helps staff function within changing operating conditions. The Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure driver also matters because collection setup increasingly depends on employees being able to access systems and resources, while the work description references corporate service providers and HR contact/support mechanisms that can help staff navigate those supports. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline is also relevant because collection readiness must occur on schedule, and HR service standards and contact structures can support timely issue resolution. The cumulative effect is that collection setup is becoming more dependent on structured workforce support, clearer service pathways, and staff readiness under modernization and workforce pressure, which this role appears positioned to support indirectly through HR/service coordination.

This subprocess is plausibly relevant because it includes considering how staff interact with systems and who is responsible for what and when across the production workflow. The work description does not show direct workflow design authority, so relevance is limited. However, the position title is "CSU Manager (CJFL)" in the Collection Support Unit, and the listed activities are all organizational support and workforce-enablement items: "HR service standards," "HR committees," "HR contact list," "Corporate service providers," and "Wellness at Statistics Canada." These suggest involvement in the support environment within which staff operate, rather than in technical workflow architecture itself. That creates a low but plausible connection to 2.6 where workforce interaction, role clarity, and support arrangements are part of workflow design considerations. Future-state drivers make this more salient even if indirect. The Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity driver is relevant because 2.6 is explicitly sensitive to role clarity, leadership capacity, realistic sequencing of work, and staff-system interaction. The work description's emphasis on HR standards, committees, wellness, and service-provider navigation suggests the role may help sustain staff through changing workflows and workforce adjustment pressures. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline may also indirectly affect the role because clearer accountability and leaner workflows increase the importance of support structures and role clarity. Still, because the work description contains no explicit evidence of designing systems, assigning workflow responsibilities, or configuring production roles, this subprocess should be treated as only low relevance.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes training users, producing user guidance, and preparing staff to operate production systems in live environments. The work description is not technical, but it is strongly oriented to workforce support and organizational readiness within a collection-support context. Evidence includes the position being located in the "Collection Support Unit (CSU)" and the listed activities: "HR A to Z index," "HR service standards," "Wellness at Statistics Canada," "HR committees," "HR contact list," and "Corporate service providers." These are consistent with helping employees access support, understand service pathways, and operate effectively in production settings, especially during rollout or stabilization periods. The role therefore appears materially connected to the human-readiness side of finalizing production systems, even if not to technical deployment itself. Future-state drivers strengthen this connection. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is especially relevant because 3.7 explicitly includes training users and preparing staff to operate modernized environments; the work description's HR and wellness content directly supports employee readiness, transition support, and sustainable operations. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure also contributes because finalization increasingly depends on employees being able to access systems and resources and use modern tools; the work description's references to corporate service providers and HR contacts suggest a support function that helps staff navigate those dependencies. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment further increases the importance of clear documentation, role clarity, and support for leaner teams, making HR service standards and support pathways more consequential. The role does not appear to own technical production finalization, but it is meaningfully connected to the workforce enablement required for that subprocess.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns recording and responding to user queries, maintaining support resources such as FAQs or knowledge bases, and supporting service access within agreed standards. Although the GSBPM definition is framed around external users and dissemination support, the work description strongly reflects an internal support function built around service navigation and response mechanisms. Evidence includes "HR A to Z index," "HR service standards," "HR contact list," "Corporate service providers," and "Wellness at Statistics Canada." These are classic support-enablement artifacts: indexes, standards, contacts, and service-provider references that help users find answers and obtain services efficiently. That makes 7.5 materially relevant as an analogue for structured support provision, even though the work description does not explicitly mention dissemination users or microdata access. Future-state drivers reinforce this relevance. AI and Automation in Statistical Production is pertinent because 7.5 is expected to shift toward knowledge bases, searchable support content, and automated support channels; the work description already points to curated support resources such as an HR index and contact list, which are the kinds of assets that become more important in automated or self-service support models. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure also matters because self-serve platforms and easier access to systems/resources are central future themes, and the work description suggests the role helps staff navigate those supports. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases the importance of triaged, reusable support content and service standards, which aligns with the listed HR service standards and support references. The role appears to fulfill an internal user-support need by organizing and surfacing support information and service pathways for staff in a collection-support environment.

This subprocess has low but plausible relevance because it gathers feedback, staff suggestions, service indicators, and other evidence used for evaluation and continuous improvement. The work description does not explicitly mention evaluation, reporting, or quality indicators, so relevance cannot be rated higher. However, several listed activities imply structures through which workforce feedback, service issues, and organizational support information may be gathered or organized: "HR committees," "HR service standards," "Wellness at Statistics Canada," and "Corporate service providers." These suggest exposure to staff concerns, service performance expectations, and support-system interactions that could generate evaluation inputs about workforce readiness and support effectiveness. Future-state drivers make this more relevant indirectly. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is important because modernization increases the value of staff feedback, well-being signals, and training/readiness evidence; the work description's wellness and HR committee references align with those kinds of inputs. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment also increase the importance of evidence on service performance and workforce strain, which HR standards and support channels may help surface. Still, because the work description does not explicitly state that the role compiles indicators, produces evaluation material, or feeds formal evaluation processes, this remains a low-relevance connection.

This subprocess is only weakly implicated. It concerns analyzing evaluation inputs, comparing results to expectations, and producing evaluation reports or dashboards with recommendations. The work description contains no explicit evidence of evaluation analysis, reporting, benchmarking, or recommendation-making. However, the listed activities such as "HR service standards," "HR committees," and "Wellness at Statistics Canada" suggest some proximity to organizational performance, staff support, and service-quality concerns that could inform evaluation discussions in a broader sense. The role may therefore be affected by evaluation findings about workforce support, service standards, or readiness, even if it does not conduct the evaluation itself. Future-state drivers contribute indirectly. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity makes workforce readiness, employee well-being, and support effectiveness more central evaluation dimensions, and the work description clearly touches those areas. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment also raises the importance of assessing support models and service trade-offs. But because there is no direct evidence that this position analyzes evaluation inputs or produces evaluation outputs, the connection should remain low.

This subprocess has low relevance because it involves decision-making authority to agree action plans based on evaluation findings and to establish monitoring mechanisms. The work description does not explicitly mention planning, governance decisions, or formal action-plan ownership. However, the position title includes "Manager," and the listed activities include "HR committees," "HR service standards," "Wellness at Statistics Canada," and "Corporate service providers," which suggest some participation in organizational coordination and support structures where workforce-related actions could be discussed or implemented. That creates a plausible but limited connection to action planning around staff support, service standards, or wellness in a collection-support environment. Future-state drivers strengthen the indirect relevance. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is especially pertinent because action plans under modernization increasingly involve training, support through transitions, leadership accountability, and workforce sustainability; the work description is centered on those support domains. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline also matter because action plans are expected to be clearer, more accountable, and more time-bound, which could affect how this role participates in committees or service coordination. Still, absent explicit evidence of approving or owning action plans, the subprocess should remain low relevance.

Positions.Position Title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer

implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it concerns identifying what statistics and statistical capabilities are needed in response to user requests, environmental change, and evolving practices. The work description shows the position regularly assesses changes in the subject area and determines implications for program content, methods, procedures and dissemination, which is a direct contribution to identifying emerging needs even if the role is more development-oriented than policy-approval oriented. The capability involved is subject-matter scanning and translating change into statistical system implications. Evidence includes: "Identifies and assesses changes and developments in the subject area; determines the impact on program subject-matter content and the implication for statistical methods and procedures and the dissemination of program results" and "Assesses changes in the subject area and determines the need to modify or replace processing systems and applications." Future-state drivers increase the importance of this role because Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will force sharper triage of which needs can be pursued, with fewer staff and more pressure to use AI, automation, machine learning and new tools and methods. That means this position's change-assessment work will increasingly need to distinguish between needs that justify system change and those that can be met through more standardized or lower-cost approaches.

This subprocess is relevant because it sets output objectives in light of user needs, quality, confidentiality and available resources. The position contributes by discussing subject-matter content requirements with managers, clients and specialists, translating requirements into specifications, and determining implications for dissemination of program results. The capability involved is converting user and program requirements into feasible output and system objectives. Evidence includes: "Discusses program subject-matter content requirements with operations managers, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others"; "Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development"; and "determines the impact on program subject-matter content and the implication for statistical methods and procedures and the dissemination of program results." Future changes are driven by Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. These drivers will tighten trade-offs among scope, timeliness and quality, and scarce resources will focus on highest-value outcomes. For this role, that means stronger pressure to design or modify processing systems and dissemination supports only for prioritized outputs, with clearer accountability and more explicit trade-offs in project plans, priorities and target dates.

This subprocess is relevant because it assesses whether available data sources and supporting ICT arrangements can meet requirements. The work description does not explicitly assign source acquisition responsibility, but it does assign responsibility for analyzing manipulation, storage and retrieval methods, conducting feasibility studies on software and systems, identifying sources of information for development and operations, and ensuring legislative and confidentiality compliance for data handling. The capability involved is assessing whether data and supporting systems are suitable for statistical use and operationalization. Evidence includes: "Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada related to the area of expertise in order to identify and select sources of information for development and operations"; "Conducts feasibility studies concerning new system and product requirements by examining existing, proposed or new software programs and systems to determine their feasibility and adaptability to the needs of the statistical program"; and "Knowledge of the Statistics and Privacy Acts is particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information." Future-state drivers materially increase the impact on this role. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production mean more non-survey, linked and geospatial sources must be assessed for fit with processing systems. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access make storage, secure access, privacy and platform compatibility core suitability criteria. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the importance of assessing metadata completeness and interoperability. As a result, this role's existing feasibility, database and system assessment work will increasingly be shaped by source diversity, secure platform requirements, and metadata-rich integration needs.

This subprocess is relevant because it documents options, costs, benefits, resources, risks and implementation plans for new or modified statistical business processes. The position is not explicitly described as writing formal business cases, but it clearly performs several constituent activities: assessing current methods and systems, identifying inefficiencies and replacement needs, planning projects, budgeting, estimating costs, allocating funds, and leading implementation teams. The capability involved is assembling operational justification for system change. Evidence includes: "Analyzes current manipulation, storage and retrieval methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modification or replacement"; "Plans and budgets for special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs"; "Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates"; and "establishes project plans, priorities and target dates." Future-state drivers make this more consequential. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will require clearer milestones, implementation readiness and go/no-go discipline. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will raise the threshold for approval and require explicit trade-offs, savings and affordability. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity mean proposals will increasingly need to justify platform alignment, reuse, training and supportability. This role's project planning, costing and system-replacement analysis therefore materially support this subprocess now and will be more tightly governed in future.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it covers detailed design of outputs, products, services and dissemination-related systems and procedures. The position title itself includes dissemination development, and the work description explicitly links system development to dissemination of program results. The capability involved is designing and implementing systems and specifications that support statistical outputs and dissemination while respecting standards, confidentiality and user needs. Evidence includes: "Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer"; "Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data"; "Identifies and assesses changes and developments in the subject area; determines the impact on ... the dissemination of program results"; and "Writes analytical reports and articles ... included into publications." Future-state drivers will materially reshape this work. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will require stronger secure-by-design dissemination controls. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will push outputs toward platform-based, metadata-rich, searchable and reusable products. Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will favour reusable dissemination components over bespoke builds. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require products and procedures that staff can operate and explain using modern digital tools. This role is directly implicated because it develops the systems and specifications that enable those outputs and dissemination changes.

This subprocess is relevant at a limited level because it defines variables, derived variables, units and classifications. The work description shows the position develops subject-matter concepts and definitions and proposes new statistical methods and approaches, which can influence variable and concept design, but it does not explicitly assign formal variable-design responsibility. The capability involved is subject-matter conceptual development that informs downstream variable structures. Evidence includes: "Develops subject-matter concepts and definitions; proposes new statistical methods, techniques and approaches or the modification of existing techniques and approaches" and "Provides guidance ... on subject-matter concepts and definitions." Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase pressure for harmonized concepts, richer metadata and derived variables from linked and alternative sources. This role may therefore be affected where subject-matter concepts must be translated into system specifications, but the connection is limited compared with processing and workflow design responsibilities.

This subprocess has limited relevance. The work description does not assign direct responsibility for collection instrument or fieldwork design. However, the role does discuss requirements with operations managers, clients and service providers, participates on departmental teams, and translates subject-matter requirements into system specifications, which can indirectly support collection design where collection choices affect processing systems. Evidence includes: "Discusses program subject-matter content requirements with operations managers ... clients, service providers" and "develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development." Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may indirectly affect this role because collection is becoming more digital, source-based and integrated with downstream production. Still, the work description is centered on processing, databases, retrieval and dissemination rather than collection design itself, so relevance remains low.

This is one of the most directly relevant subprocesses. It covers design of methodology and specifications for coding, editing, imputation, integration, validation, estimation and disclosure-control methods used in processing and analysis. The work description directly assigns system analysis and design, testing specifications, database development, manipulation/storage/retrieval methods analysis, and development of new statistical methods and approaches. The capability involved is designing the processing architecture and methodological specifications that underpin statistical production. Evidence includes: "Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data"; "Designs specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases"; "Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing ... to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems"; and "Develops subject-matter concepts and definitions; proposes new statistical methods, techniques and approaches." Future-state drivers strongly intensify this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push processing design toward AI-enabled coding, automated validation, streamlined workflows and reduced manual intervention. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will require more integration and validation across heterogeneous sources. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will require modular, metadata-aware, orchestratable processing steps. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will embed secure platform and disclosure considerations into processing design. The role is central because it already designs and implements the processing systems these drivers are transforming.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it determines the end-to-end workflow from collection to dissemination, reuse of systems and databases, and staff interaction with systems. The work description directly covers development and implementation of processing systems, database maintenance and development, project planning, procedural modification, and leadership of teams implementing new or modified statistical processing systems. The capability involved is end-to-end production-system and workflow design, including operational roles and sequencing. Evidence includes: "Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems"; "Provides subject matter advice and direction to users, negotiates procedural modifications and establishes project plans, priorities and target dates"; "Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate and manage on-going operational activities and/or special projects"; and "Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing ... to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems." Future-state drivers make this a major transformation area. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production all point toward reusable, orchestrated, automated, metadata-driven workflows with clearer handoffs and fewer manual steps. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will also reshape responsibilities, approvals, staffing models and training needs. This role is directly implicated because it already leads system implementation, negotiates procedures, and plans the work that these drivers will redesign.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is highly relevant because it concerns building or reusing components needed for Process and Analyse phases. The work description directly states that the position develops processing systems and applications, implements enhancements or modifications, designs testing specifications, and maintains and develops databases. The capability involved is technical development and reuse of processing components and supporting services. Evidence includes: "Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data"; "Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications"; "Designs specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases"; and "Knowledge of high level programming languages, utility programs or statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data." Future-state drivers strongly affect this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase demand for reusable automated coding, validation, transformation and analytical components. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will shift builds toward shared enterprise services, open-source tools, interoperability and governed reuse. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will require components with standardized interfaces for automated end-to-end flows. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase pressure for reusable components that reduce manual effort and can be maintained by a reskilled workforce. This role directly fulfills that need through system and application development.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it configures workflows, systems and transformations from collection through dissemination based on the production workflow design. The work description shows the position establishes project plans, priorities and target dates, negotiates procedural modifications, leads implementation teams, and manages development and implementation of statistical processing systems. The capability involved is operational configuration and tailoring of workflows and systems for production use. Evidence includes: "negotiates procedural modifications and establishes project plans, priorities and target dates"; "Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems"; and "plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities." Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will make workflow configuration more automation-first, standardized and exception-based. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline and Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline will tighten milestone management, approvals and reuse expectations. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will shift staff roles toward supervision and exception handling. This role is directly relevant because it already configures the practical implementation path through project planning, procedural change and system rollout.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it covers testing assembled and configured services and workflows, including technical testing, sign-off, secure channels and fit-for-use assessment. The work description explicitly assigns design of testing specifications and knowledge of system design and testing, and the role leads implementation of new or modified processing systems. The capability involved is specifying, coordinating and supporting technical and operational testing of production systems. Evidence includes: "Designs specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases"; "Knowledge of system analysis and design ... to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems"; and "Leads project teams ... in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems." Future-state drivers increase both scope and rigor of testing. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production require more end-to-end, automated and model-aware testing. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access add platform, access-control and secure transmission testing. Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development increases interoperability and validation demands. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline compresses testing windows while increasing readiness discipline. This role is materially connected because it defines testing specifications and supports implementation readiness.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes documentation, user manuals, training users, and moving components into production. The work description does not explicitly mention writing manuals or delivering formal training, but it does show the role provides subject-matter advice and direction to users, provides guidance to professionals, leads implementation teams, and manages operational rollout of new or modified systems. The capability involved is operational readiness and user enablement for production systems. Evidence includes: "Provides subject matter advice and direction to users"; "Provides guidance to other STC professionals"; and "Leads project teams ... in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems." Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will increase the need for training, documentation, supportability and controlled deployment. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will also tighten cutover readiness. This role is therefore meaningfully involved in finalization, though less explicitly than in design, build and testing.

This subprocess has limited relevance. The work description does not assign direct collection setup responsibility. However, because the role develops processing systems, liaises with operations managers and service providers, and translates subject-matter requirements into system specifications, it may be indirectly involved where collection setup depends on downstream processing interfaces or system readiness. Evidence includes: "Discusses program subject-matter content requirements with operations managers ... service providers" and "develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development." Future-state drivers such as Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may increase indirect effects on this role because collection setup is becoming more digital and integrated with processing systems. Still, the work description does not show direct responsibility for collection readiness, so relevance remains low.

This subprocess is only plausibly connected. It concerns loading collected data and metadata into electronic environments, conversion, archiving and pseudonymisation. The role's responsibilities for manipulation, storage and retrieval systems, databases, and testing specifications suggest indirect involvement in the environments into which collected data are loaded, but not explicit ownership of collection finalization. Evidence includes: "Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data" and "Designs specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases." Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure may increase the degree to which collection handoff is embedded in the systems this role develops. Even so, the work description does not directly assign collection-finalization duties.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it integrates data from one or more sources, harmonises figures, performs linkage and creates consolidated datasets. The work description directly covers manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data, database development, analysis of methods and procedures, feasibility studies for systems, and resolving technical problems in data handling. The capability involved is designing and implementing the systems and methods that support multi-source integration and harmonisation. Evidence includes: "Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data"; "Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data"; "Identifies and evaluates problems in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical information"; and "Analyzes current manipulation, storage and retrieval methods and procedures." Future-state drivers make this one of the most transformed areas. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production make integration of administrative, alternative, linked and geospatial data central. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will embed integration in automated end-to-end flows. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will require standardized metadata for interoperability. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will shape secure linkage environments, de-identification and access controls. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase reliance on integrated existing sources instead of labour-intensive collection. This role is directly implicated because its core work is building and improving the systems used to manipulate, store, retrieve and operationalize statistical data.

This subprocess is relevant because it classifies and codes input data using automated or manual routines. The work description does not explicitly mention coding operations, but it does assign development of processing systems and applications, use of programming languages and statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data, and development of subject-matter concepts and definitions. The capability involved is enabling and improving coding processes through system development and subject-matter standards. Evidence includes: "Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data"; "Knowledge of high level programming languages, utility programs or statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data"; and "Develops subject-matter concepts and definitions." Future-state drivers make this more important. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production directly target AI-enabled automated coding, while Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases pressure to reduce clerical coding effort. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability and Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increase the need for harmonized classifications across diverse sources. This role is materially connected because it develops the processing systems and subject-matter structures that coding routines depend on, even if it is not explicitly described as performing coding itself.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it detects errors, discrepancies, outliers, duplicates and other quality issues before correction. The work description directly includes designing testing specifications for data, identifying and evaluating problems in manipulation/storage/retrieval, resolving conceptual and technical problems, and analyzing current methods and procedures for relevance and replacement. The capability involved is designing and supporting validation controls and quality checks within processing systems. Evidence includes: "Designs specifications for the testing of data"; "Identifies and evaluates problems in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical information to provide solutions"; and "Analyzes current manipulation, storage and retrieval methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy." Future-state drivers strongly affect this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push validation toward automated anomaly detection, rule-based checks and exception handling. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increases validation complexity across heterogeneous and linked sources. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration embeds validation checkpoints in automated workflows. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases validation of metadata completeness and consistency. This role is directly relevant because it designs the systems, specifications and problem-resolution approaches that make validation operational.

This subprocess is relevant because it changes incorrect, missing or unreliable data values and produces metadata on those changes. The work description does not explicitly assign editing or imputation, but it does assign development of processing systems, proposal of new statistical methods and approaches, implementation of system enhancements, and resolution of technical problems in data manipulation. The capability involved is enabling and improving rule-based or model-based correction processes through system and method development. Evidence includes: "Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data"; "Develops subject-matter concepts and definitions; proposes new statistical methods, techniques and approaches"; and "Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications." Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase automation and model-assisted editing/imputation. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will require source-prioritized correction logic. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the importance of recording edit and imputation metadata. This role is materially connected because it develops the processing systems and methods that would operationalize these functions, though the work description does not explicitly state direct execution of editing/imputation.

This subprocess is relevant because it derives variables and units not directly collected but needed for outputs. The work description shows the role develops subject-matter concepts and definitions, proposes new statistical methods and approaches, and develops systems used to manipulate data. The capability involved is creating the conceptual and technical basis for derived variables and derived structures in production systems. Evidence includes: "Develops subject-matter concepts and definitions; proposes new statistical methods, techniques and approaches" and "Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data." Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase reliance on derived variables from linked, administrative and geospatial sources. Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will require correct sequencing of derivations in automated workflows, while Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will require clearer derivation lineage. This role is relevant because it combines subject-matter method development with processing-system development, though the work description does not explicitly state direct derivation responsibility.

This subprocess has limited relevance. The work description refers broadly to proposing new statistical methods and improving surveys and data, which could indirectly affect weighting methodology, but it does not explicitly mention weighting, calibration or non-response adjustment. Evidence is limited to general statements such as "proposes new statistical methods, techniques and approaches" and "conducts studies and analytical projects to improve existing surveys and data." Future-state drivers indicate weighting will evolve with adaptive collection and administrative auxiliaries, but the supplied work description does not provide enough evidence that this position materially performs or manages weighting work. Relevance is therefore low.

This subprocess has plausible but limited relevance. The role writes analytical reports and articles on survey interpretation and methodology and provides subject-matter interpretation to media, which implies use of aggregated outputs, but the work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for calculating aggregates. Evidence includes: "Writes analytical reports and articles on the interpretation of surveys, statistical applications or project findings" and "Provides subject-matter interpretation and analysis ... on the results of surveys or projects." Future-state drivers such as Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may affect the kinds of aggregates produced, but the direct connection in the work description is weak.

This subprocess is relevant because it assembles the results of processing into datasets used as input to analysis. The work description directly concerns systems and applications for manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data, database maintenance and development, and implementation of processing-system enhancements. The capability involved is preparing and managing the technical environments and workflows that produce analysis-ready datasets. Evidence includes: "Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data"; "Designs specifications for ... the maintenance and development of databases"; and "Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications." Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will make final data files more standardized, metadata-rich, versioned and automatically handed off to analysis. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will also increase pressure for timely preliminary and final files. This role is materially connected because it develops the systems and databases that support those finalization and handoff functions.

This subprocess is relevant because it transforms processed data into statistical outputs and prepares methodological notes. The work description shows the role writes analytical reports and articles for publications, explains methodology, and provides interpretation of survey and project results. The capability involved is preparing analytical and methodological content that supports draft outputs. Evidence includes: "Writes analytical reports and articles on the interpretation of surveys, statistical applications or project findings and the methodology used. These reports and articles are to be reviewed by program managers and included into publications" and "Provides subject-matter interpretation and analysis ... on the results of surveys or projects." Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the need for methodological explanation, metadata-rich output packages, and clearer communication of AI- or model-based methods. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment may also increase templating and automation of recurring outputs. This role is materially connected through its analytical writing and methodological explanation responsibilities.

This subprocess is relevant because it validates outputs against expectations, prior cycles, metadata and auxiliary information. The work description shows the role identifies and assesses changes and impacts on dissemination, writes analytical reports on interpretation and methodology, and provides subject-matter interpretation of survey results. It also requires knowledge of current or emerging issues to identify conflicts, duplication and gaps. The capability involved is applying subject-matter intelligence and methodological understanding to assess whether outputs make sense. Evidence includes: "Knowledge of current or emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and resolve existing and potential subject-matter conflicts, duplication and gaps"; "Writes analytical reports and articles on the interpretation of surveys"; and "Provides subject-matter interpretation and analysis ... on the results of surveys or projects." Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will make output validation more complex because outputs may reflect linked, administrative and model-based methods. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the importance of validating metadata, quality indicators and automated outputs. This role is relevant because it combines subject-matter expertise with methodological interpretation, though the work description does not explicitly assign formal output-validation sign-off.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it interprets outputs, explains their meaning and assesses them against expectations. The work description directly assigns interpretation of surveys and statistical applications, writing analytical reports and articles for publication, providing subject-matter interpretation to media, and advising clients and professionals on concepts, methods, techniques and results. The capability involved is analytical interpretation and communication of statistical outputs and methods. Evidence includes: "Writes analytical reports and articles on the interpretation of surveys, statistical applications or project findings and the methodology used"; "Provides subject-matter interpretation and analysis to media representatives on the results of surveys or projects, and the interpretation of statistical data"; and "Exchanges information and provides advice ... on subject-matter concepts and definitions, statistical survey methods and techniques." Future-state drivers will materially change this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will require clearer explanation of outputs produced through automated, linked or model-based methods. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will require analysts to explain source substitution, linkage effects and comparability issues. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need for analytical expertise and clear communication using new tools. This role is directly implicated because interpretation and explanation are explicit core duties.

This subprocess is relevant because it ensures outputs and stored data do not breach confidentiality rules. The work description explicitly emphasizes knowledge of the Statistics Act, Privacy Act and related legislation, and responsibility to ensure that neither the incumbent nor subordinates release identifying information without consent. The capability involved is applying confidentiality and legislative requirements to data handling and release-related activities. Evidence includes: "Knowledge of the Statistics and Privacy Acts is particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent." Future-state drivers make this more significant. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure increase the importance of secure access, privacy-preserving controls and controlled use environments. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion raises re-identification risks in linked and richer datasets. Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development increases the need for embedded governance and standard controls. The role is materially connected because confidentiality compliance is explicitly part of its contextual knowledge and operational responsibility, even though the work description does not explicitly mention statistical disclosure-control techniques.

This subprocess is relevant because it completes consistency checks, caveats, commentary, technical notes, briefings and approval preparation for release. The work description shows the role writes analytical reports and methodological articles for publication, provides interpretation to media and clients, and explains technical concepts in common terminology. The capability involved is preparing supporting analytical and technical material that makes outputs fit for use. Evidence includes: "Writes analytical reports and articles ... included into publications"; "Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional program content and applications"; and "Provides subject-matter interpretation and analysis to media representatives." Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will increase the need for caveats, technical notes, uncertainty communication and disciplined release preparation under tighter timelines. Governance and prioritization will also sharpen approval and trade-off decisions. This role is materially connected through its analytical writing, explanation and publication-support responsibilities.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it formats, loads and links data and metadata into systems used for dissemination. The work description directly covers development of processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data, database maintenance and development, and implementation of system enhancements. The capability involved is maintaining and improving the technical systems that hold dissemination-ready data and metadata. Evidence includes: "Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data"; "Designs specifications for ... the maintenance and development of databases"; and "Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications."
