Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and AI and Automation in Statistical Production will make output-system updates more automated, metadata-linked, platform-based and standardized. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will also strengthen controls on dissemination stores. This role is directly implicated because it develops and modifies the systems and databases that support dissemination readiness.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it assembles dissemination products such as publications, websites, tables, maps and downloadable files. The position title explicitly includes dissemination development, and the work description includes writing analytical reports and articles for publications, explaining technical concepts for program content and applications, and providing interpretation used for dissemination to the public. The capability involved is supporting the technical and analytical production of dissemination products. Evidence includes: "Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer"; "Writes analytical reports and articles ... included into publications"; "Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts ... to explain and clarify divisional program content and applications"; and "Provides subject-matter interpretation and analysis to media representatives ... disseminated to the Canadian population." Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will push dissemination products toward reusable, metadata-rich, digital and partially automated forms. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will require richer quality statements and methodological explanation for mixed-source and model-based outputs. This role is directly relevant because dissemination development and publication-support activities are explicit in the work description.

This subprocess has limited relevance. The work description supports dissemination through analytical reports, publications and media interpretation, but it does not explicitly assign release scheduling, embargo management, subscriber provision or researcher-access administration. Evidence includes publication and media-facing duties, but not release operations. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access may indirectly affect this role through tighter release coordination and confidentiality expectations, especially where the incumbent contributes briefings or explanatory material. However, the supplied information does not support a stronger connection.

This subprocess is relevant because it records and responds to user queries and supports partner organizations involved in dissemination. The work description explicitly states that the position provides subject-matter advice and direction to users, liaises with clients and service providers, exchanges information with professionals from other agencies, and provides guidance to other Statistics Canada professionals. The capability involved is user-facing subject-matter and technical support related to statistical concepts, methods, applications and results. Evidence includes: "Provides subject matter advice and direction to users"; "Discusses program subject-matter content requirements with ... clients, service providers and others"; "Exchanges information and provides advice to professionals from the private sector or from other statistical agencies abroad"; and "Provides guidance to other STC professionals." Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will change support models toward more self-service, knowledge-base and AI-assisted support, while Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will increase the importance of controlled responses for restricted-access services. This role is materially connected because user advice and guidance are explicit responsibilities.

This subprocess is relevant because it gathers feedback, process metadata, system metrics and staff suggestions for evaluation. The work description shows the role analyzes current methods and procedures, conducts feasibility studies, identifies problems, participates on teams and working groups, and leads project teams, all of which generate operational evidence and staff feedback relevant to evaluation. The capability involved is producing and interpreting operational evidence about system performance and improvement needs. Evidence includes: "Analyzes current manipulation, storage and retrieval methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy"; "Conducts feasibility studies concerning new system and product requirements"; "Identifies and evaluates problems"; and "Participates as a subject area representative on teams and working groups throughout the department." Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the volume of system metrics, paradata and workflow telemetry relevant to this role's systems work. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will also increase the importance of capturing evidence on workload, adoption and sustainability. The role is therefore meaningfully connected as a producer and interpreter of evaluation inputs.

This subprocess is relevant because it analyzes evaluation inputs, compares them to expectations and recommends changes. The work description directly includes analyzing current methods and procedures for relevance, determining need for modification or replacement, conducting feasibility studies, and conducting studies and analytical projects to improve surveys and data. The capability involved is evaluative analysis of systems, methods and operational performance. Evidence includes: "Analyzes current manipulation, storage and retrieval methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modification or replacement"; "Conducts feasibility studies"; and "Plans and implements the review and development of new subject-matter methods, concepts and definitions and conducts studies and analytical projects to improve existing surveys and data." Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make evaluation more dashboard-driven and more focused on efficiency, quality, timeliness, workforce readiness and sustainability. Governance and prioritization will also increase the importance of evidence-based recommendations. This role is materially connected because evaluative analysis and improvement recommendation are explicit parts of the job.

This subprocess is relevant because it brings together decision-making authority to agree actions based on evaluation findings and monitor their impact. The work description shows the role leads project teams or work units, determines goals, priorities and milestones, plans and schedules work, resolves conflicting priorities, negotiates procedural modifications, establishes project plans and target dates, and allocates project funds within budget. The capability involved is turning analysis and evaluation into concrete implementation plans and monitored actions. Evidence includes: "Leads project teams or work units. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work"; "negotiates procedural modifications and establishes project plans, priorities and target dates"; and "Plans and budgets for special projects." Future-state drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make action planning more disciplined, milestone-based, resource-constrained and dependent on clear ownership and workforce sequencing. This role is materially connected because it already converts identified needs and problems into planned, budgeted implementation actions.

Positions.Branch/Division: Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division

implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is directly relevant because it concerns gathering evaluation material such as user feedback, process metadata, system metrics, staff suggestions, and reports against prior action plans for use in evaluation. The position title is explicitly "Junior Evaluation Officer" in the "Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division," which is strong evidence that the role contributes to evaluation functions rather than production, collection, processing, or dissemination operations. The listed key activities—"HR service standards," "Wellness at Statistics Canada," "HR committees," "HR contact list," "Corporate service providers," and "HR A to Z index"—indicate work centered on internal corporate services and organizational supports, which are plausible sources of evaluation inputs about service performance, user needs, and organizational functioning. Future-state drivers make this subprocess even more important. Under AI and Automation in Statistical Production, evaluation input gathering is expected to rely more on continuous monitoring, documentation, and system metrics; under Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, milestone and schedule evidence become more central; under Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, evidence on productivity, service trade-offs, and workforce impacts becomes more necessary; and under Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, staff feedback, training outcomes, well-being, and transition impacts become important evaluation inputs. Those drivers align especially well with the work description's emphasis on HR services and wellness-related topics. The role is therefore materially connected to collecting and organizing evidence about internal services, workforce supports, and organizational conditions that can feed evaluation.

This subprocess is directly implicated because it covers analysing evaluation inputs, comparing them to expected results, synthesising findings into evaluation reports or dashboards, identifying quality or performance issues, and making recommendations. The work description provides direct organizational evidence: the incumbent is a "Junior Evaluation Officer" in the "Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division." That is a direct match to the evaluation function described in this subprocess. The key activities suggest likely subject matter areas for evaluation or evaluative support in the corporate domain, including "HR service standards," "Wellness at Statistics Canada," "HR committees," and "Corporate service providers." These are consistent with evaluating internal services, organizational supports, and performance against standards. Future-state drivers reinforce the importance of this subprocess for the role. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline increases the need for evidence-based assessment and explicit recommendations; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline shifts evaluation toward milestone-based and operational performance assessment; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases demand for evaluation of savings, productivity, service impacts, and sustainability under reduced staffing; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity makes workforce readiness, training, leadership effectiveness, employee well-being, and cultural change core evaluation dimensions. Those workforce implications are especially relevant given the work description's explicit references to HR and wellness. AI and automation, enterprise platforms, and integrated pipelines also imply richer dashboards and metrics for evaluators to assess over time. Based on the supplied evidence, this role is not merely adjacent to evaluation—it is explicitly part of the evaluation function and therefore highly relevant to conducting evaluations now and under future transformation.

This subprocess is relevant because it brings together decision-making authority to agree an action plan based on evaluation findings and includes monitoring mechanisms for future iterations. The work description does not state that the Junior Evaluation Officer has approval authority, so the role should not be interpreted as owning final decisions. However, the role is still materially connected because evaluation staff commonly support the transition from findings to actionable recommendations, and the work description places the position in the "Evaluation Division." The listed activities—particularly "HR service standards," "Wellness at Statistics Canada," "HR committees," and "Corporate service providers"—suggest that the role may contribute evaluative evidence and recommendations in internal corporate-service areas where action plans, service improvements, or committee follow-up could arise. Future-state drivers increase the significance of this connection. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline emphasizes accountability, prioritization, and transparent trade-offs in deciding which actions proceed; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline requires milestone-based, time-bound action planning; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment pushes action plans toward simplification, prioritization, and efficiency measures; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity makes leadership ownership, realistic sequencing, training, and workforce sustainability central to improvement planning. These drivers are especially pertinent where evaluation findings concern HR services, wellness, and internal supports. Because the work description does not explicitly assign decision authority, the relevance is medium rather than high, but the role is still meaningfully connected through evaluative recommendations and support to action planning.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns assessing whether available data sources, related ICT resources, legal constraints, and access conditions are suitable for statistical use. The position regularly works with complex, high-impact statistical data and integrates data from multiple sources, including 'financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses,' and must ensure continuity, compatibility, confidentiality, and security. Evidence includes: 'Investigates requirements for statistical information and analysis, defines the nature and scope of special studies, data requirements, and decides the methods and approaches to be used to satisfy complex data requirements'; 'integrate conceptually different data from other programs'; and knowledge of 'data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements' and of the 'Statistics Act' and privacy/confidentiality requirements. These responsibilities align with assessing source suitability, restrictions on use, and operational feasibility. Future-state drivers increase the importance of this work: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will expand the range of candidate sources and increase the need to assess linkage readiness, metadata quality, continuity, and interoperability; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will intensify scrutiny of privacy, authorizations, secure access, and legal conditions; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will make platform fit, centralized repositories, and secure ingestion tooling more central; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make source metadata quality and discoverability more important. Workforce implications point to the need for a skilled and adaptable workforce and tools/training for assessing non-survey sources, which would materially affect this role's source assessment and integration responsibilities.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position develops and maintains dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and high-impact statistical programs. The subprocess covers detailed design of outputs, products, services, and dissemination-related systems and procedures. Evidence from the work description is explicit: 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases'; 'Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination'; and 'Provides expert advice and guidance ... on statistical program results, dissemination methods, concepts, and techniques applied.' The capability involved is designing dissemination-ready outputs, ensuring standards, usability, and policy compliance, and coordinating with multiple partners to deliver them. Future drivers will reshape this work: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will require outputs to be more metadata-rich, standardized, and discoverable; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will strengthen confidentiality-by-design and secure access considerations for outputs; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will push output design toward platform-based, reusable digital dissemination services; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase pressure for standardized, lower-cost, reusable dissemination products; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require staff to operate and explain outputs using newer digital tools while maintaining accessibility and clear communication.

This subprocess is one of the strongest matches because the position designs and improves processing, validation, integration, and quality-assurance methods for high-impact statistical outputs. The subprocess covers specification of routines and rules for coding, editing, imputation, integration, validation, and estimation. Evidence includes: 'Innovates and implements the design, evaluation, and applications for the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of high-impact statistical data'; 'Operationalizes specialized conceptual and measurement frameworks in the development of production, validation and dissemination systems, processes and databases'; 'Develops and implements quality-assurance processes for high-impact statistical outputs'; 'Research and validation is required to evaluate the effectiveness of the processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications, to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria'; and 'Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs.' The capability involved is methodological and systems design for processing and validation, including multi-source integration and quality control. Future-state drivers are highly material here: AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will shift design toward automated coding, validation, editing, and integrated pipelines; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase the need for source-specific integration and validation rules; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will require methods to be designed as orchestratable, reusable pipeline steps; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata an operational input to processing design; Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will push toward reusable validation and processing modules; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase pressure to replace manual effort with automated, sustainable methods; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require stronger analytical, digital, and governance capability in method design.

This subprocess is directly implicated because the position designs, improves, and coordinates end-to-end production systems, databases, and workflows for ongoing statistical production, validation, and dissemination. Evidence is extensive: 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes'; 'Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications'; 'Evaluates alternatives and develops and applies new strategies to maintain and improve operational systems, processes and databases'; 'Occasionally leads project teams and undertakes complex technical projects in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems'; and 'Establishes and coordinates schedules for the production, validation and dissemination of regular statistical outputs across multiple production teams.' The subprocess explicitly includes ensuring processes fit together efficiently, reusing existing services and databases where possible, and considering staff interaction and responsibilities. That matches the role's coordination of multiple divisional and external partners, schedule management, and system/process design. Future drivers will strongly reshape this work: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development all point toward enterprise workflows, reusable services, orchestration, and platform-based production; AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will reduce manual intervention and embed AI and automation into workflows; Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will increase pressure for clearer handoffs, accountabilities, milestone-driven workflows, and leaner designs; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will reinforce reuse, fewer handoffs, and workflows sustainable with fewer staff; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is especially relevant because this subprocess explicitly considers how staff interact with systems and who is responsible for what and when.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because the position not only designs but also develops and implements processing systems, databases, and technical solutions used in production. Evidence includes: 'Innovates and implements the design, evaluation, and applications for the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of high-impact statistical data'; 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information'; 'Develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs'; and 'Occasionally leads project teams and undertakes complex technical projects in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' The capability involved is building or adapting processing, transformation, validation, and database components that support Process and Analyse phases. Future-state drivers indicate that this work will increasingly involve reusable enterprise components, AI-enabled coding and validation services, linkage and harmonization services, workflow tools, and metadata services. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will push component development toward shared services and enterprise architecture compliance; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will require modular components with standardized interfaces; AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will expand AI-enabled and automated processing components; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase demand for linkage, transformation, and geospatial services; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will favour reuse over bespoke builds; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need for new programming, analytical, and open-source skills.

This subprocess is materially connected because the position coordinates and operationalizes production schedules, specifications, and multi-team workflows, even if the work description emphasizes design and implementation more than explicit workflow configuration tooling. Evidence includes: 'Establishes and coordinates schedules for the production, validation and dissemination of regular statistical outputs across multiple production teams'; 'Coordinates input and specifications from multiple partners to implement specialized solutions according to established production schedules'; and 'plans, organizes and functionally coordinates the work of multiple partners.' The capability involved is translating designed processes into operationally configured flows, handoffs, and schedules across collection-independent production stages. Future drivers make this more important: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will shift work toward automated handoffs, event-driven workflows, and exception handling; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will standardize workflow orchestration across enterprise platforms; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will increase emphasis on milestone-based sequencing and rapid implementation; Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline will constrain customization and reinforce standard configurations; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward simplified, lower-touch workflows; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require stronger workflow configuration and monitoring skills.

This subprocess is directly relevant because testing, acceptance criteria, and evaluation of processing systems are explicit responsibilities in the work description. Evidence includes: 'Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications'; 'Research and validation is required to evaluate the effectiveness of the processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications, to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria'; 'Interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations, and feasibility studies'; and 'Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs.' The capability involved is technical and operational testing of assembled services, workflows, parameters, and data handling to ensure coherent production performance. Future-state drivers intensify this work: AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the need to test automated routines, AI-enabled components, and integrated workflows; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access expand integration, performance, access-control, and secure transmission testing; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration increases the importance of end-to-end interaction testing, sequencing, and failure handling; Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development raises interoperability and validation demands; and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline compresses testing windows while increasing the need for disciplined sign-off.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance because the role works with production systems and external/internal partners involved in statistical processing and may support readiness for receiving data from suppliers and programs, but the work description does not indicate direct responsibility for collection operations or respondent-facing setup. Relevant evidence is indirect: the position 'Coordinates activities of multiple Statistics Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data' and has 'Knowledge of data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements.' This suggests some involvement in preparing systems and arrangements for incoming data, especially non-survey or administrative inputs. Future drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access could increase the role's exposure to secure intake, APIs, source-management readiness, and mixed-source operational setup, but based on the supplied work description this remains secondary rather than core.

This subprocess is only weakly implicated. The role works on loading, manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data and on databases used in production, which plausibly touches the handoff from collection into processing environments. Evidence includes 'manipulation, storage, and retrieval of high-impact statistical data' and 'Interprets the results of tests ... to produce data bases and data retrieval packages used for the production of integrated statistical information.' However, the work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for collection finalization, archiving collection instruments, or pseudonymisation at collection close. Future drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure may increase the automation and metadata-rich nature of collection-to-processing handoffs that affect this role's downstream systems, but the connection remains limited.

This subprocess is one of the clearest matches. The role directly integrates, harmonizes, and operationalizes data from multiple sources into production databases and outputs. Evidence includes: 'Integrates input from multiple economic subject matter areas to develop and maintain complex systems and frameworks for the ongoing production, validation and dissemination'; 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats ... Some studies may involve ... the integration of data from a wide variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Often, the data has been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts'; and 'Knowledge of other statistical programs ... is also required ... to integrate conceptually different data from other programs.' The capability involved is multi-source integration, harmonisation, prioritisation, and continuity/compatibility management for official statistics. Future-state drivers strongly amplify this work: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production make integration of administrative, alternative, linked, and geospatial data central; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access increases the importance of controlled linkage environments and de-identification; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure enables integration at scale through centralized repositories and cloud platforms; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration makes integration a core automated production backbone; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability improves interoperability and reuse; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases reliance on integrated existing sources instead of labour-intensive collection; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity raises the need for advanced integration skills and disciplined trade-off management.

This subprocess is relevant because the role reviews and approves classification and coding systems and works with data from multiple sources that must be translated into common concepts. Evidence includes: 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats or develops new ones to meet specific needs' and 'Often, the data has been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.' The capability involved is ensuring that source data are coded and classified consistently enough for production, integration, and dissemination. The work description does not emphasize routine coding operations, so relevance is medium rather than high. Future drivers will still materially affect this work: AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase automated coding and machine-assisted classification; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will increase the need to map source-system codes to statistical standards; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will reinforce common classifications and semantic consistency; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will favour automated coding over clerical effort; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require staff to supervise and validate AI-enabled coding workflows.

This subprocess is directly central to the role. The work description repeatedly emphasizes validation, quality assurance, inconsistency resolution, and review of processing parameters and outputs. Evidence includes: 'Develops and implements quality-assurance processes for high-impact statistical outputs'; 'Coordinates activities ... to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data'; 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies'; 'Communicates ... to resolve differences that can affect ... the quality of outputs'; and 'Research and validation is required to evaluate the effectiveness of the processing systems.' The capability involved is detecting and diagnosing errors, inconsistencies, and quality issues in complex, high-impact statistical production. Future-state drivers will significantly change this work: AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase automated anomaly detection and validation routines; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will introduce new validation challenges such as linkage errors, source drift, and structural inconsistencies; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will embed validation checkpoints into automated workflows; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata completeness and consistency part of validation; Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will increase the importance of reusable validation rules and governed controls; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will reduce capacity for manual review and increase reliance on automated exception handling; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require stronger analytical and digital skills for interpreting validation outputs.

This subprocess is relevant because the role devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies, modifies approaches and techniques as necessary, and develops quality-assurance and validation processes that support correction of problematic data. Evidence includes: 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies'; 'Recommends and executes solutions to resolve complex technical issues pertaining to data production and dissemination'; and 'reviews, and modifies approaches and techniques as necessary.' The work description does not explicitly mention imputation, so relevance is medium rather than high. The capability involved is establishing and applying correction logic and quality controls for problematic data in production systems. Future drivers suggest meaningful change: AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase model-assisted editing and automated correction; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will require source-aware correction rules and replacement from administrative values; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will embed editing as repeatable pipeline modules; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will increase the importance of standardized metadata on edits; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward automated editing with fewer staff; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require staff to oversee more advanced correction methods.

This subprocess is materially connected because the role develops databases for time-series information, operationalizes conceptual and measurement frameworks, and integrates conceptually different data into common statistical outputs. Evidence includes: 'Operationalizes specialized conceptual and measurement frameworks in the development of production, validation and dissemination systems, processes and databases'; 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information'; and the need to 'translate into common concepts' data collected for other purposes. These activities imply derivation of variables and possibly derived units needed for integrated outputs, even though the work description does not explicitly use the term 'derive.' Future drivers increase the importance of this work: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase reliance on derived variables and units from linked and administrative records; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will require explicit sequencing of derivation logic; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will require standardized documentation of derivations; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will encourage deriving variables from existing data rather than collecting them directly; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need for advanced analytical capability in model-based derivation.

This subprocess is relevant because the role brings together processed data into databases and retrieval packages used for integrated statistical information and ongoing dissemination. Evidence includes: 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases'; 'Interprets the results of tests ... to produce data bases and data retrieval packages used for the production of integrated statistical information'; and responsibilities for continuity, compatibility, and approval of processing parameters. The capability involved is assembling and preparing coherent, analysis- and dissemination-ready datasets and database outputs. Future drivers will materially affect this work: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will make finalised data files standardized pipeline outputs with automated handoffs; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will change how final datasets are stored, versioned, and accessed; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will require final datasets to be packaged as metadata-rich enterprise assets; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase complexity due to multi-source integrated files and iterative preliminary/final outputs; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will increase pressure for timely readiness of analysis-ready files; and AI and Automation in Statistical Production will increase automation, traceability, and standardized handoff patterns.

This subprocess is relevant because the role supports the transformation of processed data into dissemination-ready analytical database outputs and provides expert advice on results, dissemination methods, and explanatory materials. Evidence includes: 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases'; 'Provides expert advice and guidance ... on statistical program results, dissemination methods, concepts, and techniques applied'; and knowledge of preparing 'statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination.' The capability involved is preparing structured outputs and supporting methodological or explanatory material for users and internal decision-makers. Future drivers will affect this work through more metadata-rich outputs, stronger methodological explanation for AI- or model-based methods, and more automated output preparation. In particular, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward templated, faster, more transparent draft output preparation.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the role validates high-impact outputs, interprets preliminary results, explains variances, and ensures continuity and compatibility across programs. Evidence includes: 'Develops and implements quality-assurance processes for high-impact statistical outputs'; 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information, interprets preliminary results, reviews, and modifies approaches and techniques as necessary'; 'Knowledge of other statistical programs ... to explain variances'; and 'Communicates subject matter concepts ... to explain the results of studies.' The capability involved is validating outputs against expectations, quality standards, and domain understanding before dissemination. Future-state drivers will intensify this work: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the need to assess methodological breaks, linkage effects, and model-based outputs; AI and Automation in Statistical Production will require stronger scrutiny of automated outputs and associated metadata; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will embed validation into release flows; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata completeness part of validation; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward more risk-based validation with fewer staff; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need for advanced analytical judgment and disciplined release decisions.

This subprocess is relevant because the role provides expert advice on results, interprets preliminary results, explains variances, and communicates specialized concepts and technical definitions to internal and external clients. Evidence includes: 'Provides expert advice and guidance ... on statistical program results'; 'Interprets specialized information ... to present arguments and options to clients within and outside the department'; 'Develops data bases ... interprets preliminary results'; and knowledge needed 'to explain variances.' The capability involved is interpreting statistical meaning, explaining results, and communicating implications of methods and data choices. Future drivers will make this more complex: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will require explanation of mixed-source outputs, linkage effects, and methodological changes; AI and Automation in Statistical Production will require transparent explanation of AI-assisted production; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase demands on analytical expertise and communication skills.

This subprocess is relevant because the role has explicit responsibility to ensure confidentiality, privacy, and security requirements are applied in statistical production and dissemination. Evidence includes: 'Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security ... data quality)'; 'Knowledge of the Statistics Act ... and of the Statistic and Privacy Acts is particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent'; and work on dissemination outputs and databases. The capability involved is ensuring outputs and stored data comply with confidentiality rules and secure handling requirements. The work description does not explicitly mention suppression or perturbation methods, so relevance is medium. Future drivers make this more important: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access directly strengthens privacy and secure-access requirements; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increases re-identification risk in linked and geospatial data; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure expands access possibilities and therefore the need for robust controls; and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development increases the need for embedded governance and standard disclosure controls.

This subprocess is relevant because the role contributes to ensuring outputs are fit for dissemination, supported by explanatory materials, and coordinated across multiple partners and subject-matter areas. Evidence includes: 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs'; 'Provides expert advice and guidance ... on statistical program results, dissemination methods, concepts, and techniques'; 'Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices'; and coordination of multiple divisional partners for production, validation, and dissemination. The capability involved is preparing outputs for release with appropriate consistency, explanatory notes, and policy-compliant dissemination practices. Future drivers will affect this work through stronger metadata requirements, more caveats and technical notes for modern methods, tighter approval discipline, and streamlined release preparation under resource constraints. Relevant drivers include Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position is a database expert responsible for manipulation, storage, retrieval, and dissemination-oriented database outputs. Evidence includes: 'Innovates and implements the design, evaluation, and applications for the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of high-impact statistical data'; 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases'; and 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information.' The capability involved is formatting, loading, linking, and maintaining data and metadata in systems used for dissemination. Future-state drivers will materially reshape this work: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make metadata linkage and final metadata readiness checks central; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will automate downstream loading into dissemination systems; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will move output-system updates toward enterprise repositories and cloud-hosted platforms; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access will strengthen controlled updates and access; Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will favour standard loading services and interoperable output systems; and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase pressure for lower-touch automated updates.

This subprocess is directly implicated because the role develops dissemination outputs for analytical databases and has explicit knowledge and responsibilities related to tables, charts, explanatory notes, and dissemination practices. Evidence includes: 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases'; 'Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination'; and communication responsibilities involving results, dissemination methods, and technical explanations. The capability involved is assembling and maintaining dissemination products that meet publication standards and user needs. Future drivers will materially affect this work: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will require products to be metadata-rich and reusable; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will support more scalable and interactive digital products; AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase templating and automation of recurring products; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will require richer quality statements and methodological explanation for mixed-source and model-based outputs; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need for digital product skills, accessibility, and clear communication.

This subprocess has plausible but limited relevance. The role is clearly involved in dissemination processes and outputs, but the work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for release timing, embargoes, subscriber management, or retractions. Evidence for a limited connection includes coordinating 'production, validation and dissemination of regular statistical outputs across multiple production teams' and providing expert advice on dissemination methods. Future drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure may increase the role's exposure to release readiness, controlled access, and timing coordination, especially where dissemination systems and outputs are tightly integrated with production databases, but based on the supplied description this remains peripheral.

This subprocess is relevant because the role evaluates technological developments, interprets test results and feasibility studies, and produces evidence used to improve systems, processes, and outputs. Evidence includes: 'Evaluates the impact of technological developments on operation and production procedures and prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines'; 'Interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations, and feasibility studies'; and 'Research and validation is required to evaluate the effectiveness of the processing systems.' The capability involved is gathering and interpreting system metrics, test evidence, quality indicators, and operational findings that inform improvement. Future-state drivers make this more important: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will generate richer monitoring, telemetry, and process metadata; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion will require new indicators on source quality and linkage performance; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase demand for evidence on productivity and sustainability; and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make staff feedback and adoption metrics more important evaluation inputs.

This subprocess is materially connected because the role evaluates systems, procedures, technological developments, and operational effectiveness, and recommends improvements. Evidence includes: 'Evaluates alternatives and develops and applies new strategies to maintain and improve operational systems, processes and databases'; 'Evaluates the impact of technological developments on operation and production procedures and prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines'; and 'Research and validation is required to evaluate the effectiveness of the processing systems.' The capability involved is synthesizing evidence on quality, performance, and operational fit into recommendations for change. Future drivers will broaden this evaluation work beyond technical effectiveness to include automation benefits, workflow efficiency, platform readiness, governance effectiveness, workforce readiness, and sustainability under staffing constraints. Particularly relevant are AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production.

This subprocess has limited relevance because the role recommends modifications, improvements, and technical approaches, and occasionally leads projects, but the work description does not explicitly assign formal decision-making authority to agree enterprise action plans. Evidence includes: 'Recommends and implements modifications and improvements to existing procedures'; 'prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines'; and 'Occasionally leads project teams.' The capability involved is contributing expert recommendations and technical direction that can feed action planning. Future drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity may increase the importance of disciplined prioritization, ownership, and monitored improvement actions around this role's recommendations, but based on the supplied information the role appears to contribute to, rather than own, formal action-plan agreement.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it concerns assessing whether existing data sources, including administrative, alternative and linked data, are suitable and available for statistical use, along with the conditions for access and use. The work description explicitly states that the position 'undertakes technical projects requiring data integration, data linkage and use of alternative data sources' and 'participates in data acquisition negotiations,' which aligns with assessing and operationalizing source availability, suitability, and supplier arrangements. The capability involved is technical and methodological expertise in evaluating non-survey sources, linkage readiness, and acquisition conditions. The role fulfills this need by providing specialized technical and consultative services on data integration and alternative sources, and by developing recommendations on new methods of acquiring and processing data. Future-state drivers make this even more central: the 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion' driver directly expands the use of administrative data, alternative data, SDLE and data linkages; 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' increases the need to assess linked, unstructured and integrated-source feasibility; 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure' makes platform fit, centralized repositories, secure access and scalable ingestion part of source suitability; 'Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access' increases scrutiny of privacy, authorizations and secure handling before sources can be used; 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' raises the importance of metadata quality and interoperability in source assessment; and 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' increases pressure to replace labour-intensive collection with reusable external sources. Evidence from the work description includes 'data integration,' 'data linkage,' 'use of alternative data sources,' 'participates in data acquisition negotiations,' and 'new methods of acquiring... data.'

This subprocess is relevant because it involves documenting options and recommendations for new or modified statistical business processes, including costs, benefits, risks, technical resources and implementation implications. The work description does not say the position formally prepares business cases, so relevance is not High; however, it clearly contributes substantive technical input by 'develop[ing] recommendations, provid[ing] advice to management and implement[ing] initiatives pertaining to new methods of acquiring, processing, modeling, analyzing or disseminating data to meet user needs.' The capability involved is expert advisory support on modernization options, technical feasibility and methodological change. The role fulfills this need by advising management on new acquisition, processing, modelling, analysis and dissemination methods, which are exactly the kinds of options and recommendations that would feed a business case. Future-state drivers increase the importance of this contribution: 'Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline' and 'Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline' mean recommendations will increasingly need to support explicit trade-offs, approval discipline and executable plans; 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' means proposals will be judged more heavily on savings, automation and sustainability with fewer staff; 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion' and 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' mean business cases will increasingly compare survey-based approaches with linked, administrative, alternative-data and modernized production models; and 'Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity' means recommendations will increasingly need to account for training, technical support and workforce readiness. Evidence includes 'develops recommendations,' 'provides advice to management,' and 'implements initiatives pertaining to new methods of acquiring, processing, modeling, analyzing or disseminating data.'

This subprocess is directly relevant because it covers detailed design of statistical outputs, products and services to be disseminated. The work description explicitly states that the position performs analytics and in-depth analysis 'towards producing dissemination and data visualization products' and develops recommendations on new methods of 'disseminating data to meet user needs.' The capability involved is analytical and product-design expertise for dissemination-ready outputs, including visualization and user-oriented products. The role fulfills this need by producing dissemination and visualization products and by advising on improved dissemination methods. Future-state drivers indicate that this work will evolve materially: 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' means outputs will increasingly need to be metadata-rich, searchable and reusable; 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure' means dissemination design will increasingly assume platform-based delivery, secure access and reusable tooling; 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production' may enable more automated and interactive dissemination products while increasing transparency requirements; 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' pushes toward standardized, reusable, lower-cost digital products; and 'Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity' implies staff will need to operate and explain outputs using newer digital and analytical tools. Evidence includes 'producing dissemination and data visualization products' and 'new methods of ... disseminating data to meet user needs.'

This subprocess is one of the strongest matches because it covers design of methodology for coding, editing, imputation, integration, validation and estimation during processing and analysis. The work description centers on 'data integration, data manipulation, data analytics and in-depth analysis' and on implementing 'new methods of acquiring, processing, modeling, analyzing or disseminating data.' The capability involved is methodological and technical design of processing and analytical approaches, especially for integrated and linked data. The role fulfills this need by undertaking technical projects requiring integration and linkage, providing specialized technical and consultative services, and recommending new processing, modelling and analytical methods. Future-state drivers intensify this connection: 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' directly reshapes processing and analysis toward advanced methods, integrated pipelines, linked data and reduced manual intervention; 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production' increases use of automated coding, validation and analytical routines; 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion' increases the need for source-specific integration, validation and prioritization rules; 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration' pushes methods to be modular, orchestrated and automatable; 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' makes metadata an operational input to processing design; 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' increases pressure to redesign methods for sustainability with fewer staff; and 'Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity' means the role will increasingly require advanced tool, method and oversight capability. Evidence includes 'data integration,' 'data manipulation,' 'data analytics,' 'in-depth analysis,' 'new methods of ... processing, modeling, analyzing,' and 'specialized technical, advisory and consultative services.'

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns designing end-to-end workflows, reuse of systems and services, and how staff interact with systems across production. The work description does not explicitly assign workflow architecture ownership, so relevance is Medium rather than High. However, the position is materially connected because it implements initiatives for new methods across acquisition, processing, modelling, analysis and dissemination, and may supervise employees 'to perform statistical processes, outputs or projects.' The capability involved is operational and technical understanding of how analytical and integration work fits into broader production processes and projects. The role fulfills this need by contributing technical expertise to initiatives that span multiple production stages and by potentially supervising statistical processes and projects. Future-state drivers increase the degree of impact on the role: 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration' shifts work toward end-to-end automated flows and exception handling; 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure' and 'Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development' push production toward reusable enterprise services and standardized workflows; 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production' embeds work directly into production workflows and reduces manual effort; 'Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline' clarifies responsibilities and reuse expectations; and 'Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity' changes staff-system interaction, role clarity and supervision needs. Evidence includes 'implements initiatives pertaining to new methods of acquiring, processing, modeling, analyzing or disseminating data' and 'may supervise employees directly or in a matrix environment to perform statistical processes, outputs or projects.'

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it covers building or reusing components needed for processing and analysis, including transformation functions, workflow tools and information services. The work description does not explicitly say the position builds software components, so responsibilities should not be overstated. However, the role is materially connected because it performs data manipulation, analytics and integration work, undertakes technical projects, and implements initiatives involving new processing, modelling and analysis methods. The capability involved is technical implementation of analytical and integration approaches in operational tools, routines or project components. The role fulfills this need by carrying out technical projects and implementing new methods that would often require reuse or creation of processing and analysis components. Future-state drivers suggest this work will increasingly be shaped by reusable enterprise components: 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' and 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production' increase use of reusable coding, transformation and analytical services; 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion' increases need for linkage, harmonisation and geospatial processing components; 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration' pushes components to operate as pipeline modules; 'Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development' shifts work from bespoke approaches toward shared, governed components; and 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' favours reuse over one-off development. Evidence includes 'data manipulation,' 'data analytics,' 'technical projects requiring data integration, data linkage and use of alternative data sources,' and 'implements initiatives pertaining to new methods of ... processing, modeling, analyzing.'

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns configuring workflows, systems and transformations from collection through dissemination. The work description does not explicitly mention workflow configuration tools or orchestration systems, so relevance is Medium. Still, the role is meaningfully connected because it implements initiatives spanning acquisition, processing, modelling, analysis and dissemination, and may supervise staff performing statistical processes and projects. The capability involved is configuring or adapting operational analytical processes so they function coherently across stages. The role fulfills this need by contributing technical implementation expertise to cross-stage initiatives and by supporting or supervising statistical processes. Future-state drivers make this more important: 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration' will shift work toward automated handoffs, event-driven workflows and exception handling; 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production' embeds work into production workflows; 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure' and 'Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development' increase use of standardized enterprise workflow patterns; 'Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline' increases pressure for fit-for-purpose, quickly deployable workflows; and 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' pushes toward simplified, lower-touch flows. Evidence includes 'implements initiatives pertaining to new methods of acquiring, processing, modeling, analyzing or disseminating data' and 'may supervise employees ... to perform statistical processes, outputs or projects.'

This is the most directly implicated subprocess. It covers combining data from multiple sources, record linkage, harmonisation, prioritisation across sources, and creation of consolidated datasets. The work description explicitly states that the position 'performs data integration,' 'undertakes technical projects requiring data integration, data linkage and use of alternative data sources,' and performs 'data manipulation' and analytics. The capability involved is core expertise in multi-source integration, linkage, harmonisation and analytical use of integrated data. The role fulfills this need directly through its named responsibilities and title, 'Data Analytics and Integration Officer.' Future-state drivers strongly amplify this work: 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion' makes integration, linkage and source prioritisation central production activities; 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' makes integrated survey, administrative, alternative and geospatial data a core production model; 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration' turns integration into a repeatable pipeline backbone; 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure' provides centralized repositories and scalable environments for integration; 'Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access' makes controlled linkage, de-identification and secure access central; 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' improves interoperability and reuse across sources; 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' increases reliance on integrated existing sources instead of labour-intensive collection; and 'Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity' raises the need for advanced integration skills and disciplined prioritization. Evidence includes 'Performs data integration,' 'data manipulation,' 'undertakes technical projects requiring data integration, data linkage and use of alternative data sources,' and the position title itself.

This subprocess has plausible but limited relevance. It concerns assigning codes and classifications to input data, often through automated or manual coding routines. The work description does not explicitly mention coding or classification responsibilities, so this cannot be treated as a core duty. It is only indirectly relevant because the position performs data manipulation, analytics and integration, and such work may interact with coded or harmonized inputs, especially when using alternative data sources. Future-state drivers suggest some indirect impact on the role: 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion' means more non-standard external inputs may require harmonisation to statistical classifications; 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' and 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production' increase automated coding in surrounding workflows; and 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' increases automation pressure. However, the supplied work description does not provide evidence that this position materially performs classify-and-code functions. Evidence is limited to broader references such as 'data manipulation' and 'use of alternative data sources.'

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns identifying errors, discrepancies, duplicates and anomalies in data before and after integration. The work description does not explicitly use the word validation, but the role's responsibilities in data integration, manipulation, analytics and in-depth analysis imply meaningful involvement in assessing data quality and fitness, especially in technical projects using linked and alternative sources. The capability involved is analytical review of integrated data, identification of inconsistencies, and quality-oriented examination of complex datasets. The role fulfills this need through in-depth analysis and technical integration work that necessarily depends on reviewing and validating source consistency and integrated outputs. Future-state drivers increase the importance of this connection: 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion' introduces heterogeneous sources, linkage errors, duplicates and source drift; 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' increases validation complexity across automated and integrated workflows; 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production' enables more automated anomaly detection but shifts staff toward oversight of exceptions; 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration' embeds validation checkpoints into workflows; 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' adds metadata completeness and consistency as validation targets; and 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' increases reliance on automated validation with fewer staff. Evidence includes 'data integration,' 'data manipulation,' 'data analytics,' 'in-depth analysis,' and 'technical projects requiring data integration, data linkage and use of alternative data sources.'

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance. It concerns correcting, replacing or imputing incorrect or missing data and producing metadata on those changes. The work description does not explicitly mention editing or imputation, so these responsibilities should not be inferred as direct duties. There is some indirect connection because the role performs data manipulation and technical integration projects, which may expose it to correction or source-prioritization activities in practice. Future-state drivers such as 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion,' 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production,' and 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' suggest that integrated-source environments will increasingly rely on automated, source-aware correction methods. Still, the evidence in the work description is insufficient to claim material responsibility. Supporting evidence is limited to 'data manipulation' and 'technical projects requiring data integration, data linkage and use of alternative data sources.'

This subprocess is relevant because it covers deriving variables and units not directly collected, often from integrated or linked data. The work description does not explicitly say 'derive variables,' but it strongly indicates related work through data integration, manipulation, analytics, modelling and use of alternative data sources. The capability involved is transforming integrated data into analytically useful constructs through modelling, derivation and combination of variables. The role fulfills this need by implementing new methods of 'processing, modeling, analyzing' data and by undertaking technical projects involving linked and alternative sources, which often require derived variables or units to support outputs. Future-state drivers strengthen this relevance: 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion' increases reliance on deriving variables from administrative and linked records rather than collecting them directly; 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' expands model-based and linked-source derivation; 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration' requires explicit sequencing of derivation logic; 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' increases the need to document derivations clearly; and 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' encourages derivation from existing data where feasible. Evidence includes 'data integration,' 'data manipulation,' 'implements initiatives pertaining to new methods of ... modeling, analyzing,' and 'use of alternative data sources.'

This subprocess is plausibly relevant because it assembles the results of processing into datasets ready for analysis. The work description does not explicitly mention finalizing data files, packaging datasets, or handing off analysis-ready files, so relevance remains Low. There is some indirect connection because the role performs data integration, manipulation and analytics, which may contribute to preparing consolidated datasets for downstream use. Future-state drivers such as 'Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration,' 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability,' and 'Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure' suggest that standardized, metadata-rich, analysis-ready datasets will become more important around this role's work. Evidence is limited to 'data integration,' 'data manipulation,' and 'data analytics.'

This subprocess is directly relevant because it transforms processed data into statistical outputs and prepares methodological notes and explanatory material. The work description explicitly states that the position performs analytics and in-depth analysis 'towards producing dissemination and data visualization products.' The capability involved is analytical transformation of processed data into user-facing outputs, including visualization and explanatory products. The role fulfills this need directly by producing dissemination and visualization products and by advising on new dissemination methods to meet user needs. Future-state drivers indicate that this work will change materially: 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' expands mapped, granular and model-based outputs and increases the need for methodological explanation; 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion' means outputs will increasingly reflect integrated administrative, linked and geospatial data and require explanation of source combinations; 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production' may accelerate draft production while increasing transparency requirements for AI-supported methods; 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' means outputs must be packaged with richer metadata; and 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' encourages templated and lower-touch preparation of recurring products. Evidence includes 'data analytics and in-depth analysis, towards producing dissemination and data visualization products' and 'new methods of ... disseminating data to meet user needs.'

This subprocess is relevant because it involves validating outputs against expectations, auxiliary information, metadata and quality indicators. The work description does not explicitly assign output validation responsibility, but the role's in-depth analysis, technical integration work and production of dissemination products imply meaningful involvement in assessing whether outputs are coherent and fit for use. The capability involved is analytical judgment over integrated outputs, including comparison, interpretation of anomalies and quality-oriented review. The role fulfills this need through in-depth analysis and technical advisory work that supports confidence in outputs derived from integrated and alternative sources. Future-state drivers increase the importance of this connection: 'Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion' introduces methodological breaks and comparability issues that require stronger validation; 'Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production' increases reliance on linked, model-based and automated outputs that need stronger benchmark and domain validation; 'AI and Automation in Statistical Production' increases scrutiny of outputs influenced by automated methods; 'Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability' makes metadata completeness part of validation; and 'Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment' pushes toward more targeted, risk-based validation. Evidence includes 'in-depth analysis,' 'producing dissemination and data visualization products,' and 'technical projects requiring data integration, data linkage and use of alternative data sources.'

This subprocess is directly relevant because it concerns understanding outputs, explaining their meaning, and carrying out in-depth analysis to assess them against expectations.
