Future drivers such as Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase automation, metadata handling, secure loading, pseudonymisation and digital archiving. The role is materially affected because collection operations increasingly depend on seamless, secure handoff and transmission.

This subprocess combines data from multiple sources and performs harmonisation and linkage. The work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for data integration, but there is limited relevance because the role identifies trends in data processing and dissemination systems, evaluates data quality and completeness, and negotiates agreements for acquisition and dissemination of data. The capability involved is indirect operational support to environments where integrated data are increasingly used. Evidence includes 'Identifies trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and processes' and 'Negotiates agreements... for the acquisition and dissemination of data.' Future drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will affect the role by shifting collection away from survey-only models and toward mixed-source operations. However, the description does not state that the position performs linkage or integration itself, so relevance remains low.

This subprocess identifies errors, discrepancies, duplicates and quality issues before and after integration. The position is materially connected because it monitors and evaluates cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of collection systems and processes; evaluates quality and completeness of data; analyzes relative quality of data, gaps and inconsistencies; and determines reasons for variances. The capability involved is operational quality assurance and validation of collection outputs and processes. Evidence includes 'Monitors and evaluates the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of regional data collection systems and processes,' 'Evaluates the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes and the quality and completeness of data,' and 'Analyses the relative quality of data, researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection methods and procedures used, determines reasons for variances.' Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase automated validation, exception handling, metadata checks and multi-source quality assessment. This role is regularly involved because collection quality problems directly affect program outputs and respondent burden.

This subprocess transforms processed data into draft statistical outputs and methodological notes. The position is only indirectly connected, but there is some relevance because it provides advice on program results, prepares summaries used by senior management and client divisions, and provides feedback to subject matter experts on response patterns and collection impacts. The capability involved is supplying operational context that informs draft outputs and explanatory material. Evidence includes 'Responds orally or in writing... to provide information and advice on the operation and use of systems and processes and the use of program results' and 'Prepares work plans and summaries... used by senior management... and/or client divisions.' Future drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may increase the need for operational explanation of source and collection changes, but the role is not described as preparing statistical outputs directly. Relevance is therefore limited.

This subprocess validates outputs against expectations, prior cycles and auxiliary information. The position has limited but plausible relevance because it analyzes response patterns, data quality, comparability over time and relevance in light of changing requirements and socio-economic conditions, which can inform output validation. Evidence includes 'Analyses the relative quality of data... reviews the comparability of data over time and its relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.' The capability involved is providing operational and quality intelligence that can support output validation. Future drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase the need to understand methodological breaks and collection effects, but the work description does not assign formal responsibility for validating released outputs. Relevance remains low.

This subprocess handles user queries, service requests and support to partner organizations. The position has limited relevance because it responds to inquiries from managers, employees and the general public, provides information and advice on systems, processes and program results, and resolves complaints related to survey participation and respondent relations. The capability involved is operational support and stakeholder communication rather than formal dissemination support. Evidence includes 'Responds orally or in writing to inquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information and advice on the operation and use of systems and processes and the use of program results' and 'Develops strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations... and resolves complaints and problems related to survey participation and non-respondents.' Future drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment may shift support toward self-service, chatbots and knowledge reuse, affecting how this role handles inquiries. Still, user support is not a central responsibility in the description.

This subprocess gathers feedback, paradata, system metrics, staff suggestions and quality indicators for evaluation. The position is materially connected because it monitors and evaluates collection systems and processes, extracts and interprets analytical reports, identifies trends in response patterns and respondent behaviour, and evaluates effectiveness of systems and quality/completeness of data for senior management use. The capability involved is generating and compiling operational evidence for evaluation and continuous improvement. Evidence includes 'Monitors and evaluates the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of regional data collection systems and processes,' 'Extracts and interprets information from analytical reports to assess the content and operation of collection activities and programs,' and 'Senior management uses the studies to assess the attainment of program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of regional resources.' Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the volume and importance of continuous metrics, telemetry, workforce feedback and efficiency indicators. This role is directly involved in producing and interpreting those inputs.

This subprocess analyzes evaluation inputs, compares them to targets and produces evaluation reports or dashboards with recommendations. The position is relevant because it evaluates effectiveness of systems and processes, quality and completeness of data, cost and efficiency of regional resources, and proposes modifications, enhancements and alternative approaches. The capability involved is operational evaluation and recommendation-making for future improvements. Evidence includes 'Evaluates the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes and the quality and completeness of data,' 'Senior management uses the studies to assess the attainment of program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of regional resources,' and 'Reviews and interprets the methods, concepts, techniques and practices applied in the operation of existing systems and processes; proposes modifications and enhancements or develops alternative approaches.' Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make evaluation more dashboard-driven, more focused on efficiency, workforce sustainability, modernization outcomes and explicit trade-offs. This role is materially affected because it both contributes evaluation evidence and uses evaluation to redesign regional operations.

This subprocess brings together decision-making authority to agree actions based on evaluation findings and monitor their impact. The position is relevant because it develops and implements long-term strategies and business solutions, leads multidisciplinary teams, approves work plans and priorities, assigns responsibilities, monitors progress, and provides advice on modifications to operational procedures. The capability involved is turning operational findings into concrete improvement actions with assigned responsibilities and follow-up. Evidence includes 'Develops and implements long term strategies and business solutions,' 'Approves work plans and priorities... assigns responsibilities... monitors progress,' and 'Leads or participates in task forces, committees or departmental multidisciplinary project teams as a data collection expert and provides advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures.' Future-state drivers are strong here: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all increase the need for disciplined, time-bound, resource-aware action planning under flatter structures and staffing pressure. Because this role manages budgets, workforce, priorities and operational change, it is materially involved in agreeing and implementing action plans in the regional collection context.

Positions.Branch/Division: Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division

implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is directly relevant because it concerns gathering evaluation material from across the statistical business process, including user feedback, process metadata, system metrics, staff suggestions, and reports against prior action plans. The work description identifies the position as a "Senior Evaluation Analyst" in the "Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division," which is explicit evidence of an evaluation function. Even though the detailed technical responsibilities are not provided, the title and organizational placement materially connect the role to assembling evidence for evaluation. Future-state drivers strengthen this connection. AI and Automation in Statistical Production increases the volume and usefulness of monitoring outputs, documentation, and continuously captured process metrics that evaluation staff would need to gather. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion adds new evaluation inputs such as source-quality indicators, linkage metrics, online-response and adaptive-collection paradata. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration increase the availability of centralized telemetry, workflow logs, and operational dashboards, changing evaluation work toward more continuous, data-rich evidence gathering. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability also matters because metadata quality, discoverability, and reuse indicators become evaluation inputs. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is relevant because staff feedback, training outcomes, workload sustainability, and adoption of new tools become part of the evidence base. The cumulative effect is that evaluation input gathering becomes more automated, broader in scope, and more dependent on digital, metadata-rich, cross-process evidence.

This subprocess is the strongest match to the work description. It covers analysing evaluation inputs, comparing them to expected results, synthesising findings into evaluation reports or dashboards, identifying quality issues and performance deviations, and making recommendations for change. The position title "Senior Evaluation Analyst" is direct evidence that the role materially aligns with conducting evaluations, and the placement in the "Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division" further confirms that evaluation analysis is a core responsibility area. Future-state drivers materially reshape this work. AI and Automation in Statistical Production makes evaluation more dashboard-driven and continuous, while also requiring explicit assessment of transparency, governance, public trust, and whether automated methods are properly controlled. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline makes schedule adherence, milestone attainment, implementation effectiveness, and rapid corrective action central evaluation criteria. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment strongly affects this subprocess because evaluations will increasingly assess productivity, savings, automation benefits, service trade-offs, sustainability under reduced staffing, and whether activities should be redesigned, scaled back, or stopped. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline adds emphasis on evidence-based prioritization, accountability, transparent trade-offs, and identifying owners for follow-up actions. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability all expand the range of measurable performance evidence available and the dimensions to be assessed, including platform readiness, interoperability, metadata completeness, reuse, and end-to-end flow performance. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is also highly relevant because modernization success must be evaluated not only on statistical quality but also on workforce readiness, training uptake, leadership effectiveness, cultural change, and sustainability. The work description provides limited task detail, but the role title and division are sufficient evidence that this subprocess is materially central.

This subprocess is relevant because it uses evaluation findings to support decision-making and agreement on an action plan, including mechanisms to monitor the impact of those actions in future iterations. A Senior Evaluation Analyst would plausibly contribute substantively to this subprocess by providing the evaluation evidence, findings, and recommendations that inform action planning, even if the work description does not explicitly state decision authority. The evidence available is the position title "Senior Evaluation Analyst" and its location in the "Audit and Evaluation Branch – Evaluation Division," which indicates regular involvement in the evaluation-to-improvement cycle. Relevance is Medium rather than High because the supplied work description does not explicitly say the position approves or owns action plans. Future-state drivers increase the importance of this subprocess. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline makes action planning more explicit, accountable, and constrained by scarce resources, requiring transparent trade-offs and clear ownership. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline pushes action plans toward milestone-based, time-bound commitments with clarified authorities and active monitoring. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment means action plans will increasingly focus on simplification, automation, service prioritization, and workforce adjustments. Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is also important because agreed actions will often involve training, leadership support, realistic sequencing, and workforce sustainability measures. AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development further shape action plans toward shared solutions, governance controls, reuse, and monitoring of adoption impacts. Based on the supplied evidence, the role is materially connected to informing and supporting this subprocess, but direct decision-making authority cannot be inferred.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns identifying what statistics are needed and considering user requests, environmental change, and practices across organizations. The position is materially connected through its responsibility for "outreach and collaboration with a variety of stakeholders ... to ... understand user needs and keep abreast of economic trends and developments" and for "providing expert advice and analysis." That is direct evidence that the role helps surface and interpret statistical needs. The capability involved is stakeholder engagement and analytical interpretation of emerging needs. Future-state change is driven by Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment: with scarce capacity, need identification becomes more selective and feasibility-conscious. The work description already shows this role operating where user needs, new methods, and new data sources intersect, so future pressures from automation, AI, machine learning, and fewer FTEs are likely to push the role toward sharper triage of which needs can be met and which new methods or sources are viable.

This subprocess is relevant because it sets output objectives that balance user needs, quality, scope, timeliness, and resources. The position manages "data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products," while "setting objectives" and "ensuring overall quality and completeness of program results." That is direct evidence that the role helps define and operationalize output expectations. The capability involved is translating user needs into concrete analytical and dissemination deliverables with quality expectations. Future changes are shaped by Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. Those drivers imply more explicit trade-offs, clearer accountability, and tighter scope decisions under constrained resources. Because the role already sets objectives and manages quality for outputs, it is likely to face stronger pressure to prioritize highest-value outputs, standardize products, and make trade-offs among scope, timeliness, and granularity more explicit.

This is one of the most directly implicated subprocesses. It concerns assessing whether existing data sources, including administrative, alternative, linked, and external sources, can meet user requirements and under what legal, technical, and operational conditions. The work description directly states that the position "manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation," and "leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs." It also says the role is "responsible for outreach and collaboration ... to leverage new methods and data sources" and "participates in or leads data acquisition negotiations." These are direct matches to source assessment, partnership development, and acquisition feasibility. The capability involved is expert assessment of source suitability, acquisition conditions, linkage potential, and operational use. Future-state impacts are cumulative and strong: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion directly expands the role's focus on alternative data and linkage; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access increases scrutiny of privacy, authorizations, secure access, and legal agreements; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure makes platform fit, secure ingestion, and scalable repositories more central; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the importance of metadata quality and reuse; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production expands the need to assess linked, unstructured, and integrated pipeline-ready sources; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases pressure to substitute lower-cost reusable sources for labour-intensive collection. The work description provides explicit evidence for nearly all of these mechanisms through acquisition, linkage, alternative data use, stakeholder collaboration, and negotiations.

This subprocess is relevant because it documents options, costs, benefits, risks, timelines, and resource implications for new or modified statistical processes. The role does not explicitly say it writes business cases, so relevance is not high. However, it does say the position "leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources," "develops mitigation strategies to address delays and briefs senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary." That is direct evidence of responsibilities closely tied to business-case style decision support: articulating risks, scope changes, timelines, and mitigation. The capability involved is project leadership and strategic briefing on modernization initiatives. Future-state drivers make this more important: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline increases emphasis on milestones, go/no-go discipline, and implementation readiness; Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline raises the threshold for approval and explicit trade-offs; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment foregrounds savings and affordability; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity increases the need to account for training and readiness. Because this role already briefs senior management on cost and scope changes in complex data modernization projects, it is meaningfully connected to the approval and justification environment around business cases.

This subprocess is relevant because it covers detailed design of outputs, products, services, and dissemination procedures. The work description directly states that the position manages "the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products" and "authors analytical papers and other types of material supporting data development and dissemination." That is direct evidence of responsibility for shaping analytical and dissemination outputs. The capability involved is designing and preparing analytical products, visualizations, and dissemination-ready materials that meet user needs and quality expectations. Future-state impacts come from Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. These drivers imply outputs will increasingly need richer metadata, platform-based delivery, secure access controls where relevant, and more standardized, reusable digital products. The role's existing responsibility for dissemination and visualization means it is likely to be materially affected by digital-first, metadata-rich, and more standardized dissemination design expectations.

This subprocess concerns defining variables, derived variables, units, and classifications. The work description does not explicitly assign variable design responsibility. However, the role's responsibilities for "data integration, data manipulation, data analytics" and leading projects involving "integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources" plausibly create limited involvement in how variables are harmonized or derived across sources. The capability involved would be analytical harmonization across integrated datasets, but the evidence is indirect. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production suggest that roles working with linked and alternative data will increasingly be affected by standardized metadata, harmonized concepts, and derived variables. Still, because the work description does not explicitly mention variable or classification design, relevance remains low.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it covers design of methodologies for integration, validation, estimation, and analysis. The position "manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis" and leads projects involving "data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources." That is direct evidence that the role is deeply involved in the analytical and processing approach used to turn complex source data into outputs. The capability involved is designing or leading sophisticated analytical and integration approaches for multi-source statistical production. Future-state impacts are substantial and cumulative: AI and Automation in Statistical Production will increase automation, monitoring, and repeatable workflows; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion increases complexity of linkage, source prioritization, and heterogeneous validation; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access strengthens secure handling and disclosure-aware processing; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration pushes methods into orchestrated, automatable modules; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases reliance on metadata as an operational input; Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production expands advanced methods, integrated pipelines, and alternative data processing; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases pressure to reduce manual intervention; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity raises expectations for advanced analytical and technical capability. The work description strongly evidences this through its repeated emphasis on integration, analytics, processing, tools/software implementation, and quality assurance.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns end-to-end workflow design, reuse of systems, and how staff interact with systems. The work description says the position manages "implementation of various tools or software," ensures quality and completeness of results, and "supervises directly or in a matrix environment to plan and coordinate teams responsible for statistical outputs or projects." That is evidence of meaningful involvement in how analytical production work is organized and supported by tools, though not explicit ownership of enterprise workflow architecture. The capability involved is coordinating analytical production activities and implementing tools that support integrated workflows. Future-state drivers such as Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity suggest this role will increasingly work within standardized, orchestrated, reusable production environments with clearer handoffs and more automation. Because the role already coordinates teams and implements tools/software in data integration and analytics contexts, it is meaningfully affected even if not the primary workflow architect.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it covers building or reusing components for processing and analysis. The work description does not explicitly say the role develops software components, but it does say the position manages "implementation of various tools or software" and manages activities in "data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis." That is evidence of meaningful involvement in selecting, implementing, or operationalizing analytical components. The capability involved is applying and integrating analytical tools and processing capabilities into production work. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity indicate that analytical work will increasingly rely on reusable enterprise components, open-source and modern tools, and automated services. The role is therefore likely to be materially affected as processing and analysis become more componentized and platform-based.

This subprocess is relevant because it configures workflows, systems, and transformations from collection through dissemination. The work description provides indirect but meaningful evidence through responsibility for "implementation of various tools or software," management of processing and dissemination activities, and supervision in a direct or matrix environment to coordinate teams responsible for outputs or projects. The capability involved is operational configuration and coordination of analytical workflows rather than enterprise workflow engineering. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity suggest that this role will increasingly need to work within configured automated workflows, monitor exceptions, and coordinate staff around standardized production flows. Because the role already coordinates projects and tools across integration, analytics, and dissemination, it is meaningfully connected.

This subprocess concerns testing assembled services, workflows, secure channels, and supplier files. The work description does not explicitly mention testing systems. However, the role's responsibility for implementing tools/software, ensuring "overall quality and completeness of program results," and leading acquisition and integration projects implies some plausible involvement in validating whether tools and data flows work as intended. The capability involved would be quality assurance of analytical production arrangements, but the evidence is indirect. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration suggest that roles implementing tools and integration projects will increasingly be affected by stronger testing and sign-off expectations. Relevance remains low because testing is not explicitly stated.

This subprocess includes documentation, training users, and moving components into production. The work description does not explicitly mention production deployment or training users, but it does mention "implementation of various tools or software" and supervision/coordination of teams. That suggests limited plausible involvement in operationalizing analytical tools and workflows. The capability involved would be helping transition analytical tools and processes into regular use. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development imply that roles implementing tools will increasingly be affected by documentation, training, and production-readiness expectations. The future-state drivers attached to this subprocess are especially relevant to infrastructure-oriented roles: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all point to stronger reuse, platform standardization, clearer accountabilities, automation, and changed staff-system interaction. However, the supplied work description provides no technical activities, no explicit production-system responsibilities, and no evidence of workflow design duties. The only listed activities are generic corporate resources such as "HR A to Z index," "HR service standards," "Wellness at Statistics Canada," "HR committees," "HR contact list," and "Corporate service providers," which do not demonstrate direct responsibility for this subprocess. Relevance is therefore limited to plausible organizational exposure rather than evidenced operational responsibility.

Positions.Position Title: Unit Head, Metadata Development, Dissemination and Evaluation

implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it concerns the initial investigation of what is needed and consideration of practices across other statistical organizations. The position directly investigates client metadata requirements and reviews Canadian and international trends in statistical metadata management. The work description states that the incumbent 'investigates client metadata requirements, determining the capacity and ability of existing methods, procedures and systems to fulfill these requirements' and 'reviews trends and developments in the area of statistical metadata management' to prepare proposals and recommendations. That is a material contribution to identifying needs for metadata products, services and systems, even though the role is focused on metadata rather than defining statistical subject-matter outputs themselves. Future-state change is driven by Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment: stronger prioritization under fiscal constraint, fewer staff, and pressure to find efficiencies will likely force sharper triage of which metadata needs can be supported, more explicit feasibility assessments, and greater use of AI, automation, machine learning and new tools and methods to meet needs at lower cost. Evidence also shows the role already assesses feasibility and resource implications, which aligns with the driver's impact mechanisms.

This subprocess is relevant because it establishes objectives, quality measures and resource-aware constraints for outputs. The position helps define objectives for metadata development, dissemination and quality evaluation by determining short- and long-term projects and strategies, recommending plans to improve the 'scope, quality and level of integration' of metadata programs, and translating policy requirements into concrete implementation plans. The work description also shows responsibility for determining the overall approach to reporting, analysis and presentation of metadata quality assessment results. This reflects capability in setting objectives for metadata outputs and associated quality expectations. Future changes are likely from Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment. Those drivers imply more explicit trade-offs among scope, quality, timeliness and resources, clearer accountability, and tighter prioritization of highest-value metadata outputs. This is especially relevant because the role already manages priorities, budgets, and recommendations to senior management, and therefore would be affected by stronger enterprise decision discipline and constrained staffing.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it is fundamentally about assessing whether existing sources, metadata and related conditions are suitable for use. The work description repeatedly emphasizes assessing capacity and suitability: the incumbent 'investigates client metadata requirements, determining the capacity and ability of existing methods, procedures and systems to fulfill these requirements effectively and efficiently' and analyzes 'the suitability of methods, procedures and systems with respect to the short-term and long-term program impacts and benefits.' The role also has strong contextual knowledge of confidentiality, security and legislative requirements under the Statistics Act and Privacy Act, which aligns with this subprocess's concern for restrictions on use, legal frameworks, ICT resources and metadata quality. Future-state impacts are substantial. Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability is especially central because the role leads corporate metadata integration, coherence and consistency across programs; searchable, standardized, metadata-rich repositories will increase the importance of this work. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will change how metadata sources and repositories are assessed, with more emphasis on interoperability, secure access, platform fit, metadata completeness, and reuse across enterprise systems. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment and Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline will further push the role toward disciplined selection of reusable, high-value metadata assets and lower-cost approaches.

The evidence shows the incumbent already evaluates impacts, resources, training and systems implications, so the role is meaningfully connected even if not the final approval authority.

The work description's emphasis on high-quality metadata dissemination, coherence, consistency and training is direct evidence.

Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all strongly affect this subprocess. This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance because the role recommends changes to methods, procedures, guidelines, training plans or systems to improve metadata quality and analyzes gaps and inconsistencies in metadata. This role fulfills that need directly by designing frameworks, tools, methods, and quality approaches used in evaluation and performance reporting. Future-state drivers materially affect this work. Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration all point toward more automated, reusable, metadata-dependent, and integrated analytical methods. Workforce implications are also strong: staff will need new skills in AI, digital tools, and modern methods, and this role already provides technical guidance, coaching, and methodological leadership. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment further increases pressure to redesign methods to reduce manual effort while preserving quality and transparency.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it concerns end-to-end workflow design, reuse of systems and services, role clarity, and staff interaction with systems. The work description explicitly states that the incumbent makes decisions, in consultation with colleagues, regarding 'the development, use and maintenance of various system applications such as the Corporate Strategic Planning system which will significantly influence all aspects of systems development, implementation, maintenance and use.' It also includes responsibilities to develop policies, procedures, practices and standards; integrate strategic plans across branches and fields; organize and coordinate multidisciplinary teams; and establish operational guidelines, standards and methodologies. Evidence includes leadership over project teams, assigning work, setting schedules, allocating people across teams, and resolving assignments as work progresses. The capability involved is workflow and operating-model design for planning, evaluation, and accountability functions, including how people, methods, and systems fit together. This role fulfills that need directly through system-application decisions, methodology standardization, cross-organizational coordination, and team leadership. Future-state drivers make this one of the most affected areas. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all bear directly on workflow redesign. The work description already emphasizes change management strategies, organizational structure, resource allocation, and system application decisions, so future transformation toward reusable enterprise workflows, clearer handoffs, flatter structures, and more automated processes will materially reshape this role's advisory and managerial responsibilities.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because it concerns building or reusing analytical and processing components needed for process and analysis phases. The work description does not show hands-on software development, but it does show direct responsibility for developing methodologies, tools, techniques, and system applications that support evaluation and reporting work. Evidence includes 'develop and originate methodologies, tools and techniques,' knowledge of 'computer software applications to conduct analysis and document project results,' and decisions regarding 'development, use and maintenance of various system applications such as the Corporate Strategic Planning system.' The capability involved is specifying and shaping analytical components and tools rather than coding them directly. This role fulfills that need by defining methodological requirements, guiding tool use, and influencing system development and implementation. Future-state drivers such as Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure suggest that analytical tools will become more reusable, standardized, and platform-based. That means this role's methodological and governance input into component reuse, validation, and supportability will become more important, even if technical build remains with specialized teams.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns configuring workflows, systems, and transformations based on designed production workflows. The work description does not indicate direct workflow-configuration in a technical BPM sense, but it does show substantial responsibility for organizing, coordinating, and operationalizing multidisciplinary work, setting operational guidelines, and influencing system application use and maintenance. Evidence includes: 'organize, coordinate, and assign work; set work schedules and short-term plans'; 'establish operational guidelines, standards and methodologies'; and decisions on 'development, use and maintenance' of the Corporate Strategic Planning system. The capability involved is translating designed processes into operational practice through standards, assignments, schedules, and system-use decisions. This role fulfills that need managerially and methodologically. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need for standardized, monitored, lower-touch workflows with clearer authorities and exception handling. The role's existing responsibilities for team coordination, standards, and system-use decisions make it meaningfully affected.

This subprocess is relevant because it includes documentation, training, user guidance, and moving processes into production-ready operation. The work description shows strong alignment on documentation, guidance, and staff development rather than technical deployment. Evidence includes producing reports, briefings, presentations, and methodological documents; providing 'technical and operational guidance'; 'provide learning opportunities to develop skills and abilities'; 'Provide leadership and mentorship'; and responsibilities related to system applications that influence implementation, maintenance and use. The capability involved is operational readiness through documentation, guidance, and workforce preparation. This role fulfills that need by mentoring staff, setting procedures, and communicating methodologies and standards to colleagues, senior management, and stakeholders. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure will increase the importance of training, user readiness, and clear operating guidance as systems and workflows modernize. The role is therefore materially affected even if not the technical release owner.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns combining data from multiple sources, harmonising information, and creating consolidated evidence for analysis. The work description shows that the incumbent has latitude to decide 'what data, from which sources will be used, and how information will be created, developed or gathered,' and to scope, plan, authorize, and guide collection and analysis of foundation data to create new information about programs and effectiveness. It also emphasizes synthesising information from diverse disciplines and integrating strategic plans and information-related initiatives. The capability involved is source selection, evidence integration, and synthesis for evaluation and planning purposes. This role fulfills that need by directing data collection and analysis, choosing sources, and integrating diverse evidence into evaluation findings and strategic advice. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase the complexity and importance of integrating multiple data sources and reusable evidence assets. While the role is not a production data engineer, it is materially connected through methodological authority over source choice and evidence synthesis.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it concerns identifying errors, discrepancies, quality issues, and validating data and outputs against expectations. The work description repeatedly emphasizes monitoring, evaluating, assessing results, quality control, challenging assumptions, judging evidence, and ensuring adherence to approved levels of quality and service. Evidence includes: 'The work involves establishing performance measurement criteria and processes; monitoring, evaluating and assessing results'; 'Effort is required to ensure a quality control and to challenge assumptions and underlying logic used by multi-disciplinary teams'; 'judge the evidence gathered in relation to the review criteria'; and 'Monitors and performs quality control over work performed under contract.' The capability involved is analytical validation and quality assurance across evidence, methods, and outputs. This role fulfills that need directly through evaluation-review work, methodological scrutiny, and quality control responsibilities. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase reliance on automated checks, exception handling, metadata-aware validation, and risk-based review. The role's expertise in evaluation, performance measurement, and quality control makes it directly and materially connected.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance because it concerns correcting, replacing, or imputing problematic data values. The work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for editing or imputation of statistical records. However, it does show methodological expertise in advanced statistical methods, performance measurement, and the design of analytical frameworks and tools, which could influence how correction or replacement logic is assessed in evaluation contexts. Evidence is indirect: expertise in 'advanced statistical methods and techniques,' 'problem analysis,' 'quantitative approaches,' and 'design and integration of sophisticated computer-based and manual evaluation methodologies.' Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may affect the role indirectly because methodological leaders will need to understand and assess increasingly automated correction methods. Still, the work description does not show direct operational responsibility for editing or imputation, so relevance remains low.

This subprocess is plausibly relevant at a limited level because the role designs analytical frameworks and creates new information from foundation data, which can involve deriving indicators or performance measures not directly collected. Evidence includes authority 'to scope, plan, authorize, and guide the collection and analysis of the foundation data in order to create new information about programs and their effectiveness' and responsibilities for establishing performance measurement criteria and processes. The capability involved is conceptual derivation of indicators and evaluative measures rather than direct statistical variable engineering. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production may increase the importance of derived indicators from linked and administrative sources, but the work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for deriving statistical variables or units in production. Therefore relevance is low.

This subprocess has limited relevance because it concerns assembling final datasets for analysis. The work description does not indicate direct responsibility for finalizing production data files. However, the role does maintain custody of active hard copy and electronic project working files and senior management performance reviews and evaluations, and these files contain evidence, analysis documentation, findings, conclusions and recommendations. Evidence includes: 'Create, maintain and has custody of active hard copy and electronic project working files' and these are 'the Department’s only official record and depository of project results.' The capability involved is stewardship of analytical records and evidence packages rather than technical finalization of statistical data files. Future-state drivers around metadata, automation, and enterprise platforms may affect how such records are organized and handed off, but the connection remains limited.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it transforms processed evidence into outputs and accompanying methodological notes. The work description directly includes preparing evaluation-review reports, executive summaries, briefing notes, presentations, position papers, Parliamentary questions and answers, and other documents for senior management and stakeholders. Evidence includes: 'develop oral and written presentations, briefing materials, position papers, Parliamentary questions and answers'; 'develop, create and communicate information to Senior Management and to stakeholders in the form of assurances, evaluations advice, and recommendations'; and strong writing requirements for 'balanced and convincing evaluation reports.' The capability involved is drafting analytical outputs and explanatory materials that communicate findings, methods, and implications. This role fulfills that need directly and extensively. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will change how draft outputs are assembled, standardized, and explained, especially where AI-supported methods or more complex mixed-source evidence require clearer methodological notes and efficient production.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it concerns validating outputs against expectations, prior evidence, quality indicators, and domain intelligence. The work description strongly aligns through responsibilities to assess program relevance, success, cost-effectiveness, socio-economic impacts, and achievement of objectives; to judge evidence, materiality, sensitivity and risk; and to ensure recommendations are linked to departmental strategic priorities and senior management needs. Evidence includes: 'judge the evidence gathered in relation to the review criteria'; 'judge each finding in terms of materiality, sensitivity and risk'; 'develop conclusions; and make recommendations'; and 'monitoring, evaluating and assessing results.' The capability involved is expert validation of analytical outputs and findings before they inform decisions. This role fulfills that need directly through evaluation-review leadership and quality assurance. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and AI and Automation in Statistical Production will increase the need to validate outputs produced from mixed sources, automated methods, and changing methodologies. The role's domain knowledge, methodological expertise, and advisory function make it central to this subprocess.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it concerns understanding results, explaining them, and assessing them against expectations. The work description directly emphasizes strategic thinking, synthesis of complex information, production of authoritative options and strategic advice, and persuasive communication of findings to senior management, stakeholders, and sometimes Parliament or the Deputy Minister. Evidence includes: 'Strategic thinking is required to evaluate the relevance, success and cost-effectiveness of programs'; 'produce authoritative options and strategic advice'; 'Skill is required to write balanced and convincing evaluation reports'; and repeated requirements to explain complex, controversial, or politically sensitive issues to varied audiences. The capability involved is interpretation of analytical findings and explanation of their meaning, implications, and limitations. This role fulfills that need directly through evaluation reporting, briefings, presentations, and strategic advice. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the need to explain outputs produced through more complex methods, mixed-source evidence, and automated tools while preserving transparency and trust.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it ensures outputs are fit for purpose, supported by caveats, technical notes, briefings, and approvals. The work description directly includes producing final reports, briefings, presentations, position papers, and recommendations for senior management and stakeholders, and ensuring compliance with standards and guidelines in major accountability documents. Evidence includes the leading role in completion and review of 'Planning Reporting and Accountability Structures, Business Plans, Reports on Plans and Priorities, Departmental Performance Reports'; preparation of 'briefing materials, position papers, Parliamentary questions and answers'; and communication of 'assurances, evaluations advice, and recommendations.' The capability involved is final analytical packaging and readiness of outputs for executive use, governance review, and external accountability. This role fulfills that need directly by collating findings, interpretation, recommendations, and supporting documentation for decision-makers. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase pressure for disciplined sign-off, clearer caveats, richer metadata, and faster but controlled finalization under constrained resources.

This subprocess has limited relevance because it concerns responding to user queries and support requests. The work description does not describe a formal user-support function, but it does show extensive consultation, explanation, and stakeholder engagement responsibilities. Evidence includes ongoing consultations with senior management, interaction with program staff and other planning organizations, and oral and written communication to explain guidelines, priorities, objectives, strategic goals, and methodological approaches. The capability involved is expert advisory support to internal stakeholders rather than operational service-desk support. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment may indirectly affect how this role provides explanatory support, especially through more self-service and standardized knowledge resources, but the connection remains limited.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it gathers evaluation material, quality indicators, feedback, metrics, and evidence for evaluation. The work description is directly centered on evaluation and review activities, collection and analysis of foundation data, performance measurement, monitoring, and maintenance of project files containing evidence and findings. Evidence includes authority 'to scope, plan, authorize, and guide the collection and analysis of the foundation data'; responsibilities for 'establishing performance measurement criteria and processes; monitoring, evaluating and assessing results'; and custody of project working files containing 'evidence (specimens, analysis-documentation, project findings, conclusions and recommendations).' The capability involved is assembling and stewarding the evidence base for evaluation and accountability work. This role fulfills that need directly and continuously. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will increase the volume and richness of process metrics, paradata, system telemetry, and staff feedback available for evaluation. The role's existing emphasis on evidence gathering, monitoring, and analytical records makes it central to this subprocess.

This subprocess is one of the most directly relevant. The work description is fundamentally about conducting evaluations, assessments, reviews, and performance analyses, then synthesizing findings into reports and recommendations. Evidence includes: 'assess the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of programs, operations and initiatives'; 'monitor and assess management accountability for departmental programs'; 'create new information about programs and their effectiveness'; 'The information provides Senior Management with independent, new and unique insights'; and 'develop/recommend ways to improve departmental policies, programs and operations.' The capability involved is expert evaluation of programs, policies, operations, accountability structures, and strategic planning processes. This role fulfills that need directly as a Planning and Evaluation Manager with expert-level program evaluation knowledge, advanced statistical and analytical skills, and authority to lead multidisciplinary evaluation teams. Future-state drivers strongly affect this work. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all change what must be evaluated: efficiency gains, automation impacts, governance effectiveness, workforce readiness, schedule performance, and sustainability under staffing reductions. The role is explicitly positioned to assess these cumulative impacts and recommend future changes.

This subprocess is highly relevant because it turns evaluation findings into agreed actions with accountable owners and monitoring mechanisms. The work description shows that the incumbent's recommendations are used by senior management to make decisions on program scope, structure, redefinition or termination; to implement corrective action; to strengthen strategic and business planning; and to allocate resources effectively. Evidence includes: 'This information is used by Senior Management to make studied decisions respecting organizational performance and changes'; 'recommendations ... to implement corrective action'; 'recommendations are made to the Director ... to effect changes in Divisional plans and programs'; and prioritization of projects for the annual Evaluation Plan with input to strategic planning. The capability involved is translating evaluation evidence into actionable recommendations, priorities, and governance decisions. This role fulfills that need directly through advisory authority, strategic planning input, and leadership in evaluation planning and reporting. Future-state drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity make this even more important. Action plans will increasingly need explicit ownership, milestone discipline, workforce-transition measures, and prioritization of highest-value improvements under constrained resources. The work description's emphasis on change management strategies, resource allocation, strategic planning, and corrective action provides direct evidence of this connection.

This subprocess is relevant because the position directly investigates and identifies evolving statistical needs for the temporal and spatial consumer price index program and considers external practice and emerging developments. The capability involved is strategic program stewardship: determining what statistics are needed, how client needs are changing, and what methodological directions should be pursued. The work description explicitly states that the position 'performs detailed analysis, evaluation and review of statistical methods and concepts to improve existing data and determines changes in the statistical needs of clients' and 'develops new methods and techniques based on leading edge international developments.' It also notes advice to senior managers, Finance Canada, the Bank of Canada, industry, academia, and international statistical institutions, which aligns with identifying needs across multiple users and considering practices of other statistical organizations. Future-state drivers intensify this work: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will force sharper prioritization of which needs can be pursued, with explicit trade-offs under reduced staffing and pressure to find efficiencies. The work description already shows this discipline through assessing impacts, risks, costs, efficiency and productivity of new methods and systems, including big data sources such as scanner and web-scraped data.

This subprocess is implicated because the role helps define what outputs the consumer price index program must produce, at what quality level, and for which users. The capability involved is setting and defending output objectives under methodological, legal, quality and resource constraints. Evidence includes that the position 'plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation' of the program, 'implements new systems or methodologies and processes to meet client demands,' and determines impacts on critical programs and stakeholders. The work also emphasizes that outputs are used by the Bank of Canada for inflation targeting and by other major programs such as Producer Prices and the Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts, showing direct responsibility for ensuring outputs remain fit for high-value uses. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline will increase the need for explicit trade-offs among scope, quality, timeliness and resources, while Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will tighten constraints on what can be sustainably delivered. The position already performs this kind of trade-off analysis by evaluating costs, limitations, short- and long-term impacts, and risks of methodological and system changes.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the position evaluates new data sources, including big data, for suitability in the temporal and spatial CPI program. The capability involved is assessing whether existing or emerging sources can meet statistical requirements, including quality, reliability, operational viability, legal/confidentiality constraints, and technical feasibility. The work description explicitly states that the position 'identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources,' 'evaluates various data sources for relevance and accuracy when integrating them into the statistical program data,' and 'continuously researches and evaluates new data sources in order to maintain the program's relevance and accuracy.' It also references big data such as 'scanner data' and 'web-scraped data,' and notes knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Acts 'particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided' and 'within the context of establishing big data applications.' Future-state impacts are substantial and cumulative: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the importance of assessing non-survey and unstructured sources; AI and Automation in Statistical Production expands usable source types through extraction from unstructured sources; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access raises scrutiny of privacy, authorizations and secure handling; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure makes platform fit, secure access and scalable ingestion core feasibility criteria; Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability increases the importance of metadata completeness and reuse. The position's existing responsibility for evaluating hardware/software suitability, source reliability, and legal/confidentiality implications shows strong alignment.

This subprocess is relevant because the role develops options, assesses costs and benefits, evaluates risks and impacts, and makes recommendations for major methodological and system changes, even though the work description does not explicitly say the incumbent writes formal business cases. The capability involved is building the analytical basis for approval decisions on new or modified production approaches. Evidence includes that the position 'assesses the implications of new approaches and makes recommendations for their adoption,' 'implements new systems or methodologies and processes,' 'evaluates their cost, efficiency and productivity,' and identifies 'short and long term program impact and benefits.' The role also manages project teams, financial resources, milestones and priorities, which supports business-case-like planning. Future-state drivers make this more important: Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline raises the threshold for approval and requires explicit trade-offs; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline emphasizes executable plans, milestones and go/no-go discipline; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment requires stronger justification of savings and affordability; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity means proposals must increasingly account for training, leadership and workforce readiness. The work description already shows these elements through cost assessment, risk analysis, resource planning and recommendations to senior management.

This subprocess is relevant because the role develops and evaluates statistical concepts and methods for temporal and spatial price indexes, which necessarily affects how variables and classifications are defined and derived, even though the work description does not explicitly describe questionnaire-variable design. The capability involved is methodological design of statistical concepts, classifications and derived measures used in CPI production. Evidence includes 'expert knowledge of statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of temporal and spatial price index data' and work to 'develop new methods and techniques.' The role also works with big data and massive volumes of data, implying adaptation of concepts and variables to nontraditional sources. Future-state drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase pressure to harmonize concepts across scanner, web-scraped and other alternative sources, document metadata more rigorously, and support derived variables from integrated data. The relevance is medium because the work clearly shapes concepts and methods, but the supplied description does not explicitly assign direct responsibility for formal variable specification.

This is one of the most directly implicated subprocesses. The role designs and reviews statistical methodology for producing, evaluating and analyzing temporal and spatial consumer price indexes, including integration of large and novel data sources. The capability involved is advanced methodological design for processing, validation, integration, estimation and analysis. Evidence includes that the position 'reviews and evaluates statistical program methods and concepts to improve existing data, to develop new techniques and methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data,' 'selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data,' and 'investigates and challenges existing conceptual frameworks' to generate new solutions. The work also includes evaluating source quality, comparability over time, and operational viability. Future-state drivers strongly reinforce this area: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative/Alternative/Linked Data Expansion, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture and Reusable Components, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition all point toward more automated, metadata-driven, reusable, integration-heavy and model-based processing. The work description already references big data, new hardware/software, systems design knowledge, and the need to assess risks and impacts on major downstream uses such as monetary policy.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position not only develops methods but also implements new systems, evaluates hardware and software, oversees review of processes, and has expert knowledge of systems design relevant to maintaining and developing the CPI program. The capability involved is end-to-end production design: ensuring methods, systems, workflows and responsibilities fit together for sustainable production. Evidence includes 'implements new systems or methodologies and processes to meet client demands,' 'oversees and coordinates the review of established statistical methods and processes,' and 'expert knowledge of systems, systems design and practices relevant for the maintenance and development of the temporal and spatial price index statistical programs.' The role also supervises project teams and sets objectives and training, which aligns with designing how staff interact with systems and workflows. Future-state impacts are major and cumulative: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Governance/Prioritization, Modular Architecture and Reusable Components, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition all point to more standardized, automated, reusable and tightly governed workflows with clearer handoffs and more exception-based human oversight. The work description already shows responsibility for assessing system suitability, operational viability, efficiency and long-term program impacts.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because the role implements new methodologies and systems and evaluates software/hardware suitability, which materially influences the build or reuse of processing and analytical components, though the description does not explicitly state hands-on component development. The capability involved is specifying and steering the operationalization of methods into production components. Evidence includes 'initiates changes and implements new systems or methodologies and processes,' 'evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software,' and expert knowledge of systems design and development environments. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Modular Architecture/Reusability will increasingly convert methodological work into reusable enterprise components and automated services. The role is materially connected because it determines and recommends the methods and systems those components must embody, but the evidence does not explicitly show direct software build responsibility.

This subprocess is relevant because the role implements new systems and methodologies, oversees process reviews, and manages projects and priorities, all of which affect how workflows are configured operationally. The capability involved is translating methodological and system changes into functioning production flows with appropriate sequencing, controls and responsibilities. Evidence includes 'implements new systems or methodologies and processes,' 'oversees and coordinates the review of established statistical methods and processes,' and project management responsibilities for scope, schedule and cost. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility/Timelines, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will make workflow configuration more standardized, automated and milestone-driven. The role is relevant because it shapes and governs these changes, though the description does not explicitly assign direct workflow-configuration duties.

This subprocess is relevant because the role leads implementation of new systems and methodologies, manages project teams, and establishes work objectives and training related to project requirements. The capability involved is preparing modernized methods and systems for operational use, including workforce readiness. Evidence includes 'implements new systems or methodologies and processes,' 'for project team members, establishes work objectives and training related to project requirements,' and advanced knowledge of project management to deliver high-priority projects. Future-state drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increase the importance of documentation, training, controlled deployment and sustainable operating models. The role is materially affected because future implementation work will require more structured workforce enablement and production readiness, even if the description does not explicitly mention final deployment documentation.

This subprocess has limited but plausible relevance because the role works with big data sources such as scanner and web-scraped data and evaluates source availability, reliability, confidentiality and system suitability, which can affect readiness for non-survey source acquisition. The capability involved is ensuring methodological and technical readiness for new source intake rather than managing collection operations directly. Evidence includes identifying availability and reliability of new data sources, evaluating hardware/software, and applying Statistics Act and Privacy Act requirements in establishing big data applications. Future-state drivers around Administrative/Alternative Data Expansion, Cyber Security/Privacy, Enterprise Platforms and Modern Statistical Methods will increase the importance of secure setup for APIs, digital acquisition and source-management processes. Relevance remains low because the work description does not assign direct operational responsibility for collection setup, staff preparation for collection, or supplier onboarding.

This subprocess is directly implicated because the role selects analytical techniques to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data, evaluates multiple data sources for relevance and accuracy, and researches big data applications for the CPI program. The capability involved is multi-source integration, harmonization and source prioritization in a high-stakes statistical program.
