Evidence includes 'selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data,' 'evaluates various data sources for relevance and accuracy when integrating them into the statistical program data,' and research on 'cutting-edge applications of new data sources, including those related to big data.' Future-state drivers strongly amplify this work: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production make integration of scanner, web-scraped and other nontraditional sources central; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access raises the importance of controlled linkage and de-identification; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration make integration more scalable and automated; Metadata-Driven Data Management improves interoperability and reuse. The work description shows this is already core to the role.

This subprocess has plausible but limited relevance. The role works with big data and unstructured or externally coded sources such as scanner and web-scraped data, and develops methods for producing and analyzing data, which may indirectly affect coding and classification approaches. The capability involved would be methodological oversight of how nontraditional inputs are standardized to statistical concepts. Evidence is indirect: references to big data, development of new methods, and expert knowledge of statistical concepts and practices. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods suggest more automated coding of nontraditional inputs, but the work description does not explicitly mention responsibility for coding routines or classification operations. Therefore relevance is low.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role continuously evaluates data quality, comparability, relevance and variance explanations, and assesses impacts and risks of program changes on critical downstream uses. The capability involved is methodological and analytical validation of input and integrated data. Evidence includes 'interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevance in light of changing requirements,' and 'evaluates various data sources for relevance and accuracy when integrating them into the statistical program data.' The role also reviews methods and concepts to improve existing data and assesses risks associated with proposed changes. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative/Alternative/Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Integrated Data Pipelines, Modern Statistical Methods, Modular Architecture/Validation, Operational Efficiency and Workforce Skills Transition all increase the need for scalable, automated, metadata-aware validation with human oversight of exceptions. Given the economic significance of CPI outputs and the stated 'extremely high' impact of errors, this validation role is material and central.

This subprocess is relevant because the role designs and evaluates statistical methods for producing and improving data, including methods suited to large and alternative data sources, which can materially affect editing and imputation strategies even if the description does not explicitly mention those terms. The capability involved is methodological design of correction and replacement approaches for missing, inconsistent or unreliable data. Evidence includes developing 'new techniques and methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data,' evaluating source quality and reliability, and selecting analytical techniques for massive data integration. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Administrative/Alternative Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment point toward more automated, model-assisted and source-prioritized editing/imputation. The role is relevant because it shapes the methods and assesses their impacts, but the supplied description does not explicitly assign operational editing/imputation responsibility.

This subprocess is relevant because temporal and spatial consumer price indexes are themselves highly derived statistical outputs, and the role develops methods and techniques for producing these specialized indexes from multiple data sources. The capability involved is deriving analytical measures and index constructs from collected and integrated data. Evidence includes expert knowledge of 'price index number theory,' development of 'new methods and techniques,' and work to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data in the context of temporal and spatial price index programs. Future-state drivers such as Administrative/Alternative/Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Metadata-Driven Data Management will increase reliance on derived variables and model-based constructs from scanner, web-scraped and other alternative sources. The relevance is medium because derivation is inherent to index production, but the description does not explicitly describe this subprocess in operational terms.

This subprocess is relevant because the role oversees statistical outputs for temporal and spatial consumer price indexes, which are aggregate statistical measures used across government and the economy. The capability involved is producing and assuring aggregate outputs from detailed data using specialized index methodologies. Evidence includes supervision of project teams responsible for 'statistical outputs,' expert knowledge of price index theory, and responsibility for methods used in outputs that affect Producer Prices, macroeconomic accounts and monetary policy. Future-state drivers such as Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production and integrated automated pipelines may change how aggregates are produced, especially with more granular and alternative-source inputs. Relevance is medium because aggregate production is clearly part of the program's outputs, though the description emphasizes methodological leadership more than direct aggregate-calculation operations.

This subprocess has limited relevance because the role oversees methods, systems and outputs that depend on finalized analytic datasets, and future automation and integrated pipelines will affect how those datasets are assembled and handed off. Evidence is indirect through responsibilities for implementing systems/methodologies, reviewing processes, and managing outputs. Future-state drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines, Enterprise Platforms and Metadata-Driven Data Management may materially affect the environment in which the role works. However, the work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for assembling or packaging final data files, so relevance is low.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role is directly responsible for statistical outputs, expert interpretation, methodological explanation and communication of temporal and spatial CPI results to senior officials, policy makers, the public and the media. The capability involved is transforming processed statistical results into usable outputs with supporting methodological explanation. Evidence includes 'supervision of project teams responsible for statistical outputs,' providing expert advice on 'the results of research and analytical studies,' and explaining 'the interpretation of complex data and conceptual frameworks, reasons for variances in the results and the trends derived.' The role also writes papers, articles and reports and determines content of studies and reports disseminated widely. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase automation of standard output preparation while also increasing the need for methodological notes, transparency and explanation of AI- or alternative-data-supported methods. This aligns strongly with the role's communication and analytical responsibilities.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the role validates whether CPI outputs are credible, comparable, relevant and suitable for critical uses such as monetary policy and indexation. The capability involved is domain-informed output validation against expectations, prior patterns, quality indicators and downstream use requirements. Evidence includes interpreting data quality and reasons for variances, assessing comparability over time, evaluating impacts and risks of program changes on other programs and on government-wide and economy-wide uses, and the statement that 'impact of errors is extremely high.' The role also provides expert advice to senior officials and defends the validity of methods in decision-making venues. Future-state drivers such as Administrative/Alternative/Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will make output validation more complex because source substitution, linkage, automation and model-based methods can introduce methodological breaks and new quality risks. The role's deep domain expertise and high-stakes accountability make this a strong match.

This subprocess is one of the clearest matches. The role explicitly interprets and explains CPI outputs to a wide range of audiences, from senior policy makers to the public and media, and provides expert advice on economic and statistical meaning. The capability involved is substantive interpretation, contextual explanation and defense of outputs and methods. Evidence includes providing expert advice to senior officials and policy makers, explaining complex data and conceptual frameworks to the public, giving more detailed explanations to specialized audiences, and defending 'the viewpoint, priorities, conceptual integrity and the validity of methods of the program.' The role also requires expert knowledge of economic and sociological principles, price index theory, and current/emerging economic issues in Canada and internationally. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative/Alternative/Linked Data Expansion, Modern Statistical Methods and Workforce Skills Transition will increase the need to explain outputs produced from mixed-source, automated and model-based methods in clear and trustworthy ways. This is already central to the position.

This subprocess is relevant because the role contributes directly to ensuring outputs are fit for purpose, properly caveated, supported by technical notes and approved for release through expert internal discussion and advice. The capability involved is final analytical and methodological stewardship before release. Evidence includes supervision of statistical outputs, writing and editing papers/articles/reports for wide dissemination, providing expert recommendations to senior managers and external stakeholders, and explaining methods and results to specialized and general audiences. The role also determines impacts of methodological changes on major users and defends conceptual integrity in decision-making venues. Future-state drivers such as Agility/Timelines and Execution Discipline, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Modern Statistical Methods, Governance/Prioritization, Cyber Security/Privacy and Workforce Skills Transition will increase the need for disciplined sign-off, stronger metadata packages, clearer caveats and more explicit explanation of methodological change. The position's senior advisory and stewardship role makes it materially connected.

This subprocess is relevant because the role contributes to the content and explanation of dissemination products through papers, reports, articles, presentations and public/media explanations, though it is not clearly responsible for dissemination production systems. The capability involved is preparing explanatory and analytical content that accompanies released statistics. Evidence includes 'writing and editing skills to write papers, articles and reports,' determining the design and content of studies and reports 'that will be disseminated widely or published,' and explaining results and methods to the public, specialized users and media. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods, and Workforce Skills Transition will increase the need for richer quality statements, methodological notes and accessible digital products. Relevance is medium because the role clearly shapes dissemination content, but the description does not show direct responsibility for assembling publication products or managing dissemination platforms.

This subprocess has limited relevance because the role supports release through briefings, expert explanation and defense of methods, but the work description does not explicitly assign responsibility for release timing, embargoes, subscriber management or controlled-access release operations. Evidence includes advising senior officials, representing the division in meetings where decisions are made, and explaining results to media and the public. Future-state drivers such as Agility/Timelines and Cyber Security/Privacy may affect how the role participates in release-related discussions and briefings, especially given the sensitivity of CPI outputs. However, direct operational release management is not evidenced, so relevance is low.

This subprocess is relevant because the role provides expert advice and consultative services to a broad range of internal and external users and responds to questions about methods, results and interpretation. The capability involved is high-level user support for statistical outputs and methods rather than routine service-desk support. Evidence includes providing expert advice to senior officials, policy makers, business, national agencies and academics; explaining results and methods to the public and specialized audiences; and responding when media representatives challenge or misinterpret results. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Metadata-Driven Data Management, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition may shift some routine support toward self-service and AI-assisted channels, leaving more complex interpretive and methodological support to roles like this one. The role is materially connected through expert user-facing support, though not through formal support-case management.

This subprocess is relevant because the role continuously assesses methods, data quality, source suitability, client needs, impacts and risks, generating the kinds of evidence used in evaluation and continuous improvement. The capability involved is collecting and interpreting analytical evidence on program performance and methodological effectiveness. Evidence includes investigating changes in client needs, evaluating data sources for relevance and accuracy, interpreting quality and comparability, assessing impacts of proposed changes, and monitoring project scope, schedule and cost. Future-state drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative/Alternative Data Expansion, Agility/Timelines, Enterprise Platforms, Integrated Pipelines and Workforce Skills Transition will increase the volume of process metrics, source-quality indicators and workforce-readiness evidence that affect this role's work. The description does not explicitly mention formal evaluation-input compilation, so relevance is medium rather than high.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the role evaluates methods, concepts, systems, data sources, impacts, risks, efficiency and productivity, and makes recommendations for change to the CPI program. The capability involved is formal and informal evaluation of whether the statistical business process is meeting quality, relevance, efficiency and stakeholder requirements. Evidence includes 'performs detailed analysis, evaluation and review of statistical methods and concepts,' 'oversees and coordinates the review of established statistical methods and processes,' 'evaluates their cost, efficiency and productivity,' and 'determines departmental and government-wide impacts and implications and makes recommendations for change.' The role also assesses operational viability, conceptual integrity and user needs. Future-state drivers such as Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Agility/Timelines, Governance/Prioritization, Modern Statistical Methods, Enterprise Platforms and Workforce Skills Transition all make evaluation more central, more dashboard-driven and more focused on trade-offs, sustainability, workforce readiness and modernization outcomes. This is already core work for the position.

This subprocess is relevant because the role not only evaluates and recommends changes but also plans long-term strategies, sets priorities, manages projects and resources, and advises senior management on courses of action. The capability involved is translating evaluation findings into prioritized improvement actions and implementation direction. Evidence includes 'plans and implements long term strategies,' 'assesses the implications of new approaches and makes recommendations for their adoption,' 'determines objectives and priorities for specific studies and provides expert advice and innovative solutions and recommendations to senior management on course of action,' and manages project teams and financial resources. Future-state drivers such as Governance/Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility/Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, Modular Architecture/Reusability, and Workforce Skills Transition will make action planning more explicit, more constrained by scarce resources, and more dependent on clear ownership and sequencing. The role is materially connected because it shapes and recommends action, though the description does not explicitly state formal authority to approve enterprise action plans.

This subprocess is relevant because it covers collection strategy, collection methods, fieldwork operations, respondent engagement, and monitoring of collection arrangements. The work description directly states that the position 'directs statistical data collection activities for the assigned CFOs' and 'contributes to the planning and implementation of collection methodologies and techniques related to the Census Program.' It also says the Area Manager monitors 'response patterns and respondent behaviour, variances in response rates' and advises on options to resolve problems, which aligns with collection design concerns around respondent behaviour, mode strategy, and field operations. The capability involved is operational and managerial expertise in census collection methods, field coordination, and adapting collection approaches across multiple Census Field Offices. Future-state drivers make this even more material: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production point to adaptive collection design, online-first strategy, and changing field roles; AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure point to more digital, monitored, platform-enabled collection operations; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment increases pressure to use lower-touch, standardized, and more efficient collection methods. The work description provides evidence that the incumbent already contributes to methodology and technique decisions and manages large-scale field operations, so these drivers would materially reshape how this work is done over time.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns end-to-end workflow design, reuse of systems and processes, and defining who is responsible for what and when across production. The Area Manager's role is strongly connected to operational workflow design and execution: the position 'contributes to the development of regional strategies and operational plans,' manages 'organization, planning, scheduling and control of Census data collection activities,' and oversees multiple CFOs in a large regional area. The capability involved is operational design and coordination of collection workflows, resource deployment, escalation paths, and role clarity across field offices. This is reinforced by the duty to manage financial, human and material resources and to provide expert guidance to CFO Managers and staff. Future-state drivers are highly relevant here in combination: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline aligns with the role's planning, scheduling, and deadline-driven census operations; Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline aligns with resource allocation, accountability, and trade-offs across offices; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration and AI and Automation in Statistical Production imply more automated, monitored, and standardized workflows; Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development imply more platform-based, reusable operational processes; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is especially relevant because this subprocess explicitly considers staff interaction with systems and responsibilities, and the work description shows the incumbent leads managers, training, and operational guidance. Evidence includes managing a '7-day, collection operation,' resolving resource and recruitment issues, and representing the region on committees discussing modifications to operational procedures.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns configuring workflows and systems for operational use based on designed workflows. The work description does not indicate technical system configuration, but it does show strong operational configuration of collection workflows in practice: the Area Manager manages planning, scheduling, control, and day-to-day operations across multiple CFOs, and resolves operational and resource problems. The capability involved is configuring the operational flow of work across offices, staff, schedules, and collection activities rather than building systems directly. This is supported by evidence that the incumbent makes decisions on 'strategies and operational plans,' 'organization, planning and scheduling of Census data collection activities,' and 'day-to-day management of financial, human and material resources of the CFOs.' Future-state drivers suggest this work will increasingly be affected by workflow standardization, automation, orchestration, and secure digital platforms. Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will intensify milestone-driven operational configuration; Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration will shift more work toward monitoring automated flows and exception handling; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will require managers to help staff operate within new configured workflows; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will push toward simpler, more standardized flows with fewer manual checkpoints. Relevance is medium because the role operationalizes and manages configured workflows rather than technically configuring systems itself.

This subprocess is directly relevant because it covers ensuring people, processes, and technology are ready to collect data, including planning, training, staffing, communications, and operational readiness. The Area Manager's duties map closely to this: managing the organization, planning, scheduling and control of census collection; managing financial, human and material resources; resolving recruitment strategies for CFOs; providing expert direction and guidance to CFO Managers and staff; and leading the preparation and delivery of training to CFO Managers. These are core setup responsibilities. The capability involved is large-scale operational readiness for census collection across multiple field offices, including staffing, training, resource deployment, and readiness monitoring. Future-state drivers intensify this connection. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure is highly relevant because collection setup increasingly depends on digital infrastructure, secure access, and workforce readiness; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production imply more online-first, mixed-source, and digitally enabled collection preparation; AI and Automation in Statistical Production implies new tools and training requirements; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access adds secure setup obligations; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline aligns with the role's deadline-sensitive census readiness responsibilities; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is especially material because the work description explicitly includes training and guidance responsibilities. Evidence includes managing recruitment strategies, leading training, and ensuring effective operations of CFOs within budgets and policy requirements.

This is one of the most directly implicated subprocesses because the work description is fundamentally about running census collection operations. The Area Manager 'manages the organization, planning, scheduling and control of Census data collection activities' for a large regional area, 'directs statistical data collection activities for the assigned CFOs,' monitors response patterns and respondent behaviour, assesses impacts on field operations, and advises on corrective options. The capability involved is operational command of live collection, including field management, response monitoring, issue resolution, respondent participation promotion, and coordination across multiple field offices. The role also represents the department at public relations venues intended to promote Census participation, which supports live collection performance. Future-state drivers compound the impact: Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline is highly relevant because census collection operates to fixed windows and targets; AI and Automation in Statistical Production and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production imply more automated monitoring, adaptive interventions, and digital respondent support; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion implies more mixed-source and online-first collection environments; Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure imply more secure, platform-enabled live operations; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment implies pressure for lower-touch, more efficient collection management; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity implies managers must support staff through changing tools and methods. Evidence is explicit throughout the work description, especially the direct management of collection activities, monitoring of response rates, and decisions to resolve unacceptable response patterns.

This subprocess is relevant at a limited level because it includes pre-release discussion with subject matter experts, supporting information, and approval readiness, and the work description shows the Area Manager contributes operational evaluation and program enhancement input rather than statistical content approval. The position 'oversees the dissemination and collection of evaluation reports for the assigned Region or Regional Census Center' and 'contributes, through briefings to discussions on enhancements to the overall Census Program.' It also represents the region on committees and multidisciplinary project teams as a census collection expert and provides advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures. The capability involved is operational subject-matter expertise feeding into final program and output readiness discussions, especially around collection quality, operational caveats, and lessons learned. Future-state drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production suggest that supporting notes, caveats, and internal briefings will increasingly need to explain operational and methodological changes. Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline may also increase the importance of disciplined briefings and release-readiness discussions. Relevance is low because the work description does not show direct responsibility for approving statistical outputs, but it does show contribution of operational evidence and briefings into those discussions.

This subprocess is directly relevant because the role gathers and oversees operational evidence used for evaluation. The work description states that the Area Manager 'oversees the dissemination and collection of evaluation reports for the assigned Region or Regional Census Center' and monitors response patterns, respondent behaviour, and response-rate variances, assessing their impact on field operations. These are classic evaluation inputs: operational metrics, response indicators, and reports from the field. The capability involved is collecting, interpreting, and organizing operational performance evidence across multiple CFOs so that the census program can assess quality, effectiveness, and needed improvements. Future-state drivers make this more important: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, and Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure all increase the volume and usefulness of monitoring data, paradata, and system metrics; Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production increase the need to gather indicators on mixed-source operations, online response, and changing workloads; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline increases the importance of milestone and schedule evidence; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity increases the importance of staff feedback and readiness indicators. Evidence from the work description includes monitoring response patterns and overseeing evaluation reports, both of which are direct evaluation-input activities.

This subprocess is relevant because the Area Manager does more than gather inputs; the role also analyzes them and contributes to improvement discussions. The work description states that the incumbent 'oversees the dissemination and collection of evaluation reports' and 'contributes, through briefings to discussions on enhancements to the overall Census Program.' It also notes decision-making responsibility for 'the analysis of evaluation reports for the assigned Region or Regional Census Center and recommendations for enhancements to the overall Census Program.' The capability involved is operational evaluation of census collection performance, identifying issues, synthesizing findings, and recommending changes. Future-state drivers suggest evaluation will become more dashboard-driven, continuous, and tied to modernization outcomes: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration increase available performance evidence; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline increase emphasis on productivity, timeliness, and execution performance; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity adds evaluation of training, readiness, and sustainability; Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline increases the need for evidence-based recommendations and prioritization. Relevance is medium rather than high because the work description shows contribution to evaluation and enhancement discussions, but not sole ownership of formal enterprise evaluation reports.

This subprocess is relevant because the Area Manager participates in decision-making and recommendations arising from evaluation and operational issues. The work description shows the incumbent contributes to regional strategies and operational plans, analyzes evaluation reports, makes recommendations for enhancements to the Census Program, represents the region on committees and multidisciplinary project teams, and provides advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures. The capability involved is translating operational evidence into improvement actions, prioritizing responses to collection issues, and contributing to governance discussions on future changes. Future-state drivers reinforce this role: Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline is especially relevant because the role already makes recommendations and participates in committees where trade-offs and accountability matter; Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline aligns with the need for timely operational decisions and action-oriented planning; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will increase pressure to prioritize high-value improvements and efficiencies; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity is relevant because the incumbent leads managers and training and will need to support implementation of agreed changes. Evidence includes recommendations on strategies and operational plans, recommendations for enhancements to the overall Census Program, and advice on modifications to operational procedures. Relevance is medium because the role contributes materially to action planning and implementation discussions, though the description does not state final enterprise approval authority.

This subprocess is relevant because it concerns the initial investigation of what statistics are needed and how needs are identified and scoped. The work description directly states that the position 'investigates client requirements for statistical information,' 'evaluates changes in the statistical needs of clients,' and determines 'sources of information, methods and approaches' for collection, capture, coding and processing. That is direct evidence of identifying and interpreting statistical needs before operational solutions are chosen. The capability involved is translating client and program needs into feasible statistical work, including assessing uniqueness of projects and impacts on other programs. Future-state drivers make this more consequential: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment means needs identification will increasingly require sharper triage, explicit feasibility judgments, and prioritization under reduced staffing and flatter structures. The position is already doing this through decisions on methods, sources, and project objectives, so future changes are likely to intensify the need to balance client demand with efficiency, automation, and lower-cost approaches.

This subprocess is implicated because the role helps define what outputs will be produced, their quality expectations, and the operational trade-offs needed to deliver them. Evidence includes 'defines project objectives and priorities,' 'evaluates the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes, the quality and completeness of outputs,' and 'prepares studies and reports for use by senior management... in assessing the attainment of divisional program objectives.' The capability involved is setting and managing objectives for statistical outputs within legal, methodological and resource constraints. The role is relevant because it not only assesses outputs but also proposes modifications to content, coverage, concepts, methods and operational procedures, which directly shapes output scope and quality. Future drivers matter strongly here: Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline will require clearer accountability, transparent trade-offs, and stronger cross-field prioritization; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will tighten decisions on scope, timeliness, granularity and acceptable quality-service trade-offs. Since this position already plans work, sets priorities, and evaluates output quality and completeness, it will likely face more explicit enterprise constraints and approval discipline in defining what can be sustainably delivered.

This subprocess is materially connected because the work description explicitly requires determining data sources and assessing whether they are suitable for statistical use. Evidence includes 'determines the sources of information,' 'modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones,' 'proposes modifications to program content and coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources,' and 'reviews and modifies existing operational techniques... [including] the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses).' The capability involved is assessing source suitability, comparability, continuity, concepts, and operational feasibility, including translating data collected for other purposes into common concepts. This aligns directly with the subprocess focus on checking whether existing sources can meet requirements and under what conditions. Future-state drivers intensify this connection. Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase reliance on administrative and linked sources rather than survey-only approaches. Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access is also directly relevant because the work description includes responsibility for 'maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files' and emphasizes knowledge of the Statistics Act, Privacy Act, confidentiality and security requirements. Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure and Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability will make platform fit, metadata quality, secure access and interoperability more central to source assessment. Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will further push the role toward lower-cost reusable sources and away from labour-intensive collection.

This subprocess is relevant because the role prepares proposals, work plans, resource estimates and recommendations for changes to systems, methods and tools, even if the description does not explicitly use the term business case. Evidence includes 'defines project objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements to conduct developmental projects; prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources,' 'develops proposals and recommends changes and improvements,' 'plans and budgets for on-going operations and/or special projects,' and 'provides input to budgets based on operational needs.' The capability involved is assembling the operational, methodological, resource and implementation rationale needed for management decisions on new or modified processes. The role fulfills this need by evaluating current systems, identifying inefficiencies, proposing new hardware/software and revised methods, and preparing reports for senior management. Future drivers suggest these activities will become more formalized and demanding: Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline and Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline will require clearer go/no-go logic, milestones, accountability and trade-offs; Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will raise the threshold for approval and emphasize savings, reuse and automation; Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make training, sequencing and workforce readiness more explicit parts of proposals.

This subprocess is relevant because the position helps shape what information is collected, coded and processed, including concepts, definitions and classifications. Evidence includes 'proposes modifications to program content and coverage... concepts, methods and definitions,' 'develops proposals and recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage,' and knowledge requirements covering 'statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data' as well as departmental classification systems. The capability involved is defining and refining the variables, concepts and classifications needed for collection and downstream processing. The role is relevant because it modifies content and definitions and develops new approaches when client needs change. Future drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production will increase pressure to harmonize variables across sources, document metadata more rigorously, and design variables that can be derived or linked rather than only directly collected.

This is one of the most directly implicated subprocesses. The work description repeatedly refers to designing and improving collection methods and procedures: 'evaluates changes in the statistical needs of clients and develops new methods of collecting, coding and processing data,' 'provides advice and guidance to users on the development, operation and use of collection systems and processes,' 'supervises a unit or project team involved in the development of collection procedures,' and 'develops proposals and recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design... revisions to collection or production systems and processes.' The capability involved is designing collection strategy, instruments, procedures, respondent-facing processes and operational systems. The role fulfills this need directly through method development, questionnaire and content changes, operational guidance, and supervision of teams doing collection development. Future drivers will materially reshape this work: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment all point toward online-first, more automated, mixed-source and lower-touch collection models. Workforce implications are also strong because the role supervises staff and develops guidelines, so it will need to support reskilling, digital collection operations, and clearer handoffs across collection and downstream production.

This subprocess is highly relevant because the position develops and evaluates the methods, systems and rules used to process and assess statistical data. Evidence includes 'develops statistical systems and processes,' 'reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures used,' 'reviews and resolves technical and conceptual problems,' 'integrates and analyzes statistical outputs and reviews/certifies the quality and completeness,' and 'reviews and modifies existing operational techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones.' The capability involved is designing processing methodology, integration rules, coding approaches, validation logic and analytical procedures. The role directly fulfills this through system/process development, quality evaluation, integration of multiple sources, and preparation of analytical reviews. Future drivers are especially important here: AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment all point to more automated, reusable, metadata-driven and integrated processing designs. The work description's emphasis on guidelines, procedures, system safeguarding, and technical problem resolution shows the role is already positioned where these changes will land.

This subprocess is directly implicated because the role designs and manages end-to-end statistical systems and operational processes, including staff responsibilities and workflow guidance. Evidence includes 'develops statistical systems and processes,' 'develops and distributes guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of statistical systems and processes,' 'establishes and implements specifications, guidelines and procedures for the maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files,' and 'supervises a unit involved in statistical operations and/or leads project teams.' The capability involved is designing how collection, coding, processing and quality review fit together operationally, including who does what and under what procedures. The role fulfills this need through system/process design, operational supervision, guideline development, and project planning. Future drivers will strongly affect this work: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity all point to more standardized, automated, reusable and tightly governed workflows. Because the work description explicitly includes supervision, planning, role-setting, and system safeguarding, the position is likely to be heavily affected by shifts toward pipeline supervision, exception handling, flatter structures and clearer accountability.

implicated_gsbpm.gsbpm_name: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated_gsbpm.justification: This subprocess is relevant because the role develops statistical systems and processes and recommends new hardware/software and system changes used in processing and analysis. Evidence includes 'develops statistical systems and processes,' 'develops proposals and recommends changes and improvements... revisions to collection or production systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software,' and 'establishes and implements specifications, guidelines and procedures for the maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.' The capability involved is specifying, adapting and operationalizing processing components and supporting services. The role is relevant because it appears to lead or supervise the operational side of such component development and reuse, even if it is not framed as hands-on software build. Future drivers such as Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment suggest greater reuse of shared components, more automation, and stronger governance over production-ready tools. This will likely shift the role further toward selecting, governing and operationalizing reusable enterprise components.

This subprocess is relevant because the role develops procedures and operational guidance that determine how systems and processes are actually run. Evidence includes 'develops and distributes guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of statistical systems and processes,' 'prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources involved in the operation of statistical systems and processes,' and supervision of units involved in statistical operations. The capability involved is translating designed workflows into configured operational practice, including sequencing, responsibilities and controls. The role fulfills this need through operational planning, procedure-setting and supervision rather than explicit technical workflow configuration. Future drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will make workflow configuration more standardized, automated and milestone-driven. That means the role's current responsibility for procedures, priorities and operational coordination will likely shift toward managing automated flows, exceptions and enterprise-standard configurations.

This subprocess is relevant because the role already develops operational guidance and supervises staff who must use statistical systems and processes. Evidence includes 'develops and distributes guidelines, instructions and procedures,' 'prepares and explains specifications and guidelines to be used by others in developing and operating systems and processes,' and leadership responsibilities including recruiting staff, evaluating performance and developing training plans. The capability involved is preparing systems and users for production operation through documentation, procedures, training and operational readiness. The role fulfills this need through guidance, explanation, supervision and training planning, even if the description does not explicitly mention deployment. Future drivers such as Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development will increase the importance of user training, documentation, secure production readiness and support for staff transitioning to modernized systems.

This subprocess is relevant because the role supervises collection-related operations and develops the procedures and systems needed before collection runs. Evidence includes 'provides advice and guidance to users on the development, operation and use of collection systems and processes,' 'supervises a unit or project team involved in the development of collection procedures,' and leadership responsibilities for staffing, training plans and operational planning. The capability involved is ensuring people, processes and systems are ready for collection. The role fulfills this through operational supervision, guidance, staffing and training planning rather than direct field setup. Future drivers such as Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will make collection setup more digital, secure, mixed-source and training-intensive, increasing the operational management burden on this kind of supervisory role.

This subprocess is relevant because the position is an Operations Supervisor and acts as a divisional data collection and operations representative.
